### S-1013 candidates

C28. ID I1 (the guest cannot read or write any host path outside its export) and I4 (the guest cannot reach host-local services),
with I7 when the directory holds another session's sockets; A5's --mount is the mode. Attacker: guest root, driven by a malicious
repository or hostile model output. Precondition the attacker does not control: the operator runs a mount session in a directory
that holds os.TempDir(), as in `cd /tmp && workcell run --mount -- <cmd>` with TMPDIR unset, or with TMPDIR set to a path under
the repository, as a repository's .envrc does once the operator has allowed it (direnv). Where: cmd/workcell/run_vm.go boot (the
S-F14 check is filepath.IsAbs(os.TempDir()) alone, then MkdirTemp("", "wc") and Listen of vsock_5000, vsock_5001 and vsock_5002 in
it, then openMount(cwd), so the sockets lie inside the live export; the comment there says they must not land under a mountable
directory, so this is a gap, not a design); internal/fileserve/ops_linux.go opSymlink (Symlinkat with any target) and opUnlink
(any name under the export); internal/vmm/firecracker/firecracker.go Listen and the unjailed exec as the operator's uid; the
pinned Firecracker's vsock muxer, which connects to <uds_path>_<port> by path on each guest CONNECT (ADR-001 and
internal/vmm/vmm.go record it). Input: the operator runs `cd /tmp; workcell run --mount --allow api.example.com -- claude`. Guest
root: `p=$(find /workspace -name vsock_5001); rm "$p"; ln -s /var/run/docker.sock "$p"` (or any unix socket the operator's uid may
connect to: ssh-agent, gpg-agent, the session bus, another session's attach or vsock socket), then any connect() to an allowed
port, which the init relays to CID 2 port 5001, or a direct AF_VSOCK dial. The guest finds the directory because the whole of cwd
is its /workspace, and firecracker.json beside the sockets names the uds_path. Effect: Firecracker connects to <dir>/vsock_5001,
connect(2) follows the guest's symlink, and the guest's bytes reach the host socket as the operator's uid: docker.sock is root on
the host, ssh-agent and gpg-agent sign with the operator's keys. I1 and I4 broken; the relay listener lives for the whole session,
so every later CONNECT is redirected. Lesser variants: rm of vsock_5001 ends the guest's own network, rm of attach breaks workcell
attach. Evidence: the auditor ran the real binary in a mount session with TMPDIR equal to cwd and below it against a stand-in VMM
that listed its directory: both runs passed every refusal into boot and the stand-in listed <cwd>/tmp/wcNNN holding
firecracker.json and the three sockets with uds_path inside the export; an overlay test against the real fileserve Server answered
0 to UNLINK of a listening socket and SYMLINK of its name to a victim socket, after which a host dial of the export path reached
the victim; the muxer source of the pinned v1.17.0, fetched as data, builds the per-port path and connects by it. Reproducing
test: escape/_pending/S-F20/c28_test.go TestC28TempDirInMountExport (redteam; package main in cmd/workcell, arms cwd and cwd/tmp):
drives the real session() in mount mode with cwd as the export and TMPDIR equal to cwd and a subdirectory of it, with c19Data's
dummy artifacts, and wants an error naming os.TempDir(), no new session directory with a vmm boot record, and no wc* left under
TMPDIR. On d998add both arms fail in 0.02 s: `session failed with "start firecracker: invalid argument", want a refusal naming the
temp directory ... inside the export` and `the session reached boot: the VMM's sockets were made in .../wcNNN, inside the mount
export ... (I1, I4)`. Outcome: CONFIRMED, medium, by the verifier, who ran the test (both arms fail the same way), traced the
chain by code (Symlinkat with an arbitrary target and Unlinkat for any name under the export, sockets visible to the guest as row
21 of the adversarial fileserve table shows; Firecracker execs unjailed as the operator with uds_path <Dir>/vsock; the per-CONNECT
connect by path in ADR-001 and vmm.go), and found no escape mount row that places TMPDIR in the export, so nothing contradicts it;
the test takes only the operator's step and no attacker power; the precondition is operator-chosen, so medium under S6, not high;
not S14, because Firecracker's connect by path is its documented design and the defect is the socket placement here. Fix unit:
S-F20, below S-1013 in PLAN.md: boot() refuses an os.TempDir() that lies inside the mount export, comparing resolved paths as
holds() does, before MkdirTemp; clone mode needs nothing, since the export is taken before the sockets are made. Variants the
redteam could not express without a VM: the symlink-and-dial itself against vsock_5001, vsock_5000 and vsock_5002, TMPDIR that is
a symlink resolving under cwd, a trailing slash or .. components, the attach socket redirected to a guest-chosen socket, and
racing the unlink against the init's first CONNECT. Not ported.

C29. ID I7 (nothing a session writes is visible to another, and rm leaves nothing behind), with the operator's stop and rm verbs
turned against the host; I9 and I13 hold, because no cwd strictly inside the data or config directory contains audit.key or
config.toml. Attacker: guest root, by a malicious repository or hostile model output. Precondition the attacker does not control:
the operator's cwd, or the pull destination, lies strictly inside the data directory, as in `cd ~/.local/share/workcell/sessions
&& workcell run --mount -- <cmd>`, or layers/<agent>, caches or sessions/<id>. S-F12's holds() asks whether the held directory
lies below cwd and never whether cwd lies below it, so this is the half of C19 that S-F12 left open. Where: cmd/workcell/data.go
holds (filepath.Rel(resolved(dir), resolved(held)) one way); run_vm.go session and pull_vm.go fetch, its callers; session.go
supervisor (trusts the pid text in lock), removeSession (RemoveAll of every existing absolute wc* directory that vmm names),
stopSession (the SIGTERM, SIGTERM, SIGKILL ladder while running() is true) and newest (trusts repo); layer.go findLayers (trusts
layers/<agent>/current, no digest check). Input: clone: `cd <data>/sessions && workcell run -- true`. Mount: the same with
--mount, then guest root under /workspace reads any <id>/workspace.ext4 and <id>/audit.log, writes "<victim pid>\n" to its own
<id>/lock, appends another running session's /tmp/wcNNN to its own <id>/vmm, rewrites another session's repo or workspace.ext4, or
in a layers/<agent> cwd writes current and a new image. Effect: clone: the new guest's image carries every other session's image
and record (I7). Mount: all of that live, and afterwards `workcell stop <id>` signals the pid the guest wrote (the real
supervisor's flock keeps running() true, so the ladder reaches SIGKILL), `workcell rm <id>` removes the other session's socket
directory, a later `workcell pull` boots the guest's chosen image, and a layers cwd lets the guest choose the next session's
/opt/<agent>. Evidence: the auditor's overlay test showed holds(<data>/sessions), holds(<data>/layers/claude) and
holds(<data>/caches) returning nil, and session() with cwd <data>/sessions in clone mode ran to boot and left an image in which
debugfs listed the other session's audit.log, repo and workspace.ext4 and returned its marker bytes; the mount variants are read
from session.go and fileserve's write path. Reproducing test: escape/_pending/S-F21/c29_test.go
TestC29RefusesACwdInsideTheDataDirectory (redteam; package main in cmd/workcell; arms clone_in_sessions, mount_in_sessions,
mount_in_layers and pull_into_sessions): with XDG_DATA_HOME under a temp directory, c19Data's dummy artifacts and an earlier
session, the real session() with cwd <data>/sessions (clone and mount) and <data>/layers/agent (mount) must return an error naming
both cwd and the data directory, and pull into <data>/sessions from a repository elsewhere must exit 1 with one stderr line naming
both; then no new session directory and no vmm boot record. Naming cwd in the message matters, because the boot error already
names <data>/firecracker. On d998add all four arms fail in 0.04 s: `session failed with "start firecracker: invalid argument",
want a refusal naming .../workcell/sessions inside .../workcell`, `a session directory ... was made inside the directory the guest
gets (I7)`, and for pull `the session reached boot: .../workcell/sessions/<idOld>/vmm was written`. Outcome: CONFIRMED, medium, by
the verifier, who ran the test (all four arms fail the same way), showed the clone effect follows from Export copying everything
under cwd (the log proves Export of <data>/sessions succeeded, since boot was reached) and the mount effects from supervisor,
stopSession, removeSession, newest and findLayers trusting guest-writable bytes; the test takes only the operator's step; the
precondition is a cd into the product's private state, not attacker-controlled, so not high, and a break of I7 is shown by
mechanism, so not low: medium by S6's letter, as C19, though its precondition is far less ordinary than C19's `cd ~`. One
correction: the test's first draft reported audit.key as minted inside the directory the guest gets, a leftover of c19Untouched,
where for these cwds the key lies at <data>/audit.key above the export; the redteam reworded that judge before the file was

C30. ID I6 (on a terminated connection the upstream certificate matches one allowed name under the host's trust) and through it I5
(the real secret is injected only into a verified connection). PARKED line 77, the S-F14 reviewer's finding, now with a
reproducing test. Attacker: a malicious repository supplying ca.pem, a CA the attacker made whose leaf key it keeps, completed by
the network attacker as the host's DNS for an allowed name (the rebind position of the rebind-* rows) or on path. Precondition the
attacker does not control: the operator's environment holds a relative SSL_CERT_FILE, such as `SSL_CERT_FILE=ca.pem` or a literal
`~/ca.pem` left unexpanded by /etc/environment or environment.d, the same class as C21's relative XDG value. Where:
internal/proxy/terminate.go upstreamRoots (os.ReadFile(certFile) with no IsAbs check), called from Terminate with
os.Getenv("SSL_CERT_FILE") as it is; and x509.SystemCertPool there, whose Linux loader reads SSL_CERT_FILE against cwd too, before
the product does, so a check after the pool is built is too late. cmd/workcell/run_vm.go session takes the repository as cwd from
Getwd and boot builds the proxy in-process, and nothing in cmd/workcell touches SSL_CERT_FILE or changes directory, so the proxy
reads the file from the repository. Input: the repository holds ca.pem. The operator, with SSL_CERT_FILE=ca.pem in the
environment, runs `workcell run --allow api.anthropic.com -- <cmd>` with a [[secret]] row bound to that host. The network attacker
answers the host's lookup of api.anthropic.com with its own address and presents a leaf for api.anthropic.com signed by the
repository's CA. Effect: the terminating proxy's upstream transport verifies the attacker's leaf against a pool that holds the
repository's CA, forwards the request with the real secret swapped into the bound header, and the secret reaches the attacker: I6
and I5 broken for every terminated name of the session. Evidence: the auditor's overlay test in package proxy, with cwd a
directory holding a NewSessionCA certificate as ca.pem, saw upstreamRoots("ca.pem"), ("./ca.pem") and ("../<dir>/ca.pem") each
return a pool and a nil error, and a leaf that CA issued for example.com verified against each pool. Reproducing test:
escape/_pending/S-F22/c30_test.go TestRelativeSSLCertFileIsRefused (redteam; package proxy in internal/proxy, two arms in one
test): with cwd a temp directory holding a ca.pem the test made, upstreamRoots must return an error for "ca.pem", "./ca.pem" and
"../<dir>/ca.pem"; then end to end, with SSL_CERT_FILE=ca.pem through t.Setenv, a real Proxy from testProxy with the roots left to
Terminate, a loopback TLS upstream presenting a leaf for api.example.com issued by that CA and echoing X-Api-Key, a fake broker
holding "real-secret" and a client request carrying the placeholder, the response must be 400 or more and carry no "real-secret",
or Terminate must refuse. On d998add it fails in 0.01 s: the three spellings `read the repository's file against the working
directory without error; want a refusal`, and `through a relative SSL_CERT_FILE the attacker's upstream answered (200,
"real-secret"); want the secret withheld`. Outcome: CONFIRMED, medium, by the verifier, who ran the test (the same four lines; the
package is green with this one test skipped), checked the fixture against the real path (boot builds the proxy in-process and bind
calls Terminate; session's cwd is the repository; Terminate passes the environment value straight to upstreamRoots; Go 1.27.4's
loadOnDiskRoots also reads the file against cwd), found that the test gives itself only the repository's ca.pem, the shared lookup
and dial seams that stand for the MITM I6 exists to defeat, and the environment precondition, and held medium under S6 as C21 was:
a demonstrated break with one uncontrolled precondition, where low would mean no demonstrated break. Fix unit: S-F22, below S-1013
in PLAN.md: upstreamRoots refuses, not ignores, a relative certFile with one error naming SSL_CERT_FILE before x509.SystemCertPool
runs, so termination fails closed as it does for an unreadable file. Variants the redteam could not express: a relative
SSL_CERT_DIR (Go's own loader reads it against cwd too; the product never reads it, and the process-wide pool cache makes a unit
test order-dependent), a relative SSL_CERT_FILE that is a symlink or a directory in the repository, a bundle with a hostile CA
appended after a legitimate operator one, a CLI-level arm, and the macOS platform verifier, where only the product's own read
matters. Ported: also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go.

C30 FIXED by S-F22, commit 9577f31 (PR #239). upstreamRoots in internal/proxy/terminate.go refuses a non-empty certFile that does not
start with / before x509.SystemCertPool runs, with one error `SSL_CERT_FILE "<value>" is relative: set an absolute path`, so Terminate
returns it before p.ca or p.transport are set, bind in cmd/workcell/run_vm.go returns it through fail(0, err) before any VM boots, and
run prints it as one line; an absolute file or an unset variable behaves as before. HasPrefix("/") equals filepath.IsAbs on Linux and
macOS, the only hosts, and saves the import; the four-line doc comment folded to one, so net 0 product lines, product 15000 of 15000.
Test: internal/proxy/c30_test.go TestRelativeSSLCertFileIsRefused, moved by git mv unchanged; its four arms fail on 5e4fec8 (the
three spellings return a pool and nil, and the attacker's upstream answered 200 with "real-secret") and pass at 9577f31 under -race
with the rest of internal/proxy, including the absolute-file and missing-file cases of terminate_test.go. The reviewer confirmed the
failure in a worktree at 5e4fec8 and considered "~/ca.pem", "//x", "/./x", NUL, a directory and a symlink (refused, absolute,
absolute, read error, read error, the operator's own). Also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go.

C31. ID none directly: I12's "confuse the host" in spirit and the product's own rule, set by C20 and S-F13, that a guest-chosen
name is quoted before it reaches the operator's terminal; hardening, as C20. Attacker: guest root in a mount session, since
fileserve honours Mkdirat's mode (codec.go takes Mode and Name from the guest, checkName refuses only "", ".", "..", "/" and NUL,
and ops_linux.go opMkdir applies Mode&0o777, so a mode-0 directory owned by the operator with ESC and BEL bytes in its name is
left in the operator's tree); hostile model output naming the directory. A malicious repository alone cannot carry the trigger:
git stores no directory mode and pull creates directories 0o755, so a cloned tree carries the hostile name but not the open
failure that prints it. Where: internal/guest/walk.go lines 31, 44, 50 and 57 (`%s` with the raw entry name; compare in
cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go returns it unwrapped and diff prints it with Fprintln) and internal/workspace/workspace.go lines 91, 109,
119, 131 and 152 (`%s` with the raw host path; run prints `copy <cwd> for the guest: ...` with it); only shown in pull.go and the
guest-side Walk error in pull_vm.go quote. Input: in a mount session the guest runs `mkdir -m 0 "/workspace/$(printf
'\033]0;owned\a\033[2J\033[31mREADME')"`; later the operator, not root, runs a clone-mode `workcell run` in that tree, or
`workcell diff` where the newest session is a clone one and the mount session ran in a subdirectory. Effect: run prints `copy
<cwd> for the guest: open <cwd>/\x1b]0;owned\a\x1b[2J\x1b[31mREADME: permission denied` and diff prints `open \x1b]0;owned...:
permission denied` raw: the terminal's title is set, the screen cleared and recoloured, OSC 52 where the terminal allows it. No
crash, hang or confusion of the process itself. Evidence: the auditor's overlay tests in packages guest and workspace, run with
CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE and CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH dropped from the bounding set so the mode-0 directory refuses as it does for an operator,
failed with a raw 0x1b at offset 5 (Walk) and 58 (Export). Reproducing tests: escape/_pending/S-F23/guest_c31_test.go
TestC31WalkErrorQuotesName (for internal/guest) and workspace_c31_test.go TestC31ExportErrorQuotesPath (for internal/workspace)
(redteam): each makes a mode-0 directory named "\x1b]0;owned\x07\x1b[2J\x1b[31mREADME" under a temp root, calls Walk on the root's
descriptor or Export to a fresh image, skips with a reason if the open succeeds (a root runner), and otherwise fails if the error
carries any byte below 0x20 or 0x7f. On d998add, under `setpriv --bounding-set -dac_override,-dac_read_search go test`, both fail:
`the error carries a raw control byte the terminal would obey: "open \x1b]0;owned\a\x1b[2J\x1b[31mREADME: permission denied"` and
the same with the host path; as plain root both skip; the hosted gate runs as a normal user, so there they fail without any trick
(the redteam also ran the compiled test binaries as uid 65534 with the same two failures). Outcome: CONFIRMED, low, by the
verifier, who ran both tests both ways, traced walk.go's error through compare and fetch to diff's Fprintln and workspace.go's
through run_vm.go's copy error to run's Fprintln with nothing quoting on the way, confirmed the mount guest's mode-0 directory
from codec.go and ops_linux.go, refuted the repository arm on its own (no directory mode in git, 0o755 on pull), and held low
under S6: no invariant breaks, the effect is control of the operator's screen, not of the host process; FINDINGS.md's S-1008
handoff already parked the walk.go site as the C20 class. Fix unit: S-F23, below S-1013 in PLAN.md: `%s` to `%q` at the four
walk.go sites and the five workspace.go sites, net 0 product lines. Variants the redteam could not express: the other sites in the
same functions (an unlistable but readable directory, a readlink failure, tree.Put's rejection) and the end-to-end run and diff
prints, which need a VM. Not ported.

C31 FIXED by S-F23, commit 9170094 (PR #240). `%s` became `%q` at the nine sites the record names:
internal/guest/walk.go lines 31, 44, 50 and 57 and internal/workspace/workspace.go lines 91, 109, 119, 131 and 152,
so Walk's and Export's errors now carry the guest-chosen name or the host path quoted once, as `open
"\x1b]0;owned\a\x1b[2J\x1b[31mREADME": permission denied`. Line 42 of workspace.go (the operator's own cwd) is unchanged, as the
record asks. Nine in-place edits, net 0 product lines: product 15000 of 15000 before and after, test 28085 of 28500 with the two
tests now under internal/. Inner errors at the nine sites: Fstatat, Openat and Readlinkat return a bare unix.Errno and tree.Put

## S-1016: the tool findings and the Mac fuzz crasher (S10), triaged under S4 against main as it stands

Inputs, under loop/private/findings-in/, which git ignores (H-1015): three result sets of the Claude Security plugin at `high`,
A 20261117-123751 (whole repository, scanned at 7731bd9, 10 findings), B 20261118-221116 (nine directories, at 7731bd9, 16) and

fuzz targets. The findings are the candidates, so no auditor ran. Their text was read as data. Each is judged against main, not
against the scanned commit, and has exactly one outcome; S-1016 holds the closing count. Parts: S-1016b (below), S-1016c, S-1016d
and S-1016.

### S-1016b: the proxy and the secrets, at main 05a59da (twelve findings and the crasher)

Method. One redteam per topic wrote a test in the package where it will live and ran it through `go test -overlay` from
escape/_pending/, so no file lay in internal/ or cmd/; the orchestrator ran each test again and kept the logs under loop/private/
(c32-run.log to c35-run.log); one verifier per candidate got the claim, the test and the log, and tried to refute it. The Mac
gate was green on the unchanged tree before (73 rows, GATE PASS in 430s).

| finding | outcome |
|---------|---------|
| A F17, C F1 | CONFIRMED, C32 arm a (I5, high) |
| A F18, A F19, C F2, C F7 | CONFIRMED, C32 arm b (I6, medium); C F2 names both arms |
| C F9 | CONFIRMED, C33 (I5, medium) |
| A F20, B F6, B F7 | CONFIRMED, C34 (I5 through I13, medium), one defect with two paths |
| C F10 | CONFIRMED, C35 (I13, medium) |
| A F24 | DOWNGRADED to low, C36: intended prefix rule, no fix unit, PARKED |
| crasher FuzzHide/cff1bc4cc7889cf3 | REFUTED, C37: the fuzz judge, not hide |

C32. ID I5 (arm a) and I6 (arm b). Attacker: guest root. Where: internal/proxy/terminate.go, the terminated handler (its host
check near line 405, the rule loop at 415, the placeholder check at 434) and internal/proxy/signin.go tokenEndpoint (70 to 77),
which judge r.Host, r.URL.Path and EscapedPath; httputil.ReverseProxy then writes r.URL.Opaque as the request-target. Input: on a
terminated HTTP/1.1 connection the guest writes a request line whose target is `x:https://HOST/PATH`. net/url parses it to
Scheme x, Opaque `https://HOST/PATH` and an empty Path, so every check that reads the path or the URL's host sees nothing, and
the upstream receives the well-formed absolute-form target `https://HOST/PATH`, which RFC 9112 3.2.2 says a server must accept
and must prefer to the Host header. Arm a: `POST x:https://login.example.com/oauth/token` with a code grant is not marked as a
token request, so neither the body swap nor tokenResponse runs, and the endpoint's answer reaches the guest unread:
`{"access_token":"sk-acc-1",...,"refresh_token":"sk-ref-1"}`. Arm b: `GET x:https://other.example/collect` with Host
example.com and the placeholder in the bound header passes the host check on the Host header, a rule with no path admits it, the
real secret is swapped in, and the upstream at the vetted address of example.com receives
`GET https://other.example/collect | Host: example.com | X-Api-Key: real-secret`. Reproducing test: escape/_pending/S-F25/
c32_test.go TestC32OpaqueRequestTarget (redteam; package proxy, two arms, the far ends are net/http servers on loopback). On
05a59da both arms fail: `I5: the guest read a real token through an opaque target` and `I6: upstream got the real secret for
authority other.example`. Outcome: CONFIRMED by the verifier, who ran the test, wrote the raw request line over TLS in a probe of
its own with the same result, and checked the fixture against the path cmd/workcell builds (Serve, the SNI peek,
serveTerminated, the ReverseProxy over p.transport; the doubles are lookup, dial, roots and broker only). Arm a, high: the
operator has a `signin:` row and signs in for the session, the code reaches the guest's CLI as it must, the guest exchanges it
through the opaque target and keeps both real tokens, and refreshes by itself afterwards (an opaque refresh with the real
refresh token gave 200 and a new access token); an opaque refresh with the placeholder crosses unswapped and gets 400, so the
proxy adds no real value itself; origin form, plain absolute form and `x://host/path` all come back with placeholders. The only
thing needed of the server is that it serves absolute-form, which the RFC demands and unmodified net/http does; it would be
medium if that, or the unsupported state of sign-in (docs/providers.md), counted as the precondition. Arm b, medium: the peer is
the vetted address and the certificate is example.com's, so I6's letter (SNI, Host header, certificate) holds, but the product
already refuses the same request in plain absolute form with 421 host_mismatch, so the opaque form evades an existing check;
harm needs the allowed name to sit on a shared front end that routes on the target's authority, which the attacker does not
control (a neighbour tenant there is an in-scope host, not a compromised provider). Narrowed rows are safe (POST /v1/ and repos
rules gave 403); rows with no path, which is every shipped provider row, are exposed. HTTP/1.1 only: the terminated side offers
no h2. This contradicts the second half of the S-1005 sentence above ("An opaque target reaches the right host as a malformed
request-target only"): only shapes such as `x:oauth/token` are malformed. Fix unit: S-F25. Variants not expressed: an encoded
authority (`x:https:%2f%2f...`), `OPTIONS *`, a second request pipelined after a 502. Ported: also in v1 main:
egressproxy/terminate.go (signin.go is v2's own).
Upstream: the forwarding half is public as Go issue 82431 (ReverseProxy does not clear URL.Opaque; closed 2026-11-04, fixed on
Go's main branch, not in go 1.27.4, which a run on 1.27.4 showed), so S14 holds nothing back; S-F25 is still needed.

also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go
C32 FIXED by S-F25, commit 065da63 (PR #254). The terminated handler in internal/proxy/terminate.go now refuses, as its first
statement and so before the method, host, rule, token and placeholder judges, any request whose target is neither origin-form
nor absolute-form: r.URL.Opaque set (`x:https://HOST/PATH`, `x:oauth/token`, an encoded authority) or a scheme with no host
(`x:`, `x:/p`, `https:///p`); 400 with a constant body, one deny record `target_refused`, nothing dialled or sent upstream, and
the broker is not asked. Origin-form, plain absolute-form (userinfo and http scheme included), `OPTIONS *` (C27) and CONNECT (405)
behave as before; the reviewer wrote each form raw over TLS and read what the upstream double received. Both arms of
internal/proxy/c32_test.go, moved from escape/_pending/S-F25/, fail on 717c747 and pass on the fix, and now also require 400.
Paid by two folds in terminate.go (a doc comment re-wrapped, the Rewrite assignments joined): product 15000 of 15000.

C33. ID I5 (a placeholder is useless outside its binding). Attacker: guest root. Where: internal/proxy/terminate.go admits (128
to 130) with fold in internal/proxy/signin.go (84). Input: under a rule narrowed to POST with path `/v1/`, the guest sends
`POST /v1/a%2Fb/../../admin` with the placeholder. admits judges the path as sent (the prefix /v1/ holds) and fold's reading,
which decodes %2F before path.Clean and gives /v1/admin; no reading cleans the still-encoded path, and the path is forwarded as
sent. An upstream that removes dot segments while %2F is still opaque and decodes afterwards (RFC 3986 5.2.4 on the raw path)
serves /admin with the real secret, outside the rule; the comment above admits promises that neither an encoded slash nor `..`
leads out on either reading. Reproducing test: escape/_pending/S-F26/c33_test.go (redteam; package proxy, C10's fixture, an
upstream that reads path.Clean of EscapedPath). On 05a59da it fails: `I5: upstream served "/admin" with the real secret, outside
the rule's path "/v1/"`. Outcome: CONFIRMED, medium, by the verifier: not a duplicate of C10, whose test upstream decodes first and serves this
spelling inside the rule, and whose nearest row needs a ;param; a WHATWG URL parser gives /admin for it (checked with node),
which is how fetch-style runtimes read a path, and from memory Kestrel, Envoy with normalize_path and Jetty or Tomcat with
encoded separators allowed do too, while nginx and HTTP.sys decode first and Apache and default Tomcat refuse %2F; Go's ServeMux
answers 307 to /admin, whose resend the product refuses. Medium as C10: the bound host must sit behind such a router. Fix unit:
S-F26. Variants not expressed: double percent-decoding (PARKED), the same spelling against a repos rule. Ported: also in v1
main: egressproxy/terminate.go.

also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go
C33 FIXED by S-F26, commit 5983bd9 (PR #255). admits in internal/proxy/terminate.go and tokenEndpoint in internal/proxy/signin.go
now judge a path under a third reading beside the path as sent and fold's: fold of the path with each encoded slash or backslash
(%2F, %5C, any hex case) doubly encoded, so that ;params are cut, everything else is decoded, a backslash is folded and the dot
segments are resolved while the separators stay opaque, as a router that removes dot segments before it decodes reads it. A path
is admitted under a prefix, or within a repository, only when every reading stays inside; a token-endpoint path is claimed when
any reading names it. The builder drove %2E%2E and .%2E dot segments, lowercase hex, mixed %2F and %5C, %252F, a ;param beside
the dot segment and a trailing .. through a throwaway test: all refused under POST /v1/, and /v1/a%2Fb/c, /v1/a%2Fb/./c and
/v1/a/../b served as before. internal/proxy/c33_test.go, moved from escape/_pending/S-F26/, states the accept text in three
arms; the two bad arms fail on 482ad45 with `got 200 "/admin real-secret", want 403` and pass on the fix. Paid by re-wrapping the
sign-in paragraph of signin.go: product 15000 of 15000, test 28498 of 28500. The review round did not finish: a safeguard stopped
the reviewer, which was not retried or rephrased (S11).

C34. ID I5, reached through I13. Attacker: the malicious repository. Where: internal/policy/policy.go Narrow (the name path at
140, the allow path at 147), cmd/workcell/policy.go loadPolicy, and internal/proxy/signin.go tokenEndpoint, which rewrites a
token answer only for a host that has a sign-in rule. Input: the user's config has a [[secret]] row with a `signin:HOST/PATH`
source. The repository's workcell.toml either names a [[secret]] row of another name (A F20), or gives an allow array that keeps
the token host and leaves out the row's API host (B F6); B F7 is both, seen from loadPolicy. Narrowing drops the row and leaves
the token host allowed and terminated on 443, so the session starts with no rule that reads that host's token answers, and when
the operator completes a sign-in in that session the real access and refresh tokens reach the guest. `run` says nothing: it
discards the note that `explain` prints. Reproducing test: escape/_pending/S-F27/c34_test.go TestC34SignInRowDropped (redteam;
package main in cmd/workcell, through loadPolicy as run calls it; it first checks that without a repository file the rule
exists). On 05a59da both subtests fail: `I5: the session starts with the token host login.c34.test allowed on 443 and no rule
that rewrites its token answers`. The test stops at the effective policy. Outcome: CONFIRMED, medium, by the verifier, who
closed that gap with a scratch test on the sign-in fixture of internal/proxy: with the rule the guest reads placeholders, and
with Terminate given no rule, which is what run builds once the row is gone, it reads `200 {"access_token":"sk-acc-1",...,
"refresh_token":"sk-ref-1"}`. Not intended: docs/policy.md documents dropped rows as a narrowing and nowhere says that a dropped
sign-in row leaves its token host open and unread. Medium, not high: it needs a user config with a sign-in row, and an operator
who signs in inside that hostile session; sign-in is supported for no shipped provider, which narrows reach and does not make it
low. Fix unit: S-F27. Variants not expressed: the wire proof on a real VM (the sign-in sandbox plus a workcell.toml in the
workspace), a mount session whose earlier guest wrote workcell.toml, a repository naming only a second row on the same host.
Not ported: internal/policy, cmd/workcell and signin.go are v2's own.

C34 FIXED by S-F27, commit 4ffa02b (PR #256). loadPolicy in cmd/workcell/policy.go keeps the user's policy and builds the
allowlist and the bindings from the narrowed one; once the --allow entries are added and the final allowlist is built, it walks
the user's rows and refuses the session, before any boot, for a row whose source parses as a sign-in, whose token host is on the
final port-443 allowlist (TLSHosts, so letter case and port spellings are judged as the proxy judges them) and which narrowing
dropped: `<config.toml>:<line>: secret "k": workcell.toml drops this sign-in row but keeps its token host "login.c34.test": name
the row there, or drop the host`, exit 2 from `explain` and `run` alike, since both call loadPolicy. A dropped row whose token
host went with it, a repository file that keeps the row, and no repository file behave as before. Both paths of the finding, a
[[secret]] row of another name and an allow array without the API host, are closed, and so are the --allow re-adding of either
host, two user rows sharing a token host, and a row that bindings itself refuses (reviewer, about 25 shapes through `explain`).
cmd/workcell/c34_test.go, moved from escape/_pending/S-F27/ unedited, states the accept text; both subtests fail on f796f2d
and pass on the fix. Paid by re-wrapping the doc comment of loadPolicy (8 to 4 lines): product 15000 of 15000, test 28498 of
28500. One review round, no findings. docs/policy.md says in one sentence what the refusal is for.

C35. ID I13 (workspace content can only narrow), with I5 through it reasoned and not shown. Attacker: the malicious repository,
and a mount guest that writes the file live. Precondition the attacker does not control: the user's config has a `cmd:` row
whose program honours its working directory. Where: internal/secret/source.go run, which sets cmd.Env and no cmd.Dir; nothing
in cmd/workcell changes directory, session takes the workspace from os.Getwd, and the in-process broker resolves on each use of
the placeholder (terminate.go 424, Lookup, Resolve, run), so the helper's working directory is the repository and the guest
picks the moment. Input: the repository holds what the helper looks up from its working directory. Reproducing test:
escape/_pending/S-F28/c35_test.go TestC35CmdHelperDoesNotObeyTheRepository (redteam; package secret, a helper the test builds).
On 05a59da it fails: `I13: the helper resolved "repository-value in <dir>": the repository's c35.conf decided the value; want
operator-value`; with cmd.Dir set to / in an overlay copy it passes. Outcome: CONFIRMED, medium, by the verifier, whose own
probe through Resolve with a system program showed more than the test's stand-in: `cmd:/usr/bin/python3 -m keyring get workcell
anthropic`, the documented use of that tool, with a planted keyring/__main__.py in the working directory returned the
repository's value and wrote a marker as the operator's uid, and a planted base64.py beat the installed module for
`python3 -m base64`: repository code running on the host as the operator, outside the guest and the egress policy. The redteam
saw the same with `git config --get` and a `!` alias from the directory's .git/config. Value substitution alone gains nothing,
since the guest can already send any value to the bound host; the break is the code. The fixed program path and the scrubbed
environment stop PATH and variable hijack and not the search of the working directory; docs/policy.md lists what the helper
inherits and is silent on the directory, and the `cmd:` form gives the operator no way to set one. Medium as C21 and C30, on an
operator-side precondition that here is a documented config form. `keychain:` and `secret-service:` are not affected. Fix unit:
S-F28. Variants not expressed: the live mount race on a VM, a helper that prompts on the supervisor's terminal, a relative HOME
inherited by the helper. Ported: also in v1 main: credbroker/cli.go (resolveSource, the origin U-400b names).

C35 FIXED by S-F28, commit 32c6e7d (PR #257). run in internal/secret/source.go sets cmd.Dir to `/` before it starts any
program, so a `cmd:` helper, `/usr/bin/secret-tool` and `/usr/bin/security` all run with the root directory as their working
directory, whatever directory the operator started the session from: `/` is root-owned, mode 755, and is never under TMPDIR
(C28). A helper that honours a file or a module of its working directory now finds nothing of the repository's; a relative
HOME resolves under `/` too, and a relative argument is looked up in `/` (reviewer, probes through Resolve from the repository,
/tmp and $HOME, with HOME unset, `.`, `./sub` and a bare name). internal/secret/c35_test.go, moved from
escape/_pending/S-F28/ with only its head comment changed, fails on main 1a57192 with the recorded I13 message and passes on
the fix under -race. Paid by folding the secret-tool comment onto the loop line it explains: product 15000 of 15000, test
28498 of 28500. docs/policy.md says in one sentence that the program runs in `/`. One review round, no findings.
also in v1 main: credbroker/cli.go.

C36. A F24: a rule's path is a raw string prefix with no segment boundary, so under path `/repos/acme/app` the request

C37. The crasher internal/proxy/testdata/fuzz/FuzzHide/cff1bc4cc7889cf3, `string("10sk-acc%2F")`. It still fails FuzzHide on
05a59da (`hide("10sk-acc%2F") = "10sk-acc%2F10", carries sk-acc%2F1`) and minimises to `1sk-acc%2F`. Outcome: REFUTED as a
product finding by the redteam, with no test: hide's own output for the minimised input is `1sk-acc%2F`, which holds no spelling

### S-1016c: mount mode and the workspace export, at main c588645 (twelve findings)

Method. The Mac gate was green on the unchanged tree first (73 rows, GATE PASS in 423s). internal/fileserve is Linux only, so
its tests ran as linux/arm64, as root, in a workcell guest on the Mac (a cross-compiled test binary in a clone-mode session, no
network); the regression tests of C17 and C18 pass there (TestGrowthCap, TestGrowthCapAppend create and open,
TestGrowthCapEntries symlink, mkdir and create), and those of C19, C28, C29, C20 and C31 pass on the Mac itself. One redteam per
topic compared each finding, input by input, with what the fix covers on main, by running; a test for what was left went under
escape/_pending/ and ran by `go test -overlay`; the orchestrator ran each again and kept the logs under loop/private/; one
verifier per candidate got the claim, the test and the log.

| finding | outcome |
|---------|---------|
| C F3 | DUPLICATE of C17 (fixed by S-F10) |
| B F1, C F6 | DUPLICATE of C18 (fixed by S-F11) |
| C F4 | DUPLICATE of C19 and C29 (fixed by S-F12 and S-F21) |
| C F14, C F15, C F16 | DUPLICATE of C28 (fixed by S-F20), one claim three times |
| C F23, C F24 | CONFIRMED, C38 (low), the sites of C31's class that S-F23 did not touch; C F23's pull arm is a DUPLICATE of C20 |
| C F26 | DOWNGRADED to low, C39: no break shown, no fix unit, PARKED |
| B F8 | REFUTED, C40: the stated meaning of --mount, residual risk for the report |
| C F5 | CONFIRMED, C41 (I1, medium), public on the maintainer's ruling, together with its fix; fixed by S-F30 |

Duplicates, with what was run. C F3: openFlags keeps O_ACCMODE and O_TRUNC only, so no host descriptor carries O_APPEND whatever
access mode the guest asks for, and TestGrowthCapAppend passes. B F1 and C F6: charge takes one 4096-byte block before each
Symlinkat, Mkdirat and create, and removal gives nothing back; TestGrowthCapEntries passes on all three arms. Nothing else makes
an entry: raw MKNOD, LINK and SETXATTR frames against the real Server are answered ENOSYS (a raw MKDIR built the same way was
served, so the frames were well formed), RENAME between 250-byte names reuses freed slots, and create-then-unlink churn only
makes the cap stricter. C F4: holds() refuses, on resolved paths, a cwd that holds or lies inside the data or the config
directory, before newSession, the key and the export; beyond the arms of the C19 and C29 tests, a config directory inside a
mount session's cwd and a cwd strictly inside the config directory were run and are refused. C F14 to C F16: session refuses a
mount session whose cwd holds os.TempDir() before any socket directory is made; beyond the arms of the C28 test, a TMPDIR with
a trailing slash, with a `..` component and equal to cwd were run and are refused, and cwd `/` holds every directory.

C38. ID none directly: I12's "confuse the host" in spirit and the product's own rule, set by C20 and C31, that a guest- or
repository-chosen name is quoted before it reaches the operator's terminal. Attacker: a malicious repository alone, which C31's
trigger could not be. Where: internal/rootfs/ext4file.go openSource (line 98 returns os.OpenFile's *os.PathError unwrapped,
line 104 formats `%s changed while the image was written`) and fileSink.file (line 87, `copy %s: %w`); WriteExt4File prefixes
`rootfs: write image:`, cmd/workcell/run_vm.go wraps it (126) and run prints it with Fprintln (77). Input: the repository holds
a non-empty file whose absolute path passes PATH_MAX (1024 on macOS, 4096 on Linux) below a directory whose name holds ESC, BEL,
the C1 CSI or a bidi override. Git commits, clones and checks out such a path, because it works relative to the work tree
(checked with git 2.56.1: a relative path of 1015 bytes, clone exit 0, status clean). The descriptor-relative walk reaches the
file and openSource then opens it by absolute path. Effect: the operator's first clone-mode `workcell run` in the checkout
exits 125 before any boot and prints one line, `workcell: copy <cwd> for the guest: rootfs: write image: open <path>: file name
too long`, with the name's control runes raw: a title set, a screen cleared, the line reordered, a forged `workcell:` line
where the name holds CR or LF. Reproducing test: escape/_pending/S-F29/c38_test.go TestC38ExportErrorQuotesFilePath (redteam;
package workspace; arm 1 is Export on a tree past PATH_MAX on both systems, arm 2 is WriteExt4File with a source that is no
longer the file the walk saw, the line-104 site; the judge is strconv.IsPrint per rune). On c588645 both arms fail: `the error
carries a rune the terminal would obey`. Outcome: CONFIRMED, low, by the verifier, who built the repository with git, ran the
built binary in the clone with scratch data and config directories and found the bytes raw on stderr (1 ESC, 1 BEL, 1 C1 CSI,
1 RLO), which the redteam had only read; not a duplicate, since C31's and C20's tests pass on this tree while this one fails
and neither record names ext4file.go. No invariant breaks; the effect is C31's and the reach is wider (no earlier session, both
systems). Line 104 printed raw in 3 runs of 3 with a host-side writer, which alone is out of scope; a live mount guest on the
same tree is its in-scope route, read and not run. Other inputs were run and are covered: an unreadable directory and a name
over 255 bytes are quoted by S-F23, and a mode-0 non-empty regular file, the lead S-F23's reviewer parked, prints raw through
the same line 98 (guest root of an earlier mount session, operator not root). Fix unit: S-F29, net 0 product lines by quoting.
The fix must quote, not open by descriptor: arm 1 fails the test if Export succeeds. Variants not expressed: line 87 (ENOSPC or
EIO while copying, no deterministic trigger), the Linux run of the test (vet only). Not ported: internal/rootfs is v2's own.

C38 FIXED by S-F29, commit 04b8f34 (PR #258). `%s` became `%q` at the three sites the record names in
internal/rootfs/ext4file.go: line 87 (`copy %q: %w`), line 98 (os.OpenFile's *os.PathError is now `open %q: %w` with the
PathError's Err as the wrapped errno, so errors.Is still finds ENAMETOOLONG) and line 104 (`%q changed while the image was
written`). The path is quoted once: the probe of Export on a tree past PATH_MAX below a directory named with ESC, BEL, U+009B
and U+202E, wrapped as run_vm.go wraps it, printed `copy <cwd> for the guest: rootfs: write image: open "<path>": file name too
long` with the runes escaped and the cwd, the operator's own, unquoted as C31 intends. cmd/workcell/update.go's image errors
quote the operator's paths too, as the unit line accepts. Three in-place edits, net 0 product lines: product 15000 of 15000 and
test 28498 of 28500 before and after. Test: internal/workspace/c38_test.go TestC38ExportErrorQuotesFilePath, moved from
escape/_pending/S-F29/ with only its head comment changed; both arms fail on 292a046 (main b95bd10 plus the claim line) and
pass on the fix, also under -race. Not ported: internal/rootfs is v2's own.

C39. C F26: session takes cwd as a string from os.Getwd, and workspace.Export opens that path again (workspace.go 40, no
O_NOFOLLOW) after holds(), newSession and the audit start, so the guest of a mount session on an ancestor directory could swap
the directory for a symlink in that window and the new clone session's image would be built from another host directory (I1).
The redteam's test made the path a symlink and showed that Export copies its target. Outcome: DOWNGRADED to low by the verifier,
no break shown: the test cannot tell the attack from `cd ~/link-to-project; workcell run`, where os.Getwd gives the logical
path and following it is intended (S-1008 calls the symlinked cwd DX), so it shows no power an attacker has. The mechanism is
real (the window exists, nothing resolves again after holds(), and fileserve renames a directory and symlinks its old name),
but the break needs a second, clone-mode session that the operator starts inside a live mount's tree, a won race, and a way
out for what the second guest reads under default-deny egress; the first guest cannot itself read through a link it plants
(ELOOP, ENOTDIR). The tool rated it low too. No fix unit under the freeze; the test left the tree; a PARKED line holds the
hardening (open cwd once in session and hand that descriptor to Export and to the mount service; O_NOFOLLOW on the leaf alone
would refuse a symlinked cwd), and S-1018 lists it (S7). A real proof would be a VM row: a mount guest that swaps while a
clone session starts in a subdirectory.

C40. B F8: mount mode serves the repository's .git read-write, while pull and diff refuse every .git component, so a hook or
a git config the guest writes there runs at the operator's next git command on the host. Outcome: REFUTED as a break by the
redteam, no test: .git lies inside the mounted directory, so I1 holds; I8 binds what brings results back, and a mount brings
nothing back; `workcell explain` says of a mount session "The agent writes directly to the real tree: every change it makes
lands there as it is made", and what a human later does with a tree a session wrote is out of scope (SPEC section 2), as a
hostile Makefile in the same tree is. S-1008 noted the same as residual risk. What no document says is that .git, hooks and
git config are part of that tree; S-1018 carries the sentence (PARKED).

C41. C F5, recorded on the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-20: it is the ordinary behaviour of a live mount and is handled in
public, with a fix unit. ID I1. Attacker: guest root in a `--mount` session. Where: internal/fileserve/ops_linux.go open (235 to
249, through openFile in serve_linux.go 432) and setattr (276 to 333), none of which looks at st.Nlink. Input: the mounted tree
holds a regular file that has a second name elsewhere on the host (a hard link: a pnpm or uv store, `git clone --local`,
`cp -l`). The guest sees Nlink 2 in every attribute answer, so it can pick such files, and writes through its own name for
them. Effect: a host file that no path inside the export names is changed. Reproducing test, as the audit left it (S-F30 moved it to internal/fileserve/c41_test.go and added arms):
TestC41MountDoesNotWriteThroughHardLink (redteam; package fileserve, linux; the harness fixture, whose export file `hl` shares
its inode with dir/other beside the export; four arms, each judged only by what dir/other holds afterwards, so a fix may answer
any errno, and a one-name file `victim` must stay writable). On f441fb0 every arm fails, run as linux/arm64 in a workcell guest
on the Mac (log loop/private/c41-run.log): `I1: the guest changed a host file outside the export through the hard link:
dir/other is now "pwned"` after an O_WRONLY open and a WRITE, and `is now ""` after an O_WRONLY|O_TRUNC open, after SETATTR size
by node, and after SETATTR size by a writable fh. An arm with SETATTR size through an O_RDONLY fh passed on main and was left
out. Outcome: CONFIRMED, medium, by the verifier, who ran the test, a probe of its own and three simulated fixes. The harness
is fileserve.Open and Serve over a pipe, as cmd/workcell/mount_linux.go and run_vm.go wire them; root adds nothing (as uid 1000
the write, the truncate and an O_RDWR write land too); a 0444 target does not protect (the open is EACCES, then SETATTR mode
0644 succeeds and the write lands). Medium and not high: the tree must already hold the second name, and the guest cannot make
one (LINK, MKNOD and RENAME2 are ENOSYS, run; RENAME moves the one name; CREATE is O_EXCL; git carries no hard link, so a
malicious repository cannot either). Not low: a break is shown. No duplicate: S-1008's observation above (the sharing is "residual risk",
row 18 pins that the link is served) had no reproduction and no C number, and this record replaces that reading; C40 is .git
inside the export. Weaknesses of the test, for S-F30's redteam step: it passes after a partial fix that refuses only a
non-O_RDONLY open and SETATTR size, while an `O_RDONLY|O_TRUNC` open still empties dir/other (openFlags lets it through); it
has no arm for SETATTR mode (0644 became 0777 on dir/other) or times (mtime became 12345) and none for O_RDWR; the by-fh arm
is vacuous once the open is refused. A fix that refuses by Nlink also turns TestAdversarial rows 35, 36, 39, 40 and 44 to 47
red for the wrong reason, because the fixture's a.txt has a second name dir/hl2 beside the export and those rows open it
O_RDWR; row 18 must change with the fix. Fix unit: S-F30. Variants not expressed: extending through the link (bytes outside the
export against the growth cap), a link made by a host process during the session, a fh opened before the second name appears,
and two names that both lie inside the export, which a fix by Nlink also refuses. Not ported: internal/fileserve is v2's own.

C41 FIXED by S-F30, commit 41d1bd4 (Mac mode, no pull request of its own; the same hand-over as this record). internal/fileserve now
refuses with EPERM, before anything changes, every open that is not exactly O_RDONLY and every SETATTR of mode, size or times
on a non-directory that has a second name, or had one when its node (LOOKUP or READDIRPLUS) or its handle (OPEN) first saw it;
O_TRUNC is an Ftruncate after the check and no longer reaches openat for an existing file. Reading, UNLINK and RENAME are as
before, and a one-name file is unchanged but for an `O_RDONLY|O_TRUNC` open, now EINVAL. The mark is kept because the count
alone was not enough: the unit's reviewer opened hl O_RDONLY, removed the export's name (UNLINK, or RENAME over it), so that
the count fell to 1, and changed dir/other's mode through the held fh; by node, a request batched with the UNLINK landed 7 to
10 times in 5000, and 0 times in 5000 after. A file whose names all lie inside the mounted tree is refused too, as docs/policy.md
and `workcell explain --mount` now say. Test: internal/fileserve/c41_test.go, 11 arms judged by dir/other's bytes, mode and
mtime (two writes, two truncating opens, SETATTR size, mode, mtime and mtime-now by node, mode by an O_RDONLY fh, and mode by a
held fh after UNLINK and after RENAME over); nine fail on f441fb0, all pass on 41d1bd4, run as linux/arm64 in a workcell guest on
the Mac. No real mount session ran there, so the hosted gate is the first run of the `mount-` rows on this change. Not covered:
a second name made by a host process during the session, and what PARKED.md lists under S-F30.

Handoffs: one open fix unit, S-F29, below S-1016c in PLAN.md, starting with the move of its parked test (51 test lines);
S-F30 landed with this record. This part confirmed one medium finding, C41; S-1016b already raised the sweep count (S8). Seven of the twelve
findings were duplicates of fixes that landed after the scans, and each fix covered every input its findings gave. For S-1018:
after S-F30 the residual risk of --mount is what the guest does inside the tree (C40), not a second name outside it.

### S-1016d: `pull`, `attach`, `update` and artifact verification, at main ab0b8cd (eighteen findings)

Method. The Mac gate was green on the unchanged tree first (73 rows, GATE PASS in 422s; its row `I12
channel-first-frame-rollback` passes under vz). One redteam per topic, five at once, compared each finding, input by input, with
main by running; a test for what was left went under escape/_pending/ and ran by `go test -overlay`; the orchestrator ran each
again and kept the logs under loop/private/s1016d/ (d1-run.log to d3-run.log); one verifier per candidate got the claim, the test
and the log, and each wrote a probe of its own.

| finding | outcome |
|---------|---------|
| A F21, A F22, C F17, C F18 | DOWNGRADED to low, C42: real mechanism, no in-scope attacker, no fix unit, PARKED |
| A F23, B F10, B F11 | DUPLICATE of C1 (fixed by S-F1) and of its accepted residual C2 |
| (found beside them) | CONFIRMED, C43 (I12 with B10, medium), fix unit S-F31 |
| B F2, B F4, B F5, C F8, C F12, C F13 | CONFIRMED, C44 (I8, medium), one claim six times; fixed by S-F32 |
| B F9, C F19 | REFUTED under R2, C45: the mechanism is real, its attacker is not in section 2, PARKED |
| B F14, B F15, C F20 | DUPLICATE of C20 (fixed by S-F13) |

Duplicates, with what was run. A F23, B F10 and B F11: TestFail, TestOutput, TestUpdate and TestChannel of cmd/workcell pass, and
the vz row passes in the gate. An Exit of kind 2 as the guest's first frame changes nothing outside the start that installed the
layer (TestFail row 1), no image is deleted any more (rows 2 and 3), and B F11's "repeating it leaves no layer" is false on main.
What is left in the fresh start is C2, confirmed low and accepted as B9's own self-rollback. B F11's remark that the match is on
filepath.Base(args[0]) gives the forger nothing: only the operator's own command line reaches it (PARKED). B F14, B F15 and C F20:
TestC20PullWriteErrorQuotesGuestPath passes; both os.NewFile sites in cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go (327 and 394) pass shown(e.Path).
The redteam drove the real write, put, compare and manifest code with eight hostile names (ESC, BEL, OSC 52, C1 controls, bidi
overrides, a lone CR, LF, DEL, zero-width runes) through EFBIG, a real ENOSPC on a 2 MB image, a read-only destination, names
over 255 bytes, wrong entry kinds, every manifest refusal and the diff lines: no rune that strconv.IsPrint rejects in about 1100
messages, each finding's own name among them; with the fix undone in an overlay copy the same probe flags all three. Not forced:
fchmod, EDQUOT and EIO, which take the same route. The fix landed on main as d998add (PR #235); 128d5aa in C20's record is the
branch commit.

C42. A F21, A F22, C F17 and C F18, one claim. Rule: B5, not an invariant. Where: internal/artifact/verify.go tarMember (near
305), which for a pin with Signing.Members checks the Sigstore bundle against the SHA-256 of the one tar entry whose name equals
the member and skips every other entry, while the row pins the SHA-256 of the whole tarball and unpack in cmd/workcell/update.go
applies every entry and takes bin/<binary> if there is one, else the one root file. Input: a release tarball that keeps the
genuine signed member and adds an entry `bin/<binary>`, a later `./<member>`, or a whiteout `.wh.<member>` with another root
file. Effect: Verify accepts it, the tarball's digest is pinned, and the layer's binary is the added bytes, which upstream's
release workflow never signed. The redteam's test (package artifact, three shapes, judged by which bytes become the binary)
failed on ab0b8cd: `verified, yet the binary of the layer is "trojan", not the signed member`; `././<member>`, an opaque whiteout
with bin/<binary>, and bin/<binary> as a hard link or a symlink did the same through the real unpack, while the member twice by
exact name, an extra root file and an alias of the member are refused. Outcome: DOWNGRADED to low by the verifier, who ran the
real Verify and the real unpack on the same bytes (all four shapes install the added bytes 0755; the genuine one-member tarball
and a swapped member behave as they should). No attacker of section 2 can replace an upstream release asset: guest root, the
repository and model output never touch a pin, the network attacker has availability only (TLS, digest-pinned), and S-1012 ruled
a hostile upstream an allowlisted provider's own service, out of scope. I14 holds as written, since the installed digest is the
one in the signed manifest; B5 is met to the letter and misses its purpose for member pins, the asset swap that the suite's own
row `2E meta-matches-swapped-body github member` models. The end state is hostile code as guest root, which A1 and A10 assume.
Today the codex row pins no version and bump is a dry run until H-905. The tool rated it low four times. No fix unit under the
freeze; the test left the tree; a PARKED line holds the hardening (tarMember refuses any entry but the member, which turned the
test green in a scratch overlay and needs TestTarMember's two-entry rows changed), and S-1018 lists it (S7). It answers the two
parked tool notes on the same code. Not ported.

C43. ID I12, with B10 ("the user stays in control": `workcell update --to` and `--rollback`). Attacker: guest root, reached by a
malicious repository, as in C1. Where: cmd/workcell/update.go apply (275: fresh gets the provider's NAME) and fail (291: acts
when the provider is in fresh, on whatever `current` names when the session ends). S-F1 meant "only a layer that this very start
installed"; the check compares the provider and not the image. Input: in the start in which apply installed version N, guest
root holds PID 1's channel and stays silent, as C1's forgery does; the operator, seeing a session hang right after an update
line, runs `workcell update <agent> --rollback` (or `--to`) in another terminal; the guest then sends one Exit frame of kind 2
as its first frame. Effect: the layer the operator chose, N-1, is marked failed although this session never booted it,
`current` moves forward again to the N the operator rejected, `previous` is emptied so the next `--rollback` is refused, and
updates.log says N-1 failed. Reproducing test: escape/_pending/S-F31/c43_test.go TestFailSparesALayerThisStartDidNotInstall
(redteam; package main of cmd/workcell, through the real installer.update and installer.fail). On ab0b8cd it fails: `after the
operator's --rollback and one forged first frame: current "1.0.3-bb.ext4", failed "1.0.1-aa.ext4"; want the operator's
"1.0.1-aa.ext4" and nothing set aside`. Outcome: CONFIRMED, medium (at its floor), by the verifier, whose own probe ran the verb
`update --rollback claude` while a session lock was held (exit 0: update takes no lock), then fail: current 1.0.3, previous
empty, failed 1.0.1, both images kept, a second --rollback refused with `there is no earlier layer to roll back to`. `update
--to 1.0.1` restores from disk while the manifest still lists 1.0.1 as previous, and is refused once it lists 1.0.3 and 1.0.2,
so then no command brings the operator's choice back. Not C2's accepted residual: C2 sets aside the image this start installed
and goes back, which B9 orders; here the operator's own choice is set aside and the host goes forward, the side of the line
that fail's comment draws ("for a layer an earlier start installed, nothing"). Harm is bounded: both versions are
manifest-verified (I14 holds), nothing is deleted, the terminal shows the line. Three preconditions the attacker does not
control: the session is the one that installed the layer; the forgery beats the agent's first byte and any acknowledged Stdin
frame (one keystroke on a tty, or at once with stdin at EOF); and the operator updates that provider while the session is
silent. Graded by harm it would read as low; by S6's wording it is medium. Not shown: the silent hold end to end on a VM (the
forgery leg rests on C1's row). Fix unit: S-F31: fresh holds the image that apply installed, and fail acts only while `current`
is still that image, which replaces a check and adds none. Variants not expressed: a later start's apply installing N+1 while
the silent session lives, which is then set aside and skipped until the pin changes; guest root freezing PID 1 and answering
the host's frames itself, so that keystrokes do not close the window. Not ported.

C43 FIXED by S-F31, commits b8d3148 and 0f127ff (PR #259). In cmd/workcell/update.go, apply (line 275) now puts into fresh,
per layer it installed, the image it installed paired with the image it replaced, newline-joined, in place of the provider's
name; fail (line 291) acts only while `current` and `previous` are still exactly that pair, in place of the name check, so
the check is replaced and none added. The review of the first commit, which paired nothing and compared `current` alone,
found one R2 variant (I12 with B10, low): a second start's apply installs N+1 during the silent session, the operator runs
`--rollback`, and `current` is this start's image again while `previous` is N+1, so a forged first frame still set the
operator's choice aside, moved `current` forward to N+1 and emptied `previous`; the pair closes it, and the second commit
is that fix round. Probes through the real installer.update and installer.fail: the plain B9 case still sets the fresh
layer aside and goes back; after `--rollback`, after `--to` of a version this start did not install, and after a second
start's install plus `--rollback`, a forged first frame changes nothing. Parked as C2's accepted residual: `--rollback` then
`--to` of the very version this start installed leaves the disk as the plain case, so fail acts and `update --to` restores
it from disk. Net 0 product lines, paid by re-wording three comments: product 15000 of 15000; test 28500 of 28500, the
moved test grew from 30 to 35 lines for the second-start arm, paid by re-wrapping three comments in update_test.go. Test:
cmd/workcell/c43_test.go TestFailSparesALayerThisStartDidNotInstall, moved from escape/_pending/S-F31/ with fresh holding
the pair and a second arm for the variant; the first arm fails on main 0c7d80f with the recorded message, the second fails
on b8d3148 with `current "1.0.5-cc.ext4" previous "" failed "1.0.3-bb.ext4"`, and both pass on 0f127ff, also under -race.
TestFail's rows hold the pair too. escape/_pending/ is gone. Not ported: cmd/workcell/update.go is v2's own.

C44. B F2, B F4, B F5, C F8, C F12 and C F13, one claim. ID I8. Attacker: guest root in a clone session, or anything that can
name a file in the work tree. Precondition the attacker does not control: the destination of `workcell pull` lies on a
case-insensitive HFS+ volume. Where: cmd/workcell/pull.go checkPath (84), which refuses a component only when
strings.EqualFold(c, ".git"), as does the init's walk (internal/guest/walk.go 35), and put in cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go with
dirBeneath and createBeneath in pull_darwin.go, whose O_NOFOLLOW_ANY does not object because no symlink is involved. Input: the
work tree holds `.g<U+200C>it/hooks/pre-commit`, executable, or `.g<U+200C>it/config`. Case-insensitive HFS+ ignores U+200C in
a name, so the spelling resolves to the real `.git`. Effect: pull creates `.git/hooks/pre-commit` 0755 in the destination
repository, and the operator's next git command there runs it on the host. Measured on this Mac (macOS 27.2.1) with images made
by hdiutil, a real `.git` beside each spelling: on case-insensitive HFS+ all sixteen ignorable code points the findings list
(U+200C to U+200F, U+202A to U+202E, U+206A to U+206F, U+FEFF) alias `.git` and a write through them lands in it; on the boot
APFS volume, an APFS image, case-sensitive HFS+, exFAT and FAT32 none does. `GIT~1`, a trailing dot or space and
`::$INDEX_ALLOCATION` alias on no volume a Mac mounts. The older lead of S-1008 is refuted: U+0130 and U+0131 fold to i on no
volume, and `.git` is ASCII, so NFC and NFD do not differ. Reproducing test: escape/_pending/S-F32/c44_test.go (redteam; package
main of cmd/workcell, darwin; it makes the HFS+ image while it runs and skips where it cannot; the real manifest.add and write;
judged by whether `.git/hooks/pre-commit` exists afterwards, so a fix in checkPath or in put both pass). On ab0b8cd it fails:
`I8: guest wrote the real .git/hooks/pre-commit through the U+200C alias on HFS+`. Outcome: CONFIRMED, medium, by the verifier:
nothing earlier on the real path stops the name (DecodeEntry checks UTF-8 and size, Walk forwards it, the fold map sees no
collision, holds(dest) asks the filesystem nothing); the guest's ext4 keeps the name distinct, so the stock init reports it;
on a fresh image of its own a plain `git commit` ran the planted hook; on default APFS the two names are two directories.
Medium and not high on the precondition: HFS+ has not been the macOS default since 2017, and `workcell pull [dir]` promises no
restriction to APFS. Not a duplicate: C40 is `.git` under --mount. Public: the filesystem's behaviour is what git's own
core.protectHFS documents, the defect is this repository's check, and no v1 release holds a pull. Fix unit: S-F32. Variants not
expressed: a Linux casefold directory (needs a Linux host with the feature), NTFS or vfat aliases behind SMB or 9p, the same
spelling as a symlink or directory entry kind, `.g<U+200C>it` as the last component (a file named like `.git`).

C45. B F9 and C F19, one claim: attach (cmd/workcell/run_vm.go 593 to 622) takes the socket directory from the session's `vmm`
record and dials `<dir>/attach` without asking whether the session still holds its lock, whose the directory is, or who the
peer is; the directory is removed when the session ends and the record stays until `workcell rm`. Outcome: REFUTED as a finding
under R2 by the redteam, with no test in the tree. The mechanism is real, run with the built binary on an ended session: with
the directory gone attach says `connect: no such file or directory`, and with the directory made again 0777 and a listener the
probe started, the listener got the typed bytes as Stdin frames and its Stdout frames reached the terminal. But the only party
who can make that directory and listen is another local user of a host with a shared temp directory, or a process of the
operator's own, and section 2 names neither. Every in-scope route was tried and is closed: a mount session with TMPDIR below
cwd in three spellings is refused (C28, TestC28TempDirInMountExport passes), a session whose data or session directory lies in
the tree is refused (C19, C29), no guest byte reaches `vmm` (recordBoot alone writes it, with MkdirTemp's own name), and
attach's id is an anchored pattern. The guest of a live session already owns that session's terminal. Correction to the tool:
macOS is covered only while TMPDIR is set; with it unset os.TempDir() is the shared /tmp. Low at most, as the tool rated it; a
PARKED line holds the hardening (attach refuses unless the session's lock is held and the recorded directory is the caller's,
0700), and S-1018 lists it (S7).

Handoffs: two fix units, S-F31 and S-F32, below S-1016d in PLAN.md, each starting with the move of its parked test. This part
confirmed two medium findings; S-1016b already raised the sweep count (S8). Six of the eighteen findings were duplicates of
fixes that landed after the scans. For S-1018: C43 is the third reading of one decision (C1, C2), a host state change at the
guest's first frame, and C44 is the one place where the host's filesystem, not the product's string check, decides what `.git`
is. Leads set aside are in PARKED.md under S-1016d.

C44 FIXED by S-F32 (Mac mode, no pull request of its own; this record lies in the fix's own commit, subject `S-F32: keep pull
out of any .git, judged by device and inode`, so it cannot carry that commit's hash). The unit's second route, on the
maintainer's ruling, and at every directory level: put in cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go now opens an entry's path one component at a
time, and isGit refuses a component, and the entry's own last name, that is the same device and inode as what `.git` names in
that same parent, both read at that moment. It asks before a directory is opened, before what is there is kept or removed, and
again right after put has made a name: a name that has just become the directory's `.git` is removed and refused, so a
destination with no `.git` before a pull has none after it. The fix does not depend on a list of code points; checkPath keeps
its EqualFold test and gained nothing. The moved test, cmd/workcell/c44_test.go, makes a case-insensitive HFS+ image and has
six arms: a hook through `.g<U+200C>it`, a config through `.g<U+FEFF>it`, the same one level down in a nested repository, a
destination with no `.git`, a `.git` that is a file (a worktree) named as the last component, and an ordinary name with a
directory `git`, which must land. On main 9c41f1c it fails in the first five; on the fix all pass. The reviewer's own runs on
HFS+ (every one of the sixteen code points in several positions and spellings, as file, directory, link and inner component,
against `.git` as directory, file, symlink or absent; and every BMP code point put into or in place of a character of `.git`)
left `.git` unchanged in every case and found no ordinary name refused, on HFS+ and on APFS. GATE_MACOS=1 loop/gate.sh green.
Left as they were: the diff path only reads; the destination itself is the operator's choice and is not judged.

### S-1016: the last ten findings, at main 071ca1a, and the closing count

Method. The Mac gate was green on the unchanged tree first (73 rows, GATE PASS in 424s). Three redteams at once, one per
topic, judged each claim against main by running its mechanism on copies and throwaway files in a temporary directory outside
the repository; none wrote a test and none changed a file. No candidate was offered as confirmed, so no verifier ran (S4 asks
for one per reproducing test). Six of the ten findings are about the maintainer's kit under loop/, which is locked, no part of
the product and deleted at cutover; no invariant or target names it.

| finding | outcome |
|---------|---------|
| A F25, C F22 | REFUTED under R2, C46: the mechanism is real, its attacker is not in section 2, PARKED |
| B F3, C F11 | DOWNGRADED to low, C47: kit recovery guide, not R2-valid, for the maintainer, PARKED |
| B F13 | DOWNGRADED to low, C48: kit checker, not R2-valid, for the maintainer, PARKED |
| B F16 | DOWNGRADED to low, C49: kit checker, not R2-valid, for the maintainer, PARKED |
| A F26, B F12, C F21, C F25 | needs the maintainer, see the run's transcript |

C46. A F25 and C F22, one claim: on Linux the escape adapter builds the session's environment from os.Environ()
(escape/sandbox/workcell_vm.go 373) and steered (escape/sandbox/workcell_linux.go 240 to 245) appends every word that holds `=`
to the argv of the command that asRoot wraps in `sudo -n`, which parents the steered run, so the environment of whoever runs
the suite is readable in /proc by other local users and written to sudo's log. Outcome: REFUTED as a finding under R2 by the
redteam, with no test in the tree. The mechanism is real: the lines, copied into a throwaway program on the Mac with a canary
variable, gave `argv[0]=sudo argv[1]=-n ... argv[15]=FAKE_TOKEN=canary-f25-not-a-secret`. Only read, not observed, for want of
a Linux host with sudo: that sudo stays the parent for the run and logs the command. The attacker is another local account on
the test host or a reader of its system log, and section 2 names neither. No invariant applies: I5 speaks of the guest, and the
suite's own secret is a canary in a file source. Hosted CI is not affected as the repository shows it: the `gate` job has
`contents: read`, a checkout without persisted credentials, one step variable (`GATE_REQUIRE_VM`) and no secret, and the jobs
that hold a token do not run the suite. So the exposure is a person's own Linux test host with credentials exported. On a Mac
steered returns argv unchanged. The tool's patch no longer applies to main. Low at most, as the tool rated it twice; a PARKED
line holds the hardening, and S-1018 lists it (S7). The parked note beside it (an environment name that starts with `-`) was
run with GNU env 9.12: env reads such a word as an option only when it is the first word, and after the privilege drop, so it
crosses no boundary. Not ported.

C47. B F3 and C F11, one claim: loop/REFERENCE.md section 8, "Rebuild the kit" (528 to 533 on main), has the maintainer judge a
checkpoint fetched from GitHub by eye from `git verify-tag -v`, which prints the tag's own text before the verdict. Outcome:
DOWNGRADED to low by the redteam. Run on git 2.56.1 with throwaway repositories: an unsigned tag object whose message copies
gpg's wording and ends in a terminal sequence was taken by the documented fetch, and `git verify-tag -v` printed that text
first, then `error: no signature found`, exit status 1; `git verify-tag --raw` printed no VALIDSIG line. The gpg-signed cases
were not run (no gpg command was allowed in the session); git's ssh signing format stood in and behaved alike. The guide
itself says that nothing protects those copies, and never names the exit status; in a rebuild the scripts and the pinned
fingerprint come from the tree the tag names, so nothing checks again. This is git's documented behaviour (`-v` prints the
tag before validating it), so not S14. Not R2-valid: the attacker is whoever can push to refs/checkpoints/ together with a
maintainer who misreads the screen in a rare recovery, section 2 holds neither, and no ID names the kit. The file is locked
and the maintainer's; a PARKED line says what would close it (`--raw` and the exit status, the check that signed_by in
loop/lib.sh already makes).

C48. B F13: loop/test/check-plan.py line 200, the expression for an accept line that adds IDs to an enforced file, lets a
backtick end one item or start the next. Outcome: DOWNGRADED to low by the redteam. Run on a copy with `python3 -I` and one
added unit whose accept line is n items joined by a backtick: n=20 0.15s, 22 0.53s, 24 2.09s, 26 8.22s, n=40 (133
characters) not finished at 15s, so the time doubles per item; the unchanged plan takes 0.02s and 1000 items without a
backtick 0.03s. Neither `guard` nor the checker bounds the length of an accept line. Not R2-valid: the writer of PLAN.md is
the loop, the effect is a hang of a checker that is run by hand (neither loop/gate.sh, loop/guard.sh nor a workflow names
it), and no gate or signature depends on it. PARKED for the maintainer.

C49. B F16: loop/test/check-prompt.sh line 71 asks its question only when a command of the clone's PROMPT.md is no part of
any line of the kit's copy (`grep -qF`, a substring), and runs the command through `bash -c` at 179, 183 and 300. Outcome:
DOWNGRADED to low by the redteam. Run on a byte-identical copy with every program replaced by a stand-in that logs and runs
nothing: a C0 line that the kit does not hold was asked about and stopped; a C0 line cut out of another line of the kit (the
bundle command of section 7b) was handed to bash with no question, as was a line spliced from two code spans. Not run: any
write to /Users/Shared. The reach is text that already stands in a line of the kit's PROMPT.md, so no attacker-chosen
command. Not R2-valid: it needs a draft PROMPT.md that the maintainer accepted in adopt.sh, in their own account, and no ID
names the kit. PARKED for the maintainer.
