## S-1002, sweep 2: host-guest channel, guest init, supervisor lifecycle (I7, I10, I12), as built at main e0adb15

Sweep 2 (S8), fresh context (S3), the whole surface read as built after S-F1 to S-F32, not a diff. Auditor on the top tier
in the cloud session, which has no hypervisor; what needs a VM runs on the unit's pull request.

Trust boundary. Attacker bytes reach the supervisor (the operator's uid; owns the VM, proxy, resolver, broker, audit log,
data dir, cwd and terminal) at exactly these points: the one accepted connection on vsock 5000 (wire.ReadFrame, then
run_vm.go output(): Stdout and Stderr raw to the seat and the terminal, Ack through DecodeAck, Exit through DecodeExit; on
pull Entry, Data and Exit through pull_vm.go); later connects to 5000 and 5002, refused by once; the VMM's console pipe
(tail of 4 KiB, lastLines sanitiser) and its exit (fixed strings); and the guest-written workspace.ext4, never parsed on
the host. Host-to-guest bytes (kernel cmdline, Exec JSON with placeholders and the session CA, Stdin, Resize, Signal, Ping,
Pull) are host-built. New since sweep 1: TypePing every 2 s on vz only (S-F24; on Linux probeEvery is 0 and time.Tick(0)
is nil), SIGPIPE ignored in client() (S-F2), fail() gated by the exact current and previous image pair apply installed in
this start (S-F1, S-F31), holds() both ways and the TMPDIR-in-export refusal (S-F12, S-F20, S-F21). The host relies on
the init only for liveness, the fresh-window first-frame heuristic (B9, accepted as C2), Ack flow control on the input
side, and Sync before Exit. Persistent host state a guest frame can change: the command's exit code, session_end's exit N,
and in the fresh window layers/<agent>/{failed,current,previous} plus one updates.log line. No file of this surface
carries // Ported from v1 (every header checked; the markers are only in internal/proxy/{proxy,terminate,allowlist}.go,
internal/secret/{broker,source}.go and internal/audit/lines.go, none of them this surface's handling code), so nothing
falls under S14.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: 6-byte header, 64 KiB cap before allocation, 5 s per frame once begun, no resync
after an error; every decoder bounded and round-tripping; 45 s each of FuzzReadFrame (5.4M execs) and guest FuzzDecode
(3.2M execs), no crasher; %q and %.8x on every guest byte that reaches stderr (strconv.Quote escapes Cf runes such as
U+202E too); console tail bounded (TestTailIsBounded). The one unbounded figure is the supervisor's own CPU per guest
frame, outside the S-F3 affinity pin, which covers the Firecracker child alone (C51). Logic and state: output() ends on
Exit, a bad Ack or an unknown type; frames after Exit are never read; a forged Exit{Code} as the first frame yields that
code, which equals the guest ending its own command; first-frame rollback: apply pairs the installed and the replaced
image and fail acts only while current and previous are still that pair; every operator sequence walked (--rollback,
--to another version, double --rollback, a second start's install, a channel-driven rollback to prev, a first install
with empty previous) leaves only the accepted C2 residual (--to or a double rollback back to the very version this start
installed); markers are written by rename; point keeps the failed image; update --to restores from disk (TestFail,
c43_test). Concurrency and check-to-use: once closes the listener after the first accept (TestOnceTakesOneConnection);
the first 5000 connection is the init's because no guest code runs before Exec; the seat mutex covers send against sit;
the channel has one writer goroutine (session's select, Ping included) and one reader; a stolen-fd guest that stops the
init reading only parks the host's Stdin writes, which fail after 5 s; fail's two reads of previous race only against
the operator's own update verb; stop's pid-reuse window is not attacker-timed since C29. Cryptography and identity: none
on the channel by design; the CA sent is the public certificate only (16 KiB cap). Failure modes: every boot, export,
listen, bind and channel error tears the VM down (closeAll on each exit from boot) and exits 125; a zero installer after
a failed startup has nil fresh; Kill on the Firecracker child is SIGKILL with Pdeathsig on a locked thread; session_end
bypasses the log limits and is written after the VM is gone; nothing fails open. One wait has no bound: session()'s
<-shown after the command has ended (C50). Downgrade, rollback, replay: no sequence numbers by design; C1, C2 and C43
are the only host state changes a frame reaches, gated as above; channel.serial advances only on a verified manifest;
apply skips the failed digest until the pin changes. Interaction between surfaces: Exec carries placeholders and the CA
only (I5, I6); the daily goroutine fetches channel.json from the host side with the configured roots and dies with the
process (A9); the proxy's listeners and the relay end when closeAll closes the vsock listeners, and Firecracker's death
closes every accepted relay stream; an audit Note error in the relay's deny is discarded but the stream is closed either
way (S-F16); pull boots the newest image without the session lock (PARKED U-205); the attach socket lies in the 0700
socket dir, which C28's fix keeps out of any export.

Refuted by the auditor before any candidate was raised: a flood of forged Acks or empty Stdout frames only ends the
guest's own session or drops its own stdin bytes; TypePing or TypePull forged from the guest end the session 125
(self-denial); ptrace-freezing PID 1 from the guest hangs only an idle session, as a sleeping command does, and on vz the
Ping ends it; a bench or pull SIGKILLed mid-boot leaves wc* dirs that rm cannot name (operator action, I7's rm clause
unaffected); the paced console thread is the pinned one; tail cannot grow (the slice start advances); a session-id
collision needs the same nanosecond and 32 random bits. C2 to C5 of sweep 1 are not re-raised: C2's residual is
unchanged and accepted, C3's fix holds (TestClientEndsAsADetach), C4 is inherent to a PTY, C5 is closed on vz by the
Ping and on Linux by reboot=k.

Evidence gaps, not findings. Unchanged from sweep 1: no escape row exercises workcell stop or rm on a running session,
and stopSession has no test of any kind (the smallest rows are in the sweep-1 S-1002 record). New: a guest that halts
without restarting still holds a headless run open on both backends (S-F24's note); the Mac's accumulating wc*
directories (an S-1016 lead) most likely come from runs the harness SIGKILLs after its WaitDelay or from a killed bench,
whose directories no session record names, not from the product's own exits; that is reasoned, not measured. For
PARKED.md (R3): recordBoot is skipped for bench, so a SIGKILLed bench leaves directories rm cannot find; the vz console
copy still runs through the poller (S-F3 fixed Firecracker's side only, and I10 is not enforced on macOS).

### S-1002 candidates, sweep 2

C50. ID I9 (the session's end is a lifecycle event the host must record) and I7 (the temp directory stays until rm); the
sibling of C3. Attacker: guest root or hostile model output choose the moment; the trigger is the operator's stdout reader
taking nothing (workcell run -- <cmd> | sleep 1000, or any reader that stops), which no section-2 attacker causes, so R2
is met only as thinly as C3's was. Where: cmd/workcell/run_vm.go session(), the arm case r = <-done: theirs.Close();
<-shown; return r, and client(), os.Stdout.Write of guest Stdout frames with no bound; the seat drops the client after
frameLimit, but a client parked in a blocking write(2) on fd 1 is not woken by theirs.Close(). Input: the command writes
more than the pipe holds (64 KiB) while the reader reads nothing, then exits. Effect: output() delivers the Exit to done,
and session() waits on <-shown for the reader's lifetime: the VM stays alive, the lock held, no session_end written, SIGINT
and SIGTERM no longer read; workcell stop ends it only at its SIGKILL rung after about 10 s, the VMM dies by Pdeathsig,
the temp directory stays for rm and verify says the log is incomplete. Reproducing test: TestRunEndsWithAStoppedReader,
a cmd/workcell package test written by the redteam from the candidate alone, which dup2's fd 1 to a pipe whose reader
stays open and never reads, drives the real seat, client() and output() with 1 MiB of Stdout frames then Exit{Code:3},
and replays session()'s done arm with a 5 s bound. On a6b50c5, three plain runs, -race and the whole package under the
overlay: done = {code:3 err:<nil> first:false} then "run did not end after Exit: stuck waiting for the stdout reader
(<-shown) 5 s after done delivered the Exit"; the goroutine dump shows client() parked in write(2) at os.Stdout.Write;
the package is green without the overlay. Outcome: CONFIRMED, low, by the verifier, who ran the test and read
run_vm.go: the product's output(), seat and client() run unchanged and the done arm is replayed verbatim, nothing differs
in a real run, and the test takes no power the attacker or operator lacks. Overstatements, which do not change the
outcome: the wait lasts the reader's lifetime, not for ever (EPIPE ends it); Ctrl-C at a terminal still ends run | sleep
because SIGINT reaches the reader too; stop does end it at the SIGKILL rung. I7 is not broken (rm removes the recorded
temp dir after a killed supervisor); I9's end record is delayed, and lost only if the operator SIGKILLs, so under S6 this
is hardening with no demonstrated break, judged as C3 was. Fix unit: S-F33, below S-1002 in PLAN.md: bound the <-shown
wait (select with time.After(frameLimit)), or drop it, since the seat hands the Exit to the client synchronously before
done is sent (the latter pays for itself). The blocked write is a raw blocking syscall on the shell's pipe, which no
deadline or Close interrupts, so the fix lies in session() or in keeping client()'s ReadFrame loop responsive; the test
replays the done arm as a literal copy, so a fix inside session() should extract that arm into a function the test can
call. A goroutine parked in os.Stdout.Write holds the descriptor's write lock, so any other stdout write in the process
blocks too; harmless today, since the supervisor reports on stderr. Variants not expressed (test budget full): a real-VM
row beside chatterJudge in escape/suite/lifecycle.go with a Config.Stall sibling of Config.Head (a stdout pipe whose
reader stays open and never reads, closed only after the judge's bound; command yes | head -c 200000; judge: Exec
returns within about 15 s with the command's code, Audit shows session_end, ls shows exited); the same stall on stderr;
a PTY session whose terminal reader stops. Not S14: run_vm.go is not ported.

C50 FIXED by S-F33, commit 4d76ab5 (PR #262). In cmd/workcell/run_vm.go, session() no longer waits for its first client:
the `shown` channel is gone, the client starts as `go client(theirs, restore, tty)`, and the done arm returns
`end(theirs, r)`, a new one-line function that closes the client's pipe end and returns r at once. No wait is needed,
because the first client sits on a net.Pipe: seat.send of the Exit returns only once the client has read it, and the
client reads the Exit only after each earlier stdout write returned, so the last output reached the terminal before done
was sent; when no Exit came, the close is what ends the client, which takes the detach path. Paid by joining the probe
and signalled declarations and one blank line: product 15000 of 15000, test 28500 of 28500. The test moved to
cmd/workcell/c50_test.go (52 lines, as before) and calls `end` in place of its verbatim copy of the arm; the redteam and the
reviewer each ran the pending copy on main by go test -overlay (fails with the recorded message, client parked in write(2)
on fd 1) and the moved test on the fix three times under -race (passes in about 5 s, the seat's frameLimit drop). Probes
through the real seat, client and output: with a draining reader, every stdout byte was on fd 1 when end ran; with no
Exit, end returned in microseconds and the client printed detached and restored the terminal; a first client that had
lost the seat to an attached one changed nothing. Review: one round, no findings; two notes parked (a no-Exit tail cut
by process exit while a slow reader is mid write, and client's double restore on the detach path). Not S14.

C51. ID I10 (host CPU), the supervisor's own share under a guest channel flood, which the S-F3 affinity pin does not
cover (it pins the Firecracker child alone); the residual bound C6's verifier named. Attacker: guest root, via a
malicious repository hook or hostile model output, on the init's channel. Where: cmd/workcell/run_vm.go output(),
seat.send and client(); internal/wire/wire.go readFrame (three read syscalls and two deadline sets per frame, one 64 KiB
allocation per frame). Input: take over the init's connection to the host (pidfd_getfd on pid 1, as the suite's
stealChannel does) and write small valid frames as fast as the host takes them: Acks, or zero-length Stdout frames,
which output() relays without end and which produce no output bytes. Effect claimed: the supervisor's goroutines burn
about one host core for as long as the flood lasts, outside the --cpus bound. Auditor's evidence, host side only and
without a VM (the real output(), seat and client() against a child flooding a unix socket): Ack flood 1.01 to 1.02 CPU
seconds per wall second at 665K to 687K frames/s (7 MB/s of guest bytes); empty Stdout frames with no client 1.01 at
930K/s; 1-byte Stdout frames with a client whose stdout is a drained pipe 1.23 at 50K/s; 64 KiB Stdout frames 1.44 to
1.46 at 2 GB/s (allocation and copy, which scales down with real vsock throughput). Severity claimed: low (the C6
class, an overrun bounded near one host core above --cpus, not exhaustion); the hosted row decides the margin.
Reproducing test: escape row I10 channel-cpu-flood (escape/suite/channel.go frame-flood kind, escape/suite/tests.go,
cpuJudge in floods.go now taking an opener for the channel address), written by the redteam from the candidate alone:
steal the init's channel, run cpuProbe so the guest's one vCPU sits at its cap, write 64 KiB batches of six-byte
zero-length Stdout frames for 3 s, each batch under the remaining deadline, ending on a frame boundary; the existing
host-side CPU judge and its 1.0 s slack are unchanged. T2 on control: fail, the host spent 11.4 CPU seconds in 3.0 s of
wall time while the guest, capped at 1 CPU, loaded it (allowed 4.0; 2.1M empty Stdout frames, 12 MiB, in 3 s). Paid
for with 16 folded lines under escape/. Two hosted runs errored before the row measured anything: on cd7484f (Acks) and
8ac60a5 (empty Stdout frames) the row reported payload exited 125: workcell: detached, and the log's next line was wire:
frame too large: 17104896 bytes declared, limit 65536, that is 0x01050000, a Stdout header read as a length: the stolen
duplicate shares the init's non-blocking socket, so a write returns a partial count, the flood stopped mid-frame at its
deadline, and the init's own result frame landed inside the cut one; output()'s ReadFrame failed, the run ended 125. A
guest that does this on purpose only ends its own session (the auditor's refuted list). The third run, on 11a6fff,
floods whole frames only.
On 11a6fff the row produced a judged fail, not an error (hosted gate, log line 282): the host spent 6.8 CPU seconds in
3.5 s of wall time while the guest, capped at 1 CPU, loaded it (allowed 4.5; the host took 469646 empty Stdout frames,
2 MiB, on the init's channel in 3 s); passed 144, failed 1, errors 0. Outcome: CONFIRMED, low, by the verifier from
that log: the adjacent rows under the same judge on the same runner (cpu-flood 3.4 CPU s in 3.3 s, device-cpu-flood 3.5
in 3.4) put the noise floor near 0.1, so the flood costs about 3.3 CPU s in 3.5 s, roughly 0.94 of a host core above the
guest's cap; cpuJudge reads the whole host's /proc/stat cpu line over the run, S-F3 pins the Firecracker thread that
forks the child so vCPU and vsock device threads together are bounded to one core, which the guest's own spinner already
fills, so the remainder can only be the host side of the channel: output(), readFrame (two deadline sets and two reads
per six-byte frame; the per-frame allocation is make([]byte, 0) for zero-length frames, which changes nothing),
seat.send over net.Pipe, client(), stdout and the harness draining it. The attacker is in scope: guest root with native
code; pidfd_getfd on pid 1 needs only CAP_SYS_PTRACE, which it has; the harness passing the channel address is
convenience, not power. Not a break of I10's text (exhaust host CPU): the supervisor reads exactly one guest connection
(once; later connects are refused, as channel-connect-storm and -flood show) and output() is one sequential goroutine, so
the overrun is bounded near one core whatever the flood rate, about 2 of the runner's 4 cores here. This is the C6
class exactly (hardening, bounded near vCPUs plus one plus the supervisor's share) and measures the share C6 left
unmeasured. S6: low, no demonstrated break; S7 lists it. Fix unit: S-F34, below S-1002 in PLAN.md: read the channel
through a bufio.Reader inside wire.Conn (one field set in New, used by readFrame; the first-byte wait and the per-frame
deadline keep their meaning), which turns the syscalls per tiny frame into one per 4 KiB, and reuse the payload buffer
in output() (pull keeps rest across frames) if the bulk path matters; about three product lines, to be paid by folds.
The row waits under escape/_pending/S-F34/framefloods.go; the cpuJudge opener in floods.go stays live. Variants not
expressed: 1-byte Stdout frames while an attach client sits (needs Exec rather than Run); the same flood on a fresh
vsock connection, to load the acceptor path; a storm of connections each carrying frames; a longer flood to average out
the slack, which the 20 s bound precludes. Residual risk of the row: if the init writes a frame of its own during the
3 s (a Ping reply on vz), the same desync as on the first two runs can occur mid-flood; the Linux runs showed none. Not
S14: no file involved is ported.

C51 FIXED by S-F34, commits 32b5d2e, a4d0453 and 18b8057 (PR #263). In internal/wire/wire.go, Conn reads through a
bufio.Reader set in New (4 KiB fills, so one read syscall serves hundreds of six-byte frames); the first-byte wait still
has no deadline and a clean io.EOF there is still a clean end; the now+limit deadline is armed only at the first read of
a frame that finds fewer buffered bytes than it needs, so a frame already in the buffer sets none and a peer that stalls
mid-frame still fails with the deadline error; ErrTooLarge is still checked before any allocation; and the header is
read into a buffer owned by Conn, so no frame allocates (the header array used to escape into io.ReadFull). In
cmd/workcell/run_vm.go, output() coalesces adjacent buffered Stdout or Stderr frames into one send bounded by
wire.MaxPayload, flushes before any frame of another kind or an error (Ack and Exit order unchanged) and never relays
an empty output frame; Buffered() on Conn is the one new method. The payload reuse the unit line named was measured as
below noise (an empty payload never allocates) and was not done. Paid by folds in wire.go (package, Conn and ReadFrame
comments, trailing const and var comments, the unexpected helper folded into readFrame) and run_vm.go (bootLimit and
frameLimit on one line, tail.bytes as a one-liner, one blank line): product 14995 of 15000, test 28482 of 28492. The
row channel-cpu-flood is back (escape/suite/channel.go frame-flood case and frameFlood, tests.go after
device-cpu-flood) and escape/_pending/ is gone. Hosted gate on the real VM: on 6ddbd17 (the row alone) fail, 7.0 CPU s
in 3.6 s, allowed 4.6, 404114 frames in 3 s; on 32b5d2e (bufio alone) fail, 6.3 in 3.5, allowed 4.5, 1343406 frames,
so the decoder was no longer the cost but the per-frame stdout relay was, as the builder's local chain measurement
said (6991 to 3415 ns a frame, still one core); on a4d0453 pass, 4.4 in 3.4, allowed 4.4, 31335218 frames (179 MiB),
with cpu-flood and device-cpu-flood at 3.5 beside it (local chain 48 ns a frame); on 18b8057 pass, 4.4 in 3.5, allowed 4.5, 63500508 frames (363 MiB), cpu-flood 3.5 and device-cpu-flood 3.7 beside it. T2 on control
stands from the record above (11.4 CPU s in 3.0 s, allowed 4.0); a control run in the cloud session was refused by its
safeguard, and S12 asks for none there. Review: one round, one low I10 finding accepted and fixed in the fix round (the
per-frame header allocation: 34 to 22 ns a frame and 65540 to 5 allocs in a 65536-frame benchmark). The reviewer's
probes: header then stall (deadline error), 5 bytes then EOF (ErrUnexpectedEOF), frames split across fills, idle four
times the limit before the first byte and between frames (both read), a 0xffffffff length after a frame (ErrTooLarge
before any allocation), 148 deadline calls for 100000 buffered frames, every error sticky, and a seated client fed
Stdout, Stderr, Ack, an empty frame, a MaxPayload-1 frame and Exit with byte order kept and no frame over MaxPayload.
Residual: the hosted margin is a few tenths of a second, since the guest's push rate rises with the host's speed; what
still costs the host per frame is the bufio and ReadFull call chain (about 20 ns) and one vsock read per 4 KiB fill.
Variants not expressed (redteam): 1-byte frames, Stdout and Stderr alternating, the flood on a fresh connection to the
port, a flood cut mid-header at its deadline. Not S14: no file involved is ported.
C51 margin (Mac, after the halt main-red of issue 274). The residual above was the cause of the halt: in nine hosted
gate runs after PR #263 the row passed eight times with 0.0 to 0.2 CPU s of room (4.2 of 4.4, 4.3 of 4.4, 4.2 of 4.4,
4.3 of 4.4, 4.3 of 4.3, 4.4 of 4.5, 4.4 of 4.4, 4.1 of 4.3) and failed once, on the claim commit of S-F36, which
changes no code (4.6 of 4.6 as printed, 50525172 frames); cpu-flood and device-cpu-flood beside it kept 0.7 to 1.0 of
room in all nine. First try, refused by the hosted gate and not on main (PR #275, commit a4b517f): a decoder path that
takes a whole buffered frame from one Peek, and a 64 KiB buffer. On the Mac it halved the cost a frame (decoder 22 to
8.3 ns, output() behind a unix socket 36.5 to 17.8 ns of process CPU). On the real VM the row failed harder: 5.2 CPU s
in 3.4 s, allowed 4.4, with 123964700 frames (709 MiB), more than twice the frames of any run before. So the residual
line above was right and its remedy was not: a cheaper host takes a bigger flood, and the cost follows what the guest
is allowed to push, not what a frame costs. Second try, this record: output() in cmd/workcell/run_vm.go takes at most
paceFrames (65536) frames per paceEvery (64 ms), about a million frames a second, and sleeps the rest of the 64 ms
when a block came faster, so the channel fills and the guest waits. A stream of 64 KiB frames at that rate would be
64 GiB/s, so only a flood of small frames ever waits, and it loses time, never a frame. wire.go is as on main. On the
Mac (no VM) a 3 s flood over a unix socket gets 3082079 frames through, against 100285804 before. Paid by joining
five wrapped comment lines in cmd/workcell/session.go. The hosted number is the row's line in the gate of the pull
request that lands this record.

Trust boundary. Attacker bytes on this surface are what the guest does with the devices the host hands it (virtio-blk
requests to root ro, workspace rw, layers ro, caches ro or rw by flag; AF_VSOCK connects to CID 2 at any port; bytes on the
serial console, ttyS0 on Firecracker and hvc0 on vz; virtio-rng reads on vz; the guest's own reboot, halt, panic and kexec),
the guest-written ext4 images the host reattaches later (sessions/<id>/workspace.ext4 to the pull guest rw, caches/<name>.ext4
to later guests of any repository with --cache; the host never parses either), the VMM process's exit code and Firecracker's
stdout and stderr on the paced console pipe, and the vz state channel. Entry: Firecracker's device threads (child process,
operator uid, default seccomp, no jailer, CPU mask pinned to --cpus by S-F3); on vz Apple's helper and the supervisor's pump
and console goroutines; firecracker.go Start (paced reader into a 4 KiB tail) and Wait (fixed strings), run_vm.go accept (the
tail printed only through lastLines), vz.go listener pump (backlog 16) and console copy. Host-built inputs the guest cannot
touch: the kernel cmdline (integers, fixed words, build-time provider names ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$, validated cache names
^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$, uint16 ports), firecracker.json 0600 in a 0700 MkdirTemp directory under an absolute TMPDIR, drive
paths under the IsAbs-guarded data directory and sessions/<id>/. Authority: the supervisor (operator uid) execs
<data>/firecracker by absolute path with cwd = the repository, makes and removes the wc* socket directory, creates cache images
and holds their flocks, writes the session directory; the Firecracker child (same uid) connects by path to <Dir>/vsock_<port>
on every guest CONNECT (pinned v1.17.0 muxer, confirmed from vsock.md and muxer.rs fetched as data) and listens on <Dir>/vsock
for host-initiated connects, which nothing uses. Persistent host state a guest changes through a device: its own workspace
image and an rw cache it was given (operator opt-in). No file of this surface carries `// Ported from v1`.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: no parser of guest bytes here (exit status is an *exec.ExitError string, the console tail is
bounded and sanitised, vz state is an enum); CPU is pinned on Linux by S-F3 and unpinned on vz, where I10 is not enforced;
memory is bounded by mem_size_mib, Firecracker's MAX_CONNECTIONS and the relay's 1024 slots; disk space by the image's fixed
capacity (tree plus --disk, sparse, truncated) and the charged mount growth of S-F10 and S-F11; disk bandwidth is unbounded by
any Firecracker rate_limiter and cache_type Unsafe advertises no flush, so it is bounded in practice by --disk per dirty_expire
and no invariant names bandwidth (R3 note); descriptors by the muxer's cap, the relay slots and FUSE's maxFDs; a cmdline
truncation only drops trailing args (PARKED 48). Logic and state: drive order and the cmdline's letters agree on both backends
(root, workspace, layers, caches; vz skips empty paths exactly where the letter logic does); a duplicate Firecracker drive_id
would overwrite, but no id is guest- or repository-chosen; once{} takes one connection then unlinks the socket (Firecracker,
RST after) or refuses and closes queued ones (vz); openCaches stats, locks, creates under a temp name and renames, the lock
outliving the VM; findLayers refuses non-bare marker names and missing images; reboot=k and panic=-1 end the VMM on Linux, the
Ping of S-F24 ends a restarted run on vz; a guest that halts without restarting equals sleep infinity (PARKED 110).
Concurrency and check-to-use: Listen before Start, every boot exit path runs closeAll; a connection accepted after the select
returned leaks one descriptor until the process exits, with no effect; Pdeathsig follows the forking thread, which is locked
for the child's life; the TMPDIR-in-export check of C28 (S-F20) and the holds() check of C19 and C29 (S-F12, S-F21) are
evaluated once before anything is made and compare spellings (filepath.Abs, EvalSymlinks, Rel) where the kernel compares
identities: candidate C52. Cryptography and identity: none by design; the vsock peer is the VMM by the 0700 directory and the
per-VM device. Failure modes: nothing fails open (a missing socket is RST to the guest, a failed cache or layer mount is no
cache or no agent on PATH, a boot with no connection in 20 s, a dead VMM or a signal tears down and exits 125 or 128+sig);
vz Close waits on exited only if the framework refuses to stop a Running VM, which the guest cannot cause. Downgrade,
rollback, replay: not applicable to the device model; the pull guest boots the image again with no more authority than the
first guest had. Interaction: the relay and FUSE listeners end with m.Close, which ends the proxy's Serve loops (A9); an rw
cache is a guest-to-guest channel across repositories by operator opt-in, ruled by S-1013; pull and bench guests get no
layers, caches or network; TMPDIR and the data directory are S-1009's row 40 and their IsAbs guards (S-F14) hold here.

Refuted or re-checked before anything was raised. A TMPDIR of the form <dir>/<symlink into the export>/../tmp passes within()
(Clean folds the `..` before EvalSymlinks sees the link) and MkdirTemp makes the directory inside the export, but Listen's and
encode's filepath.Join clean the same `..` and bind under a directory that does not exist, so the boot fails closed and
RemoveAll removes the directory through the raw path: cosmetic error only (R3 note; probe arm a). pull with TMPDIR under the
destination (PARKED 97): the guest cannot name wcNNN. A retargetable symlink component in TMPDIR or XDG_DATA_HOME: the random
wc name, or an environment set by repository tooling (S-1009 row 40). Caches as a cross-repository channel: operator opt-in
(S-1013). Firecracker drive_id overwrite: build-time names only. cache_type Unsafe and the absent rate_limiter: bandwidth is
named by no invariant. Console and logger on one paced pipe: a full pipe blocks the child's writer, the guest's own loss. A
guest that halts without restarting (PARKED 110); kexec and virtio reset end the muxer's connections or leave the same idle
wait. CID 3 on every VM: the muxer is per process and userspace, vz ignores the CID. vz Close after a failed Stop, vz backlog
16, Pdeathsig thread lifetime, drive letters and truncation (PARKED 48), pin() placement, bench's boot record and the vz
console through the poller (PARKED 50, 150, 151): unchanged. A7: six methods, per-OS constants only. The export walk is
S-1008's. The nil audit log in pull and bench: append and Close check l == nil. Sweep 1's C5 and C6 fixes hold as recorded.

C52. ID I1 and I4 through the TMPDIR rule of C28 (S-F20), and I7, I9 and I13 through the holds() rule of C19 and C29
(S-F12, S-F21). Attacker: guest root, driven by a malicious repository or hostile model output, exactly as in C28 and C19.
Where: cmd/workcell/data.go:48 within() and :54 resolved(), called by data.go:33 holds() and run_vm.go:94 (the mount-mode
TMPDIR refusal); the backend then gets the unresolved Dir (run_vm.go:251-277). Input: within() compares spellings
(filepath.Abs, EvalSymlinks, Rel) where the kernel compares identities, and a bind mount is not a symlink. Mount mode: the
operator's working directory is a second name of a tree that holds TMPDIR (mount --bind /home/u/repo /mnt/repo; cd /mnt/repo;
TMPDIR=/home/u/repo/tmp workcell run --mount). Clone or mount mode: the working directory is a second name of a tree that
holds the data directory. The guest then takes C28's step (replace /workspace/tmp/wc*/vsock_5001 by a symlink to any operator
socket and dial 2:5001) or C19's (the export carries audit.key, every session's record and image, root.ext4 and the firecracker
binary, and pull writes the guest's versions back). Effect: neither refusal fires; the VMM's socket directory is made and
vsock_5000, 5001 and 5002 are bound inside the live export, or audit.key is minted inside the exported tree and the whole data
directory is copied into the guest image. Auditor's evidence: an overlay probe of the real session() with dummy artifacts, both
arms, by inode identity (os.SameFile). Severity claimed: low (hardening of a check; the operator's step is rarer than C28's
cd /tmp, and the Mac form was judged R3 by S-F12's reviewer, PARKED 91), with the note that S6's letter makes it medium.

## S-1004, sweep 2: network path and proxy core: routing, SNI, ECH, connection handling, fail-closed behaviour (I2, I4, I11), as built at main 7110fb2

Fresh context, the whole surface read in full as built (not a diff), after the 32 fix units of sweep 1 and S-F33 to
S-F35 of sweep 2, at the claim commit 640800c on main 7110fb2. One auditor run, finished without a stop: no model
declined and no safeguard re-ran a request. No hypervisor in the session, so nothing that needs a VM ran. Result:
no candidates.

Trust boundary. Guest root owns every byte of every vsock connection to host port 5001: the 20-byte relay header
(version, proto, port, 16-byte address), all that follows it (a ClientHello on 443, raw bytes on a forward port,
one 2-byte length-framed DNS message on UDP 53), and the count, rate and timing of streams (bounded by Firecracker's
1023-connection muxer cap on Linux and by vz's backlog of 16 per listener on macOS). The network attacker owns the host
resolver's answers for allowed names (the rebind model, map row 14) and every upstream byte on a forward port; on 443
the upstream's identity is bound by x509 (S-1005). The malicious repository and hostile model output reach this surface
only through the guest. Entry, in order: cmd/workcell/run_vm.go boot (m.Listen(relay.Port), newAdapters(allow.Ports()),
proxy.New, bind to Terminate for every port-443 name, one p.Serve per port, go serveRelay); cmd/workcell/relay.go
serveRelay (1024 slots) and stream (exactly 20 bytes under 5 s, relay.Decode, UDP 53 to the resolver, TCP to a served
port to its adapter with the deadline lifted, anything else closed, a TCP header to an unserved port recorded first);
internal/relay/relay.go Decode and ReadFrame; internal/proxy/proxy.go Serve (1024 slots, a shed connection closed with
no record), handle (route, one Allowed record before anything else, then terminated or connect and splice), route (the
forward map, or a 16 KiB and 10 s ClientHello peek with the ECH refusal and an ASCII-only lower-case exact match),
connect (one rooted lookup, nets() read per connect, every answer through blockedAddr before any dial, a 30 s budget
shared across addresses, the dial by IP literal), splice, closeWrite and Deny; internal/proxy/allowlist.go. Trusted
from here: internal/proxy/terminate.go (S-1005), internal/resolver/resolver.go (S-1006), internal/audit/audit.go
Note (S-1010), both backends' Listen and Close, and the init's net.go as data (A1). Authority: the supervisor, as the
operator's uid, dials TCP from the host to a policy host's vetted address at a policy port, holds up to 1024 relay and
1024 proxy slots (about 50 to 70 KiB each), writes one audit line per attempt, and on 443 injects secrets (S-1005,
S-1007). The guest-chosen header address is never dialled; it reaches only relayConn.LocalAddr, whose port (always
the adapter's) sameHost reads. Ported from v1: internal/proxy/proxy.go, allowlist.go, terminate.go and their three
tests. Not ported: cmd/workcell/relay.go, run_vm.go, internal/relay, internal/resolver, signin.go, both backends, the init.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: the header is a fixed 20-byte array read with ReadFull under an absolute 5 s deadline
before any allocation, and Decode is total (exact length, version, proto); FuzzDecode and FuzzReadFrame ran about 2
billion execs each in S-1014 with no crasher; a DNS frame is at most 65535 bytes in one allocation and the resolver
bounds every index and replies at most 287 bytes; the ClientHello is read by crypto/tls on a recording conn capped at
16 KiB with a 10 s absolute deadline, and a hello spread over tiny records, a 64 KiB record, plaintext, a truncation
and an empty SNI are each refused (TestPeekSNI, FuzzPeekSNI); memory per slot is the peek buffer plus crypto/tls's
input, or io.Copy's two 32 KiB buffers on a splice, or about 69 KiB terminated (S-F6), and slots cap at 1024 twice;
host CPU of the splice path measured in this session at 0.86 CPU s per GiB with client and sink in the same process
(an upper bound), about 0.2 CPU s per wall second at ADR-003's 238 MiB/s vsock rate, inside the class of C6 and C51;
nets() is one netlink dump per connect, bounded by the vsock connect rate. Logic and state: a port other than 443
routes to the forward map's one host with no SNI (ADR-003); 443 routes by SNI, lower-cased with a length check so a
non-ASCII fold (Kelvin sign, invalid UTF-8) never matches, by exact set membership, the lowered name used thereafter
for the leaf, the Rewrite and the record; every allowed 443 host is terminated in production, so the 443 splice
branch is reached only in tests; the relay's served set equals allow.Ports(); ParseAllowlist refuses IP literals,
port 0, non-DNS names and two hosts on one forward port. Address vetting is Unmap, then IsGlobalUnicast, IsPrivate,
IPv6 outside 2000::/3, the explicit list (0/8, CGNAT, 192.0.0/24, Azure 168.63.129.16/32, 2001::/23, 2002::/16,
documentation, benchmarking, the 6to4 relay, 240/4, 2001:db8::/32, 3fff::/20) and every interface prefix of the host;
the auditor walked the IANA special-purpose registries for v4 and v6 (every block refused or public anycast; AS112
192.175.48.0/24 is the suite's isolated net on purpose) and the metadata endpoints of AWS (v4, the v6 ULA, ECS and
EKS), GCP, Azure (IMDS and WireServer), Oracle, Alibaba, Tencent, Huawei, OpenStack, Hetzner, DigitalOcean, Vultr,
Linode (v4 and fe80::a9fe:a9fe), Scaleway, IBM, Yandex, Fly (fdaa::/16) and Tailscale (100.64/10 and its ULA): all
refused. Concurrency and check-to-use: p.terminate, p.allow, p.transport and p.ca are written once in Terminate before
any Serve goroutine starts; SessionCA.leaf is under a mutex; slots are channels; every path that takes a relayConn
closes it exactly once, and Close releases the slot through sync.Once; one lookup per connection, every answer vetted
before any dial, the dial by literal, no second lookup (TestConnectVetsEveryAnswerOnEveryConnection), and the terminated
transport re-enters connect per upstream connection; the peek and the terminating server parse the same bytes with
the same library, so the routed name and the leaf's name cannot diverge; a first write that carries bytes after the
hello gets a reset and no dial (probe); nets() and the dial are microseconds apart and only the operator's own network
change could move the list between them; the S-F8 reviewer's nanosecond window (proxy slot released after the relay slot)
stands as recorded. Cryptography and identity: SNI is routing identity only; on 443 the upstream is checked by x509 with
ServerName the SNI host, system roots plus an absolute SSL_CERT_FILE (S-F22), TLS 1.2 or later, no proxy environment;
forward ports carry no identity check by design (ADR-003, docs/policy.md). ECH was re-verified on go1.27.4 by reading
crypto/tls (processECHClientHello runs before GetConfigForClient, and with no keys the outer hello is handed through
with extension 0xfe0d in hello.Extensions) and by probe: a real ECH hello built with a config list, inner and outer
names both allowed, gets no name and the route no_sni, an inner-type ECH extension on a plain hello is refused too,
and the empty-body form fails earlier as malformed; the row ech-hidden-sni proves the same on a real VM. A fresh
tls.Config per connection, so no resumption across connections; no client certificate is requested. Failure modes:
every error path refuses or closes (a SetReadDeadline error or a peek failure is no_sni, a lookup error or an empty
set resolve_failed, an unreadable interface list or one blocked answer blocked_address, a dial failure dial_failed,
a failed replay write a close); the Allowed record precedes the dial and the terminated handshake, and a record that
cannot be taken half-closes, drains for at most 10 s and returns (S-F16, TestUnrecordedConnectionIsNotServed on both
paths); a nil audit log (pull, bench) refuses everything, and those boots pass a nil allowlist, so no adapter exists;
serveRelay ends on any Accept error and closes every adapter, which ends every Serve loop (TestRelayCloseEndsAdapters,
TestStreamAfterAdaptersClosed); on Firecracker a closed 5001 listener is an unlinked socket and the muxer resets
every later connect, on vz drop() closes the queued ones; proxy and resolver are in-process, so a dead helper is
a dead supervisor, and Firecracker dies with it by Pdeathsig (vz's VM object with the process); no panic reachable
from guest bytes was found. I11 holds on every path traced. Downgrade, rollback and replay: header version 1 only;
TLS 1.2 minimum on both sides; a replayed stream is another connection meeting the same checks; the relay holds no
state across streams; the product caches no DNS answer and vets per connection; HTTP/1.1 only on the terminated side,
an h2-only ALPN fails closed. Interaction: streams go to the proxy and DNS frames to the in-process resolver (S-1006),
443 to serveTerminated (S-1005), refusal records to audit (S-1010, fail closed after SoftLimit since S-F16: a loss
of the guest's network, never a gain); the sockets the backend connects by path lie in the 0700 MkdirTemp directory
that S-F20, S-F21 and S-F35 keep out of any export; m.Close ends the listeners and so the Serve loops (A9); a handle
goroutine mid-connect at teardown can finish one dial to a vetted address and then meets a closed guest conn; the
forward-port path dials the allowed upstream the moment a stream is delivered, before the guest sends a byte (probe),
which opens only a connection the guest could open anyway.

Refuted or re-checked before anything was raised. ECH, real and inner-type, on go1.27.4: refused before any name is
read; GREASE ECH from a Chrome-class client still means no_sni, a cost in experience (PARKED 55). Mixed, changing and
IPv6 answer sets, mapped and compatible encodings, the NAT64 well-known prefix, 6to4, Teredo, ORCHID, documentation,
benchmarking, CGNAT, AS112 v6, a zone-bearing fe80::1%eth0, ::ffff:0.0.0.0 and ::ffff:255.255.255.255: all refused,
and 2001:200::1, 2620:0:ccc::2 and 2001:470::1 allowed (probe, TestBlockedAddr). A host prefix with host bits set still
matches its network (Prefix.Contains masks). The relay header's address is never dialled; only its port is read, and
only on the 443 adapter, where it is always 443 (relay-header rows, TestStreamDemultiplexes). Port 0 in a TCP header:
served[0] never exists, recorded as port_not_allowed with no port (S-1010's note). A UDP header to a port other than
53 is closed without a record (C14's intended behaviour) and so is a connection at the slot cap (C8's); on Linux the
muxer's 1023 cap keeps the relay below 1024. A guest that closes a forward-port stream while the upstream holds keeps
its slot until the upstream closes (probe: one slot held after the guest's close, none after the upstream's): self-harm
inside the same 1024 (R3 note). An upstream half-close becomes a full close of the guest stream (PARKED 75). A hello
followed by junk in one write: reset after the server's first flight, nothing dialled. SNI bytes: API.EXAMPLE.COM
routes to api.example.com; a leading 0xFF byte, a NUL, a trailing space and an xn-- spelling are sni_not_allowed; the
raw SNI reaches the record clipped and JSON-escaped (S-1010). serveRelay ignores the error of its first SetDeadline:
a fail-open shape that is unreachable, since SetDeadline on a UnixConn or a vz FileConn fails only once closed (R3
note). serveRelay ends on any Accept error, EMFILE included, where Serve retries: the guest then loses its network
for the session, self-inflicted and fail closed, and Serve's retry branch is dead because the adapter never errors
(R3 and less-code note). EMFILE cannot reach the audit record, whose files are opened at Create (S-1013). Interface
hot-plug between nets() and the dial: a microsecond window the attacker cannot time, and a splice that outlives a host
network change gains nothing. The resolver's hint address, search suffixes, /etc/hosts and CNAME chasing: S-1006's
record stands. C9 (interface prefixes, not routes) stands as residual, with two variants named for the report and
not demonstrated: a NAT64 network-specific prefix inside an ISP's global space (an AAAA that embeds a private IPv4 is
accepted and the NAT64 gateway decides the reach) and an ISATAP-style tunnel address; both need an operator network
of that shape and a route-table read to close. A guest that holds every slot idle, fills the audit log to lose its
own network, or dials the allowed provider 1024 times with no data: bounded, by design, no reach. Sweep 1's C7 fix
(168.63.129.16/32) holds, the IPv4-mapped form included.

## S-1005, sweep 2: TLS termination and HTTP handling: smuggling, HTTP/2, WebSocket, redirects, CONNECT, CA handling (I5, I6), as built at main 8f61f34

Fresh context, the whole surface read in full as built (not a diff), after the 32 fix units of sweep 1 and S-F33 to
S-F35 of sweep 2, at the claim commit 85fdfdb on main 8f61f34. One auditor run, finished without a stop: no model
declined and no safeguard re-ran a request. No hypervisor in the session, and nothing on this surface needed a VM.
Result: one candidate, C53.

Trust boundary. Guest root and hostile model output own every byte of a 443 stream after the relay header: the
ClientHello (peeked and replayed by S-1004's path), then everything the per-connection tls.Server decrypts and
net/http parses in internal/proxy/terminate.go serveTerminated: request line, target, headers, bodies, pipelining,
count, rate and timing, and the token-endpoint bodies that signin.go tokenRequest reads whole. The malicious
repository owns the working directory of the supervisor (cmd/workcell/run_vm.go session takes cwd from Getwd and
nothing changes directory before bind calls Terminate), the one thing on this surface that reaches the host process
from outside the guest. The network attacker owns the host resolver's answers for allowed names (the rebind position),
the TCP path to whatever they name, and every byte of an upstream that is not the real provider; it does not own an
allowed host's x509 identity. Authority: the supervisor, as the operator's uid, dials the vetted address of the SNI
host (the transport's DialContext re-enters p.connect), verifies the upstream chain against upstreamRoots (system
roots plus SSL_CERT_FILE, ServerName the SNI host, TLS 1.2 or later, no proxy environment), asks the broker per
request (Lookup and Refresh, a host process per use for cmd: and secret-service: sources), writes the real value into
the outgoing header or token body, rewrites token-endpoint answers before the guest reads a byte, and records one
Allowed record per connection and one refusal record per refused request. sameHost's port is the relay header's port,
which stream delivers to the 443 adapter only when it is 443. Ported from v1: terminate.go, proxy.go, allowlist.go and
their tests. Not ported: signin.go, relay.go, run_vm.go, policy.go, internal/guest/trust.go.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: the header block is bounded at 64 KiB (S-F6) and the handshake plus header read at
10 s absolute; the token body and the token answer at 256 KiB plus 1 before and after gzip (the transport's own gunzip
runs under readToken's LimitReader, so a bomb stops at the bound); hide and learn decode with UseNumber under
encoding/json's depth cap of 10000 and fall to the plain-bytes pass on any decode error; fold's regular expressions are
linear in a header-bounded path; every index on guest bytes is guarded; url.ParseRequestURI refuses control bytes and
bad escapes with 400; no panic was found reachable from guest bytes, and net/http recovers a handler panic per
connection; a terminated connection costs about 69 KiB idle and three goroutines inside the 1024 slots, and upstream
dials are bounded by TLSHandshakeTimeout and MaxConnsPerHost (S-F8). Logic and state: the handler's order is an opaque
or scheme-without-host target (400, S-F25), TRACE and CONNECT (405), sameHost against the connection's SNI (421), the
per-rule swap gated by admits (403), the token endpoint read whole and swapped (502 on any reason), carriesPlaceholder
(502), then ReverseProxy with Rewrite forcing scheme, URL host and Host to the SNI host; sameHost's ASCII-only fold is
sound, since the one non-ASCII letter that lowers to ASCII (the Kelvin sign) changes the byte length; absolute-form
wins over the Host header in Go's reader, so the upstream never sees a foreign Host; //host/path stays a path;
userinfo tricks name another host (421) or fail to parse (400); the judge and the wire agree, since both read
EscapedPath and Go re-encodes a raw #, backslash, quote and non-ASCII byte before either sees them; of 25 spellings
tried under a rule narrowed to POST /v1/, each one that a known router would read outside the prefix is refused by at
least one of the three readings (C10, C33), except the residuals already parked (double decoding, NUL truncation,
trailing-space stripping, overlong UTF-8, and /v1/;%2F../admin of the S-F26 note); sign-in claims the endpoint by
EqualFold, the wide and safe direction, swaps a refresh token only in its own field of a form or of top-level JSON,
refuses a second placeholder anywhere, wants one JSON object at 2xx, and issues before hide, with the carried token
(S-F9) and both tokens the broker holds, in the verbatim, URL-escaped and JSON-escaped spellings (S-F7). Concurrency
and check-to-use: p.terminate, p.signin, p.ca, p.broker, p.transport and p.upstreamRoots are written once in Terminate
before any Serve goroutine starts; SessionCA.leaf is under a mutex and its cache is keyed by allowed names only; the
token context rides the request context into the cloned outgoing request, so a retry reuses it; the broker is under
a mutex; rules are read-only per connection; nothing changes r.URL between admits and the clone that ReverseProxy
sends; the peek and the terminating server parse the same replayed bytes with the same library; three generations of
a refresh token under concurrent requests (the C15 class) are covered by the carried swap. Cryptography and identity:
the session CA is P-256, lives at most 24 h, NotBefore one minute back, with critical PermittedDNSDomains equal to
the 443 allowlist, every IP range excluded, path length 0 and KeyUsageCertSign; a leaf has the routed SNI host as its
SAN, the ServerAuth usage and a random 128-bit serial, and is issued only for the routed, lowered, allowed name; the
key stays in host memory, and the guest gets the certificate PEM, at most 16 KiB, as a convenience (A1); a fresh
tls.Config per connection, so no ticket resumption across connections, and Go has no 0-RTT; upstream, RootCAs is the
explicit pool, ServerName comes from the rewritten URL host, HTTP/1.1 only, connections pooled per host string, no
Proxy; wildcard, CN-only, expired, other-SAN and other-root leaves behave as x509 says, as in sweep 1. Not held: the
pool itself takes a relative SSL_CERT_DIR entry from the working directory (C53). Failure modes: every error path
refuses or closes: a leaf error fails the handshake; an upstreamRoots error (an unreadable or relative SSL_CERT_FILE,
a SystemCertPool error) fails Terminate before any VM boots; a broker error is 502; a token reason is 502 with no
byte forwarded; a ModifyResponse error is 502 with an empty body; a 101 answered to a token request or to a plain
request is 502; a connection that cannot be recorded half-closes before any dial or handshake (S-F16); an
SSL_CERT_FILE that holds no certificate adds nothing and leaves the system roots. Nothing was found to fail open
but the pool of C53. Downgrade, rollback and replay: TLS 1.2 or later on both sides; HTTP/1.1 only on the terminated
side (an h2-only ALPN is refused, and the h2 preface is a PRI request without a Host, 421); HTTP/1.0 without a Host is
421; a replayed request carries placeholders only and meets every check anew; the guest never holds a real refresh
token to replay; the broker holds one generation and zeroes the replaced one. Interaction: the refusal records of a
kept-alive connection fill the audit log in seconds, and S-F16 then refuses every connection, a loss of the guest's
network and never a gain; the ledger record precedes every release (S-1007); the resolver's hint is never dialled
(S-1006); loadPolicy's C34 check works per row, so two rows on one token host cannot leave one unread; the escape
adapter hands the product an absolute SSL_CERT_FILE and the runner's environment as data. The one hole between
surfaces is the repository's directory reaching the x509 loader through the supervisor's working directory (C53).

Refuted or re-checked before anything was raised. CL.TE, TE.CL, a duplicate Host, obs-fold, chunk extensions,
declared and undeclared trailers, `Connection: X-Api-Key`, `OPTIONS *`, the h2 preface, an h2c upgrade and a
lower-case connect: sweep 1's results stand on a reading of go1.27.4's request reader, and each pipelined request
is judged on its own. A 101 answered at a sign-in token endpoint (probe): no 101 reaches the guest; the handler waits
in readToken on the hijacked body with no deadline, and its slot is held after the guest closes until the upstream
closes (one slot held, then none); bounded by the 1024 slots and MaxConnsPerHost, and it needs a token host that
upgrades at its token path (R3 note). Path readings (probe): /v1/%2e%2e, .%2e, ;/.., x;/../.., %5c..%5c, ..%5c/,
//.., ./.., a/..%2f..%2f, %2f.., chained %2e%2e and ..;x=1/.. are all refused; %252e%252e, ..%00, x%00/.., ..%20,
three dots, the overlong forms %c0%ae%c0%ae and %e0%80%ae, ;%2F.., #/.. and ?/.. are admitted, and each is either a
residual already parked that needs a router of that kind, or harmless (a query, or a fragment byte that Go
re-encodes); %u002e is 400. No new spelling. sameHost and the port: an IPv6 literal, an empty port, 0443, two colons,
a trailing dot with a port, and the Kelvin and ideographic-stop spellings are all false or fail closed. Transparent
gzip: the transport adds Accept-Encoding: gzip after tokenRequest drops the guest's, and gunzips under readToken's
bound; x-gzip takes readToken's own branch; any other encoding is 502. JSON in learn and hide: null, arrays, strings,
a BOM, comments, trailing commas, NaN and two values are refused at 2xx; duplicate keys collapse to the last, with the
real value gone from both; a non-string access_token or a nested token reaches the guest as issued (the U-403 class,
a provider's shape, no in-scope attacker). Lookup and Refresh run before carriesPlaceholder refuses, so a refused
request can leave a granted record while the value never leaves the host (R3 note). Issue stores tokens before its
ledger record; after one failed write the audit log fails for the rest of the session, so an unrecorded sign-in's
tokens are never released. The guest-side trust installation (internal/guest/trust.go and the init) is a convenience,
and nothing flows back to the host from it. C30 stays fixed: upstreamRoots refuses a relative SSL_CERT_FILE before
SystemCertPool runs, and c30_test.go is green.

### S-1005 candidates, sweep 2

C53. ID I6 (on a terminated connection the upstream certificate matches one allowed name under the host's trust), and
through it I5 (the real secret is injected only into a verified connection); the sibling of C30 that the S-F22 reviewer
parked for this sweep. ATTACKER: the malicious repository, which ships a directory of PEM files holding a CA whose key
it keeps, completed by the network attacker as the host resolver's answer for an allowed name or on the path.
Precondition the attacker does not control: the operator's environment holds a relative SSL_CERT_DIR entry (certs, ".",
or one entry of a list such as /etc/ssl/certs:certs), the class of C30's relative SSL_CERT_FILE and C21's relative XDG
value. SEVERITY: medium (S6). WHERE: internal/proxy/terminate.go upstreamRoots (lines 301 to 313): the HasPrefix("/")
refusal covers SSL_CERT_FILE alone, then x509.SystemCertPool runs, and go1.27.4's loadOnDiskRoots splits SSL_CERT_DIR
by the list separator and reads every file of every entry, a relative entry against the working directory, which is the
repository (run_vm.go session, boot, bind, Terminate; nothing in cmd/workcell reads SSL_CERT_DIR or changes directory).
INPUT: the repository holds certs/ca.pem; the operator runs a session with a [[secret]] row bound to an allowed host
and SSL_CERT_DIR=certs in the environment; the attacker's upstream for that host presents a leaf for the name signed
by that CA; the guest sends the placeholder in the bound header. EFFECT: Terminate returns no error, the transport
verifies the attacker's leaf, swaps the real secret into the bound header and sends it to the attacker, for every
terminated name of the session; on Linux the default files still load beside the directory, so every other connection
works and nothing shows; an absolute SSL_CERT_FILE beside it changes nothing. Reproducing test, by the redteam, who
was given the claim and not the auditor's probe: TestRelativeSSLCertDirIsRefused, package proxy, 46 lines, parked at
escape/_pending/S-F36/c53_test.go. Go loads the system pool once per process, so the test re-runs its own binary once
per spelling (certs, ".", /etc/ssl/certs:certs) in a fresh working directory; the child writes ca.pem and certs/ca.pem,
starts a loopback TLS upstream with a leaf of that CA for api.example.com that echoes X-Api-Key, and asserts that
Terminate refuses, or that a GET with the placeholder gets a status of 400 or above and never the real secret. Run by
the orchestrator by go test -overlay on 85fdfdb, plain and -race, log saved: all three spellings fail with "through a
relative SSL_CERT_DIR the attacker's upstream answered (200, "real-secret"); want the secret withheld"; with an empty
SSL_CERT_DIR the child passes (the upstream logs a bad certificate, the guest gets 502). The 46 lines were paid by 45
folded lines under escape/ (the lookup rows of resolver.go joined as bothLookups already was, and wrapped expressions
and short declarations joined in fifteen more files), no row removed or renamed and no verdict changed. Outcome:
CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, who ran the test (three failures, plain and -race, as in the saved log, the rest
of the package green), found that the fixtures give the test only what C30 was confirmed with (a repository directory
of PEM files, the lookup and dial seams standing for the DNS position that I6 exists to defeat, a fake broker, and the
environment precondition), traced the real path from session() to x509.SystemCertPool with no product code bypassed,
and read go1.27.4 crypto/x509 root.go: one loadSystemRoots falls through to loadOnDiskRoots whenever SSL_CERT_DIR is
set, on darwin as on Linux, so the claim holds on both launch hosts (the redteam had taken macOS to ignore the
variable; no Mac ran the test). Severity by S6: a demonstrated break with one precondition the attacker does not
control, so medium, not high and not low. Fix unit: S-F36, below S-1005 in PLAN.md: refuse a relative entry of
SSL_CERT_DIR in upstreamRoots as the relative SSL_CERT_FILE is refused, before x509.SystemCertPool runs, about two
product lines; the auditor ran such a change by overlay (the test and the package pass under -race) and paid for it
by folding closeNotifyConn.Close to one line. Product is at 15000 of 15000 and test at 28500 of 28500. Variants not
expressed (redteam): an absolute SSL_CERT_DIR entry that is the repository's own path, or a symlink to it, which
needs the operator's environment to name the repository and is no distinct finding. Not S14: terminate.go is ported,
and no v1 release holds it (SPEC section 13); the Go behaviour is Go's documented reading of SSL_CERT_DIR, not a
defect of that project.
also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go

C53 FIXED by S-F36, commits e508702 (the test moved) and 67c52ba (the fix) (PR #277). upstreamRoots in
internal/proxy/terminate.go now reads SSL_CERT_DIR itself, splits it with filepath.SplitList as go1.27.4's loadOnDiskRoots does,
and refuses, in the one check that refuses a relative certFile and before x509.SystemCertPool runs, any entry that is non-empty and
does not start with /, with one error `SSL_CERT_FILE "<file>" or SSL_CERT_DIR "<list>" holds a relative path: set absolute paths`;
so Terminate returns it before p.ca or p.transport are set, bind in cmd/workcell/run_vm.go returns it through fail(0, err) before
any VM boots, and no terminated connection is served. An empty entry (/etc/ssl/certs:), an empty or unset variable and absolute
entries behave as before; an absolute SSL_CERT_FILE is read as before. Reading an operator variable inside upstreamRoots is no test
hook (A11) and leaves the signature c30_test.go calls. Cost: the check grew by one line and path/filepath by one; paid by
closeNotifyConn.Close (defer the listener's Close, two body lines for three) and the Serve doc comment joined, net 0, since a net
negative product count lowers the test limit below the 28500 test lines: product 15000 of 15000, test 28500 of 28500. Test:
internal/proxy/c53_test.go TestRelativeSSLCertDirIsRefused, moved by git mv, head comment only; its three children fail on e508702 (log in
loop/private/c53-before.log: "through a relative SSL_CERT_DIR the attacker's upstream answered (200, "real-secret")") and pass at

and gofmt clean. A throwaway overlay probe, not kept, showed Terminate refusing with an error naming SSL_CERT_DIR under certs, "."
and /etc/ssl/certs:certs, and accepting /etc/ssl/certs, /etc/ssl/certs:, an empty and an unset variable. Not done: naming only the

go1.27.4 root.go: SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR are the only environment sources of the pool, on Linux and on macOS.

## S-1006, sweep 2: resolver: tunnelling, rebinding, cache and case tricks (I3, I4), as built at main 80b8d9d

Fresh context, the whole surface read in full as built (not a diff), after the 32 fix units of sweep 1 and S-F33 to
S-F36 of sweep 2, at the claim commit a7456d7 on main 80b8d9d. One auditor run, finished without a stop: no model
declined and no safeguard re-ran a request. No hypervisor in the session, and nothing on this surface needed a VM.
Result: no candidates.

Trust boundary. Guest root, and through it the malicious repository and hostile model output, owns every byte of a
vsock stream to host port 5001 after the 20-byte relay header (cmd/workcell/relay.go stream, internal/relay Decode);
on a version-1 UDP header to port 53 at any address it owns the 2-byte length and up to 65535 bytes of DNS message
(relay.go exchange, internal/relay ReadFrame, internal/resolver Answer); and it owns the count, rate and timing of
streams, within 1024 slots. The guest's resolv.conf, /etc/hosts, the init and its listeners are data only (A1):
cmd/workcell-init/net.go shapes traffic and enforces nothing, and the host trusts nothing it says. The network
attacker owns the host's DNS answers for allowed names (internal/proxy/proxy.go, net.DefaultResolver.LookupNetIP of
the rooted name, the rebind position of map row 14) and every upstream byte on the vetted address. The operator, out
of scope, chooses the allowed set: allow.Hosts(), lowercase, unrooted and dnsName-validated (internal/proxy
allowlist.go, cmd/workcell/policy.go), reaches the resolver and the proxy as the same canonical strings. Authority:
the supervisor, as the operator's uid, answers DNS from policy alone and forwards no query; writes one audit Note per
refused name through proxy.Deny and one per TCP header to an unserved port; on a delivered TCP stream resolves the
policy host itself on the host, vets every answer against blockedAddr and the host's interface prefixes, and dials
one vetted address by literal (proxy.go connect); the terminated transport's DialContext re-enters connect for each
upstream connection (terminate.go). The header's address is never dialled: it reaches only relayConn.LocalAddr,
whose port, always the adapter's, sameHost reads. In the supervisor's product code the one name lookup is in
proxy.go and the one dial is by IP literal (a grep of Lookup and Dial over cmd/ and internal/); update.go's is the
operator's own channel URL (S-1011).

Lenses (S9), with what was checked and what held; this is also the refuted list.

Parsing and resources. The header is a fixed 20-byte ReadFull under an absolute 5 s deadline set once per stream and
not lifted for a DNS stream, so a DNS stream holds its slot at most headerWait; ReadFrame allocates at most 65535
bytes per stream, 64 MiB at the slot cap. question() wants QDCOUNT 1, plain labels of at most 63 bytes and a text of
at most 253 bytes with the separating dot counted before the check, and reads type and class only when four bytes
remain; any label-type byte above 63 (0x40 extended, 0xC0 pointer) is refused as a long label; reply() copies the
question (at most 255 wire bytes) plus the 16-byte record, so maxReply 287 holds exactly; TC, AA, Z, AD and CD are
masked, RD echoed, RA clear. Probe, package resolver by overlay, 27 inputs beyond TestAnswer: TC or Z, AD, CD set on
the query are answered with the bits cleared; class 0 and class 254 are REFUSED with no callback; type 0 and type
65535 on an allowed name are NOERROR with no record; a NUL byte, a dot inside a label, a 0xC9 byte, an underscore
label and a wildcard label give the name "" and a REFUSED; a leading-hyphen label is refused as the name
-allowed.example; 127 one-byte labels (253 text) parse and are refused with a 271-byte reply, 128 are FORMERR; a
valid question followed by 60000 junk bytes is answered; ANCOUNT 1 on a query is overwritten; ID 0 with RD clear
echoes RD clear. No reply over 287 bytes, no panic. FuzzAnswer 40 s (7.8 million execs), FuzzDecode 20 s and
FuzzReadFrame 20 s: no crasher, on top of S-1014's runs. Host CPU per stream, the I10 question that tunnelling
raises: a probe drove refused DNS queries through the real serveRelay, resolver and a real audit.Create log wired as
boot wires them: 84.7 microseconds of host CPU per refused query before SoftLimit (164 bytes per record, SoftLimit
after about 55,000 queries, about 4.7 CPU s in all), 29.7 after it; audit.Note alone 25.8 (the ed25519 seal per
line), resolver.Answer alone 0.31. Over a real unix socket, which is what Firecracker's muxer hands the supervisor:
a bare connect 22 microseconds, an allowed-name answer about 13 supervisor-side and unrecorded, a refused-name answer
and a TCP header to an unserved port 60 to 90 supervisor-side. Bound: on the real VM the relay took 738 connects in
3 s under the device-cpu-flood row (S-F3's run), about 250 streams a second, so recorded refusals cost the host about
20 ms of CPU per second there, inside the C6 and C51 class and far below cpuJudge's slack; after SoftLimit a query
costs about a bare stream. Refuted as a candidate (S6: no demonstrated break), parked as a note.

Logic and state. Case: both sides fold ASCII only and the allowed set is ASCII, so no non-ASCII spelling matches; a
policy entry spelled with the Kelvin sign lowers to k at parse time, and the resolver, the proxy and explain all use
that one canonical string, which the operator typed. Allowed set: the resolver answers every allowlist host on any
port with the hint 127.0.0.1, the proxy then scopes by port (the SNI set, or the port's one host); the hint is never
dialled, connect's own rooted lookup decides (I4). An allowed name's AAAA, TXT, ANY, type 0 and 65535 are NOERROR
with no record; REFUSED against nodata tells the guest the allowed set, which PermittedDNSDomains and workcell.ports=
already disclose. stream(): UDP to a port other than 53 is closed without a record (C14, intended and tested); TCP to
an unserved port is recorded, then closed; a Decode error leaves the zero header, port 0, which ParseAllowlist never
serves; deliver has the done escape; relayConn.Close releases the slot once. Go's resolver, read in go1.27.4
(absDomainName, nameList, the answer walk, LookupNetIP): a rooted name tries only itself; A and AAAA records are
taken whatever their owner name, which gives the attacker who already owns the allowed name's answer nothing more
(sweep 1's CNAME probes stand); /etc/hosts matches a rooted dotted name and is the operator's own.

Concurrency, ordering and check-to-use. One lookup per connection, nets() read after it, every answer vetted before
any dial, the dial by literal with a shared 30 s budget, no second lookup and no Happy Eyeballs
(TestConnectVetsEveryAnswerOnEveryConnection, 12 rows, re-run green); Go's singleflight merges concurrent lookups of
one name and each caller vets the same set; the terminated transport pools per host string and re-enters connect for
each new upstream connection, so a pooled connection reuses the address vetted when it was dialled; p.terminate is
written once before any Serve goroutine; the interface-list window is S-1004's microsecond note. The refused
callback runs with no lock held and p.Deny serialises on the audit mutex; the DNS exchange runs under the stream's
absolute deadline, so a guest that never reads its reply holds a slot at most 5 s.

Cryptography and identity. None on this surface. DNSSEC is not consulted (no DO bit, AD ignored); the one identity
check on the path is the upstream x509 of the terminated connection (S-1005); the one cryptographic operation this
surface drives is the ed25519 seal per refused-name record, measured above.

Failure modes (I11, I12). The resolver is in-process and dies with the supervisor; a ReadFrame error or a nil Answer
(a message shorter than a header, or a response) closes the stream with nothing written, so nothing is reflected;
the refused callback's record error is ignored and the answer is REFUSED either way; a lookup error or an empty set
is resolve_failed, an unreadable interface list or one blocked answer is blocked_address, a dial failure is
dial_failed; an Accept error ends serveRelay and closes every adapter (TestRelayCloseEndsAdapters,
TestStreamAfterAdaptersClosed); pull and bench boot with a nil allowlist and a nil log, so no adapter exists, every
name is refused and every Note returns ErrClosed. The flood probe also showed S-F16's behaviour from this side:
after 55,000 refused queries filled SoftLimit the last record is the log_full marker and p.Deny returns "audit: the
log is full", so handle refuses every later connection while the resolver still answers the hint for allowed names:
a loss of the guest's network, never a gain. No error path reaches a dial or a splice.

Downgrade, rollback and replay. Header version 1 only; the resolver is stateless and a replayed frame gets the same
reply; the product caches no DNS answer and vets per connection; the OS caches (mDNSResponder on a Mac,
systemd-resolved) hold answers for allowed names only, since the host asks for nothing else, and a stale answer can
only change which vetted address is dialled or give resolve_failed.

Interaction with other surfaces. Audit (S-1010): 164 bytes per refused-name record, SoftLimit after about 55,000,
then fail closed. Proxy core (S-1004): a forward-port stream is dialled on delivery, one rooted lookup per stream,
bounded by the vsock rate. Termination (S-1005): DialContext's vetting is proven on a real VM by the rebind-*-sni
rows, and S-F8's bounds (TLSHandshakeTimeout dialTimeout, MaxConnsPerHost maxConns) are present in terminate.go. The
init (S-1002) is data. explain agrees with the resolver. The suite: steered runs bind the session's resolv.conf over
the product's in a private mount namespace (escape/sandbox/workcell_linux.go), so the judge's resolver, not the
runner's, answers the product on every row with a Resolver.

Parked leads checked against the code as built. PARKED line 7 (dnsName as a regexp) is style, unchanged. Lines 25
and 62 (the forwarded Want has no Resolver) still hold in escape/suite/tests.go, so allowed-port-raw-ip-tcp4 and
relay-header-allowed-port make the product look up allowed.escape.test. through the runner's resolv.conf: suite
hygiene under S12 and T8, no attacker. Line 39 (a Mac's negative cache across sessions) changes suite verdicts only;
the product vets per connection. Line 54 (C9, prefixes not routes) is S-1004's residual, unchanged. Line 61 (the C14
relative: a malformed or refused UDP-53 frame leaves no connect record) is intended: the refused name is recorded
and the malformed frame has no destination to record. Line 108 (rebindJudge takes any question type as proof) still
holds in escape/suite/rebind.go. The sweep 1 fix on this surface, C13 by S-F8, is in place; C14 stays refuted.

Coverage. Read in full: internal/resolver/resolver.go and resolver_test.go; internal/relay/relay.go and
relay_test.go; cmd/workcell/relay.go, relay_test.go, run_vm.go and policy.go; internal/proxy/proxy.go, allowlist.go,
terminate.go, signin.go and proxy_test.go; internal/policy/policy.go; internal/audit/audit.go;
cmd/workcell-init/net.go and main.go, as data (A1); escape/suite/dns.go, dnstests.go, resolver.go, rebind.go,
tests.go, helpers.go, relay.go, suite.go and addr_linux.go; escape/sandbox/sandbox.go, workcell_vm.go,
workcell_linux.go and control_resolver_linux.go; docs/adr/003-network-path.md; docs/policy.md; both enforced lists;
SPEC sections 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 11 and 13; this file's map, its C6 and C51 records, its sweep 1 record of this surface
and the sweep 2 records of S-1004 and S-1005; PARKED.md whole; go1.27.4 net/dnsclient.go, dnsclient_unix.go,
lookup.go, lookup_unix.go and conf.go's mdns and localhost cases. Read in part: escape/suite/floods.go (cpuJudge and
the load judges) and floods_linux.go (emulationProbe); escape/suite/https.go and terminate.go and
escape/sandbox/control_linux.go, by grep; cmd/workcell/explain.go lines 118 to 142; docs/threat-model.md (the I3, I4
and I11 lines); cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go and bench_vm.go (the boot calls). Not opened: escape/suite/dns_test.go,
resolver_test.go, rebind_test.go, packets.go, icmp_linux.go and the suite files of other surfaces;
escape/sandbox/workcell_darwin.go, workcell.go, control_relay_linux.go and the adapter tests; cmd/workcell/log.go
and ocsf.go (sweep 1 read them, and the bytes they take from this surface are unchanged: lowercase [a-z0-9.-] of at
most 253 bytes, or ""); the other tests of internal/proxy; ADR-004 and ADR-005; _legacy/. The clone is shallow, so
nothing was compared with sweep 1's base 64eeaad: the audit is of the code as built, against this record. Ran: go
test on internal/resolver, internal/relay, internal/proxy and cmd/workcell, green; the three fuzz targets above;
three probes by go test -overlay from the session's scratch directory against the real packages (the refusal flood
with a real audit log, the parser edge table, the per-stream cost over a unix socket), nothing in the tree changed,
every target a net.Pipe, a unix socket under a temporary directory or an in-process call, no packet left the session
(S12, T8). Not run: anything on a real VM, the escape suite. Ported files on this surface: internal/proxy/proxy.go,
allowlist.go, terminate.go and proxy_test.go; nothing was found in them, so nothing falls under SPEC section 13.

### S-1006 candidates, sweep 2

None. The auditor raised no candidate: nothing at any severity names an invariant that an in-scope attacker puts at
risk with a reproducible input (R2). So no reproducing test was written, no verifier ran, no fix unit is added and
escape/_pending/ stays absent; the next candidate number is still C54. The shapes found are R3 notes, copied to
PARKED.md: the host CPU of a recorded refusal on the relay and the missing row that sends refusals at rate, the
missing row that judges the set of questions the host asked, the unrecorded refused queries after the log_full
marker, and the reply's clear RA bit and absent OPT record. Not S14: the ported files of this surface hold nothing

Sweep 2 verdict for this surface: no candidates, so it adds nothing at medium or above; sweep 2 already confirmed two
