## S-1007, sweep 2: secrets: sources, placeholders, sign-in token swap, git credentials, logs, crash output (I5), as built at main ad99986

Fresh context, the whole surface read in full as built (not a diff), after the 32 fix units of sweep 1 and S-F33 to
S-F36 of sweep 2, at the claim commit 6177141 on main ad99986. One auditor run, finished without a stop: no model
declined and no safeguard re-ran a request. No hypervisor in the session, and nothing on this surface needed a VM for
its Go-level evidence. Result: two candidates, C54 and C55.

Trust boundary. Guest root and hostile model output own every byte of a terminated HTTP/1.1 request after S-1005's
parser: the header names and values that placeholderForm judges (internal/proxy/terminate.go), the method and path
that admits and tokenEndpoint judge (terminate.go, internal/proxy/signin.go), the token-endpoint body that
tokenRequest reads whole under 256 KiB, and the count, rate and timing of requests. They own the guest's environment,
disk and memory, where only placeholders arrive (wcph- plus 32 hex, 16 bytes of crypto/rand per rule and per sign-in
row, minted per session by bindings in cmd/workcell/policy.go; placeholderEnv is the only form that enters the guest,
through guest.Exec.Env in run_vm.go). Through a clone export they also own every byte of whatever lay under the
session's working directory when it started (workspace.Export copies .git, ignored files, all of it), and under
--mount they write that directory live. The malicious repository owns the working directory the supervisor runs in
(run_vm.go Getwd; nothing changes directory) and workcell.toml, which only narrows (I13). The network attacker owns
no byte here: a token host's answer is x509-verified upstream of the swap (S-1005), and an allowed provider's own
behaviour (its router, its echo, its framing) is a provider trait, not an attack; it is the precondition of C55. The
operator, out of scope, owns the [[secret]] rows: source, host, header, env, method, path, repos. Authority: the
supervisor, as the operator's uid, reads a value per use (a file open, or a child at a fixed path with a scrubbed
environment plus HOME, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, no shell, cwd /), writes it into one outgoing
header or token body, records every release and denial in the fsynced session ledger before the value leaves
(broker.go), holds sign-in tokens for the session in broker memory (one generation, replaced tokens zeroed), rewrites
claimed token-endpoint answers before the guest reads a byte (signin.go tokenResponse), and exports or serves the
working directory to the guest (run_vm.go).

Lenses (S9), each worked. Parsing and resources: file: needs an absolute path, Stat then a regular-file check, one 64
KiB+1 buffer, one line, CR refused; cmd: is Fields of operator text, an absolute program, no shell; secret-tool and
security at fixed paths; the child's environment is PATH, LC_ALL and the three names; Output keeps stderr in
ExitError.Stderr, which %v never prints; a timeout gives signal: killed. Placeholders are an exact regex over 128
bits. Bounds: token body and answer 256 KiB+1 before and after gzip, header block 64 KiB, Basic value 4 KiB of strict
base64, ledger line 4 KiB. The broker's rate limiter is a fixed window, 300 grants and 300 recorded denials a minute
(C16 stays low). hide and learn decode with UseNumber under encoding/json's depth cap and fall to the plain-bytes
pass on any decode error. Nothing new. Logic and state: the handler's order is opaque target 400, TRACE and CONNECT
405, Host 421, the per-rule swap gated by admits 403, the token endpoint read whole 502, carriesPlaceholder 502, then
ReverseProxy with Rewrite to the SNI host. A placeholder of another rule, of another session or in any other place is
refused; the Basic form swaps the password only and re-encodes; a real value that is placeholder-shaped fails closed.
Repository scope is within on the path as sent and on both folds, twelve spellings refused, a real git clone and push
through the proxy. Sign-in: claimed by EqualFold on three readings of the path; the refresh placeholder is swapped
only in its own field of a form or of top-level JSON; a second placeholder anywhere in the body is refused; a 2xx
must be one JSON object; a non-2xx is hidden and passed; Issue runs before hide with the carried token (C15, S-F9).
What no code does became the two candidates: nothing reads an answer of the token host from a path tokenEndpoint did
not claim (C55), and nothing compares a file: or cmd: source path with the directory the session exports, although
holds() in cmd/workcell/data.go does exactly that for the product's own key and config (C54). Concurrency, ordering
and check-to-use: the grants and tokens maps are immutable after NewBroker; held and Issue run under mu and hand out
clones; a lookup's value goes into the header in the same goroutine; record follows Resolve and a failed record
zeroes and withholds the value; concurrent refreshes are covered by the carried token (c15_test.go green). C54's
windows are real but are not races: under --mount the guest rewrites a cmd: program at leisure and then sends the
placeholder. Cryptography and identity: placeholder entropy; the session CA and leaves are S-1005's and the ledger
seal is S-1010's; the secret record's Host is the lowered, allowlisted SNI and its Header the lowered rule header,
and the guest chooses neither. Failure modes: every error path answers 403, 405, 421 or 502, or closes; a missing
tool, a bad scheme or an unreadable file is a per-use broker_denied whose text the proxy drops; a closed, failing or
nil ledger withholds every value; a ModifyResponse error is an empty 502; handler panics are recovered per connection
by net/http into the discarded ErrorLog; a supervisor traceback prints pointer and length words, never string bytes.
Only C54 (the export) and C55 (the unclaimed answer) fail open. Downgrade, rollback and replay: placeholders are
fresh per session, so one a CLI persisted in the workspace is refused next session; a replayed code grant replaces
the held tokens with those of the attacker's own account and gains nothing the guest could not do by sending its own
key raw; the broker keeps one generation and zeroes the replaced one; the window uses monotonic time. Interaction
with other surfaces: audit records carry Event, Host, Header, Name and Result only; workcell log prints the raw
secret line and --format ocsf maps the same fields with SafeHost; explain prints name, header, host, narrowing,
sign-in endpoint and $ENV, never a source; start-up errors name file, line, host and name, and NewSignIn's %q holds
no value; the guest Exec environment is PATH, HOME, LANG, the trust variables, the cache variables, placeholders and
TERM. I13: loadPolicy's C34 check holds as built; a row whose own host is narrowed away goes with it, and a sign-in
row whose token host is narrowed away refuses the session.

Refuted or re-checked before anything was raised. A form-encoded 2xx token answer at the claimed path
(access_token=...&scope=...): learn refuses a 2xx that is not a JSON object; by probe 502, an empty body, one
token_answer_refused record, the guest reads nothing: fail closed. The refresh placeholder spelt wcph%2D... in a
grant is neither swapped nor refused and goes upstream as the useless string it is. A Basic value holding the
placeholder as user and as password: the password is swapped, the user still carries the placeholder,
carriesPlaceholder refuses 502 before the upstream hears of it. A refresh through C55's side spelling: not claimed,
the placeholder crosses raw and the provider rejects it; the side spelling yields real tokens only for a grant the
guest already holds (a code or a device code), which is the initial sign-in. A file: source that is a symlink from
inside cwd to a file outside: the export copies the link as a link, dangling in the guest, so no leak; a hard link
inside the repository to the operator's secret needs the operator to make it. A file: or cmd: source under the data
or config directory: holds() already refuses such a cwd. Two rules on one host: each swaps its own header, a
placeholder in the other rule's header is refused, and the same header twice is refused at Terminate. The refresh
placeholder in a header, a query, a cookie-shaped value, another JSON field, a nested field, an array, a second
refresh_token field or a ;-separated form: refused placeholder_unswapped or passed useless. tokenEndpoint claiming an
unrelated resource (/oauth/token/../echo, /oauth/token%2F..%2Fecho, /oauth/echo/../token): the first two are not
claimed, the third is claimed and only read whole and rewritten, which is harmless. id_token, nested or non-string
tokens in a 2xx answer pass as issued: a provider shape with no attacker (U-403, parked), unchanged. An allowed host
that echoes the bound header: residual by design (parked), unchanged. env naming PATH, HOME or a trust variable fails
closed (parked). Crash output: Go tracebacks print argument words, not string bytes; product code has no log sink,
recover, GOTRACEBACK or SetTraceback, and the ReverseProxy and http.Server ErrorLogs are io.Discard. The rate limiter
as a host-resource break: bounded per window (C16, low, unchanged). Every fix recorded for this surface holds as
built: the c15, c32, c33 and c53 tests of internal/proxy, c35 of internal/secret and c34 of cmd/workcell are green in
the unchanged package runs.

Coverage. Read in full: internal/secret (source.go, broker.go and their tests, c35_test.go, keychain_darwin_test.go);

### S-1007 candidates, sweep 2

C54. ID I5 (real credential bytes never exist in guest disk or memory), reached through the clone export and the live
mount; the sibling of C19, C28 and C29, which refuse a working directory that would export the product's own
sensitive state. ATTACKER: guest root or hostile model output, reading /workspace and under --mount writing it.
Precondition the attacker does not control: the operator's [[secret]] row has a file: or cmd: source whose path lies
under the directory the session is run in (a .secrets/key or a tools/get-key.sh in the project), the class of C35,
C21, C30 and C53. SEVERITY: medium (S6). WHERE: cmd/workcell/policy.go loadPolicy, which holds cwd and takes the
bindings without comparing a source path with it, and bindings, which never sees cwd; internal/secret/source.go
readFile and run, which read any absolute path wherever it lies; cmd/workcell/run_vm.go, where the clone arm exports
cwd with workspace.Export (.git, ignored files, all of it) and the mount arm serves cwd live. holds() in
cmd/workcell/data.go refuses the same placement for the data and config directories, so the check exists for one tree
and not for the other. INPUT: config.toml holds [[secret]] name="k"
source="file:/home/me/proj/.secrets/anthropic.key" host="api.anthropic.com" header="x-api-key"
env="ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", and the operator runs a session in /home/me/proj; the same with
source="cmd:/home/me/proj/tools/get-key.sh", and with a path spelt through "..". EFFECT: the session starts and the
product mints a placeholder for a secret whose real bytes the guest already has: in clone mode the key file is in the
workspace image as /workspace/.secrets/anthropic.key, and under --mount it is readable live, so I5 is broken
outright. With the cmd: form under --mount the guest rewrites tools/get-key.sh and sends the placeholder once, and
the host runs the guest's bytes as the operator (scrubbed environment, cwd /), since the broker resolves a source on
every use; in clone mode the same lands after the operator's own workcell pull and fires at the next session's first
use. Reproducing test, by the redteam, who was given the claim and not the auditor's probe:
TestC54SecretSourceUnderTheWorkspace, package main of cmd/workcell, 63 lines, parked at
escape/_pending/S-F37/c54_test.go. Five arms (clone and mount with file:, clone with the ".." spelling, mount and
clone with cmd:), each with a fresh working directory, data, config and temporary directory, dummy artifacts from
c19Data, then loadPolicy and, if that accepts the row, session() with a VMM that cannot start; an arm passes when
loadPolicy refuses, and fails when a session directory exists under --mount or when the clone's workspace.ext4 holds
the key bytes (bytes.Contains on the image, no debugfs, no root, no VM). Run by the orchestrator by go test -overlay
on 6177141, plain and -race, log saved: all five arms fail, with "I5: the key of file:<cwd>/.secrets/anthropic.key
lies in the export <data>/sessions/<id>/workspace.ext4, which the guest gets as /workspace" in the three clone arms
(in the cmd: arm the key bytes are those of the script's own text, which is the claim: the program reaches the
export) and "I5: the session <id> started with <cwd> served live as /workspace, where the guest reads <source>" in
the two mount arms; every session ends with "start firecracker: invalid argument", after the export exists. Outcome:
CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, who ran the test (five failures, plain and -race, as in the saved log), found
that it takes only the operator's step (a config.toml row and cwd) in the session()-with-dummy-artifacts pattern of
the C19, C28 and C29 tests and gives the attacker no power, and judged the effect direct for clone (the produced
image is read and holds the real key while the product mints a placeholder for it; I5, A4) and by mechanism for mount
(cwd is the live export, and the workspace and file service exclude nothing but sockets, FIFOs and devices). The cmd:
consequence under --mount, the host running a program the guest rewrote, is real but reasoned, not shown by the test:
the broker calls Resolve on every Lookup, and docs/policy.md says a source is read on each use, never at start. Not
intended behaviour: the product is told by the row exactly which path is a credential and still exports or serves it,
where holds() refuses the like for its own key; docs/policy.md warns about the cmd: working directory and says
nothing about keeping a source outside the exported directory. Severity by S6: a shown break with an operator-chosen
precondition the attacker does not control, as C19, C28, C29 and C35 are recorded; not high, because the ordinary
set-up (keychain, secret-service, or a file under the user's config directory) is unaffected; not low, because the
break is direct in the clone arms. Fix unit: S-F37, below S-1007 in PLAN.md: in loadPolicy, after bindings, refuse a
row whose file: path or cmd: program lies within cwd, by within(), before any session directory is made, about five
product lines; the auditor ran such a change by overlay (its own probe's three arms pass with a refusal naming the
file, the secret, the path and the directory, and cmd/workcell stays green) and paid for it by folding the doc
comments of bindings and loadPolicy. Variants not expressed (redteam): a symlink inside cwd to a key file outside it,
which the auditor refuted (the export copies the link as a link, dangling in the guest); a source under the parent of
cwd; secret-service: and keychain: are not path sources. Not S14: the missing comparison is v2's own, in
cmd/workcell/policy.go; source.go, which reads any absolute path, is ported and no v1 release holds it (SPEC section
13), and whether v1 exports a directory in the same way is the maintainer's reading.
also in v1 main: credbroker/cli.go

C54 FIXED by S-F37, commits 9de1e64 (the test moved), 6e7a6bd (the fix) and 6dd4f84 (the fix round) (PR #280). loadPolicy in
cmd/workcell/policy.go, after bindings and only when bindings raised no error, now judges every [[secret]] row whose source is
file: or cmd:. For file: the word judged is the path; for cmd: it is the program and every argument that is an absolute path
(strings.Fields, as source.go splits it; the broker runs the program from /, so a relative argument never means cwd). Each word is
judged as spelled and at each lexical ancestor (filepath.Dir up to the root), each resolved as within() resolves, and the row is
refused when any of them is within(cwd, .), with one error `<config>:<line>: secret "<name>": source <path> lies inside the
directory <cwd>, which the guest gets as /workspace: keep it outside`. run calls loadPolicy before loadArtifacts and session(), so
no session directory or export exists when it refuses, and explain refuses the same row with the same line. secret-service: and
keychain: rows, and file: and cmd: sources wholly outside cwd (cmd:/bin/sh /outside/script.sh, flag and relative arguments), load
as before. The fix round came from the one review: (1) cmd:/bin/sh WORK/tools/get-key.sh passed the first-word check although the
script is exported in clone mode and guest-writable under --mount; (2) a source spelled through a link inside cwd that points
outside it (cmd:WORK/tool, file:WORK/link) passed because within() judged the target, while the broker resolves the spelling on
each use and under --mount the guest replaces the link. So the unit line's clause that such a link stays accepted is reversed, in
both modes, since loadPolicy does not know the mode; the auditor's refutation of that variant held for the clone export only.
Cost: the check is 14 product lines, paid by doc comments re-wrapped with their words unchanged in policy.go (loadPolicy, binding,
placeholderEnv, bindings, allowlist) and run_vm.go (booted), net 0: product 15000 of 15000, test 28489 of 28500. Test:
cmd/workcell/c54_test.go TestC54SecretSourceUnderTheWorkspace, moved by git mv with its head comment folded, 66 lines, nine arms:
the five parked ones fail on the claim tree in the redteam's run (loop/private/c54-before.log) and in the reviewer's worktree of
main, and the four added ones (interpreter outside with the script under cwd, clone and mount; cmd: and file: through a link
inside cwd, mount) fail on 6e7a6bd by overlay; all nine pass at 6dd4f84, plain and -race, with C19, C28, C29, C34 and C52.
Residual, parked: a path inside an argument that is not itself an absolute word (--key=/work/x), and a program that reaches cwd by
its own logic, are not judged; a bind mount of the source's directory beneath cwd needs host root.
also in v1 main: credbroker/cli.go

C55. ID I5 (a real token the broker holds never appears in an answer to the guest, the sign-in flow's own contract at
the head of signin.go). ATTACKER: guest root or hostile model output, choosing the spelling of the token endpoint's
path. Precondition the attacker does not control: the provider's router serves the token action on a spelling outside
the matcher's three readings; a route with an optional format, which Rails generates by default as
/oauth/token(.:format), and the suffix patterns Spring MVC matched before 5.3 are such routers, and a
double-decoding, NUL-truncating or space-stripping one is the same hole (the parked S-1016b router note). No real
provider was probed (T8): the claim is about the proxy, and these are documented routing defaults, not defects of
those projects. SEVERITY: medium (S6), the class of C10 and C33. WHERE: internal/proxy/signin.go tokenEndpoint, which
claims an endpoint by the path's spelling, and tokenResponse, which returns at once when the request was not claimed,
so the answer is relayed unread; internal/proxy/terminate.go, whose handler sets the claim and whose ReverseProxy
relays everything else raw. The check no code performs: nothing reads a 2xx answer of a sign-in host that carries
access_token or refresh_token when the request was not claimed. INPUT: with the operator's row
source="signin:login.example.com/oauth/token", the guest, holding the code or device code of the sign-in it is
performing, sends POST /oauth/token.json (or .xml, or .JSON) with grant_type=authorization_code&code=... to the token
host. EFFECT: the provider issues the pair for that spelling and the proxy hands the guest
{"access_token":"sk-acc-2",...,"refresh_token":"sk-ref-2"} verbatim, or in a form framing
access_token=sk-acc-2&scope=&token_type=bearer: both real tokens are in guest memory, usable and refreshable outside
the session, where the same grant at /oauth/token returns placeholders. A refresh through the same spelling gains
nothing (the placeholder crosses raw and is rejected), so the exposure is the sign-in completed in that session, as
C32 arm a and C34. Reproducing test, by the redteam, who was given the claim and not the auditor's probe:
TestC55TokenEndpointFormatSuffix, package proxy, 62 lines, parked at escape/_pending/S-F38/c55_test.go. A loopback
TLS provider whose router cuts a format suffix, the real Proxy with Terminate, a sign-in rule on
login.example.com/oauth/token and the fixtures of the C10, C32 and C33 tests; the honest spelling must return the two
placeholders, then a code grant goes to /oauth/token.json, .xml and .JSON, and any real token in an answer fails the
arm; two arms, a JSON answer and a form answer. Run by the orchestrator by go test -overlay on 6177141, plain and
-race, log saved: both arms fail on all three suffixes with "POST https://login.example.com/oauth/token.json: the
guest read a real token: 200" and the body holding sk-acc-2 and sk-ref-2, or the form holding sk-acc-2, while the
honest spelling returns placeholders. Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, who ran the test (the failures of
the saved log, plain and -race), read the mechanism in the source (tokenEndpoint claims only spellings equal to the
rule's path on its readings, the handler sets the claim only then, and tokenResponse returns nil for any other
answer), and found the omission against the file's own comments, which promise that no real token appears in an
answer and say the match is wide because an answer taken for another path would reach the guest unread. The fixture
is that of C10, C32 and C33; its one modelled element, the suffix-cutting router, is the stated precondition and is
standard router behaviour, not a compromise of a provider. Gain: the guest holds the code, but it reaches the token
host only through the proxy (I2) and through the honest spelling gets placeholders; here it keeps real tokens that
work without the broker. Severity by S6: medium, not high as C32 arm a, because the precondition is specific to a
router and not required by the RFC; not low, since I5 is shown broken; that sign-in is unsupported for the shipped
providers narrows the reach and, as C34's record says, does not make it low. It is the parked S-1016b note now
reproduced, not a new class. Fix unit: S-F38, below S-1007 in PLAN.md: close it on the response side with no model of
a router: in tokenResponse, for a request that was not claimed, read a 2xx JSON or form answer of a sign-in host
whole under the token bound and refuse it (502, token_answer_refused) when it carries access_token or refresh_token,
about twelve product lines; the auditor ran such a change by overlay (every side spelling answers 502 with one
record, the honest path still returns placeholders, internal/proxy green under -race) and paid for it by folding
comments inside signin.go. That fix also covers the other parked spellings (a doubled leading slash, a double-encoded
letter) and the redteam's unexpressed variants (/oauth/token.json;jsessionid=x, /oauth/token.json/, a double suffix),
which a fix on the path side could miss. Not S14: signin.go is v2's own, not ported, so there is no v1 line.

C55 FIXED by S-F38, commits 72c601e (the test moved) and 6426077 (the fix) (PR #281). tokenResponse in
internal/proxy/signin.go no longer returns at once for a request that tokenEndpoint did not claim: when the answer is a 2xx, the
rewritten request's host (resp.Request.Host, the SNI host, spelled as p.signin is keyed, so no Host spelling of the guest's
reaches the look-up) has a sign-in rule, and mime.ParseMediaType gives application/json or the form type (parameters and capitals
fold away), the answer is read whole by readToken, as a claimed one is (256 KiB, gzip and x-gzip undone, any other encoding
refused), and the new helper tokenAnswer judges it: a form with an access_token or refresh_token field, a JSON object with either
key, or a body that does not parse as its type says. Such an answer, and one that cannot be read under the bound, is answered 502
with an empty body and the deny record token_answer_refused for that host. A 2xx JSON value that is no object, a 2xx with neither
field, a non-2xx, any other media type and every host with no sign-in rule pass as before, the last unread. No router is
modelled, so the double-encoded letter, the NUL, the trailing space and the suffix spellings are closed alike; a doubled leading
slash is claimed by tokenEndpoint's fold and answered with placeholders. Cost: the fix is paid inside signin.go by joined doc
comments (the package paragraph, tokenEndpoint, tokenRequest, swapRefresh, tokenResponse, tokenCtx and learn; tokenEndpoint's and
tokenResponse's reworded to match), and the form type is one constant beside maxTokenBody: signin.go stays at 296 lines, product
15000 of 15000, test 28498 of 28500. Test: internal/proxy/c55_test.go TestC55TokenEndpointFormatSuffix, moved by git mv with its
head comment brought up to date, 71 lines: both arms fail on all three suffixes on the claim tree in the redteam's run and in the
reviewer's worktree of main (the guest reads sk-acc-N and sk-ref-N), and pass at 6426077, plain and -race; the nine added lines
assert that each suffix is an empty 502, that exactly three token_answer_refused records name the sign-in host, and that a device
flow's {"error":"authorization_pending"} on a path that was not claimed reaches the guest as 200. The reviewer's 47-row overlay
probe found no break of the unit line. What an operator pays: on a sign-in host every JSON or form 2xx is held whole before its
first byte reaches the guest, one over 256 KiB or in br or zstd is a 502, and so are a HEAD or a 204 that carries a JSON content
type and JSON Lines labelled application/json. Residual, parked: a token in any other media type (XML, JSONP, text/json, none), in
a nested object, an array or a 206 of a byte range still passes unread; the provider chooses those, not the guest.

The two tests cost 125 lines, and the test budget stood at 28500 of 28500, so the redteam paid with 139 folded lines
under escape/ in 24 files, no row removed, renamed or given another verdict and no assertion, judge or timeout
touched: table rows packed two to four to a line in eleven test files, same-type fields and single-field structs
joined, adjacent uncommented constants joined into one declaration, and two wrapped comments folded. Test code is now
28486 of 28500, product 15000 of 15000.

Sweep 2 verdict for this surface: two candidates, C54 and C55, both confirmed at medium; sweep 2 had already
confirmed two mediums (C52 on S-1003, C53 on S-1005, both fixed), so S-1017 will call a third sweep (S8). The fix
units are S-F37 and S-F38; the next candidate number is C56. The other shapes found are R3 notes, copied to
PARKED.md: the form-framed token answer that is refused at the claimed path, the 256 KiB bound that the C55 fix puts
on every JSON or form answer of a sign-in host, the pull-borne chain of C54's cmd: arm, a bind mount of the source's
directory beneath cwd, the 2xx device-flow answer that must keep passing, a non-string token field, and the two
source tools absent from the session. In the auditor, the redteam and the two verifiers no model declined and no
safeguard re-ran a request.

## S-1008, sweep 2: workspace export in both modes, and the return path (I1, I8), as built at main 7f292b6

Fresh context, the whole surface read in full as built (not a diff), after the 32 fix units of sweep 1 and S-F33 to
S-F38 of sweep 2, at the claim commit 8ed723a on main 7f292b6. The unit line still carries its sweep-1 text (copy four
parked tests for C17 to C20); those tests are in place and S-F10 to S-F13 are done, so this run took the other branch
of the line's accept and did the audit again as S-1002 says, because S8 wants every sweep to pass over every surface.
One auditor run, finished without a stop: no model declined and no safeguard re-ran a request. No hypervisor in the
session, and nothing on this surface needed a VM for its Go-level evidence. Result: two candidates, C56 and C57.

Trust boundary. Guest root, driven by hostile model output, owns every Entry, Data and Exit frame on vsock 5000 of the
pull VM, which boots the guest-written workspace.ext4 with no network; they enter at pulled.frame in
cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go and pass guest.DecodeEntry, manifest.add, checkPath and fold (pull.go) to write and put, or to
compare and sameBytes. Under --mount the same attacker owns every FUSE frame on the one 5002 connection, raw frames on
a stolen init socket included; they enter at Serve in internal/fileserve/serve_linux.go and pass parse and checkName
(codec.go) to the operations of ops_linux.go. The malicious repository owns the shape of the working directory that
Export reads (internal/workspace/workspace.go: a descriptor walk, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW, Readlinkat, hard links by
device and inode, sockets, FIFOs and devices skipped) and that openSource re-opens (internal/rootfs/ext4file.go:
absolute path, O_NOFOLLOW, device, inode, size and file-type re-check), and under --mount whatever lies beneath the
directory that fileserve.Open serves. Authority: the CLI and the supervisor run as the operator's uid. pull holds the
destination open O_DIRECTORY, unlinks what is not a directory and directories that are empty, makes directories 0755,
symlinks with any target and files 0644 or 0755 of guest bytes, each path opened one component at a time with openat2
RESOLVE_BENEATH and RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS (Linux) or O_NOFOLLOW_ANY (macOS), and refuses a component that is its
directory's .git by device and inode (isGit, the C44 fix). Mount mode holds the export descriptor and one descriptor
per directory node (4096 at most, 128K nodes), works by the *at calls with O_NOFOLLOW, charges growth and one 4 KiB
block per created entry against --disk (the C17 and C18 fixes), and refuses a write through a file with two names (the
C41 fix). Clone mode writes sessions/<id>/workspace.ext4 0600 and attaches it read-write. Nothing from the guest is
relied on (A1). Judged by no code: the relation of a pull's destination to anything but the data and config
directories (holds), and in clone mode the relation of the working directory to the temp directory, where the VMM
sockets of every running session lie (C56).

Lenses (S9), each worked. Parsing and resources: DecodeEntry, manifest.add (1,048,576 entries, 64 MiB of names, file
bytes at most the image's apparent size, a sum that cannot wrap, fold collisions), checkPath and FuzzPath were read
again; the FUSE parser was walked per opcode against the 7.37 sizes; Export answers ErrTooLarge above 32 GiB, 8M
inodes or 65000 links, and bounds a target at 4095 bytes and a name at 255; a symlink target of 4096 bytes or more
cannot be checked out by git, so an export that a repository makes fail is an R3 note; a mount tree cannot go deeper
than about 4096 nodes, because a dentry pins its ancestors and each directory node holds one host descriptor
(reasoned). The gap: the pull charges file bytes only, never entries (C57, measured). Logic and state: put was traced
for every ordering trick: a symlink and then a path through it is ELOOP; a directory replaced by a file is ENOTEMPTY
unless it is empty; a host symlink where a directory is wanted is unlinked and never followed; the same path twice
meets the fold map; .git as any component or alias meets isGit before and after the create. The FUSE service answers
EIO before INIT and after DESTROY and EPROTO for a major other than 7, on a listener that accepts once; a failed FUSE
dial by the init leaves 5002 open to a later connection of guest root, which holds no authority beyond the init's. The
missing check: fetch compares the destination with the data and config directories only, and session compares the
working directory with the temp directory only under --mount and only with this process's TMPDIR (C56). Concurrency
and check-to-use: fileserve's life and mu, the chain re-check of at(), the RENAME cycle check, FORGET and RELEASE
under the write lock, and node ids and file handles that are never reused all stand (the package tests are green). A
pull against a concurrent mount guest in the same tree meets O_EXCL, EEXIST, ENOTEMPTY and RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, which
leave that guest able only to redirect the pull's writes and unlinks within its own export, where it can write anyway:
refuted. The window of C39 is unchanged (low, parked). Cryptography and identity: none by design; identity is (device,
inode) at use (isGit, openSource, at, the SameFile walk of within), and the 5002 stream is the init's by boot order.
Failure modes: the error paths of pull write nothing or the partial tree the docs describe, and every message that
carries guest bytes quotes them (shown, %q, the os.NewFile names of S-F13, Walk and openSource); Export's failure
removes the image and the session directory; fileserve closes every descriptor on any stream error. No error path
fails open; the one opening is a check that no code makes (C56). Downgrade, rollback and replay: wire version 1 only;
the FUSE minor is negotiated down on fixed layouts; a pull is one shot and a replayed frame is a stream error; the
teardown of a session whose socket path C56 replaced removes only the planted link, since UnixListener.Close unlinks
the path and RemoveAll does not follow (measured). Interaction between surfaces: C56 is the clone export times the
pull's judge times the VMM socket placement of C28 times a concurrent session (I7). diff with the same manifest is
inert (probe: A lines, the socket's inode and mode unchanged); rm's RemoveAll follows no link; policy.ReadRepo opens
O_NOFOLLOW and O_NONBLOCK and takes regular files only; S-F37's within(cwd, source) is not moved by guest links;
holds() covers the data and config directories. The S-F35 residual (the data directory bind-mounted beneath cwd,
PARKED line 150) belongs to the next S-1003 audit, needs host root and was not probed again.

Parked leads of this surface, tried again. Line 17: a symlinked cwd under --mount is still ELOOP (TestOpen), the mount
record precedes boot and fails closed, and the dotdot rows never reach fileserve. Line 18: fallocate, LINK and MKNOD
answer ENOSYS (adversarial rows 17 and 19), and a tmpfs rename is EXDEV: unchanged. Lines 20 and 21: os.Root, and NFC
against NFD on APFS: no Mac ran, fold does not normalise, the reading of S-F32 stands. Line 24: pull and diff without
the lock are the operator's own races. Lines 68, 69, 88, 89, 102 to 104, 124 to 128, 131 and 133: unchanged. Line 123
(C39): unchanged, low. Line 97, the S-F20 note that fetch needs no temp-directory compare because the VMM directory's
random name cannot be seen: no longer true, the name is in a concurrent clone export and the mount twin exists for a
differing TMPDIR; that is C56.

### S-1008 candidates, sweep 2

C56. ID I1 and I4 (the guest's bytes reach a host unix socket of the operator's uid by path), and I7 when that socket
is another session's; the chain of C28 through the pull destination in clone mode and through a running session's
directory beneath a mount cwd. ATTACKER: guest root, by hostile model output or a malicious repository, in two
sessions of one operator: session A shapes its tree, the guest of session B uses the rewired relay socket.
Preconditions the attacker does not control: os.TempDir() lies under the directory A is run in (cd /tmp, or TMPDIR
under the repository through an allowed .envrc, the precondition of C28), and B runs while A's export is taken and
still runs while A's tree is pulled; for the mount arm, two shells with different TMPDIR values. SEVERITY: medium
(S6). WHERE: cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go fetch, which calls holds(dest) and opens the destination with no compare against
the temp directory, and put, which unlinks what lies at a guest path and makes a symlink with any target;
cmd/workcell/run_vm.go session, whose --mount check compares cwd with this process's os.TempDir() only, and boot,
whose MkdirTemp("", "wc") makes the VMM socket directory; internal/workspace/workspace.go entry, which exports a
directory whatever it holds, skips sockets and copies regular files such as firecracker.json;
internal/vmm/firecracker/firecracker.go Listen (vsock_<port> in the directory) and Start (firecracker.json with
uds_path). INPUT: (a) TMPDIR=$PWD/tmp or cwd /tmp; session B runs, so tmp/wcBBBB holds firecracker.json and the
listening vsock_5000, vsock_5001 and vsock_5002; the operator runs a clone session A in that directory, whose image
carries tmp/wcBBBB with firecracker.json, so A's guest reads the random name; A's guest leaves tmp/wcBBBB/vsock_5001
as a symlink to a unix socket of the operator's uid (an agent socket, a container socket, another session's socket);
the operator runs workcell pull there while B runs. (b) B ran with TMPDIR=D/tmp, and the operator runs workcell run
--mount in D from a shell whose TMPDIR is elsewhere. EFFECT: in (a) the pull keeps tmp and tmp/wcBBBB as directories,
unlinks B's live listener and plants the link; the next relayed connection of B's guest makes the VMM connect to that
path, the kernel follows the link, and B's guest speaks to the operator's socket, outside every export (I1, I4) or
inside another session (I7). In (b) the session is not refused, D/tmp/wcBBBB is served live and A's guest replaces the
socket itself. The link lasts as long as B, and B's teardown removes only the link. Reproducing test, by the redteam,
who was given the claim and not the auditor's probe: TestC56PullRewiresALiveSessionsRelaySocket, package main of
cmd/workcell, 90 lines, parked at escape/_pending/S-F39/c56_test.go. It sets TMPDIR to <repo>/tmp, stands B up as boot
and the Firecracker backend leave it (MkdirTemp under the temp directory, the session's boot record and held lock,
firecracker.json naming uds_path, a listening vsock_5001) and starts a victim unix listener in a temp directory of its
own. Arm (b) wants a mount session run in the repository with TMPDIR elsewhere refused before boot. Arm (a) passes if
the product's own clone export does not carry B's directory name, or if fetch refuses before boot; otherwise it runs
the product's manifest.add and write on the guest's three entries and dials B's relay socket path, which must not
reach the victim. Run by the orchestrator by go test -overlay on 8ed723a, plain and -race, log saved: both arms fail,
with "a mount session of <repo> reached boot with the running session's VMM directory <repo>/tmp/wcNNN in its live
export" and "pull into <repo> replaced the running session's relay socket <repo>/tmp/wcNNN/vsock_5001 with the guest's
link: the VMM's connect for B's guest reached <victim>/agent.sock, a host socket outside every export". The redteam
showed by overlays of product copies that three shapes of fix each make it pass. Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the
verifier, who repeated both runs, found B's state on disk to be what run_vm.go and firecracker.go leave until Close,
the dial by path to stand for the VMM's connect as in C28, the name learnt through the real export (the test checks
the real session() image), the pull step to be the real put, and no power taken from outside the guest but the
operator's steps. Not intended and not refused elsewhere: holds() sees the data and config directories only, and both
the C28 record ("Clone, pull and bench are unchanged: their guests see no host directory where the sockets lie") and
PARKED line 97 reasoned from one session; a second running session's directory under cwd at export time hands the
guest the name. Severity by S6: a shown break whose preconditions the operator chooses, so medium and not low; rarer
than C28, as C52 was; arm (a) has the plausible workflow (an interactive session in the repository, a batch session
pulled while it runs), arm (b) is the rarer one. Not S14: cmd/workcell, internal/workspace and
internal/vmm/firecracker are v2's own, and the VMM's connect by path is its documented design, as C28 ruled. Fix unit:
S-F39, below S-1008 in PLAN.md.

C56 FIXED by S-F39, commits a49f8ea (the test moved), 73ab2d8 (the fix) and 5f58964 (the fix round) (PR #284). holds in
cmd/workcell/data.go, which session and fetch call before anything is made, now also walks the sessions of the data
directory: for each one whose lock is held it reads the vmm file, and it refuses a directory that within() finds to hold
a recorded VMM directory, in one line that names the directory, the VMM directory and the session and ends "wait for it
or workcell stop <id> first". A stale record, of a session whose lock is free, refuses nothing. So a clone or mount
session in, and a pull or diff into, a directory that holds a running session's sockets is refused before a session
directory, an export or a boot record exists, whatever TMPDIR the shell has and however the path is spelled (within
resolves links and judges by inode, as C52 made it). fetch in pull_vm.go, after holds(dest), also refuses a destination
that holds os.TempDir(), where the sockets of a session begun during the pull would lie; diff goes through fetch. The
unit line's second option, an unwritable VMM directory, was not taken: it cannot refuse before boot, and a mount guest
could set the mode back and rename the directory. Fix round, from the review's one finding, the same swap in the other
order (a mount session M runs in D from a shell whose TMPDIR is elsewhere, then a clone session anywhere, a pull or diff
of another repository, or bench boots from a shell whose TMPDIR lies under D, so that M's guest is served the new VMM
directory live): boot in run_vm.go, after its absolute-TMPDIR check and before MkdirTemp and recordBoot, refuses when
the temp directory lies within the repo of a running session that has no workspace.ext4, with "the temp directory <tmp>
lies inside <repo>, which the running mount session <id> serves live: set TMPDIR elsewhere or workcell stop <id> first".
A clone session that is still exporting has no image yet and is judged like a mount session for that window, which
also closes the window in which a starting session holds its lock but has recorded no VMM directory. Cost: 12 product
lines in the fix and 9 in the fix round, paid by joined doc comments with their words unchanged (fetch, run, newSession,
boot, write, compare, stopLadder): product 15000 of 15000, test 28494 of 28500. Test: cmd/workcell/c56_test.go
TestC56PullRewiresALiveSessionsRelaySocket, moved by git mv with its head comment brought up to date, 97 lines. Both
arms fail on the claim tree in the redteam's run and in the reviewer's worktree of main, plain and -race, and pass at
73ab2d8; the arm added in the fix round (a running mount session of the directory, then a boot as a pull of another
repository makes it) fails at 73ab2d8 and on main and passes at 5f58964. The test's two socket directories moved from
t.TempDir() to os.MkdirTemp under the temp directory, because the hosted macOS runner refused to bind a unix socket at
a path of 116 bytes: the test had never run on macOS while it was parked. The reviewer's probes found every other
spelling held: a pull into ., into the VMM directory and into the temp directory while B runs, a session in the
directory after B has ended, links and bind mounts. What an operator pays: while a session runs, no other session and no
pull works in a directory that holds its temp directory (cd /tmp with the default TMPDIR, or TMPDIR under the
repository), and a pull into such a directory is refused at any time. Not proved on a real VM: the test's listeners
stand for the VMM's sockets, as in C28.

C57. ID I10 (host disk and inodes) through the limit that pull puts on what a guest may bring back; the class of C18
on the return path. ATTACKER: guest root in a clone session, forging Entry frames on the pull VM's channel, or
re-making its read-write image as a dense ext4 so that the honest init walks the entries. SEVERITY: low (S6). WHERE:
cmd/workcell/pull.go manifest.add, which judges only an entry's Size against the limit; cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go put,
where Mkdirat, Symlinkat and the file create are charged nothing; mount mode charges one 4096-byte block per created
entry (internal/fileserve/serve_linux.go, S-F11). INPUT: a manifest of up to 1,048,576 directories, or symlinks with
short targets, under 64 MiB of names and with zero file bytes. EFFECT: every entry is accepted and written to the
operator's tree: on ext4 or xfs about 4 GiB of blocks and a million inodes in one pull, against a default --disk of 1
GiB whose honest image gives the guest 65,652 free inodes (measured by the auditor), so about sixteen times the
image's own entry budget; bounded by guest.MaxEntries and MaxNames, once per pull, into the directory the operator
named. Reproducing test, by the redteam from the claim alone: TestPullGrowthCapEntries, package main of cmd/workcell,
44 lines, parked at escape/_pending/S-F40/c57_test.go: arms dir and link feed a manifest with a limit of 100,000 bytes
200 entries and write them into a fresh directory; an arm passes when at most limit/4096 plus 2 entries are accepted
and written, the bound of c18_test.go. Run by the orchestrator by go test -overlay on 8ed723a, plain and -race, log
saved: both arms fail with "200 accepted, 200 written against a limit of 100000 bytes, want at most 26 (24 blocks of
4096 plus 2)". Outcome: CONFIRMED at low by the verifier, who repeated the run, found the test to drive manifest.add
and write as fetch does with no power borrowed, the attacker in scope (the init enforces nothing, and guest root can
also rewrite its image), and the host's cost hard-bounded: about 4 GiB of directory blocks and a million inodes, four
times the default --disk and sixteen to thirty-two times a small cap, a fixed ceiling and no exhaustion, so hardening
with no shown break of I10; not C18's case, which had no bound. An honest image keeps rough parity (one inode per four
free blocks), so the overshoot needs one of the two moves above. Not S14: v2's own code. Fix unit: S-F40, below S-1008
in PLAN.md (S7 lists a low; it is fixed all the same, as the lows of sweep 1 were).

C57 FIXED by S-F40, commits 255a945 (the test moved) and 681860d (the fix) (PR #285). manifest.add in cmd/workcell/pull.go charges every entry one block (const block = 4096) on top of
its Size: the judge is e.Size > m.limit-m.bytes-block and the sum m.bytes += e.Size+block, no wrap, as S-F11 charges
in mount mode; the refusal says "bytes of files and entries, a block for each". The pull's limit was the image's
apparent size, which an honest full image overshoots under that charge, by about a block for every inode it has: the
builder's probe (go test -overlay, not kept) exported trees with workspace.Export, read the superblock the host wrote,
walked them as the init does and let an imagined guest spend every free inode on empty files and every free block on
one file, which is more than an honest guest can. Against the bare image size every shape was refused, the small tree
on the default disk at its last entry (charge 1,342,758,912 against 1,090,871,296 bytes); against the size plus a
quarter, the unit line's fallback, the small trees passed but every dense exported tree was refused: 30,000 short
links plus 30,000 empty files at --disk 64MiB (387,825,664 against 178,073,600), 20,000 files of 4096 bytes at 64MiB
(247,943,168 against 194,580,480), 100,000 short links at 64MiB (807,677,952 against 511,672,320) and 300,000 files
of 4096 bytes on the default disk (3,800,649,728 against 3,001,743,360), because an exported tree's inodes come on
top of the quarter. So the limit is now the image's bytes plus a block for every inode the image has, which the host
records before the guest runs: rootfs.Tree.Inodes is the image's inode count after WriteExt4File, workspace.Stats
carries it, session in run_vm.go writes it to the session directory as inodes beside workspace.ext4 (a clone session
only; a failure to write it is a failed start), and fetch in pull_vm.go reads it with the image's size and passes
st.Size()+inodes*block. Nothing the guest does grows the record, and a guest that re-makes its image with more inodes
is still held to the host's count. Every probed shape is admitted at that limit, with headroom of 6 to 99 MiB (the
metadata blocks beyond the inode tables). Worst case of one pull now: the limit in bytes of blocks and limit/4096
entries, so inodes, instead of 1,048,576 entries and about 4 GiB: 331,990 blocks and entries for a small repository
on the default disk (1,359,831,040 bytes); for a 300,000-file repository on the default disk, whose image is already
2.24 GiB, 952,038. Not covered, as before the fix: a guest tree of hard links, which the pull writes as copies and
charges as such. Cost: 16 product lines, paid by joining the doc comments of manifest, checkPath, fold, pull, diff,
isGit and sameBytes with their words unchanged; product 15000 of 15000, test 28495 of 28500. Tests: c57_test.go gained
an empty-file arm on the arms' line (a Size-0 file is charged like a directory); TestManifestAdd's small limit is three
blocks and a hundred bytes, its exact-fit and over-by-one cases hold a directory as well, a case "more entries than the
image" was added, and FuzzPath, judged and the C44 test use limits that hold their entries. The C57 test fails on the
tree before the fix, both arms, and passes after, plain and -race.

The two tests cost 134 lines, and the test budget stood at 28498 of 28500, so the redteam paid with 145 folded lines
under escape/ in 37 files, layout only: no row removed, renamed or given another verdict, and no assertion, judge,

paragraphs re-flowed with their words unchanged, table rows packed up to 200 columns, eight short function bodies put
on one line where gofmt leaves that alone, same-type struct fields joined (six joins move a field next to its
type-mates; every literal of those structs is keyed and none is encoded or printed whole), and adjacent uncommented
constants joined. gofmt -l prints nothing, go build and go vet pass for Linux and for darwin arm64, go test
./escape/... is the same before and after, and the list of the control sandbox's 145 rows is identical. Test code is
now 28487 of 28500, product 15000 of 15000.

Sweep 2 verdict for this surface: two candidates, C56 confirmed at medium and C57 confirmed at low. Sweep 2 had
already confirmed four mediums (C52 on S-1003, C53 on S-1005, C54 and C55 on S-1007, all fixed), so with C56 it stands
at five and S-1017 will call a third sweep (S8). The fix units are S-F39 and S-F40; the next candidate number is C58.
The other shapes found are R3 notes, copied to PARKED.md: the 5002 port left open after a failed FUSE dial, the
exports a repository can make fail, the refuted reason of line 97, the C56 variants the test does not express, the
entry kinds and depths that C57's charge must also count, and what this audit did not run. In the auditor, the two
redteam runs that wrote the tests, the redteam run that folded and the two verifiers no model declined and no
safeguard re-ran a request.

## S-1009, sweep 2: policy loading and merge, CLI parsing, `--allow`, adapter data files (I13), as built at main 8986114

Fresh context, the whole surface read in full as built (not a diff), after the 32 fix units of sweep 1 and S-F33
to S-F40 of sweep 2, at the claim commit 0b3a1a9 on main 8986114. One auditor run, finished without a stop:
no model declined and no safeguard re-ran a request. No hypervisor in the session, and nothing on this surface
needed a VM. Result: two candidates, C58 (I5 through I13, medium) and C59 (I14 hardening, low), each given to
a redteam run as a claim only, run by the orchestrator, and ruled on by its own verifier; the records are below.

Trust boundary. The malicious repository (map row 17) owns every byte of <cwd>/workcell.toml and, in a clone
export or under --mount, everything else under cwd. It enters at loadPolicy in cmd/workcell/policy.go, through
ReadRepo in internal/policy/policy.go (O_NOFOLLOW and O_NONBLOCK, a regular-file check on the opened descriptor,
a 1 MiB cap, [update] refused), Parse (the project's own TOML subset) and Narrow. The code that handles it is
the supervisor, as the operator's uid, before any VM exists: it decides the proxy's allowlist, the resolver's
name set, the session CA's name constraints, the forward ports on the kernel command line, which [[secret]] rows
become broker grants and terminate rules, and whether a session is refused for exporting a secret source (the C54
check). Of a repository row only the allow entry's text and the secret's name are ever compared; its host, header,
source, env, method, path and repos reach nothing. But through narrowing the repository also decides which of the
user's rows survive, and one host-side check was keyed on that set (C58). Hostile model or tool output turned
into argv (row 39) enters at parseRun in caps.go: --allow is kept verbatim and judged in allowlist() (empty,
any unicode.IsSpace rune or # refused, then ParseAllowlist and dnsName), --cache by its regexp, --cpus, --memory
and --disk by bounds, session ids by validID, and the command goes verbatim into guest.Exec; --allow entries are
appended after Narrow and are the designed host approval. The environment (row 40: XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME
and HOME at xdgDir with the IsAbs guard of S-F14, TMPDIR at boot, session and fetch, TERM, SSL_CERT_FILE and
SSL_CERT_DIR, and the three variables passed to a cmd: program) is the operator's; no in-scope attacker sets
it. The user's config.toml and the embedded provider TOML (row 41) pass the same parser; FindSecret fills host,
header and env into a user row only after Narrow; [update] is the user's alone and feeds newInstaller (key, ca,
channel URL, cooloff).

Parsing and resources. The scanner and parser read again in full: tokens are constant-size, arrays and tables
are bounded by the 1 MiB cap, a carriage return is accepted only before a newline, control bytes and non-ASCII
outside strings refuse, and \u escapes are checked as scalar values; a \u0000 or \u000a inside a string survives
Parse and is then refused by allowlist() or lands quoted in the asked note. Narrow is O(user entries x repository
entries), fine at 1 MiB. FuzzParse ran 45 s, 1,319,748 executions, no crasher. allowlist() still re-parses the
joined list per entry (quadratic, operator argv only, PARKED line 70). ParseAllowlist (ported): SplitHostPort,
refusal of IP literals (bracketed, zoned, mapped), canonicalHost, dnsName, port 1 to 65535, one host per non-443
port. The only non-ASCII folds that reach ASCII are U+212A to k and U+0130 to i, typed by the operator and matching
what the glyph shows. The resource flags are as sweep 1 left them. Nothing at medium or above from this lens.

Logic and state. Narrow's three rules re-derived: allow keeps only user entries that a repository entry equals
textually; [[secret]] keeps only user rows that a repository row names; a user row whose host was in the user's
allow and is not in the kept allow goes too. --allow is added after narrowing; the asked note is computed before
that. The C34 check walks p.Secret, the user's rows, so a dropped sign-in row whose token host is still terminated
is refused, also when the host comes back through --allow (probed). The C54 check walks narrowed.Secret, the
rows the repository left, so the repository switches it off by dropping the row: C58. AllowSet semantics,
duplicate tables, provider-filled rows (fail closed in every narrowing tried), a repository [update] table
(refused) and flags after the command (they belong to it) are as recorded in sweep 1.

Concurrency, ordering and check-to-use. ReadRepo judges the descriptor it opened, and the policy is fixed before
boot. The second-session question of S-1008: a mount guest on repository R can rewrite R/workcell.toml between
the operator's sessions, or make it a link or a directory (a FIFO it cannot make: MKNOD is ENOSYS); a later
loadPolicy there sees a narrowing, or ignores the file and applies the user's grants, which are the ceiling,
so nothing widens. A mount guest on an ancestor that swaps cwd between loadPolicy and Export (the C39 class,
PARKED line 123) exchanges one attacker tree for another under the same grants. The order of refusals is policy
(the C54 check included), then holds(), then newSession, then Export, then boot. openCaches runs before holds()
(PARKED line 100, cache locks only). Nothing new beyond C58.

Cryptography and identity. On this surface: the [update] key (64 hex digits, an ed25519 public key that replaces
channel.Keys) and ca (a PEM pool that replaces the system roots for the installer's client), both the user's;
placeholders from crypto/rand; the session CA's permitted names are the canonical terminated hosts. The ca path
is read as written, so a relative value resolves against cwd: C59, the class of C21, C30 and C53 with a weaker
consequence, since the manifest signature, serial, expiry and the artifact digest still stand.

Failure modes. Every error path fails closed: an unreadable user config, EACCES or ENXIO on workcell.toml,
a socket, a file over 1 MiB, a bad line, a repository [update] table, a [[secret]] row without name or source,
provider.All failing, HOME unset or relative, and a secret row with no allow list. Two shapes are open by design:
a workcell.toml that is a link, FIFO or directory is ignored and a missing one grants the user's policy, the ceiling
in both cases. C58 is the one place where a host-side refusal is skipped because its input set is the attacker's.

Downgrade, rollback and replay. The policy has no version; cooloff refuses negative values and only lengthens;
channel must be stable, hold or an https URL; a repository cannot carry [update]. --to chooses from the manifest's
current and previous only. update --rollback re-points current at the previous marker without asking the manifest's
Withdrawn list (an observation for S-1011; B10 names the verb as the user's control). Nothing on this surface.

Interaction with other surfaces. C58 is an interaction: I13's narrowing (internal/policy) turns off the I5 check
of S-F37 (cmd/workcell) that the secrets surface relies on. A user row with env = "PATH" or a trust variable's
name makes the placeholder the last such entry, which the init's lookPath takes, so the command cannot run or
the guest's own trust breaks: fail closed, the user's own row (PARKED line 66). The host's channel and artifact
fetches honour the operator's proxy variables, while the guest's terminated transport has its own DialContext
and no Proxy, so such a variable never redirects guest traffic. holds() is not called by explain or update:
explain starts nothing and update reads the user's config at its real place since S-F14. Many --allow forward
ports can truncate the kernel command line (PARKED line 48: the operator's flags, fewer ports relayed).

Parked leads of this surface, checked against the code as built. Line 29 (U-402, provider.go) stands, R3:
bareHost still passes a host with one leading newline, two rows of one name still load, file and field are
still accepted dead keys, TestEmbeddedProviders still names four files; build-time data, and a newline host
would fail the terminated-host check. Line 33 (U-503) stands, R3: the ErrNotRegular ignore branch is still in
loadPolicy, and ignoring leaves the ceiling. Line 66 (S-1007) stands, R3, as above. Line 70 (S-1009, sweep 1):
the relative-TMPDIR clause is settled (IsAbs before MkdirTemp in boot, the within() compares of S-F20 and S-F39
in session and fetch); the rest stands, R3. Line 72 (S-F15) stands, R3: policy.go still imports unicode for the
guard. Line 141 (S-F27) stands, R3, residual for S-1018: with a repository that drops the sign-in row and narrows
the host off 443, --allow login.p.test:8443 leaves that host reachable raw on 8443 with no rule and no refusal,
because the C34 check reads the terminated hosts; the flag is the operator's and the row's token endpoint is on 443.

data_test.go, explain_test.go, c19_test.go, c21_test.go, c22_test.go, c34_test.go and c54_test.go; internal/policy
policy.go and policy_test.go; internal/provider provider.go, provider_test.go and the four TOML files (no
stray bytes); internal/proxy allowlist.go, signin.go, terminate.go and proxy.go; internal/secret broker.go and
source.go; internal/pins pins.go; pins/pins.go; internal/channel channel.go; internal/guest guest.go and trust.go;
internal/vmm vmm.go and firecracker/firecracker.go; internal/resolver resolver.go; internal/artifact verify.go;
docs/policy.md and docs/providers.md; escape/suite/repo.go; escape/sandbox/workcell.go; SPEC.md; PARKED.md;
the sweep-1 section of this surface and the C34 and C54 records. Read in part: session_test.go, update_test.go,

### S-1009 candidates, sweep 2

C58. ID I5 (real credential bytes never exist in guest disk or memory), reached through I13: the repository's
file switches off a host-side refusal, the one S-F37 added for C54. ATTACKER: the malicious repository, through
its workcell.toml, with guest root reading /workspace and, under --mount, rewriting the cmd: program that the
host later runs as the operator. Precondition the attacker does not control, the same as C54's: the operator's
[[secret]] row has a file: or cmd: source whose path lies under the directory the session is run in. SEVERITY:
medium (S6). WHERE: cmd/workcell/policy.go loadPolicy, the C54 loop, which walks narrowed.Secret; narrowed comes
from policy.Narrow, whose [[secret]] and allow rules (internal/policy/policy.go) let the repository drop any user
row. INPUT: config.toml with [network] allow = ["api.anthropic.com"] and a [[secret]] row name "anthropic", host
"api.anthropic.com", header "x-api-key", source file:<cwd>/.secrets/anthropic.key (or cmd:<cwd>/tools/get-key.sh);
the repository at <cwd> carries a workcell.toml holding either a [[secret]] row with name = "nothing" and source =
"x", which drops every user row and keeps the network, or [network] with allow = [], which drops the host and
the row with it; the operator runs workcell run, or workcell run --mount, there. EFFECT: loadPolicy returns
no error and no binding, since the row is gone from the set the C54 loop judges, and the session goes on to
holds(), newSession, Export and boot: in clone mode the key file, or the key-printing program, lies in the
session's workspace.ext4, which the guest gets as /workspace; under --mount the directory is served live, and
the guest may rewrite the cmd: program, which the broker runs on the host at the first use by a later session
that keeps the row. With the [[secret]] form the user's whole allow list stays, so the guest can carry the key
out through any allowed host that takes an upload. explain in that directory says that the repository's secret
"nothing" is not granted and "secrets: none", and nothing about the key. Reproducing test, by the redteam, who
was given the claim and not the auditor's probe: TestC58RepositoryCannotSwitchOffTheSourceCheck, package main of
cmd/workcell, 47 lines, parked at escape/_pending/S-F41/c58_test.go. Six arms: three repository files (a comment
that changes nothing, the [[secret]] form, the allow form), each in clone and mount mode, with the file: source;
it drives loadPolicy and then session() with temporary XDG directories and the dummy artifacts of the C19 and
C54 tests, and fails on any session directory made, saying whether the key's bytes lie in the export. Run by
the orchestrator by go test -overlay on the claim tree, plain and -race, log saved: the two control arms pass
(refused by the C54 check), and the four others fail with "I5: session <id> was made with <cwd> as /workspace
(mount: false; the key lies in its export: true)" in clone mode and "(mount: true; the key lies in its export:
false)" under --mount, each after the dummy VMM's "start firecracker: invalid argument", so the session directory
and the export existed before boot. Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, who repeated the run plain and
under -race with TestC54 beside it (green, so the C54 fix is present and this is a distinct gap), found that the
test calls loadPolicy and session() as run does, that only the dummy VMM stops a boot on that export, that the
workcell.toml is the attacker's and the key under cwd is the operator's precondition already accepted for C54,
and that the behaviour is not intended: the dropped row grants nothing, but the check's purpose is the key's
bytes and not the grant, the C34 check two lines above walks the user's rows for that very reason, and without
the repository's file the same setup is refused, so workspace content turns a refusal into a session that holds
the real key. Severity by S6: a shown break whose precondition the operator chooses, so medium and not high. The
auditor ran the one-token change (walk p.Secret) by overlay: its eight probe arms, cmd: included, were refused
with the existing C54 message, and cmd/workcell, internal/policy, internal/proxy and internal/provider were
green under -race. Not S14: cmd/workcell/policy.go is v2's own, nothing ported, no v1 line. Fix unit: S-F41,
below S-1009 in PLAN.md.

C58 FIXED by S-F41, commits e8b3f36 (the test moved) and e0d67ee (the fix) (PR #287). The source check in loadPolicy in
cmd/workcell/policy.go walks p.Secret, the rows of the user's own config.toml, as the C34 check two lines above does,
and no longer narrowed.Secret: one token and the comment beside it, net 0 product lines, no test line. policy.Narrow
copies a kept row unchanged, so a row the repository keeps is judged as before and the message still names the user's
file, line and secret; nothing the repository's workcell.toml holds reaches the loop. loadPolicy is called by run,
before loadArtifacts, the caches and session, and by explain, so the refusal is one line (exit 2) before a session
directory or an export exists. The test is cmd/workcell/c58_test.go, the parked file with its head comment changed,
47 lines; escape/_pending/S-F41/ is gone. Shown: the redteam ran the moved test on the claim tree, plain and -race,
four attack arms failing and two control arms passing; the reviewer repeated the fail in a worktree of main and the
pass at e0d67ee, and ran 15 arms by overlay (8 refused at e0d67ee that started on main, 7 unchanged on both): a cmd:
program under cwd with the row dropped, a cmd: argument under cwd with allow = [], a repository allow that names
another host, --allow giving the dropped host back, a source through a symlinked directory, a trailing slash, a
.. spelling and cwd itself as an argument are refused; a kept row under cwd is refused as before; a source outside

to read it. One review round, no findings, no fix round. Not S14: v2's own code, no v1 line.

C59. ID I14, as hardening of the trust root the host uses to fetch channel.json and the pinned artifacts;
the class of C21, C30 and C53, a relative path resolved against the repository. ATTACKER: the malicious
repository, which supplies the file at the relative path, completed by a network attacker on the path of the
host's fetch. Precondition the attacker does not control: the user wrote a relative ca in the [update] table,
for example ca = "ca.pem". SEVERITY: low (S6: hardening, no invariant shown broken). WHERE: cmd/workcell/update.go
newInstaller, which reads u.CA with os.ReadFile as written and makes that pool the only roots of the installer's
client, the one both the manifest fetch and the artifact fetch use; internal/policy/policy.go updateTable,
which accepts any string for ca. INPUT: config.toml with [update] holding a channel, a key and ca = "ca.pem";
the repository holds ca.pem with the attacker's CA; the operator runs workcell run, update or bench start in the
repository. EFFECT: the host's channel and artifact fetches trust only the repository's CA for that invocation,
so a network attacker on the path can present its own certificate for the channel host and the pin URLs; with no
such file in cwd the same config is refused. Not claimed and not shown: a pass of channel.Verify or of the digest
check. Reproducing test, by the redteam, from the claim alone: TestC59UpdateCAIsNotReadFromTheWorkingDirectory,
package main of cmd/workcell, 40 lines, parked at escape/_pending/S-F42/c59_test.go. It writes the user's
config with a loopback httptest TLS server as channel, puts that server's self-signed certificate as ca.pem in
a separate directory, makes that the working directory, and calls newInstaller: a refusal passes; otherwise
it fetches from the server through the installer's client and fails, reporting the fetch's error. Run by the
orchestrator by go test -overlay on the claim tree, plain and -race, log saved: it fails with "newInstaller
accepted ca = "ca.pem" from the working directory; a fetch through its transport from the attacker's upstream
gave <nil>; want the relative path refused". Outcome: CONFIRMED at low by the verifier, who repeated both runs
and found the effect to be the claimed one, the test's only powers to be the stated precondition and cwd being
the repository, as run and update have it, and the behaviour not intended: nothing documents ca as relative
to cwd, and the project refuses every comparable input (XDG in C21, SSL_CERT_FILE in C30, SSL_CERT_DIR in C53,
TMPDIR). Severity by S6: I14 is untouched, since channel.Verify still demands the key, a serial no lower than
the last seen and an unexpired manifest, and the fetch still refuses a digest mismatch, so the attacker who owns
the TLS root gains what an on-path attacker has anyway (blocking, or freezing at the last serial until expiry)
and no artifact installs past the checks: not medium. It is not nothing either: ADR-004 names TLS as the second
factor that keeps a leaked key harmless, and this hands that factor to the repository; unlike C30, where the
trust store was the only guard. PARKED line 78 and the S-1011 and S-1013 records of sweep 1 held this value
as an R3 observation; with a test that an independent verifier failed to refute it is a finding now. Not S14:
update.go and internal/policy are v2's own, nothing ported, no v1 line. Fix unit: S-F42, below S-F41 in PLAN.md.

C59 FIXED by S-F42, commits 3f11d4c (the test moved) and 52c5999 (the fix) (PR #288). newInstaller in
