## S-1010, sweep 2: audit log, seal, key storage, `verify` (I9), as built at main 78ffa16

Fresh context, the whole surface read in full as built (not a diff), after the 32 fix units of sweep 1 and S-F33
to S-F42 of sweep 2, at the claim commit 8aa5f99 on main 78ffa16. One auditor run, finished without a stop:
no model declined and no safeguard re-ran a request. No hypervisor in the session, and nothing on this surface
needed a VM. Result: no candidates. Seven leads were worked to a probe or a full trace and each was refuted;
the nine parked lines about this surface were each ruled on; no redteam and no verifier ran, since there was
no claim to test.

Trust boundary. The guest's bytes reach a record as: the raw SNI of a refused 443 connection (crypto/tls admits
any bytes but a trailing dot, within a 16 KiB hello), the name of a refused DNS query (lower-case letters, digits,
dot and hyphen, or empty), the relay header's port (a uint16, 0 admitted), the exit status in session_end ("exit N"
from one byte, or "failed"), and the rate and timing of attempts. Every other field is a constant, a config string
that the TOML scanner has already stripped of control characters, or an allowlist key. They enter through
audit.Log.append (clip to 253 bytes, json.Marshal, one mutex, one write(2) per line, a seal per line signed with
a key that lives only in the supervisor's memory) and leave through Verify, ParseLine, eachLine (ported), the log
verb's feed, denyMessage and ocsfLine, the last three passing the one free-form field through SafeHost. The
authority is the supervisor as the operator's uid, owning sessions/<id>/audit.log and audit.seal (0600) and
<data>/audit.key (0600); log and verify read as the same uid; the escape adapter reads the files and runs the verb.

Parsing and resources. Hostile fields were driven through the real audit.Create and the real log verb in text and
in --format ocsf, then verify (probe TestProbeHostileFieldsRoundTrip, package main, by go test -overlay): SNIs
holding an embedded newline followed by a forged session_end object, OSC and C1 CSI sequences, U+202E, U+2028,
NUL, 300 bytes of 0xFF, 200 e-acute (clipped inside a rune), the Kelvin sign, a quote, and 16 KiB of x, each as
sni_not_allowed and as host_mismatch. 24 records; no raw byte below 0x20 in the file and no line over 16 KiB; the
text output (2851 bytes) and the OCSF output (7560 bytes) hold no control, C1 or bidi rune; verify says intact;
the cut rune is written as U+FFFD. Bounds: the writer's most (HardLimit, the marker and session_end) is under
the reader's MaxBytes (HardLimit plus two maxLine); a record is five clipped fields at most, so under maxLine;
the seal has one fixed length of 194 bytes, so WriteAt(0) leaves no stale tail; the signing cost of a refusal
flood ends at SoftLimit (about 69,000 signatures, about 2 CPU-seconds in all, after which ErrFull costs a marshal
and a size check); durable records are at most 300 a minute through the broker's window, plus Issues bounded by
the real provider. FuzzEachLine exists; the seal reader's Sscanf is bounded by the 32-byte and 64-byte checks
that follow it.

Logic and state. The full, failed and closed states of append were traced with TestVolumeIsBounded and
TestLifecycleRecordsIgnoreTheLimit; the lifecycle bypass of the limit is host-only. Rollback of a (log, seal)
pair taken mid-session, the residual S-F17 named: probe TestProbeRollbackPairs made a six-record session, kept
the pair after Create and after each record, restored each pair under the same id once the session had closed,
and ran the verify verb on each: pairs 0 to 5 exit 1 with "incomplete: the session's end was not recorded", pair
6 exits 0 intact. audit.Verify alone accepts the empty log with its first seal (TestProbeEmptyLogInitialSeal:
no last event, nil error), and the verb refuses it. A running session shows its live state, which is right.

Concurrency and check-to-use gaps. One mutex for every writer. A record that lands after session_end (a Deny
of an allowed connection whose upstream dial fails late, timed by guest root with the network attacker) would
make verify call a complete log incomplete: probe TestProbeLateNoteAfterSessionEnd (package audit) held the
mutex for 3 ms over the session_end write, longer than sync.Mutex's starvation threshold, with a Note parked on
the lock, then Unlock and Close as session() does: the late Note landed in 0 of 50 runs, got ErrClosed every
time, Verify intact every time, green under -race. Had it landed, the effect would be a false alarm, nothing
suppressed, forged or altered. LoadKey's first-use race fails closed. verify reads the log before it probes the
lock, so at most one passing "incomplete" for a session that ends between the two (PARKED line 77).

Cryptography and identity. The seal is ed25519 over the prefix, the session id and the chain head, with a
domain-separated message and an id that holds no space; the chain is SHA-256 over digest-prefixed lines with
no split ambiguity. A copied or renamed session and another host's key are refused
(TestVerifyRefusesAnotherHostOrSession). Who can reach audit.key: host-level access only. holds() refuses a cwd
or a pull destination that holds or lies inside the data or config directory (the C19, C29 and C52 tests are
green, C52's by inode, with its check that the key was not minted inside the exported tree); workspace.Export
copies a symlink as a symlink and hard-links only inodes it met inside the tree; the file service has no LINK
operation and resolves nothing on the host; pull writes files and symlinks and follows none; the key is read
into memory by LoadKey and written nowhere else: not to the kernel command line, the Exec environment, the CA
or a secret program's environment. LoadKey fails closed on an empty, torn, wrong-mode or non-regular key, and
on a symlink planted at its path.

Failure modes. Every error path fails closed. A failed write ends the log and withholds secrets; session_end's
failure is printed; a crash gives "changed", "cut inside a record" or "incomplete" and never a false intact.
After S-F16 every Deny caller was traced: handle's route refusal, handle's Allowed before the terminate check
and before connect, connect's refusal after an Allowed record, the transport's DialContext and the six handler
refusals in terminate.go, token_answer_refused in signin.go, the relay's port_not_allowed and the resolver's
name_not_allowed through the one closure in boot, and the broker's record, which acts on nil. Issue stores
tokens before its record, and after ErrFull or a failed write those tokens can never be released, because the
record of every later release fails too. A kept-alive terminated connection accepted before SoftLimit goes on
serving after the fill, by design: the connection is recorded, each secret use is recorded durably up to
HardLimit, and a refusal on it is refused whether or not its Note fits. Nothing is served without its record.
A typed-nil *audit.Log as Recorder (the pull and bench boots) returns ErrClosed from Note with no panic, and
those boots have no listeners.

Downgrade, rollback and replay. No older seal format is accepted; rollback pairs are refused as above; copied
and renamed sessions are refused. updates.log is outside the chain by design and has carried no in-scope
attacker's bytes since S-F1.

Interaction between surfaces. I5: no value, placeholder or guest Host header reaches a record; the secret
record's host and header come from the rule. I6: Deny hosts are canonical. I7: rm removes the record, by
design. I10: the bounds above. I12: the channel never carries records. I13: the deny line's remedy cannot
widen. SafeHost admits a leading hyphen, so a refused SNI "-mount" or "--allow" prints as the remedy
"workcell run --allow -mount", and the Kelvin sign folds to an ASCII k; Go's flag package takes the next
argument as the value, and dnsName in internal/proxy/allowlist.go refuses a label that starts or ends with a
hyphen, so neither the flag nor a config entry gains a host. Wording only.

The fixes since sweep 1, asked for their second order. S-F16 holds as built (unrecorded_test.go green, every
caller traced). S-F17 holds as built, and the rollback probe extends its test to every pair. S-F12, S-F21 and
S-F35: the key cannot be minted in or exported into a workspace through cwd, pull, a symlink or a bind-mount
alias; the bench and cache boots touch no cwd. S-F33 and S-F2: session_end is written on a stopped or closed
stdout reader, a closed stderr reader takes the same EPIPE path in client(), and a SIGKILL still leaves no end
record, which verify now reports as incomplete and not intact.

The parked lines, each ruled on, none with an in-scope break behind it. Line 34 (the seal rewritten per append,
pull's nil log, updates.log outside the chain): a crash between append and seal fails closed; the pull boot
has no listeners, no network and no command; updates.log holds no connection, secret use or lifecycle event.
Line 73 (times out of order, port 0, bytes after the seal's two tokens, no record for the attach, pull and diff
boots, wording): the remedy "host:0" is refused by ParseAllowlist, and the only author of a refused relay header
in a pull boot is guest root during a boot that runs no command, the C14 shape. Line 74 (no VM row floods
audit.log): a gap in the suite and not a break; S-F16's Go test is the evidence, and R5 forbids asking for a row.
Line 76: wording. Line 77: one passing "incomplete" at most. Line 96 (two first uses race to an empty key; the
bind-mounted data directory): the race fails closed, and the alias was C52, fixed by S-F35. Line 155 (a granted
ledger line before carriesPlaceholder refuses): a record too many, not one suppressed or forged, and the value
never left the host. Line 160 (CPU per recorded refusal): bounded by SoftLimit. Line 162 (allowed names still
resolve after log_full): since S-F16 every connection after the marker is refused, and the answer tells the
guest nothing that the CA's name constraints and workcell.ports= do not.

Coverage. Read in full: internal/audit (audit.go, key.go, the ported lines.go, audit_test.go); in cmd/workcell
log.go, ocsf.go, data.go, run_vm.go, session.go, main.go, relay.go, pull.go, policy.go, update.go, bench_vm.go,
cache_vm.go, verify_test.go, log_test.go and the C19, C29 and C52 tests; in internal/proxy the ported proxy.go,
terminate.go and allowlist.go, signin.go and unrecorded_test.go; the ported internal/secret/broker.go;
internal/relay/relay.go; internal/resolver/resolver.go; internal/workspace/workspace.go; escape/suite/audit.go
and lifecycle.go; the map and sweep 1's record of this surface above, with C8, C14 and the ledger passages of
S-1005 and S-1006 of sweep 2. Skimmed or by grep: pull_vm.go (fetch, newest), the head of explain.go, Start,
Wait, Kill and Close in internal/vmm/firecracker, the Exit encoding in internal/guest, the control-character
refusal in internal/policy, the operation list of internal/fileserve, the I9 rows of escape/suite/tests.go,
escape/sandbox/workcell_vm.go lines 425 to 535, the I9 block of docs/threat-model.md. Not opened:
internal/secret/source.go, internal/vmm/vz, the control adapters, internal/rootfs, the rest of
internal/fileserve, the remaining test files, and _legacy/. Run: go test and go test -race with overlays only,
on go1.27.4; the existing internal/audit and cmd/workcell tests are green on this tree; no VM row, no fuzz run
and no macOS path. Every probe's target was a file or a process the probe itself made (S12). Not S14: nothing
concerns another project; the four ported files read hold nothing new, so no v1 line is owed.

Sweep 2 verdict for this surface: no candidates. Sweep 2 has confirmed six mediums on other surfaces (C52 on

## S-1011, sweep 2: pins, selector, verification, bump tool, channel manifest, update client (I14, section 10), as built at main 2ad2766

Fresh context, the whole surface read in full as built (not a diff), after the 32 fix units of sweep 1 and S-F33
to S-F42 of sweep 2, at the claim commit 87ca5f1 on main 2ad2766. One auditor run, finished without a stop:
no model declined and no safeguard re-ran a request. No hypervisor in the session, and nothing was run on a VM.
Result: one candidate, C60, recorded below with its test and its verifier's answer. Ten leads were worked to a
probe or a full trace and each was refuted; the parked lines about this surface were each ruled on.

Trust boundary. The network attacker's bytes are channel.json and the artifact bodies: they enter artifact.Fetch
(the manifest and fetch paths of update.go, and cmd/bump through pins.Candidates and artifact.Verify) over TLS to
the pinned host, under the system roots or the operator's own [update] ca, and no byte is used without the
manifest's signature or the pin's digest, so that attacker holds availability alone (apply's install at a start
is bounded by channelBound, 10 minutes, and the daily fetch is never awaited). Guest root reaches this surface
only through its first channel frame: an Exit with an error as the guest's first frame makes run call
installer.fail, which since S-F1 and S-F31 acts only on the exact current and previous pair that this start's
apply installed; in mount mode the guest also writes the working directory live. The repository controls the
working directory and workcell.toml: ReadRepo refuses an [update] table, and after S-F42 no [update] value is
read against the working directory. One relative read survives, in fail of the zero installer (C60). Upstream
bytes (npm packuments, GitHub release listings, vendor manifests, OCI tags and manifests, Sigstore bundles, npm
attestations, OSV answers) enter cmd/bump on the runner, a dry run until H-905; the provider's own service is
out of scope (the S-1012 ruling), so these are robustness only. The channel key holder and the operator's own
table are out of scope except where they mix with an attacker's bytes. The authority: update, start-up (apply,
daily) and fail run as the operator and write <data>/layers/<agent>/ (the images, current, previous, failed),
<data>/channel.serial, channel.day and channel.next, and updates.log; findLayers turns current into a read-only
drive that the next guest mounts read-only.

Parsing and resources. The envelope is parsed strictly and the payload leniently under one signature; the
64 KiB cap is the same in Fetch and Verify; an artifact is at most 512 MiB on disk, a tar 1 GiB in memory, and
the ext4 writer returns ErrTooLarge; the digest is checked before the unpack, so no in-scope attacker reaches
the tar or ext4 parsers. FuzzVerify (17,000 executions) and FuzzTarMember (287,000 executions) ran 12 s each
with no crasher. marker reads with os.ReadFile, unbounded and following symlinks: harmless under the data
directory, not under the working directory (C60).

Logic and state. Install, --to, --rollback, the re-install of a failed image, apply's skip of a failed digest
and fail were traced through every marker transition; choose applies the user's cooloff to Released only;
Select drops a withdrawn digest from pins and from previous; an image is reused from disk only when it is the
failed one.

Concurrency and check-to-use gaps. verify reads the serial floor, verifies and writes the floor with no lock:
two verifies at once on one data directory ended at the lower serial in 1,144 of 3,000 rounds (an observation,
below). Two applies at one instant both read channel.next (PARKED line 45). The markers are written by a
temporary file and a rename. The zero installer's fail is C60.

Cryptography and identity. The DSSE pre-authentication encoding is the specification's; the key id is the
SHA-256 of the public key; the 32-byte guard stands before ed25519.Verify; NotAfter is checked; the serial and
expiry window is [now - 14 days, now + 1 day]; the Sigstore check binds the leaf, the signed entry timestamp
and the body, and compares the identity byte for byte with versionRE; redirects are https only, and
Authorization is dropped across hosts.

Failure modes. Every refusal leaves the markers and the serial untouched; a failed verification in cmd/bump is
a token, an issue and exit 1 (B5). A failed newInstaller makes run go on with the zero installer, B9's best
effort: the one path that does not stop, and the doorway of C60.

Downgrade, rollback and replay. An equal serial passes by design; --rollback reads no manifest (PARKED line
184, for S-1018); the replay window is 14 days and 24 hours per data directory; the concurrent regression of
the floor needs two honest manifests at once and a replay that nobody in scope can serve.

### S-1011 candidates, sweep 2

C60. ID I12 (hostile traffic on the host-guest channel cannot hang the host process), on B9's self-rollback
path; the class of C59, a path read against the repository. ATTACKER: the malicious repository, which holds a
symlink at layers/<agent>/current in the tree the operator runs in, with guest root, which sends an Exit frame
with an error as the guest's first frame; no forged frame is needed, since a repository script whose
interpreter the image lacks makes the init's own Exit with an error the first frame, and under --mount the
guest alone can plant the link for the next session. Precondition the attacker does not control: the `ca` of
the operator's [update] table is relative, missing, unreadable or holds no certificate, so start-up printed one
line and went on. SEVERITY: medium (S6). WHERE: cmd/workcell/update.go: startup returns the zero installer,
whose directory is empty, when newInstaller fails; fail joins that directory with layers/<agent> and reads
current for every provider before it asks whether this start installed anything; marker is a bare os.ReadFile,
which follows links and has no bound. cmd/workcell/run_vm.go: run keeps what startup returned and calls its
fail with the command's base name when the first frame was an Exit with an error. INPUT: config.toml with
[update] ca = "ca.pem"; the working directory holds layers/claude/current as a symlink to a FIFO (or to a
terminal or a pipe on stdin); the operator runs workcell run there and the first frame is an Exit with an error.
EFFECT: after the VM is closed and session_end is recorded, workcell run blocks in a read of a file the
repository chose, against the working directory, until Ctrl-C; unattended, for good. No marker is written and
nothing is set aside, since the zero installer's fresh is empty. A link to an endless device would grow the
supervisor's memory instead (I10): reasoned only and not run (S12). Reproducing test, by the redteam, who was
given the claim and not the auditor's probe: TestC60ZeroInstallerFailReadsTheRepository, package main of
cmd/workcell, 44 lines, parked at escape/_pending/S-F43/c60_test.go. It writes the user's config with the
relative ca, makes a FIFO under a temporary repository with layers/<first provider>/current linked to it,
changes into the repository, takes the installer from the product's own startup, and calls its fail with the
provider's binary name as run does, with a bound of 3 s; on the timeout it opens the FIFO's write end to free
the read and fails. With a config that has no ca line, a healthy installer, the same body passes in 0.009 s.
Run by the orchestrator by go test -overlay on the claim tree, plain and -race, log saved: both fail after
3.01 s with "fail with the installer startup returned under ca = "ca.pem" has read layers/claude/current
against the working directory for 3s". Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, who repeated both runs
and traced the path: run keeps startup's installer and calls fail on the first-frame Exit error; newInstaller
fails for a relative, missing, unreadable or certificate-less ca; fail reads the marker of every provider
before any check of the binary's name; session never changes the working directory; the deferred close of the
VM and the session_end record run before fail, and the signal handler is already stopped, so Ctrl-C ends it.
The test's one power beyond a repository's, a FIFO that git cannot carry, is not needed: a committed link to
/dev/tty or a pipe on stdin holds the same read, and a mount guest can plant a link with an absolute target.
Not intended behaviour: the check S-F42 put before the read of ca exists to keep reads off the working
directory, and the zero installer undoes it one call later. Severity by S6: the harm is small (after
session_end, Ctrl-C recovers), but S6 grades by the precondition, which is the operator's own config, so medium
and not low. The auditor ran its own probe of the same shape (blocked for 3 s on main) and, by overlay, the
change that returns from fail when this start installed nothing: the probe passed with TestFail, TestFailSpares,
TestUpdate, TestChannel and TestFindLayers. Not S14: update.go and run_vm.go are v2's own, nothing ported, no
v1 line. Fix unit: S-F43, below S-1011 in PLAN.md.

C60 FIXED by S-F43, commits fcbbbd0 (the test moved) and 985846b (the fix) (PR #291). fail in
cmd/workcell/update.go returns at once when this start installed nothing (fresh is empty), before provider.All
and before any marker is read, so the zero installer that startup returns after a failed newInstaller reads
nothing, and nothing against the working directory; a start that installed something behaves as before, since
fresh is set only by apply after newInstaller succeeded, and dataDir gives an absolute directory or an error.
Three product lines for the guard, paid by one fold in denyMessage of cmd/workcell/log.go (the empty-host default
as cmp.Or, the form verify already uses), no behaviour changed: product 15000 of 15000, test 28500 of 28500, no
test line. The test moved by git mv with its head comment changed, 44 lines; escape/_pending/ is gone. Before: the
test fails after 3.01 s on main, plain and -race (the redteam, and the reviewer in a worktree of main). After: it
passes at 985846b, plain and -race, with TestFail, TestFailSpares, TestUpdate, TestChannel and TestFindLayers.
The review answered the questions of PARKED line 192: every cause of a failed newInstaller gives the zero
installer, whose fresh is nil; the update verb returns 2 before it uses a failed installer, so --rollback and --to
never hold an empty directory; bench start calls daily only on success. Sweep 2 now stands at seven mediums (C52
to C56, C58 and C60) and two lows (C57 and C59), all fixed.

The 44 test lines were paid by 43 comment re-flows under escape/suite (tests.go 35, https.go 8), no token
outside a comment changed, the control list of 145 rows identical before and after: product 15000 of 15000,

## S-1012, sweep 2: workflows, release, signing, image build and dependencies as a supply chain (section 9), as built at main a41a9eb

Fresh context, the whole surface read in full as built (not a diff), after the 32 fix units of sweep 1 and
S-F33 to S-F43 of sweep 2, at the claim commit 4d5c8ed on main a41a9eb. One auditor run, finished without
a stop: no model declined and no safeguard re-ran a request. Three tool permissions were refused to the
auditor by the session (a gpg decode of the maintainer key, a crafted-commit experiment against guard.sh in
a scratch clone, a crafted go.mod and tree-shape experiment against sections 1 and 2 of gate.sh); none was
rephrased or retried, the key was decoded by a scratch parser on the standard library instead, and the two
experiments are reasoned from the scripts and from the case names of loop/test/suite.sh and gate-test.sh,
which were read and not run. No hypervisor in the session, and nothing on this surface needed a VM. Result:
no candidates. No redteam and no verifier ran, since there was no claim to test. The three tool passes of
S10 were made by the orchestrator and are triaged below.

Trust boundary. Attacker bytes reach this surface in five places. (1) The hosted runner: ci.yml runs on
pull_request_target, checks out the pull request's head with persist-credentials false and runs that
head's loop/gate.sh with contents read, passwordless sudo, no secret, no environment and no id-token;
the only pull-request authors are collaborators (the non-expiring collaborators_only creation policy of
loop/settings.sh), and the Actions policy admits only pull_request_target and schedule, always from main;
the merge job holds contents and pull-requests write, runs no pull-request code and only calls the merge
API, which the ruleset judges (gate, gate-macos and guard from app 15368, strict up-to-date, squash,
no bypass). (2) Network bytes into the runner and the Mac: Firecracker and the kernels by pinned URL and
SHA-256, Debian from the registry by digest, upstream listings and advisories for cmd/bump, the tools that
setup-go, cosign-installer and attest-build-provenance fetch, and modules through the default GOPROXY and
GOSUMDB; all over TLS, so N holds availability only, and a hostile upstream is an allowlisted provider's
own service, out of scope. (3) The maintainer's signature chain: guard.yml checks out live main and runs
main's loop/guard.sh over the pull request's objects with gpg against .github/maintainer.asc, which holds
one v4 EdDSA primary key (certify and sign, no subkey, one user ID) whose fingerprint equals maintainer.fpr
and which expires on 2028-01-15. (4) The user's machine: scripts/install.sh (the asset and SHA256SUMS from
the release URL, sha256sum -c, --version, then mv), Formula/workcell.rb (sha256 placeholders of zeros until
v2.0.0, so brew fails closed), and at run time cmd/workcell/data.go, which only stats vmlinux, initrd.cpio,
root.ext4 and firecracker in the data directory. (5) The loop's own free-path output, which SPEC section 10
treats as untrusted for secrets; as in sweep 1 the loop is outside section 2 for candidates, and the record
names where only it is the writer. Build identity: every setup-go takes go-version-file go.mod, which says
go 1.27.4 with no toolchain directive; go mod verify says all modules verified; the Linux binaries link
only golang.org/x/sys v0.49.0 beyond the standard library, cmd/mkimage and cmd/bump link no third-party
module, and the darwin cmd/workcell adds vz v3.8.0, go-infinity-channel v1.0.0 and the semver package of
x/mod v0.22.0; purego v0.11.2 is required and imported by no file.

Parsing and resources. Every expression in the five workflows reaches a shell only through env; fuzz-minutes.txt
is digits only and capped at 240; the fuzz matrix is built from go list and go test -list through a strict
sed and jq, and consumed through env. gate.sh unrolls go.mod blocks and refuses replace, exclude and ignore,
refuses underscore directories, nested go.mod and go.work, vendor, odd bytes and leading dashes, and fails
a budget on an unmeasurable number. lib.sh keeps LC_ALL=C and turns newlines in names into unprintable
bytes before it filters; land.sh parses a bundle header strictly, caps the file at 256 MB and unpacks
with --strict. install.sh greps a fixed asset name, checks one SHA256SUMS line, and removes its temporary
files on EXIT: the five installer tests of spikes/install ran against a loopback server and passed (wrong
checksum, missing sums, verified, relative directory, a broken asset keeps the old binary). internal/rootfs:
the manifest is capped at 64 KiB and hashed against the requested digest before any JSON is read, every
descriptor digest is checked, a blob is streamed through sha256 and a byte count within 512 MiB, 128
layers at most, the decompressed tar stream and the file data both bounded at 2 GiB, the token realm must
be https and the anonymous token is dropped on a host change; layer.go refuses absolute names, dot-dot,
over-long names and components, NUL, out-of-range ids and device numbers, unknown types, and hard links to
directories or absent targets, and a write through a symlinked parent fails closed; build.go caps the image
at 400 MiB and ext4.go is deterministic. The unit tests of internal/rootfs, cmd/mkimage, internal/channel,
internal/bump, internal/pins and cmd/bump passed. Bounded residual: the base image's file data lives in
memory up to the 2 GiB cap (trusted registry).

Logic and state. The required checks are exactly gate, gate-macos and guard from app 15368; no required job
has an if (W3); merge runs only for claude/* heads of this repository by the owner, reads the title again
at each attempt, never merges a try: title and pins the head commit. release.yml accepts a commit only with
completed, successful gate and gate-macos check runs from app 15368, or, for a squash commit with none,
a pull request whose merge commit is this commit, whose head tree equals HEAD's tree and whose head is
green, which the strict up-to-date rule makes sound; guard is not checked again there, which follows from
the commit being on main under a ruleset with no bypass. guard.sh passes free-only changes in any shape
and admits a locked change only as one commit on the live tip, signed by the pinned key, with the reviewed
trailer as the signed message's last line, at most two hours old. bump -newest rewrites guest rows only,
only when the newest is eligible and not in a dry run, and exits 1 on a failed verification; nightly keeps
that exit and turns a missed P7 into an output that is handed on only in omkhar/workcell. publish stops
before the draft on a dry run. Refuted leads: a skipped required check, a merge of a try: title, a release
of a commit whose gate ran on another tree, a bump that writes outside pins/.

Concurrency and check-to-use. gate.sh reads the tree before anything from it runs; guard judges against
the live tip and the ruleset judges up-to-dateness again at merge; a push after a merge run started fails
the merge call on the pinned commit. If the event's head commit cannot be fetched, guard.yml's fallback
fetches the pull request's head ref, but guard.sh still judges the event's commit and dies with exit 4 when
that object is missing (closed). Release verify and build both check out the same commit, sign and publish
take artifacts from the same run, and publish hashes what it downloaded against what sign signed. The
two-hour signature window is the known residual of REFERENCE.md. One shape is recorded and parked: under
pull_request_target the Actions cache scope is the base branch's, so pull-request code could write a cache
that a run on main restores; nothing restores a cache today (cache false on all nine setup-go uses, no
cache action), so there is no path, only a hazard for a later edit.

Cryptography and identity. lib.sh matches one VALIDSIG line that ends in the pinned fingerprint and takes the
signature time from the hashed subpacket; an expired key or signature fails git verify-commit (closed). Release:
keyless cosign over SHA256SUMS with the identity of release.yml at the ref and the GitHub OIDC issuer,
verified in publish under the same identity, and one attestation whose subjects are the SHA256SUMS lines;
a dry run signs as refs/heads/main, which the documented tag identity refuses; gh attestation verify --repo
without --source-ref still accepts a dry-run build (sweep 1's note stands, for H-905). Actions are pinned
by SHA with version comments whose tag mapping could not be confirmed offline. Debian's registry publishes
no signature, so the digest pin is the identity (B5: wherever one exists). The bump channel job signs with
a throwaway ed25519 key and publish verifies under each key alone. The embedded Sigstore root has no updater
and no expiry (S-1011's code; listed below as an unmoved input).

Failure modes. Every run step is bash -e with pipefail; green() turns a gh failure into not green and exit
1; GATE_REQUIRE_VM=1 makes a missing hypervisor a Linux gate failure; guard.sh dies with exit 4 on every
error and treats only grep 1 and cmp 1 as no; mkimage removes a half-written output; install.sh installs
nothing on any failure. No fail-open path was found. By design: a missed P7 exits 0 (B12); bump.yml has no
issue job, so a red dry-run plan is seen only in the Actions tab (parked).

Downgrade, rollback and replay. The go directive is a free path and gate.sh admits toolchain and godebug
lines (PARKED line 82 stands; the only writer is the loop). Pins never move backwards (S-1011); the enforced
lists ratchet from main; the tag ruleset lets nobody create a tag until H-905, and --verify-tag with the
release-exists error keeps a re-run closed; a replayed signed commit meets the parent rule and the two-hour
window.

Interaction with other surfaces. The nightly B6 smoke runs the newest provider binary in a real VM, isolated,
with the judge's resolver, so it reaches only the loopback canary; the host-side unpack of the B5-verified
upstream bytes runs on the runner. Since S-F35, cmd/workcell/c52_test.go is a second consumer of passwordless
sudo inside go test, beside the escape suite (bind mounts in temporary directories, skipped where sudo
asks for a password). The A6 client half is still missing: data.go stats four files that nothing fetches,
the release ships guest images and a raw init that no client code loads, and the accepted ADR-001 says
Firecracker, the kernel and the image are trusted pin rows fetched under the channel manifest, while pins/
holds no such row. Since S-F12, S-F21, S-F35 and S-F39 closed the data directory's exports, no in-scope
attacker can write those files, so the gap is only the missing fetch and verification, for H-905 and S-1018.

The one lead of candidate shape, by the precedent of C27: Firecracker v1.17.0 and both kernels are pinned
in test code with no pin row (B1), no updater (W12), in two or three places (W6), and workcell fetches none
of them. It fails R2: no published advisory against those pins was shown, no fetch exists for an attacker
to subvert, and an unpublished VMM bug is section 2's hypervisor zero-day. Parked; a published Firecracker
or kernel fix that affects the pins would make it a low of C27's shape.

## S-1013, sweep 2: chains across surfaces, and the start-up, shutdown, crash and upgrade windows, as built at main 179b03c

Fresh context, the whole product read as built (not a diff), after the 32 fix units of sweep 1 and S-F33 to S-F43 of
sweep 2, at the claim commit 3941336 on main 179b03c. One auditor run, finished without a stop: no model declined,
no safeguard re-ran a request and no tool permission was refused, in the auditor, the four redteam runs or the
verifiers. No hypervisor in the session, and nothing was run on a VM: the windows were run with the real
cmd/workcell binary against a stand-in VMM, a script that execs sleep, with dummy artifacts in a scratch data
directory. Result: three candidates, C61 (medium), C62 (low) and C63 (low), each CONFIRMED by its own verifier, C63
with its effect narrowed; they are recorded below with their tests. The session's container was restarted while the
three verifiers ran; the tree and the parked tests were unchanged, the orchestrator ran the three tests again for
their logs and started the verifiers again with the same words. The parked lines of chains and windows were each
ruled on.

Trust boundary. The chained surface has no entry point of its own: its attacker bytes are those of the single
surfaces (guest frames on vsock 5000, 5001 and 5002; the guest-written workspace.ext4 and cache images, attached and
never parsed on the host; the repository tree and its workcell.toml; hostile model output as argv and as the agent's
conduct inside a mount session; the network attacker as the host's DNS and TLS peer and as the channel and artifact
server, with availability alone). What is new is where those bytes meet host state that outlives one session and the
operator's own environment: the data directory (audit.key; sessions/<id> with audit.log, audit.seal, lock, repo,
vmm, workspace.ext4 and inodes; layers/<agent> with its images, current, previous, failed and download residue;
caches; channel.serial, channel.day and channel.next; updates.log), the VMM socket directory under os.TempDir()
(vsock, vsock_5000, vsock_5001, vsock_5002, firecracker.json, attach), and the operator's cwd, TMPDIR, XDG and
SSL_CERT variables. Since sweep 1 the product judges the operator's cwd against that state before anything is made,
by name resolved to identity (S-F12, S-F20, S-F21, S-F35, S-F39, S-F37, S-F41): cwd against the data and config
directories, against the temp directory, against every running session's VMM directory, and a secret source against
cwd. The order of a start, read from run and session and checked with the real binary: parseRun, loadPolicy,
loadArtifacts, startup (apply, then the daily goroutine), findLayers, openCaches, then session: Getwd, holds, the
mount TMPDIR check, newSession (key, directory, lock, repo, audit.Create, session_start), Export and the inodes
record, boot (the TMPDIR and running-mount checks, MkdirTemp, recordBoot, Listen 5000 and 5001, adapters, proxy,
session CA, Serve, serveRelay, Listen 5002 and openMount under --mount, Start, accept), the Exec frame, the attach
listener, the seat. Every helper (audit log, proxy, resolver, broker, CA) is up before Start, so no guest exists
before they do. What the boundary trusts across that order is a spelling: the directory that session judged by name
is opened again by name, later, by Export and openMount (C61), and the liveness of a VMM directory is read from a
lock that pull and bench never take (C63). Under --mount a guest holds every byte of the names beneath its export:
RENAME to any name but the empty one, dot, dot-dot, one with a slash or a NUL, and SYMLINK to any target, which is
the primitive that every chain below uses.

Parsing and resources. No new parser on this surface. holds and boot's running-mount check cost one open, one flock
and one or two reads per session directory per start, unbounded in the count of stale sessions (operator hygiene,
R3). The vmm, repo and inodes files are host-written; inodes is bounded by ParseInt and its sum cannot wrap. A
socket path over 108 bytes fails closed: run with a long scratch TMPDIR printed the bind error, exited 125 and had
removed the directory (PARKED line 14's clause, seen). The one unbounded wait of this surface, C60's marker read
against cwd, is closed by S-F43 (read; its test is green). Refuted: that any guest-written file is parsed by the
host at a window (workspace.ext4 and the caches are attached and never read; the pull judges every entry; the layer
markers have no in-scope writer since S-F12 and S-F21).

Logic and state. With a stand-in VMM, a session directory with repo, lock, an audit.log holding session_start, and a
vmm record naming a directory that holds firecracker.json, vsock_5000 and vsock_5001 exist before the guest's first
byte can arrive. Shutdown runs the defers in reverse: attach listener closed, terminal restored, VM killed and
reaped and its directory removed, session_end recorded, lock released. The marker transitions of point, apply, fail
and update were walked for a crash at each step: a marker is a temporary file and a rename, point writes previous
and then current, a crash between them leaves previous equal to current, which the next apply or update repairs by a
new fetch, and a crash between fail's failed marker and its point leaves the set-aside image current until the
operator runs update (availability only). The state that no code judges: the name of the directory the operator's
shell sits in is the guest's to change under a mount session on an ancestor, and Export and the session records
(repo, and so the session that pull, diff, log, verify and attach pick) go by that name (C61, C62).

Concurrency and check-to-use. C61 is the gap: session takes cwd from Getwd, judges it (holds, the TMPDIR rule),
records it (newSession, measured at 4.18 ms here with its two fsyncs) and then Export opens the same string,
following a symlink at its last component. fetch opens an explicit pull destination the same way after holds; the
default dot is the cwd inode and immune (reasoned, not shown: the dummy VMM stops before any write). Refuted: the
stop ladder's read of the pid before the kill (a millisecond window, operator-timed), two applies on one
channel.next (PARKED line 45: a double set-aside is one), the serial floor's two verifies (PARKED line 191, both
signed), fail's unlocked point against the operator's update verb (PARKED line 143: the guest cannot observe the
operator's keystroke), the first-use race of LoadKey (fails closed on an empty file, read), findLayers against a
concurrent point (availability: the boot fails). C63 is a check that no code performs: fetch and bench hold nothing
that holds reads as live, so S-F39's refusal does not cover a pull in flight.

Cryptography and identity. Nothing new is signed or verified on this surface: the seal binds the session id (S-F17),
channel.next is verified again against the floor, markers are bare names. The identity primitive on which the fixes
of both sweeps converged (compare inodes, not spellings: S-F35's SameFile walk) is what C61 lacks at the open: it is
applied at the judge only. PARKED line 131's within-by-letter clause (a TMPDIR in capitals on a case-insensitive
Mac) is settled by S-F35: Rel fails on the spelling and the walk then stats the ancestors by inode (read).

Failure modes. Every error path on this surface fails closed, by reading and by the windows run: holds and boot
return list's error; within on an absent directory returns false, the safe direction; a failed Export removes the
image and the session directory; every exit of boot runs closeAll; session_end is written on the signal path too
(seen: exit 143); SIGKILL leaves no end record and verify then says incomplete, not intact (seen); a socket path too
long exits 125 with the directory removed (seen); the zero installer no longer reads against cwd (S-F43). No
fail-open error branch was found. The two openings are checks that no code makes: the identity of the directory
opened after it was judged (C61) and the liveness of a pull's or a bench's VMM directory (C63).

Downgrade, rollback and replay. apply verifies channel.next again with the floor that the daily check wrote, and
removes the file first; --rollback reads no manifest (PARKED line 184 stands, for S-1018); update --to goes through
choose and Select, so a withdrawn digest is refused; the C2 residual (a forged first frame sets aside the layer that
this start installed and goes back to the signed previous version) is also reachable with no frame by the operator's
own `workcell run ./claude` in a fresh start (PARKED line 131's clause), which hostile model output could suggest:
the same accepted residual, no new candidate. A stale vmm record left by SIGKILL is ignored by holds by design and
removed by rm (seen). The markers are rename-atomic, so no torn marker is read.

Interaction between surfaces. C61 is the clone export of S-1008 (Export opens its root by name) times the mount
guest's RENAME and SYMLINK of S-1008 (fileserve) times the start order of S-1002, under the precondition that
S-1016c accepted for C39 and left low for want of a demonstration (PARKED line 123). C62 is the same RENAME against
the decision that PARKED line 104 recorded for S-F23 (the operator's own cwd stays unquoted, "which no guest
names"): a guest does name it. C63 is the second order of S-F39 (holds refuses a directory that holds a running
session's VMM directory, liveness read from the lock) against the boots of pull and bench, which hold no lock, and
bench no record (PARKED lines 24 and 144). The sweep 1 chain fixes still hold as built: C28 (TMPDIR in a mount
export), C29 and C19 (holds both ways), C30 and C53 (relative trust-store paths refused), C31 (quoted names), C52
(the SameFile walk, run as root here) and C56, each with its test green; C56's second arm is what C63 reopens for a
pull in place of a run.

Chains tried, each as one record with another gives or does not give a break. C39 (PARKED line 123, S-1016c, low, "a
VM row would prove it") with the RENAME and SYMLINK of fileserve and Export's open of the judged name gives I1, and
I5, I7 and I9 by choice of target: C61. PARKED line 104 with the same RENAME and Getwd's fallback to the kernel's
name when PWD no longer matches gives raw terminal control bytes from ls, explain and pull: C62. PARKED lines 24 and
144 with S-F39's lock-keyed holds give a mount session that serves a pull's live VMM directory: C63. No route:
PARKED line 173 (5002 open after a failed init dial; the host listens on 5002 before Start, so the dial never
fails); line 45 with C2 (two set-asides of one image equal one); line 130 (C45: attach dials the recorded directory
without the lock) with a mount guest planting an attach link in a stale VMM directory (it needs the operator to
attach to an exited session by id, and the frames are the seat's); line 131's `./claude` clause with hostile model
output (the C2 residual, accepted); line 143 with a guest-timed first frame (the operator's timing cannot be seen
from the guest); line 148 (a dot-dot TMPDIR through a link into the export) with S-F35 (still fails closed, since
Listen binds under a directory that does not exist); S-F40's inodes record with a crash between Export and its write
(PARKED line 182: pull refuses); a guest-planted symlink chain at a stale recorded VMM path later served under a
mount export, against rm (the Lstat of the last component, the wc prefix, IsDir and a no-follow descent hand rm only
a directory the guest made inside its own export; reasoned); Firecracker dying mid-session, mid-pull or mid-boot
(EOF on the channel gives 125, an error in the pull's frame, "the VMM ended" in accept); an operator's update racing
a run's apply (each point removes what the other made current, availability only); two first uses of audit.key
(fails closed, read). S-F37 and S-F41's source check with C61's window is folded into C61's effect: the swap can aim
at the source's directory.

Windows tried. Start-up: the order above, the two arms of C61, and the socket-path refusal with the real binary.
Shutdown: the real binary with the stand-in VMM waiting in accept; `workcell stop <id>` returned 0 after 0.058 s,
run exited 143, audit.log holds session_start and session_end "exit 143", verify says intact, the VMM directory is

Upgrade: --to and --rollback racing a run, a first frame after an update, the daily goroutine against apply
(channel.day first, channel.next rename-atomic, the floor checked again), withdrawn on --rollback (PARKED line 184).
Half-written session directories read by ls, verify, rm, pull, attach and the next run: a directory with lock but no
repo lists as exited and matches no cwd; verify fails on a missing log; rm validates every vmm entry; a clone
session without inodes is refused by pull; attach fails on a missing socket; the next run's holds ignores stale

### S-1013 candidates, sweep 2

C61. ID I1 (the guest cannot read or write any host path outside the session's own workspace export), and I5, I7 and
I9 by the target chosen: the directory of a file: secret, or the data directory with audit.key and every session's
record and image, as C19 counted them. ATTACKER: guest root in a mount session, by hostile model output or a
malicious repository's hooks, whose export is a proper ancestor of the directory in which the operator later starts
a clone session. Precondition the attacker does not control: the operator runs `workcell run --mount` in a parent
directory and, while it runs, `workcell run` in a subdirectory of it. SEVERITY: medium (S6), the shape of C19, C28,
C52 and C56. This is PARKED line 123's C39, which S-1016c recorded low for want of a demonstration. WHERE:
cmd/workcell/run_vm.go: session takes cwd from os.Getwd, judges it (holds, the TMPDIR rule), records it (newSession)
and hands the same string to workspace.Export and, under --mount, to openMount; internal/workspace/workspace.go:
Export makes the name absolute and opens it with O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY and no O_NOFOLLOW, so a symlink at the last
component is followed; internal/fileserve: opSymlink takes any target and rename any name that checkName admits;
cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go: fetch opens an explicit pull destination by name after holds, the same shape (reasoned
only). INPUT: terminal 1: `cd ~/work && workcell run --mount -- claude`. The guest, as root, in a loop: rename
/workspace/proj away, link the name proj to a host directory of its choice, wait some milliseconds, remove the link,
put the directory back, wait. Terminal 2, whose shell sits in ~/work/proj: `workcell run -- make`. Getwd returns
~/work/proj while the real directory bears that name, holds and newSession judge and record that name, and Export
opens it some milliseconds later: when the link bears the name by then, the whole target is exported. EFFECT: the
clone session's workspace.ext4, handed to its guest as /workspace, is an export of the host directory that the mount
guest chose. Under --mount the swap of the last component is refused by the no-follow open of fileserve; an ancestor
swap there needs a directory of the same last name at the target, which the guest can supply only inside its own
export, so clone mode is the general case. A guest that flips the name too fast makes the start fail instead: a
denial that the ancestor's guest can always cause. Reproducing test, by the redteam, who was given the claim and not
the auditor's reasoning: TestC61CloneExportFollowsARenamedWorkingDirectory, package main of cmd/workcell, 45 lines,
parked at escape/_pending/S-F44/c61_test.go. It makes work/proj and an outside directory holding a key file with a
random canary, a data directory through c19Data, and a second session whose lock it holds and whose vmm file is a
FIFO, so that session parks in holds, after Getwd; a goroutine's open of the FIFO for writing returns at that
moment, renames proj away and links its name to the outside directory, and closes; session then runs to boot, where
the dummy VMM ends it, and the test reads the new session's workspace.ext4. Run by the orchestrator by go test
-overlay on the claim tree, plain and -race, log saved: both fail with "the clone session of .../proj exported
.../002, where a link under that name pointed by the time of the export: a key outside every export is in the
guest's image (I1)". Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, who repeated both runs and then took away the
rendezvous, since a guest cannot plant that FIFO: a variant of its own with a free-running rename, link, sleep,
restore, sleep loop and no FIFO, 100 starts per period, exported the outside directory 9 times at a period of 50
microseconds, 14 to 23 at 200 microseconds, 10 to 14 at 1 ms, 10 to 24 at 3 ms, once at 10 ms and never at 50 ms,
the same under -race and with PWD unset; the window from Getwd to the end of newSession measured 0.8 to 5 ms. So the
race is won about one start in seven, and the FIFO is a deterministic scheduler, not a power the effect depends on.
The verifier read the guest's two steps in fileserve (the adversarial rows "22 rename a to x" and "10 symlink
absolute"), found nothing in holds or boot that refuses a clone session whose cwd lies inside a running mount
session's export, and traced Getwd: with PWD matching, Go takes it, and with the link in place it falls back to
getcwd, which gives the real directory under its new name, exported harmlessly; either way Getwd gives work/proj
whenever the real directory bears the name. Not intended behaviour: R6 asks for no-follow, descriptor-relative
handling where the host reads data the guest controlled, and a clone cwd inside a mount export is that. Severity by
S6: one precondition the attacker does not control, as C28, C52 and C56; the rate per start does not lower it, since
every clone start is a new try. The verifier's note for the fix: the export's walker also opens files by name at
write time (seen as a failed "write image: open .../proj/id_ed25519"), so the fix must export from one descriptor
taken once. The auditor's own probe of the same shape failed 3 of 3 runs under -race, its free-running arm won 2 of
20 starts at an 8 ms phase and 3 of 20 at 32 ms, and with a two-file overlay that has session pass "." and Export
open the directory as given, both arms passed with cmd/workcell and internal/workspace green under -race. Not S14:
run_vm.go, pull_vm.go, workspace.go and fileserve are v2's own, nothing ported, no v1 line. Fix unit: S-F44, below
S-1013 in PLAN.md.

C61 FIXED by S-F44, commits cf9239b (the test moved) and 12ef82b (the fix) (PR #294). session in
cmd/workcell/run_vm.go still judges and records the name, and then named(unix.AT_FDCWD, cwd), new in pull_vm.go,
refuses unless the name is, by device and inode, the process's own directory; the export and the live mount take
"." and never the name again. Export in internal/workspace/workspace.go opens the directory as given, once, keeps
that descriptor open for the writer and walks a duplicate of it; a regular file's source is a path relative to
that descriptor (the new Dir field of rootfs.HostFile), and openSource in internal/rootfs/ext4file.go takes its
bytes by Openat beneath it, with O_NOFOLLOW on the leaf and the device, inode, size and regular-file check on the
descriptor it got. fetch opens an explicit pull destination first, judges the name, and refuses by the same named
unless the name still gives the directory it holds open. A start or a pull that meets the swap prints one line,
"<name> no longer names the directory it did a moment ago: it was renamed or replaced", and makes nothing: run
exits 125, pull exits 1. The repo record and the messages keep the name. Net 0 product lines, paid by folds with
no behaviour changed (the mode in put, cacheArgs and cacheEnv in layer.go, verify's session argument in log.go,
holdSession, lockCache, one deferred close in Export, two comments): product 15000 of 15000, test 28496 of 28500,
no test line. The test moved by git mv with its head comment changed, 45 lines; escape/_pending/S-F44/ is gone.
Before: the test fails on main, plain and -race, with the outside key in the new session's image (the redteam,
and the reviewer in a worktree of main). After: it passes at 12ef82b, plain and -race. The reviewer's free loop,

3 ms at 12ef82b, where main gave 14, 7 and 26; the starts that met the swap were refused with the one line, the
rest exported the real directory. The same loop under --mount: every start refused or served the real directory,

C62. ID none directly: I12's "confuse the host" in spirit, and the product's own rule, set by C20, C31 and C38, that
a guest-chosen name is quoted before it reaches the operator's terminal; hardening, the class of C31. ATTACKER:
guest root in a mount session on an ancestor of the directory the operator's shell sits in, as in C61. SEVERITY: low
(S6: no invariant broken). WHERE: cmd/workcell/session.go (ls prints the recorded repo with %s),
cmd/workcell/explain.go (explanation concatenates the directory, twice), cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go (the mount-session
and the no-session messages name cwd), cmd/workcell/run_vm.go (the TMPDIR refusal and the copy error),
cmd/workcell/data.go (holds names the directory, twice), internal/workspace/workspace.go (`open %s`, the site that
PARKED line 104 kept raw because "no guest names it"); the guest's primitive is the RENAME of fileserve, whose
checkName admits ESC, BEL and CSI bytes. INPUT: the mount guest renames /workspace/proj to a name that holds an OSC
title sequence, a CSI clear and an SGR colour. The operator's shell sits in that directory by inode and runs

records the name with its control bytes. Later `workcell ls`, `workcell explain` there, or `workcell pull` in such a
directory with no session, prints it. EFFECT: the terminal's title is set and the screen cleared and recoloured, as

compares repo with cwd), so a guest that swaps the names of two sibling directories in which the operator has
sessions chooses which session pull, diff, log, verify and attach answer for each; reasoned only, parked.

changes into it, calls session once so that the session is recorded (and proves the record with newest), and asks of

C63. ID I1 and I4 by the mechanism of C56 (a guest replaces a live VMM socket by a link and the VMM connects by
path), with I7's rm clause and I12 for the effect; the second order of S-F39 and the lockless boot of PARKED line
24. ATTACKER: guest root of a mount session that the operator starts while a `workcell pull` or diff runs, in a
directory that holds the pull's temp directory, from a shell whose TMPDIR lies elsewhere: the precondition of C56's
second arm, against a pull in place of a run. SEVERITY: low (S6: hardening). WHERE: cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go: fetch
takes no lock, and boot records the pull's VMM directory in the pulled session's vmm file, whose lock the ended run
left free; cmd/workcell/data.go: holds refuses a directory that holds a VMM directory only for a session whose state
is running; cmd/workcell/session.go: running reads the lock; cmd/workcell/bench_vm.go: bench boots with no session
and records nothing (PARKED line 144). INPUT: terminal 1, with TMPDIR=~/work/tmp: `cd ~/proj && workcell pull`.
Terminal 2, with TMPDIR=/tmp: `cd ~/work && workcell run --mount -- claude`; holds refuses nothing, because the
pulled session reads as exited. The guest then finds the pull VM's sockets under /workspace/tmp. EFFECT, as claimed
by the auditor: the pull's firecracker.json and sockets are served live to the guest, whose unlink ends the pull at
its time limit and whose link sends the pull init's frames to a host socket it names; beside it, ls shows the pulled
session exited during the pull, rm removes its image while the VM holds it open, and a pull of a running session
attaches the live image read-write to a second VM. Reproducing test, by the redteam from the claim alone:
TestC63PullHoldsNoLock, package main of cmd/workcell, 40 lines, parked at escape/_pending/S-F46/c63_test.go. It
makes a session with a free lock and an image through c19Data, makes its inodes file a FIFO so that fetch parks
after it has chosen the session and before boot, asks running of that session at that moment, and then lets the pull
go on to boot, with a bound of 10 s. Run by the orchestrator by go test -overlay on the claim tree, plain and -race,
log saved: both fail with "running(...) = false, <nil> while a pull of ... runs between its session lookup and its
boot". Outcome: CONFIRMED at low by the verifier, with the effect narrowed. The state is real and lasts the whole
pull: no code but newSession takes the lock, so fetch holds none from newest to the close of its VM, and the FIFO
only parks it. Terminal 2 does start, by trace: holds refuses only a running session, the TMPDIR rule looks at
terminal 2's own temp directory, and boot's arm looks only for running mount sessions; and the pull's VMM directory
does lie under the export, made by MkdirTemp under terminal 1's TMPDIR and recorded. But the denial and the
redirection are not attainable by the guest: the mount session cannot already run when the pull boots (boot's arm
refuses the pull then), so it must start after the pull's MkdirTemp; the pull's init connects within about a second,
the accepted listener is closed and unlinked, and a pull-mode init runs no command and never dials the relay port,
so for the rest of the pull the mount guest finds a dead vsock, firecracker.json and an idle vsock_5000, and
unlinking or linking them denies nothing and redirects no frame. A second VM booted and its agent acting inside the
pull's own boot window is not a thing the attacker controls. So no invariant break is shown, and low stands; what
stands under R2 is operator-side: the pull's session reads exited in ls, rm during a pull takes the free lock and
removes the live VMM directory and the image that the VM holds open, and a mount session of a directory that holds
the pull's temp directory is admitted. The auditor's two probes showed holds returning nil for a directory that
holds a recorded VMM directory with a listening socket under a session whose lock is free, and running false while
fetch was parked. Not S14: cmd/workcell is v2's own, no v1 line. Fix unit: S-F46, below S-1013 in PLAN.md.

C63 FIXED by S-F46, commits d4b462a (the test moved) and 22d60b0 (the fix) (PR #296). fetch in pull_vm.go takes
the session's lock right after newest finds the session, before the image is looked at, the inodes file is read
or anything boots, and holds the descriptor until the pull or diff ends. lockSession in session.go, new, opens
sessions/<id>/lock, flocks it as the caller asks, turns a held lock into the one line "session <id> is running:
workcell stop <id> first", and only once it holds the lock truncates the file and writes its own pid there, so
the pid in the file is always the present holder's and stop signals the pull, whose fetch already ends in order
on a signal. holdSession is lockSession with a blocking LOCK_EX and no O_EXCL, and removeSession takes the lock
by lockSession too, so rm records its pid while it removes. So during a pull or diff ls shows the session
running, rm refuses it, holds refuses a mount session of a directory that holds its VMM directory, a second
pull or diff is refused, and a pull or diff of a session whose run still holds the lock is refused in that one
line before signal.Notify, any VMM directory and any line in the vmm file; an rm that wins the window between
newest and the lock leaves the pull failing closed on the missing lock or image. After the pull the file holds
the pull's pid with no holder, which nothing reads, since supervisor is asked only while running is true. Net 0
product lines: five in fetch and the helper, paid by running's switch as one if, removeSession's open and switch
as the helper's call, and the pid write nested in the lock's success branch: product 15000 of 15000, test 28496
of 28500, no test line. The test moved with its head comment changed, 40 lines; escape/_pending/ is gone.

## S-1002, sweep 3: host-guest channel, guest init, supervisor lifecycle (I7, I10, I12), as built at main b87f8bd

Sweep 3 (S8), the last the SPEC allows, fresh context (S3), the whole surface read as built after S-F1 to S-F46, not a
diff. Auditor on the top tier in the cloud session, which has no hypervisor; what needs a VM runs on the unit's pull
request. The auditor wrote its own trust boundary before it opened any earlier record.

Trust boundary. The supervisor (`workcell run`, `pull`, `diff`, `bench`; the operator's uid) owns the VM child
(Firecracker, Pdeathsig SIGKILL, Setpgid, the forking thread's CPU affinity cut to --cpus), the in-process proxy, resolver
and broker, the audit log and host key, the session directory, the data directory's layer markers (through
installer.fail), the operator's terminal in raw mode, the pull destination and the mount export (each held as a
descriptor). Attacker bytes enter at six points. (1) vsock 5000, one connection (once): wire frames (6-byte header,
version 1, length at most 64 KiB checked before allocation, 5 s per frame once begun, read through bufio, every error
sticky); Stdout and Stderr coalesced and paced to the seat, Ack (4 bytes), Exit (2 to 257 bytes, Err printed %q), and on
pull Entry, Data and Exit through manifest.add, checkPath, fold, put (openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH and NO_SYMLINKS beneath the
destination descriptor) and compare; what they can change: the exit code, terminal bytes, the `first` flag that drives
installer.fail only inside fresh, and bytes under the destination. (2) vsock 5001, many connections (1024 slots on the
host, 1023 in Firecracker): a 20-byte header within 5 s, then TCP bytes to the proxy or a 2-byte-framed DNS query to the
resolver; what they can change: audit Notes (soft 8 MiB) and dials to allowlisted names. (3) vsock 5002 under --mount
only, one connection: raw FUSE requests to internal/fileserve (16 workers, 4096 descriptors, 2^17 nodes, growth charged
to --disk). (4) The serial console, through a paced pipe into a 4 KiB tail, printed sanitised only when a boot fails.
(5) Guest-written disks: workspace.ext4 (never mounted on the host, booted again for pull), rw caches (attached to later
guests only by the operator's own --cache), tmpfs (guest RAM). (6) The repository: exported by a descriptor walk, its
cwd judged by holds and within and then compared by named() against ".", which is what is used. Host-written and out of
the guest's reach: lock (pid), repo, vmm, inodes, the markers, the attach socket (0700 directory, same uid),
firecracker.json and the kernel command line. No file of this surface carries `// Ported from v1` (the markers are in
internal/proxy/{proxy,terminate,allowlist}.go, internal/secret/{broker,source}.go, internal/audit/lines.go and three
tests), so nothing here falls under S14.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: readFrame clears the deadline only when nothing is buffered, arms it once at the
first read that must wait, refuses a length over 64 KiB before allocating and never resyncs; guest.DecodeExit, Ack and
Entry, relay.Decode and ReadFrame, resolver.question and fileserve.parse are bounded and round-trip; 20 s fuzz bursts on
wire FuzzReadFrame (2.6M execs), guest FuzzDecode (1.6M), fileserve FuzzRequest (377k), relay FuzzDecode (2.0M) and
FuzzReadFrame (3.2M) and cmd/workcell FuzzPath (272k), no crasher. The channel's CPU is paced (S-F34); the relay's and
the resolver's cost per stream is bound by Firecracker's connect rate on the pinned cores; the one unpaced guest
connection is the FUSE stream (C64). Memory per guest frame is one payload; the pull manifest is bounded by MaxEntries,
MaxNames and the image's size plus a block per inode; the console tail cannot grow. Logic and state: output() ends on
Exit, a bad Ack or an unknown type and flushes held output before any frame of another kind, so an Exit keeps its place
(probe: Stdout then Exit in one write arrive in order); `first` is true only for the guest's first frame and fail acts
only while fresh pairs this start's install with what it replaced (TestFail, c43, c60); session() orders holds, the
--mount TMPDIR rule, named(), newSession, Export(".") and boot; boot refuses a TMPDIR under a running mount session's
repo before MkdirTemp; the init's serve loop halts on anything a host never sends; pull's manifest, data, end sequence
is strict and charges apparent sizes, so a sparse file in a hostile image cannot pass the cap. Concurrency and
check-to-use: once closes the listener after the first accept; the seat mutex covers send against sit; the channel has
one writer goroutine; named() closes C61's rename swap and Export walks and reads beneath one descriptor with a device,
inode and size check; lockSession writes the pid only once it holds the lock and a pull holds it for its life (S-F46);
the windows that remain (a mount session the operator starts between another session's MkdirTemp and its recordBoot,
stop's pid reuse within milliseconds, two sessions in one nanosecond with the same 32 random bits) are operator-timed or
chance, not attacker-timed. Cryptography and identity: none on the channel by design (the VM is the identity, and the
first connection to 5000 is the init's because no guest code runs before Exec); the session CA goes to the guest as the
public certificate only, capped at 16 KiB; the audit key stays under the data directory, which holds() keeps out of every
export in both directions and by inode (S-F35). Failure modes: every exit from boot runs closeAll (kill, close,
RemoveAll); session_end is recorded after the VM is gone; an export failure removes the session directory; named()
refuses when either stat fails; running() returns any flock error but EWOULDBLOCK; the file service against a guest that
never reads its replies ends in 5.0 s with every descriptor closed (probe); a partial next header after a Stdout frame
holds that output 5.0 s and then ends the session 125 (probe; self-harm). No error path fails open. Downgrade, rollback
and replay: no sequence numbers by design; frames after Exit are never read; the fresh-window first-frame rollback is the
accepted C2 residual, unchanged; apply skips the failed digest until the pin changes and `update --to` restores from
disk. Interaction between surfaces: Exec carries placeholders and the CA only (I5, I6); the pull VM boots with no
allowlist, no layers and no caches, its relay denies every header and its resolver answers nothing; a crafted image's
inputs to the init (names holding "/", 4096-byte link targets, a tree listed child before parent) end at the host's
checkPath, DecodeEntry and dirBeneath; a mount guest on an ancestor can rename the operator's cwd (C61 and C62, fixed)
and can still steer pull, log and attach among the operator's own sessions by the spelling of the repo, with the
destination always the operator's directory by descriptor inside that guest's own export.

Refuted by the auditor before any candidate was raised: a partial header after a Stdout frame (the held output arrives
after 5 s and the session ends; the guest hurts only itself); a FUSE flood whose replies are never read (Serve returns at
the 5 s write deadline with no descriptor left); the Ack window (an input-side stall only, as sweep 1 showed); a TMPDIR
through a link and `..` (within passes, but Listen and encode clean the same `..`, the sockets are bound under a
directory that does not exist, the boot fails closed and closeAll removes what MkdirTemp made; reasoned from the code);
the findLayers markers `.`, `..` and `/` (no section-2 attacker can write a marker while holds() keeps the data
directory out of every export; the one route is a data directory bind-mounted beneath cwd, S-1003's deferred variant of
C52, not raised here); sessions keyed by the spelling of cwd (a mount guest that swaps sibling names makes pull, log,
verify and attach answer for another of the operator's sessions, but pull writes into the operator's cwd by descriptor
inside that guest's own export, so it gains nothing it cannot write itself: no invariant, R3); sparse files in a hostile
image; crafted dirent names with "/" or NUL; time.After per pull frame (collected unreferenced since Go 1.23); a mount
guest swapping a subdirectory for a link during the export (S-F44's check refuses); session()'s non-Exit returns (the
process exits and the deferred restore runs); a kernel command line cut short by many forward ports (fewer ports, never
more); rw caches shared across sessions (the flag's own contract); a relay DNS flood with recorded refusals (bounded by
the soft limit and the pinned connect rate). C2, C4, C5, C50 and C51 are unchanged or fixed and are not raised again.

Evidence gaps, not findings (PARKED.md holds them, R3). The enforced I10 disk-flood row judges the guest's overlay root
