### S-1002 candidates, sweep 3

C64. ID I10 (host CPU), the C51 class on the one guest connection S-F34 left unpaced: the file service of a `--mount`
session; A1 in that the host relies on the init to shape that traffic. Attacker: guest root in a `--mount` session, by
hostile model output or a malicious repository's hook running as the agent; the precondition it does not control is that
the operator chose `--mount`. Where: internal/fileserve/serve_linux.go Serve (ReadFrame, parse, a slot of `sem` and a
`wg.Go` goroutine per request, send under one mutex with one write per reply), started by `go serveMount(...)` in
cmd/workcell/run_vm.go inside the supervisor, which the --cpus bound and the S-F3 affinity pin do not cover; output() in
the same file paces port 5000 at paceFrames per paceEvery and Serve paces nothing. Input: as a command in a `--mount`
session, pidfd_getfd on pid 1 for the socket whose peer is CID 2 port 5002, keep the one vCPU at its cap, and write 64 KiB
batches of whole frames for 3 s, ending on a frame boundary: 54-byte frames that carry a FUSE INTERRUPT request (wire
header 1, 1, length 48; fuse_in_header length 48, opcode 36, a rising unique, nodeid 1; 8 bytes of argument), which takes
no reply. Effect claimed: the supervisor spends host CPU above --cpus for as long as the flood lasts, on a session capped
at one vCPU. Auditor's evidence, host side only and without a VM (the real Serve against a child process flooding a unix
socket, 3 s an arm, a 4-core box): 10-byte frames that parse refuses 6.1M a second at 1.40 cores; INTERRUPT 1.07M a second
at 2.04; FORGET 0.93M at 2.10; ACCESS, GETATTR, STATFS, LOOKUP and READLINK 176k to 180k a second at 1.79 to 1.90; a
flood whose replies are never read ends at the 5 s write deadline, so the flood must use an opcode without a reply or
drain. Severity claimed: low, by the precedent of C51 (an overrun bounded near the server's own goroutines, not
exhaustion). Reproducing test: the escape row I10 mount-cpu-flood, written by the redteam from the claim alone (commit
774549b on the unit's pull request): a `fuse-flood` kind of channelProbe beside frame-flood, interrupt() for the frame
(pinned by a line of TestFrame), a `Files` method on the adapters (workcell: vsock:2:5002; control: its channel, where the
naive host skips the type), the existing cpuJudge with its 1.0 s slack unchanged, Want cappedLive. Paid by 26 folded
lines under escape/ (21 pairs of rows in tests.go, one map and two var runs); the list of rows is main's 145 plus this
one, by the orchestrator's compare. T2 on control, run by the redteam in the cloud session: fail, the host spent 11.3 CPU
seconds in 3.0 s of wall time while the guest, capped at 1 CPU, loaded it (allowed 4.0; 718096 frames of 54 bytes, 36
MiB, in 3 s). Hosted gate on 774549b, a real VM (log line 283): fail, the host spent 5.3 CPU seconds in 3.4 s of wall
time while the guest, capped at 1 CPU, loaded it (allowed 4.4; the host took 2754723 frames of 54 bytes, 141 MiB, on the
init's connection in 3 s); beside it under the same judge on the same runner cpu-flood 3.5 in 3.3 s, device-cpu-flood
3.5 in 3.3 s and channel-cpu-flood, the paced port 5000, 2.6 in 3.4 s; passed 145, failed 1, errors 0. Outcome:
CONFIRMED, low, by the verifier from that log and its own run: about 1.8 CPU seconds of excess over the neighbouring
rows, roughly half a host core above the guest's cap, is tied to the frames' handler and not to noise, to the vCPU (the
judge's busy ticks leave guest time out) or to the VMM (its thread is pinned); a local overlay test of the real Serve
against a unix socket gave 15.5M INTERRUPT frames at 276 ns a frame and 1.43 cores of process CPU, against 6 ns a frame
for a bare reader; the cause is that every INTERRUPT, which handle answers with nothing, still takes a slot of sem and a
goroutine, and Serve has no pacing. The attacker is in scope (pidfd_getfd on pid 1 needs only CAP_SYS_PTRACE; the harness
passing the address is convenience, not power; the row writes whole frames only). It is not a break of I10's text: Serve
is one sequential reader with at most 16 short workers, so the overrun is bounded near one core whatever the rate; and
--mount is a precondition the attacker does not control, so S6 would cap it at medium even if a break were shown. S6: low,
no demonstrated break; S7 lists it. The verifier's reservation: the hosted log holds no control run, so T2 rests on the
redteam's run above, not on the log. Fix unit: S-F47, below S-1002 in PLAN.md: pace Serve's loop as output() paces its
own (count frames and sleep the rest of paceEvery after each paceFrames), or answer an INTERRUPT and a refused frame
before a slot and a goroutine are taken; two or three product lines, to be paid by folds, since product stands at 15000
of 15000. The auditor's lowest-level pin, not written (test budget): 2M ten-byte frames over a unix socket must take
Serve about paceEvery x 2M / paceFrames rather than the 0.3 s they take now. Variants not expressed (redteam, budget):
16-byte frames with a 10-byte payload, refused as short; a second connection to port 5002; FORGET and BATCH_FORGET
floods, which take the server's write lock; the file service and the channel flooded at once; INTERRUPTs whose unique
names a request of the init in flight. The row and fuseFlood wait in escape/_pending/S-F47/mountcpuflood.go (commit
a3e2262, on the same pull request); the fuse-flood kind of channelProbe, interrupt() with its line of TestFrame and
the adapters' Files stay live, since nothing runs them without the row; test code stands at 28500 of 28500. Not S14: no
file involved is ported, and none is someone else's project.

C64 FIXED by S-F47, commits 4d2caec (the test moved), fc93985 (the fix) and 00bc7f8 (the review's fix round) (PR #300).
Serve in internal/fileserve/serve_linux.go now paces its own loop as output() paces port 5000: it reads at most
paceFrames (1024) requests a paceEvery (64 ms), 16 thousand a second, and sleeps the rest of the period, whatever the
frame is: a wrong type, a short payload, a refused request or a served one. An INTERRUPT is settled on the reader with
nothing, and a FORGET or BATCH_FORGET on the reader by s.forget, before a slot of sem and a goroutine are taken; a
BATCH_FORGET counts one toward the pace for every perForget (64) entries it carries, so a 64 KiB frame of 4093 entries
counts as 64 requests. handle lost its two arms that answered nothing and always returns a reply. Paid in product lines
by folds that change no behaviour (errno's switch as one condition, closeFD on one line, one joined comment): product
stays at 15000 of 15000. Evidence. T2 on control, the redteam in the cloud session after the move: fail, 11.1 CPU seconds
in 3.0 s, allowed 4.0. Hosted gate on a real VM, the row I10 mount-cpu-flood: on fc93985 pass, 2.9 CPU seconds in 3.5 s
of wall time, allowed 4.5, 792089 frames of 54 bytes taken in 3 s; on 00bc7f8 pass, 3.3 CPU seconds in 3.5 s, allowed
4.5, 52159 frames taken in 3 s, beside cpu-flood and device-cpu-flood at 3.5 and channel-cpu-flood at 2.9; passed 146,
failed 0, errors 0 on both, the seven mount rows among them; before the fix the same row failed at 5.3 in 3.4 s (774549b).
The review, one round, found the first fix too narrow, twice, both I10 and low, both measured on the real Serve over a
unix socketpair with a child process flooding for 3 s: at 256 thousand requests a second the pace bound only frames that
take no reply, since replied requests (STATFS, GETATTR, ACCESS, drained in bulk) saturate at about 190 thousand a second
and cost 1.72 cores, as on main; and a maximal BATCH_FORGET was paced by the frame while it costs by the entry, 1.52
cores at 9 thousand frames a second. The fix round lowered the pace and counted the entries. Server CPU in cores, main,
then fc93985, then 00bc7f8: INTERRUPT 1.81, 0.08, 0.01; short refused frames 1.25, 0.07, 0.01; BATCH_FORGET 1.80, 1.52,
0.06; STATFS 1.72, 1.72, 0.17; a refused request answered EINVAL 1.28, 0.68, 0.06; FORGET, fc93985 then 00bc7f8, 0.10,
0.01. The first two columns are the reviewer's runs and the last the builder's, on the same harness and the same 4-core
box; no reviewer ran the last column, since R1 allows one round. At 32 thousand a second replied requests still cost
1.03 to 1.09 CPU seconds in 3.25 s, above the judge's second of slack, so 16 thousand is the highest power of two that
holds. Honest traffic, by ADR-005's measurements on a VM: 2.2 to 5.7 thousand requests a second (a 10,100-entry walk, a
serial GETATTR floor of 208 us, a 100 MiB read at 5.7 thousand READs a second). Lowest-level test (T6): TestPace in
internal/fileserve/bounds_linux_test.go, the auditor's pin: eight periods of ten-byte refused frames, eight periods of
64 KiB BATCH_FORGETs, then a STATFS, whose reply must not come before 16 periods (1.024 s) have passed, a lower bound
only; it fails on main's Serve at 19 ms and on fc93985's at 913 ms, and passes at 00bc7f8 at 1.03 s, with -race too.
FuzzRequest ran 20 s with no crasher, three times. Residual, not shown on a VM: the bound for replied requests,
BATCH_FORGET and refused frames rests on TestPace and the host-side figures above, because the suite's one row floods
INTERRUPT alone; a four-vCPU guest running stat calls in parallel could, by ADR-005's floor, reach about 19 thousand
requests a second and would be held near 16 thousand (PARKED.md, the S-F47 line).

Sweep 3 verdict for this surface: one candidate, confirmed at low (C64), nothing at medium or above. It gets a fix unit
(S-F47), as the lows of sweeps 1 and 2 did. No model declined and no safeguard re-ran a request in the audit, the redteam
or the verifier, and no tool permission was refused to any of them.

## S-1003, sweep 3: VM configuration and device model, Linux and macOS backends (I1, I4, A7), as built at main 2843fad

Sweep 3 (S8), the last the SPEC allows, fresh context (S3), the whole surface read as built after S-F1 to S-F47, not a
diff. Auditor on the top tier in the cloud session, which has no hypervisor; nothing of this audit needed a VM. The
auditor wrote its own trust boundary before it opened any earlier record.

Trust boundary. Attacker bytes enter this surface by five routes. (1) The guest's use of the devices the host hands it:
virtio-blk requests to the root drive (read-only), the workspace image (read-write, the session's own), layer drives
(read-only) and cache drives (read-only, or read-write by the operator's `--cache NAME:rw`); AF_VSOCK connects to CID 2
at any port, which Firecracker turns into connect(2) on `<Dir>/vsock_<port>` (only 5000, 5001 and 5002 exist, and 5000
and 5002 take one connection through `once`) and vz into a registered listener; bytes on the serial console, read
through a paced blocking pipe into a 4 KiB tail and printed only sanitised when a boot fails; the guest's reboot, panic
and halt (reboot=k and panic=-1 end Firecracker; a 2 s Ping ends a restarted vz guest). (2) The guest-written images the
host attaches again later: workspace.ext4 to the pull guest, read-write caches to later guests by the operator's own
flag; the host never mounts or parses either. (3) The repository the operator runs in: its names, links, hard links,
FIFOs, sockets and sizes enter workspace.Export (clone) by a descriptor walk and the file service (mount) by its
(handle, name) grammar, and the pull's tree enters write and put through openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH and RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS
beneath the destination. (4) Host-written inputs the guest cannot touch: firecracker.json (0600 in a 0700 MkdirTemp
directory), the kernel command line (integers, fixed words, compiled-in provider names, cache names of a fixed alphabet,
uint16 ports), the drive paths under the data directory and sessions/<id>/, the markers, lock, repo, vmm and inodes
files. (5) The operator's environment (TMPDIR, XDG_*, HOME, flags): trusted, but the product refuses layouts that would
show its own state to a guest (holds, the TMPDIR rules), and the earlier verifiers treated an operator-made second name
of such a directory as a precondition the attacker does not control (C52). Authority: the supervisor runs as the
operator's uid with write access to the data directory, TMPDIR and cwd, execs `<data>/firecracker` by absolute path with
Pdeathsig SIGKILL, Setpgid and the forking thread's CPU mask cut to --cpus, and holds the export's descriptors and the
proxy; the Firecracker child (same uid, default seccomp, no jailer, no rlimit) holds the drive files and the sockets; on
macOS the VM runs inside the entitled supervisor and Apple's helper. Invariants held up here: I1 and I4 (sockets and
drives), I7 (per-session directories, locks, cleanup, read-only layers), I9 and I13 (the data and config directories
kept out of every export), I10 (affinity, mem_size_mib, image size, console pacing, connection caps), I12 (console
bytes, the 20 s boot limit), A2, A7 (six methods), A9. No file of this surface carries `// Ported from v1`, and nothing
here is a weakness in someone else's project, so nothing falls under S14.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: no parser of guest bytes lies on this surface (encode is json.Marshal of host
strings; the init parses the host-written /proc/cmdline, tested in root_test.go; the console goes to a bounded tail; the
vz state is an enum). CPU is bounded on Linux by pin() (TestPin) and on the console by the paced blocking pipe; on vz
the console copy is unpaced and I10 is not enforced there (already parked, unchanged). Memory is mem_size_mib plus
Firecracker's bounded vsock buffers (1023 connections) and the relay's 1024 slots; disk is the fixed sparse image (tree
plus --disk) and the file service's charged growth. A probe confirmed by execution what two earlier records only
reasoned: os.MkdirTemp hands TMPDIR to the kernel uncleaned while filepath.Join cleans `link/..`, so the socket path of
a TMPDIR through a link and `..` names a directory that does not exist and the boot fails closed. Logic and state: drive
order and the init's letters agree on both backends (encode and configure against layerArgs and cacheArgs; TestConfig,
TestLayerArgsAndPath, TestCacheArgsAndEnv); `once` takes one connection and unlinks (TestOnceTakesOneConnection);
findLayers refuses a marker that is not a bare name; openCaches stats, locks, creates under a temporary name and
renames; Firecracker's is_root_device adds a second `root=/dev/vda ro`, which the init's last-wins value() reads the
same. Concurrency and check-to-use: Listen before Start under the mutex; the Pdeathsig thread is locked for the child's
life; the operator-timed window between another session's MkdirTemp and its recordBoot is unchanged; the direction that
S-F35's inode walk does not cover, the data directory's inode beneath the working directory, is C65 below. Cryptography
and identity: none by design; the vsock peer is the VMM by the 0700 directory and the per-VM device; CID 3 on every VM
is harmless. Failure modes: every exit from boot runs closeAll; an export failure removes the session directory; Start
refuses when the affinity cannot be read; vz Close waits on exited only after a Stop the guest cannot make fail; nothing
fails open, and C65 is a check that no code performs rather than one that fails. Downgrade, rollback and replay: not
applicable to the device model; the markers are host-written; the pull guest boots the image with no network, layers or
caches. Interaction between surfaces: C19, C28, C29, C52, C56, C61 and C63 traced again in the code as built, with their
tests green; pull's openat2 masks lack RESOLVE_NO_XDEV, so a bind mount beneath the destination is crossed, and the file
service's child() opens directories with a plain Openat (both part of C65's chain); vz storage attachments pass readOnly
straight to the framework (read in the module cache, as data).

Refuted by the auditor before any candidate was raised: a TMPDIR through a link and `..` (fails closed, now by
execution: MkdirTemp makes the directory at the kernel's path while Listen, encode's uds_path and firecracker.json are
joined at the cleaned path, which does not exist, so Start fails and closeAll removes what was made; on vz the attach
socket's Listen fails the same way); the vz console copy (parked, I10 is not enforced on macOS); Go runtime threads
cloned from the pinned thread inheriting the --cpus mask (it only tightens the bound; no invariant); the window between
MkdirTemp and recordBoot (operator-timed); the second `root=` argument (last wins); a command line cut short by many
--cache flags or ports (operator-controlled, Firecracker refuses an overlong one closed); drive letters past z (the init
mounts less, never more); the findLayers markers `.`, `..` and a link (they need a writer in the data directory, which
only C65's layout gives, so they are part of its chain); vz Close blocking after a failed Stop (the guest cannot cause
it); console floods on Firecracker (the pipe fills and the guest's own vCPU blocks); CID 3, no entropy device on
Firecracker and no rlimits on the child (as the earlier records left them; the bounds are Firecracker's own limits and
the pin); reflinked workspace images (copy-on-write, the repository's blocks are never written); the export of a
repository that holds another running session's VMM directory (holds() refuses it by the vmm record); a pull guest with
a nil audit log (append and Close take a nil receiver); attach dialling the first vmm line after a pull appended a
second (no invariant).

Evidence gaps, not findings (PARKED.md holds what a retro must weigh, R3). No row proves from inside a guest that a
Firecracker layer drive is attached read-only. The vz console copy is unpaced and I10 is unmeasured on the Mac. ADR-001
names rlimits on the VMM child and the backend sets none. No code path installs or verifies vmlinux, initrd.cpio,

### S-1003 candidates, sweep 3

C65. ID I7, I9 and I13 through the holds() rule of C19 and C29 (S-F12, S-F21, S-F35); I1 in mount mode; I14 and A6
through the VMM binary and the layer markers. It is the variant of C52 that S-F35's reviewer found and that sweep 2
deferred to this audit for a test and a verifier of its own (S1, S4). Attacker: guest root, by hostile model output or a
malicious repository's hook running as the agent, in a clone session followed by the operator's `workcell pull`, or in a
`--mount` session; the precondition it does not control is the operator's layout. Where: cmd/workcell/data.go holds()
and within(), called by session() in run_vm.go and by fetch() in pull_vm.go for the destination; within() relates the
data directory's ancestors to the working directory by spelling and by inode and never finds the data directory's inode
beneath the working directory. The readers that then cross the mount: internal/workspace/workspace.go, whose walk
descends by Openat and skips only the image's own inode; internal/fileserve/serve_linux.go child(), a plain Openat with
O_NOFOLLOW; cmd/workcell/pull_linux.go, whose openat2 masks hold RESOLVE_BENEATH and RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS and not
RESOLVE_NO_XDEV. Input: the operator's layout has the data directory bind-mounted beneath the working directory (`mount
--bind "$XDG_DATA_HOME/workcell" /repo/data`, by fstab, a dev-container volume or sudo; bindfs gives the same without
root), then `cd /repo && workcell run -- <agent>`. A bind mount is not a symlink, so holds() passes. Clone mode: the
guest reads /workspace/data/audit.key, every sessions/<id>/audit.log and the images, and leaves a tree that holds
data/firecracker (its own program), data/sessions/<id>/audit.log (rewritten and sealed with the key) and
data/layers/<agent>/current naming an image of its own; the operator runs `workcell pull`, whose put() opens `data`
beneath the destination and replaces each file. Mount mode: the guest writes the same files live. Effect claimed: the
guest reads the audit key and every other session's record and image (I7, I9), rewrites records that `verify` still
accepts (I9), replaces the layer markers and images a later session boots from (I7, I14, A6) and, through pull or
--mount, replaces the VMM binary that the next `workcell run` execs as the operator; the config directory aliased the
same way gives the guest the next session's policy (I13). Auditor's evidence, without a VM: an overlay probe of the real
session(), holds() and write() with c19_test.go's dummy artifacts, both arms, in 0.03 s; and a fix-shape overlay
(RESOLVE_NO_XDEV in the three masks of pull_linux.go and in the export walker's directory open) under which the clone
and pull arms are refused with EXDEV and every other cmd/workcell and workspace test stays green. Severity claimed:
medium by S6's letter and the standard C52 was confirmed at, with the auditor's own caveat that the layout is rarer than
C52's and that an operator who mounts the product's state directory inside a repository could be read as having put it
there, which would make it low; the ruling was left to the verifier.

Reproducing test: TestC65DataDirectoryBindMountedBeneathCwd, a cmd/workcell package test (tag linux, 72 lines) written
by the redteam from the claim alone and parked at escape/_pending/S-F48/c65_test.go (commit 535cab8 on the unit's pull
request). Where the process is not root it re-runs itself under sudo -n as c52_test.go does and skips only where sudo
asks for a password; root is used once, for the bind mount that models the operator's layout. Two arms, clone and mount:
c19Data's artifacts under a fresh XDG_DATA_HOME, the data directory bound at repo/data, a chdir into repo, then
session(); each arm wants a refusal that names the data directory, nothing made in the data directory (c19Untouched), no
vmm record and no workspace.ext4 that holds the other session's record or the key's bytes; then write() beneath repo
with a judged guest tree that names data/firecracker and data/sessions/<the other id>/audit.log, and both host files
must be unchanged. It calls the pull writer directly, since fetch cannot reach it without a VM. On the current tree, by
go test -overlay as root in the cloud session, plain and with -race, run by the redteam, by the orchestrator (the saved
logs) and by the verifier: both arms fail. Clone: "session returned start firecracker: invalid argument, want a refusal
naming .../001/workcell, of which .../003/data is a second name"; audit.key minted and a session directory made inside
the directory the guest gets; "the session reached boot: .../vmm was written"; "workspace.ext4, the guest's /workspace,
holds the other session's audit log or the bytes of .../audit.key (I7, I9)"; "after the pull writer (<nil>),
.../workcell/firecracker holds "GUEST" ... not "dummy firecracker"" and the same for the other session's audit.log.
Mount: the same lines without the image. This run on the unfixed tree is the test's T2 showing: a package test has no
control adapter. No mount and no scratch directory was left behind. The 72 lines were paid by 70 joined comment lines in
33 files under escape/suite, escape/sandbox and escape/cmd/payload (every changed line is a `// ` line; tests.go is
untouched; the list of rows is main's 146); test code stands at 28491 of 28500 and product at 15000 of 15000.

Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, who ran the test as root on 535cab8 (both arms fail in 0.07 s, as in the
saved logs) and traced the real pull path, since the test calls write() directly: in fetch(), holds(dest) passes exactly
as the session arm shows; the TMPDIR rule does not fire for a data directory under the home directory; named() passes;
the guest's /workspace holds data/ because the export walk skips only the image's own inode and descends into the bind
mount; checkPath refuses only absolute and empty names, `.`, `..` and a `.git` component, so data/firecracker and
data/sessions/<id>/audit.log pass the judge (the test applies the same add); put() opens `data` by openat2 without
RESOLVE_NO_XDEV, unlinks the host's file and creates the guest's. No manifest or digest check guards the VMM binary on
this path, so I14 falls as a consequence and the next `workcell run` execs the guest's bytes as the operator. The mount
arm proves only that the session reaches boot; the live view crossing the mount is from the code (child()'s Openat has
no mount check), the standard C52 was confirmed at; fetch() refuses a mount session, so the pull half is clone mode's
alone, as claimed. The test takes no power the attacker lacks: the forged entries and bytes are guest root's own, and
the direct call to write() skips nothing that would refuse this layout. Scope: section 2 excludes host root as the
attacker and malware as the operator, not the operator's own mount tooling; the precondition is of the class of C19, C28
and C52, all confirmed at medium. Not high: the layout is the operator's and rare. Not low: I7 and I9 are shown broken
(another session's record overwritten; the key in the guest image lets it seal a rewritten log), and holds() exists to
refuse this class. Not S14: data.go, pull_vm.go, pull_linux.go, workspace.go and serve_linux.go are v2's own, nothing
ported, and no other project's weakness is involved.

Fix unit: S-F48, below S-1003 in PLAN.md. The test asks for two things. First, session() must refuse the layout before
anything is made in the data directory, with an error that names the data directory: a check in holds() that finds a
mount point beneath the directory, by /proc/self/mountinfo on Linux (the reviewer's and the auditor's option; refusing
every mount point beneath cwd also refuses a benign one such as a tmpfs node_modules, so the builder weighs refusing
only a mount whose root is the same file as the data or config directory, one of its ancestors or, by the mount's device
and root field, something beneath it). Second, the pull writer must not cross a mount point beneath the destination:
RESOLVE_NO_XDEV in the masks of pull_linux.go, which costs no new line and was probed. The same mask on the export
walker's directory open and on the file service's child() would also close a mount made after holds() judged, at about 8
and 3 lines; the auditor probed the walker and reasoned the file service. macOS has no unprivileged mechanism that gives
a directory a second name beneath another, and its firmlink direction is S-F35's, so vz stays as it is. An identity
check of (device, inode) in the walker alone would miss bindfs, whose device differs. Variants not expressed (redteam
and auditor; budget): the config directory aliased beneath cwd, where pull rewrites config.toml (I13); `workcell pull
<dest>` and `workcell diff` where the destination holds the alias and is not cwd; the reverse, cwd bind-mounted inside
the data directory; a running mount session's VMM or TMPDIR directory bind-mounted beneath cwd, where holds() reads the
vmm record's spelling only; a bindfs, overlayfs or FUSE alias whose inodes differ per mount; the layer markers `.`, `..`
and a link written through the alias; a mount made by a second process after holds() judged and before Export walks; the
macOS forms, which need the Mac.

Sweep 3 verdict for this surface: one candidate, C65, confirmed at medium. So sweep 3 has confirmed a finding at medium
or above, and S-1017 will mark itself `[!]` and stop the loop for the maintainer (S8); the fix unit S-F48 stands all the
same, since S7 wants every medium fixed before cutover. Sweep 3 so far: one medium (C65, open) and one low (C64, fixed).
No model declined and no safeguard re-ran a request in the auditor, the redteam or the verifier, and no tool permission
was refused to any of them.

C65 FIXED by S-F48, commits 02875a5 (the test moved) and af4909d (the fix) (PR #305). holds() in cmd/workcell/data.go
now reads /proc/self/mountinfo after its data and config refusal and before it reads the sessions, and refuses a
directory that holds any mount point strictly beneath it, for run's working directory and for pull's destination alike:
"<dir> holds a mount at <mount point>, which may be a second name of workcell's own directory <data directory> or of
another tree no session may see: unmount it or use another directory". The mount point is compared by prefix with the
resolved directory, after the kernel's octal escapes for a space, tab, newline and backslash are decoded. The builder
chose every mount point over only one whose root is workcell's own: a mount's root and device do not tell a bindfs,
overlayfs or FUSE alias apart, the pull writer can no longer write beneath a sub-mount in any case, and the wider
refusal also covers the unexpressed variants where the config directory, TMPDIR or a running session's VMM directory is
the tree mounted beneath the working directory. Its price is that a benign sub-mount, such as a tmpfs node_modules or a
volume inside the working tree, is refused by name; a working tree that is itself a mount point is not. macOS has no
such file, so nothing is listed and nothing refused there, which is the stub the unit asked for at no line. The three
openat2 masks of cmd/workcell/pull_linux.go carry RESOLVE_NO_XDEV, so put() stops with EXDEV at a mount point beneath
the destination and writes nothing through it. Paid by joined comment lines in data.go, pull_linux.go, run_vm.go,
session.go and cache_vm.go: product stays at 15000 of 15000, test at 28491 of 28500. The redteam's move kept the test at
72 lines and made a bind mount that fails with anything but EPERM fail the test, where before it fell through and ran
against no layout. Evidence. Before the fix, as root in the cloud session (redteam, orchestrator, and the reviewer in a
worktree of main): both arms fail, plain and -race, with the key minted, the session at boot, the image holding the
other session's record and the pull writer's bytes in the host's firecracker and the other session's audit.log. On
af4909d: both arms pass without skipping, plain and -race (builder, orchestrator, reviewer), with the C19, C28, C29 and
C52 tests and cmd/workcell, internal/workspace and internal/fileserve under -race; loop/gate.sh GATE PASS. Hosted on
af4909d: gate (288 s as a check, GATE PASS in 268 s, a real VM), gate-macos, gate-arm64 and guard green; the suite
passed 146, failed 0, errors 0, the six I1 mount rows, the two I10 mount rows and the seven I8 pull rows among them. The
hosted log runs go test without -v, so it shows the package line of cmd/workcell and not the test by name: that it did
not skip there rests on the same job's own passwordless sudo in its KVM step, the one condition under which the test
re-runs itself as root, where a failure of the child fails the test. The review, one round, had no finding; the reviewer
also probed a mount point with a space in its name, a working directory reached through a link and through "./", a
working directory that is itself a tmpfs (not refused), and the pull writer into a destination that is itself a mount
point (written) and at a sub-mount beneath it (EXDEV, nothing written). Not closed, and parked: the export walker and
the file service's child() still cross a mount made after holds() judged, since both open by plain openat and product
had no line for an openat2 there, and no section 2 attacker makes a host mount; the reverse layout, the working
directory mounted inside the data directory, passes holds() as before. Sweep 3 now stands at one medium (C65, fixed) and
one low (C64, fixed). Not S14: no file involved is ported, and none is someone else's project.

## S-1004, sweep 3: network path and proxy core: routing, SNI, ECH, connection handling, fail-closed behaviour (I2, I4, I11), as built at main fffe3b2

Sweep 3 (S8), the last the SPEC allows, fresh context (S3), the whole surface read as built after S-F1 to S-F48,
not a diff. Auditor on the top tier in the cloud session, which has no hypervisor; nothing of this audit needed
a VM. The auditor wrote its own trust boundary before it opened any earlier record.

Trust boundary. Guest root owns every byte of every vsock stream the guest opens to host port 5001: on Linux
Firecracker dials the unix socket vsock_5001 that the backend's Listen bound in the session's 0700 temporary
directory, on macOS vz's socket listener (backlog 16). First host code: serveRelay in cmd/workcell/relay.go (1024
slots), then stream: a 5 s deadline, io.ReadFull of exactly 20 bytes, relay.Decode (length 20, version 1, proto 6
or 17). Proto 17 with port 53, any address: relay.ReadFrame (a 2-byte length, at most 65535) then resolver.Answer
(S-1006 owns the parser; the relay path and its deadline are this audit's), one reply frame, close. Proto 6 to
a port in allow.Ports(): the deadline is lifted and the relayConn goes to that port's adapter, which proxy.Serve
takes (1024 slots of its own) into handle and route. A port other than 443 maps to forward[port] with no parsing at
all and a raw splice both ways with the dialled upstream. Port 443 runs peekSNI (the crypto/tls ClientHello parser
over a recording conn capped at 16 KiB under a 10 s deadline), refuses extension 0xfe0d, lower-cases the SNI with
a length check, requires membership of the allowlist, then hands every SNI host to serveTerminated (S-1005 owns
the HTTP judge; the hand-off and the leaf choice are this audit's): bind calls Terminate whenever any SNI host
exists, so 443 is never spliced in the product. Anything else closes the stream; a TCP header to an unserved port
is recorded as port_not_allowed. Guest root also controls the count, rate, timing and closing of streams and the
guest kernel's vsock behaviour. The network attacker owns the upstream bytes after the dial (raw back to the guest
on a forward port, parsed by net/http on 443) and the DNS answers for an allowed name as the host's resolver sees
them (net.DefaultResolver through /etc/resolv.conf and /etc/hosts); blockedAddr vets each answer against the netip
classes, blockedPrefixes and the host's interface prefixes. The operator, out of scope, chooses names and forward
ports; the repository can only narrow (S-1009). Authority: the supervisor `workcell run`, the operator's uid, one
process (A9) that holds the VMM child, the session CA key, the broker, the audit log and its key, and the session
directory. Its network authority is the host's: a plain net.Dialer to the vetted address and port; blockedAddr
and the allowlist are the whole fence (I2, I4). The resolve is LookupNetIP under 10 s of the rooted name; the
dial budget is 30 s shared across answers; one blocked answer refuses the host. The audit Note gates admission: a
failed Note means no dial and EOF to the guest (I9). Trusted without checking: crypto/tls's ClientHello parse and
ClientHelloInfo.Extensions on go1.27.4; the host kernel's and resolver's semantics; Firecracker and vz refusing a
guest connect to a host port with no listener (I11); netip's classification plus blockedPrefixes for every address
form; that the relay header's address is a hint for deny lines only and is never dialled. internal/proxy/proxy.go
carries `// Ported from v1`, so its candidate is an ordinary public one with a v1 line (SPEC section 13); nothing
here is a weakness in someone else's project, so nothing falls under S14's stop.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: the relay reads a fixed 20-byte array with ReadFull under an absolute 5 s deadline
before it allocates anything else, and Decode is total; the DNS frame is one allocation of at most 65535 bytes under
the same deadline; both have fuzz targets, run for 20 s each (FuzzDecode 2.58 million executions, FuzzReadFrame
2.33 million, no crasher). The ClientHello is read by crypto/tls on a recording conn capped at 16 KiB under a 10 s
deadline; a hello spread over tiny records, a 64 KiB record, plaintext, a truncation and an empty SNI are refused
(TestPeekSNI; FuzzPeekSNI 942 executions in 20 s, no crasher). A forward port is never parsed. Slots cap at 1024 on
the relay and 1024 on the proxy, and on Linux Firecracker's 1023-connection muxer keeps the relay below its cap;
per slot the host holds about 20 bytes, or 16 KiB plus crypto/tls input, or 64 KiB of io.Copy buffers, or about
69 KiB terminated (S-F6). The splice and the terminated keep-alive have no idle timeout by design, bounded by the
slots. Bytes read beyond the hello are in the recorded buffer and replayed. Logic and state: a port other than 443
routes to the forward map's one host; 443 by SNI, lower-cased with a length check so that no non-ASCII fold matches,
by exact set membership; crypto/tls rejects a trailing-dot SNI and duplicate server_name entries; the lowered name
is used for the leaf, the Rewrite and the record. The relay's served set equals allow.Ports(), which is also what
the init listens on. ParseAllowlist refuses IP literals, port 0, names that are not DNS names and two hosts on one
forward port. Address vetting: Unmap, IsGlobalUnicast, IsPrivate, IPv6 outside 2000::/3, the explicit list (0/8,
CGNAT, 192.0.0/24, 168.63.129.16/32, 2001::/23, 2002::/16, documentation, benchmarking, the 6to4 relay, 240/4,
2001:db8::/32, 3fff::/20) and every interface prefix of the host, read per connect; a zone-bearing answer is refused
as outside 2000::/3. C66 below is the one class this vetting cannot see. Concurrency and check-to-use: one lookup per
connection, every answer vetted before any dial, the dial by literal (TestConnectVetsEveryAnswerOnEveryConnection);
the terminated transport re-enters connect per upstream connection; the proxy's maps, transport and CA are written
in Terminate before any Serve goroutine starts; every relayConn is closed exactly once and frees its slot through
sync.Once; the nanosecond window between the relay's slot release and the proxy's stands as parked; a hot-plug of
an interface between nets() and the dial is microseconds and the attacker cannot time it. Cryptography and identity:
SNI is routing identity only; the leaf is issued for the lowered SNI under a CA with critical name constraints; ALPN
offers http/1.1 alone, so an h2-only client fails closed; Go checks the second ClientHello after a HelloRetryRequest
for an unchanged server name, so the routed and the terminated name cannot differ. ECH is refused by extension
type on the outer hello before any name is read, as sweeps 1 and 2 proved on go1.27; GREASE ECH clients get
no_sni. serveTerminated hands net/http a wrapper around the TLS conn, so r.TLS is nil in the handler and net/http
sets no handshake deadline of its own: nothing reads r.TLS, the handler takes the host from its closure, and the
handshake runs under ReadHeaderTimeout's deadline on the wrapped conn, so the 10 s bound holds. Failure modes: every
error path refuses. A deadline error or a failed peek is no_sni; a lookup error or an empty answer resolve_failed;
an unreadable interface list or one blocked answer blocked_address; a dial failure dial_failed; a failed replay
write a close; a failed Note half-closes, drains for at most 10 s and returns before any dial (S-F16). A nil log
refuses everything. serveRelay ends on any Accept error and closes every adapter, which ends every Serve loop;
after an EMFILE exit later guest connects wait in the listen backlog unanswered, closed and self-inflicted. I11:
proxy, resolver and broker are the supervisor; Firecracker dies with it by Pdeathsig on the locked thread, vz's
VM with the process; a closed 5001 listener is an unlinked socket that the muxer resets. No panic reachable from
guest bytes was found. Downgrade, rollback and replay: header version 1 only; TLS 1.2 at least on both sides;
a replayed stream is another connection that meets the same checks; the relay holds no state across streams; the
product caches no DNS answer and the transport pool reuses a connection only to the address it vetted; forward
ports are raw by the operator's own grant (I6 covers terminated connections only). Interaction between surfaces:
streams go to the proxy and DNS frames to the in-process resolver (S-1006); 443 to serveTerminated (S-1005);
every refusal and admission to the audit log (S-1010): past the soft limit every admission is refused and no
lookup is made, a loss of the guest's network and never a gain, which also bounds the host's DNS query rate by
the log cap. The sockets lie in the 0700 directory that S-F20, S-F21, S-F35 and S-F48 keep out of every export;
only vsock_5000, 5001 and 5002 exist, so a guest connect to any other port is reset.

Refuted by the auditor before any candidate was raised: a proxy shed without a record (each handle holds one
delivered stream, so handles never exceed the relay's slots; C8's refutation stands); serveRelay's exit on EMFILE
(fails closed, guest-only harm; Go raises the soft descriptor limit to the hard one at start); a forward entry on port
53 or 853 that lets DNS for any name leave to that server (the operator's own grant, the class of DoH to an allowed
443 host); a UDP header to a port other than 53 closed without a record (a datagram is not a connection attempt;
C14's intended behaviour); r.TLS nil on the terminated server (no reader, the bound comes from ReadHeaderTimeout);
a hairpin to the host's public NAT address (outside I4's list and reachable from the internet anyway); /etc/hosts
entries (a loopback or zone-bearing mapping of an allowed name is refused; a single-label name never matches
under the rooted lookup); pipelined or fragmented hellos (over-reads are replayed; a hello followed by junk is
reset after the server's first flight); interface addresses with host bits set (Prefix.Contains masks; a malformed
entry fails ParsePrefix and refuses everything); the guest filling the audit log or holding all 1024 slots idle
(self-harm inside the bounds); the spliced half-close that becomes a full close (a lost reply, no reach); a forward
host dialled at 443 (sni_not_allowed), port 0 in a header (no adapter), version 2 and proto 0 or 1 (closed at once);
the vz backlog of 16 and Firecracker's 1023-connection cap (both refuse before the relay's cap).

Earlier fixes on this surface, traced again in the code as built, all hold: C7 (S-F4: 168.63.129.16/32 in
blockedPrefixes, and blockedAddr unmaps first, with TestBlockedAddr's rows); C13 (S-F8: TLSHandshakeTimeout,
MaxConnsPerHost and IdleConnTimeout on the terminated transport, c13_test.go green, the shed and lost counters gone);
C23 and C24 (S-F16: handle acts only on a nil Note for the Allowed line, unrecorded_test.go on both paths); B-835
(the 16 KiB hello cap); C11 (S-F6: MaxHeaderBytes and ReadHeaderTimeout); C27 (S-F19: DisableGeneralOptionsHandler);
C30 and C53 (S-F22, S-F36: no relative SSL_CERT_FILE or SSL_CERT_DIR entry); S-F3's CPU pin of Firecracker. C8
refuted and C14 intended: both stand. C9 of sweep 1, left there as "not reproduced, reasoned only, low": raised
again as C66 with the reproduction it lacked. Row 22 of the S-1001 map still names the shed and lost counters that
S-F8 removed: stale text in the record only.

Coverage. Read in full: internal/proxy/{proxy,allowlist,terminate,signin}.go with the tests proxy, allowlist,
forward, clients, c10, c11, c12, c13, c15, c30, c53, unrecorded and terminate; internal/relay/relay.go and its test;

and cmd/workcell's relay tests on go1.27.4, all green; the three 20 s fuzz bursts; a two-namespace veth probe
of C66 (IPv4, a real dial, the canary in the neighbour's stack caught the bytes); a probe test of C66 under an

of /proc/net/route in the probe's own namespace. Every listener and namespace was the probe's own, nothing left

Evidence gaps, not findings (PARKED.md holds what a retro must weigh, R3). FuzzPeekSNI runs at about 45 executions a
second here (a TLS handshake over net.Pipe each), so S10's four hours cover about 650 thousand executions against about
110 thousand a second for the relay's fuzzers: the ClientHello parse rests on crypto/tls. relay-header-allowed-port
proves only that a name that does not resolve dials nothing; the proof that the header's address is never dialled
when the name resolves is the rebind rows'. The I11 rows kill the whole supervisor; no row covers a partial failure
(the relay loop returned, the proxy's Serve ended), and none proves that streams queued after one are refused and not
held. icmp-echo cannot fail on the product without a network device; there is no row with a native IPv6 destination;
the rebind rows take any question as proof of vetting. No row forwards port 53 or 853, and docs/policy.md does not
say that such a forward lets DNS for any name leave to that server. No row floods a forward port for host CPU or
holds all 1024 slots idle on a real VM.

### S-1004 candidates, sweep 3

C66. ID I4 ("The guest cannot reach host loopback, the LAN, link-local or cloud metadata addresses ... the vetted
address is the one dialled"). It is C9 of sweep 1, left there as "not reproduced, reasoned only, low", raised again
with the reproduction it lacked. Attacker: guest root, with the network attacker as the host's resolver for an
allowed name, the model of the rebind rows and of C7; the precondition it does not control is the host's network
layout. Where: internal/proxy/proxy.go, nets() (net.InterfaceAddrs alone), blockedAddr() and connect(), the only
gate before the dial. also in v1 main: egressproxy/proxy.go. Input: the host's interface holds its address with a
host-length prefix, a /32 (a point-to-point cloud NIC, a DHCP classless static route) or a /128 (a DHCPv6 address
with the router advertisement's on-link /64, the usual shape of a managed IPv6 network on Linux), and the prefix
around it is on-link only by a route; the policy allows one name, bare or as a forward port; the resolver answers
that name with the address of a neighbour on the link; the guest connects to the name. One answer suffices. Effect
claimed: nets() never reads the route table, so blockedAddr() does not know the neighbour; the proxy dials it from
the host's own address and relays the guest's bytes, raw on a forward port, and on 443 the TCP connect and the
ClientHello reach it, which the rebind rows' own standard counts as reach. Private, unique-local and link-local
neighbours stay refused by class, so the break needs a link in global unicast space: the usual IPv6 case, and IPv4
where the link holds public addresses. Auditor's evidence, without a VM: two network namespaces of its own joined
by a veth with no default route, the host side holding 192.175.48.1/32 with `192.175.48.0/25 dev vh scope link`,
the neighbour 192.175.48.2/25 with a canary on port 8443; in the host namespace the real nets(), blockedAddr()
and connect() under a test overlay gave nets() = [127.0.0.1/8 192.175.48.1/32], blockedAddr(192.175.48.2) = false,
and a dial that the canary in the neighbour's stack logged with the probe's token, from 192.175.48.1; on the same
run the host's own address and 10.0.0.1 were refused with nothing dialled, and 192.175.48.129, off the link,
was dialled as a public address must be. IPv6 at the function level only, since the session's kernel has none:
blockedAddr(2620:4f:8000::2) with the interface prefix 2620:4f:8000::1/128 is false. The auditor also showed the
distinction that sweep 1 said no test could draw: /proc/net/route lists the main table's unicast on-link route and
none of the local table's rows, so the suite's canary address (a local route to an address off every interface)
and a neighbour on the link can be told apart. Severity claimed: medium by S6.

Reproducing test: the row `I4 rebind-on-link-neighbour-forward`, written by the redteam from the claim alone (commit
033c9b7 on the unit's pull request), a sibling of rebind-host-network-forward with `Want: rebindingOnLink`. The
Linux isolate gives the session's namespace the claimed layout, 192.175.48.1/32 on lo and `192.175.48.0/25 dev lo
scope link` in the main table, with local routes for the neighbour 192.175.48.2, where the canary listens, and for
192.175.48.129; the resolver answers allowed.escape.test with the neighbour, the policy forwards the name's port 8443,
and the row wants the canary to see nothing. T2, the writer's showing on control, run again by the orchestrator:
fail, "the guest reached the canary at 192.0.2.2:8443 and delivered its token, 2 times", as its sibling fails
there. Hosted gate on 033c9b7, a real VM: fail, "the guest reached the canary at 192.175.48.2:8443 and delivered
its token, 2 times (guest says connected ...); the resolver was asked [AAAA, A, AAAA, A allowed.escape.test.] and
says A 192.175.48.2"; passed 146, failed 1, errors 0, with the sibling row, the same neighbour under a /25 on the
interface, passing beside it; gate-macos, gate-arm64 and guard green there, and all four green on the claim 2886c81.

Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, from the hosted log and a probe of its own: the product's vetting
compiled under an overlay and run in a namespace it made, where 192.175.48.1/25 on lo gives blockedAddr(192.175.48.2)
= true and 192.175.48.1/32 with the on-link /25 route gives false, with or without the row's local route for the
neighbour. So the isolate's model, a canary made local so that it can listen, is faithful as far as the vetting
can tell, and the extra local route could only have pushed the product toward refusing: the test takes no power
the attacker lacks. The attacker is in scope, the model of the eleven I4 rebind rows. Not intended behaviour: the
code's own comment says nets() exists to catch the networks of the host's own interfaces, and an on-link prefix
held by a route alone is such a network. Not high, because private and unique-local links stay refused by class;
not low, because the break is shown on a VM. The layout exists in practice (DHCPv6 with an on-link /64, cloud
NICs with a /32, DHCP option 121) and the attacker does not control it. Not someone else's project; a ported file,
so public under SPEC section 13.

Parked and handed on: the row and rebindingOnLink wait in escape/_pending/S-F49/rebind_on_link.go (commit 6c24914),
whose head says where each piece goes back; the live suite lists main's 146 rows, by the orchestrator's diff of
the two lists. The plumbing that is unused without the row stayed live (Config.OnLink, Want.OnLink, Hold's on-link
branch and the route helper, the payload's netns verb, the adapters' refusal of OnLink off Linux). The row's lines
were paid by 15 joined pairs of comment lines under escape/, no row and no code changed; test code stands at 28500
of 28500 and product at 15000 of 15000. Fix unit S-F49 stands below S-1004 in PLAN.md and starts with the move
back. Two things it must know. The row models the link on lo, so a fix that reads on-link routes must not skip lo,
and it must leave the local table and the default route out, or the suite's canary address 192.175.48.129 and a
tunnel's on-link default would be refused. And on a Mac the adapter answers the row with not-implemented, because
the static lo0 layout of the maintainer's setup cannot also hold a /32 with an on-link route: the fix unit gives
the row a Mac shape or a place among the Linux-only rows. Sweep 3 now stands at two mediums (C65, fixed; C66,
open) and one low (C64, fixed).

C66 FIXED by S-F49, commits 8888bab (the row moved back) and 325c477 (the fix) (PR #307). also in v1 main:
egressproxy/proxy.go, so the maintainer sends the same fix to v1. nets() in internal/proxy/proxy.go is now hostNets():
the interface prefixes as before, plus the host's on-link unicast prefixes read on every connection from
/proc/net/route and /proc/net/ipv6_route by routes(), a pure parser with the table-driven TestRoutes beside it. A row
is kept when it has no gateway, a prefix longer than 0 bits, no RTF_LOCAL flag and a destination that is not
multicast: so the local table, the default route and an on-link default are left out, lo is not skipped, and the
suite's canary address 192.175.48.129 stays dialable. A file that does not exist adds nothing (a host with no IPv6
has no ipv6_route, and a Mac has no /proc, so off Linux the vetting is what it was); any other read error or a
malformed row refuses the connection with blocked_address, as an unreadable interface list does. No build tag and no
new file. The row I4 rebind-on-link-neighbour-forward is back in the suite in the Linux build only (linuxRows beside
Hold in escape/suite/priv_linux.go, an empty stub in priv_other.go), because every I4 row must pass on the Mac gate
and the maintainer's static lo0 layout cannot hold a /32 with an on-link route; a Mac shape needs a Darwin route
reader and is left for a unit of its own. escape/_pending/S-F49/ is gone. Paid by joined comment lines in
internal/proxy, cmd/workcell-init/main.go and cmd/workcell/relay.go and by three one-to-one code folds (dnsName in
allowlist.go, within() and closeNotifyConn.Close in terminate.go): product 14994 of 15000, test 28488 of 28491.
Proof: the row fails on control (the guest reached the canary and delivered its token, twice) and passes in the
hosted gate on a real VM at 325c477 (passed 147, failed 0, errors 0; all 13 I2, 17 I4 and 4 I11 rows pass). In a
network namespace with the row's layout the unfixed nets() gave 127.0.0.1/8 and 192.175.48.1/32 and did not block
192.175.48.2; the fixed one adds 192.175.48.0/25, blocks .2 and still allows .129. IPv6 is proven by the parser's

IPv6 redirect installs it) now refuses every public address behind it, where it was dialled before. Sweep 3 now
stands at two mediums (C65, fixed; C66, fixed) and one low (C64, fixed).

## S-1005, sweep 3: TLS termination and HTTP handling: smuggling, HTTP/2, WebSocket, redirects, CONNECT, CA handling (I5, I6), as built at main de37d68

Sweep 3 (S8), the last the SPEC allows, fresh context (S3), the whole surface read as built after S-F1 to S-F49,
not a diff. Auditor on the top tier in the cloud session, which has no hypervisor; nothing of this audit needed
a VM. The auditor wrote its own trust boundary before it opened any earlier record.

Trust boundary. Guest root and hostile model output own every byte of a 443 relay stream after the 20-byte header
that stream() in cmd/workcell/relay.go reads: the ClientHello (crypto/tls over a recording conn, 16 KiB cap, 10 s
deadline, extension 0xfe0d refused, the SNI lowered with a length check and matched by exact allowlist membership),
then, replayed byte for byte into the per-connection tls.Server of serveTerminated in internal/proxy/terminate.go
(a leaf for the routed host, TLS 1.2 or later, ALPN http/1.1 alone), the whole HTTP/1.1 stream that net/http parses:
request line, target, method, headers (64 KiB), bodies, trailers, pipelining, Upgrade, Expect, count, rate and
timing. They also own the relay header's address (used only for sameHost's port, which the adapter fixes at 443),
the placeholders (wcph- plus 32 hex, fresh per rule and per session) and the public CA PEM. The handler judges in this
order: an opaque target or a scheme without a host (400), TRACE and CONNECT (405), sameHost against the connection's
SNI (421), per rule placeholderForm, then admits (403), then broker.Lookup; tokenEndpoint, then tokenRequest (502);
carriesPlaceholder (502); then httputil.ReverseProxy, whose Rewrite forces scheme, URL host and Host to the SNI
host over p.transport (RootCAs the system pool plus an absolute SSL_CERT_FILE, ServerName the SNI host, HTTP/1.1,
DialContext re-entering p.connect), with ModifyResponse = tokenResponse. The malicious repository owns the working
directory (ca.pem and certs/, refused since S-F22 and S-F36) and workcell.toml (narrow only, S-F27). The network
attacker owns every host off the allowlist and, in the project's own I4 model, the host resolver's answers for
allowed names; it does not own an allowed host's x509 identity. Authority: the supervisor as the operator's uid,
with the session CA key, the broker (file, cmd and keychain reads per use, sign-in tokens held one generation),
the audit log, and a plain dialer to any public address the resolver gives. Trusted without checking: the framing
and hop-by-hop handling of crypto/tls, net/http and httputil on go1.27.4; the host resolver and root store; the
compiled-in provider TOML; the operator's config; and every byte an allowlisted upstream answers: its redirects,
media types and echoes, its router's reading of a path, and its framework's reading of override headers. Both
candidates live in that last item. internal/proxy/terminate.go carries `// Ported from v1`, so C68 is an ordinary
public candidate with a v1 line (SPEC section 13); signin.go is not ported. Both candidates rest on documented
behaviour of providers and frameworks, not on a defect in someone else's project, so nothing falls under S14's stop.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: the header block is capped at 64 KiB and the handshake plus header read at
10 s (S-F6); a token body and a token answer at 256 KiB plus 1, before and after gzip, with br and zstd refused;
a Basic value at 4 KiB of strict base64; the hello at 16 KiB; the leaf cache is keyed by allowed names only;
1024 slots on each side, and a kept-alive or Upgrade-hijacked connection holds its slot by design. Smuggling
was run again as raw bytes over TLS on go1.27.4: CL.TE is re-framed, the upstream saw one POST with an empty
body and the smuggled GET naming another allowed Host was answered 421 host_mismatch as a second request; TE.CL
with a malformed chunk gave 502, the chunk's bytes reaching the bound host as a body only; "xchunked" is 501,
"Transfer-Encoding : chunked" 400, two Content-Length headers 400; the h2 preface without Host is 421, and with
a Host it crosses as the method PRI to the bound host; bytes pipelined behind an Upgrade request are dropped by
Go's handleUpgradeResponse, and the 101 tunnel is bound to the bound host, which alone saw the swapped key in the
judged upgrade request. Four fuzz targets ran 20 s each with no crasher (FuzzCarriesPlaceholder 233,616 executions,
FuzzSwapRefresh 656,900, FuzzHide 258,568, FuzzPeekSNI 2,821). No panic reachable from guest bytes was found. Logic
and state: sameHost's ASCII-only fold and port rule hold (an IPv6 literal, an empty port, 0443, two colons, a trailing
dot with a port and the Kelvin sign all fail closed); an absolute-form target naming another allowed host is 421,
userinfo is dropped, HTTP/1.0 without Host is 421, Host with :8443 is 421, a lowercase connect in authority form
is 400 target_refused (C32), OPTIONS * reaches the handler (C27); admits judges the path on three readings (C10,
C33) and tokenEndpoint claims on three; the swap forms are bare, Bearer and Basic only. What no code does became
the candidates: tokenResponse reads an answer of a sign-in host on an unclaimed path only when its media type is
JSON or form (C67), and nothing refuses or strips a header with which an upstream's framework reads the method or
the path from somewhere other than the request line (C68). Concurrency and check-to-use: p.terminate, p.signin,
p.ca, p.broker, p.transport and p.upstreamRoots are written once in Terminate before Serve; the leaf cache is
under a mutex; the broker is under a mutex and hands out clones; the token context rides the request context
into the cloned outgoing request; the carried refresh token covers the rotation race (C15); nothing changes r.URL
between admits and the clone; the peek and the terminating server parse the same replayed bytes. Cryptography and
identity: a P-256 CA of at most 24 hours, NotBefore one minute back, critical PermittedDNSDomains equal to the
443 allowlist, every IP range excluded, path length 0, KeyUsageCertSign; a leaf per lowered allowed name with
ServerAuth and a random 128-bit serial; the key never leaves the host and the guest gets the PEM (16 KiB cap)
as a convenience; a fresh tls.Config per connection, so no ticket resumption across connections and no 0-RTT;
the upstream is verified against the explicit pool with ServerName the SNI host, TLS 1.2 or later, HTTP/1.1,
pooled per host string, no Proxy. Nothing new. Failure modes: every error path refuses or closes. A leaf error
fails the handshake; an upstreamRoots error fails Terminate before boot; a broker error is 502; the token reasons
are 502; a ModifyResponse error is an empty 502 before any upstream header is copied; a failed Note half-closes
before any dial; HEAD at the token endpoint is 502. Nothing fails open except the unread answer and the unjudged
header of the two candidates. Downgrade, rollback and replay: TLS 1.2 or later on both sides; an h2-only ALPN is
refused and the h2 preface is 421; placeholders are fresh per session and refused anywhere else; the guest never
holds a real refresh token to replay; the broker keeps one generation and zeroes the replaced one; a replayed code
grant gains nothing. Interaction between surfaces: the refusal records of a kept-alive connection fill the audit
log at request rate, and S-F16 then refuses every connection, a loss and never a gain; loadPolicy's C34 and C54
checks read as built; the resolver's hint is never dialled; the trust store in the guest is a convenience (A1);
C67 and C68 each need a trait of the provider, as C10, C33 and C55 did.

Refuted by the auditor before any candidate was raised: a lowercase `trace` crosses as a method with the swapped
key to the bound host, and only an upstream that folds method case and has TRACE enabled would echo it (Go, Apache,
nginx, Node and Python compare case: no such server is known); `Connection: X-Api-Key` makes ReverseProxy drop
the swapped header (self-harm); bytes pipelined behind an Upgrade request reach nothing; `//host/path` stays
a path (parked line 107 stands); double percent-decoding, NUL truncation and trailing-space stripping stay the
parked residuals (no named router); an SSL_CERT_FILE that is an absolute path inside the repository needs the
operator's own environment to name it (C53's record judged it no distinct finding); a 206 of a JSON token answer
is refused as malformed JSON; a nested or camelCase token field and an id_token are the provider's shape (U-403,
parked); a token echoed in a response header or trailer has no precedent (parked); a CA PEM over 16 KiB from a
huge allowlist makes the init refuse the Exec, the operator's own availability; an Accept header at the claimed
path gains nothing, since learn refuses an XML 2xx there.

Evidence gaps, not findings (PARKED.md holds what a retro must weigh, R3). No escape row drives Upgrade, CONNECT,
pipelining, absolute-form targets or the token-answer media types on a real VM; the package's Go tests are their
proof. hide scans neither response headers nor trailers, and readToken's full read of a short original body lets
the transport fill the response's trailer, which ReverseProxy then writes after the rewritten body, so a token
in a trailer would pass (no provider sends one). A token under a non-standard key, nested, or an id_token passes
as issued at the claimed path (U-403, parked). tokenEndpoint has no method check (harmless). A 101 answered at
a token endpoint parks the handler in readToken until the upstream closes (parked, bounded). Lookup and Refresh
record a grant before carriesPlaceholder may refuse (the parked I9 wording). The terminated path emits refusal
records at request rate (parked).

### S-1005 candidates, sweep 3

C67. ID I5 ("Real credential bytes never exist in guest memory ..."), and the sign-in flow's own contract at the
head of internal/proxy/signin.go: a real token the broker holds never appears in an answer. It is the residual that
S-F38's record of C55 and PARKED.md left for the next audit, now reproduced, with a lever the guest holds. Attacker:
guest root or hostile model output, choosing the spelling of the token endpoint's path and the Accept header of
its own request. Preconditions it does not control: the provider's router serves the token action on a spelling
outside tokenEndpoint's three readings (a Rails `(.:format)` route, as C55 records), and the provider answers
in a media type other than application/json or application/x-www-form-urlencoded; GitHub's OAuth documentation
gives XML for `Accept: application/xml` beside form and JSON, so there the guest picks the media type. Where:
tokenResponse in internal/proxy/signin.go, whose early return passes unread every 2xx of a sign-in host on an
unclaimed path when the media type is neither of the two, an absent Content-Type included; and tokenAnswer,
whose form branch reads a JSON object as one form key, since url.ParseQuery does not fail on it, so a JSON token
answer under a form label counts as no token answer. signin.go is not ported, so there is no v1 line. Input:
a policy row `source = "signin:login.example.com/oauth/token"` bound to api.example.com; a provider that serves
`/oauth/token.xml` and `/oauth/token.json` as the token action and answers a code grant with real tokens as
`application/xml; charset=utf-8` (GitHub's documented XML shape), as text/json, as application/vnd.api+json,
as text/plain form text, with no Content-Type at all, or as a JSON object under a form Content-Type; the guest
posts `grant_type=authorization_code&code=c0de` to that spelling through the terminating proxy. Effect claimed:
the guest reads a 200 with the real access and refresh tokens verbatim, usable and refreshable outside the
session, where the honest spelling `/oauth/token` gives it placeholders, the honest spelling with `Accept:
application/xml` is refused 502, and `/oauth/token.json` with a JSON answer is refused 502 (C55 holds); the
leaks leave no token_answer_refused record. Auditor's evidence: a probe of nine rows by go test -overlay on the
unchanged tree, six of them leaking, and all nine refused or swapped under a fix-shaped overlay with the whole
package green under -race. Severity claimed: medium by S6, the class and grade of C55.

Reproducing test: TestC67TokenAnswerInAnotherMediaType, package proxy, 69 lines, written by the redteam from the
claim alone, on the fixture of c55_test.go; each row runs its own loopback TLS provider and asserts only that no
byte of a real token appears in the status line, headers or body the guest reads, so a fix may refuse the answer
or swap the tokens. Run by go test -overlay against the real package, plain and under -race, by the redteam and
again by the orchestrator: the control row (the honest spelling with a JSON answer, which wants 200 and both
placeholders) passes, and the six claim rows fail, each with "the guest read a real token" above a 200 and the
verbatim body: xml, text/json, vnd.api+json, text/plain form, no content-type, form label over json. No VM was needed.

Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, which ran the test itself (the control row passes, all six other
rows fail) and probed tokenEndpoint on its own: its three readings leave `/oauth/token.xml`, `.json` and `.JSON`
unchanged, so none is claimed, and the early return of tokenResponse then relays the body unread. The attacker is
in scope and the test takes no power it lacks: it reuses the harness of C55 that S-F38 accepted and changes only
the provider's answer type. Not intended behaviour: the comment that any other answer passes unread describes
the code, not an accepted leak, and docs/providers.md does not park it. Not high, because a provider that serves
only the exact path and answers JSON is out of reach; medium, because the break is shown and rests on two traits
of the provider that the attacker does not control, one already accepted in C55 and one documented by a named
provider. Not v1 code and not someone else's project.

C68. ID I5 ("A placeholder is useless at any destination other than the one it is bound to"), as C33 and the
product's own refusal text read the binding: "the credential in x-api-key is bound to method POST under path
/v1/" and "bound to repositories octo/allowed". It is the parked tool note of S-1016b, now reproduced. Attacker:
guest root or hostile model output, choosing the headers of its own request. Precondition it does not control:
the bound host's framework honours a routing-override header. That is documented behaviour and not a defect
in anyone's project: Rack::MethodOverride (in the default middleware stack of every Rails application),
ASP.NET MVC's HttpMethodOverride and Google's API front end take the method from `X-HTTP-Method-Override` on a
POST; IIS URL Rewrite with ASP.NET and Symfony HttpFoundation's Request take the path from `X-Original-URL` or
`X-Rewrite-URL`. Where: internal/proxy/terminate.go, the rule loop of serveTerminated's handler, where admits judges
r.Method and r.URL alone before the swap, and the ReverseProxy with Rewrite, which strips hop-by-hop and X-Forwarded
headers only and forwards every other header as sent. also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go. Input: rules `{Host:
n.example.com, Header: x-api-key, Method: POST, Path: /v1/}` and `{Host: r.example.com, Header: authorization, Repos:
[octo/allowed]}`, a broker holding the real secret, and an upstream that reads the method and the path as those
frameworks do; the guest sends an admitted request line with its placeholder and one override header: `POST /v1/x`
with `X-HTTP-Method-Override: DELETE` or `GET`; `POST /v1/x` with `X-Original-URL: /v2/admin` or `X-Rewrite-URL:
/v2/admin`; `GET /octo/allowed.git/info/refs` as Bearer with `X-Original-URL: /octo/other.git/info/refs`; `POST
/octo/allowed.git/git-receive-pack` as git's Basic with `X-Original-URL: /evil/repo.git/git-receive-pack`. Effect
claimed: every row is answered 200 and the upstream served, with the real secret, `DELETE /v1/x`, `GET /v1/x`,
`POST /v2/admin` (twice), `GET /octo/other.git/info/refs` and `POST /evil/repo.git/git-receive-pack`, where the
plain forms of the same requests are refused 403 binding_mismatch with the secret withheld; no record is written
for the bypassed rows. Auditor's evidence: a probe of six override rows by go test -overlay on the unchanged tree,
all served with the real secret, and all six refused 403 under a fix-shaped overlay with the whole package green
under -race. Severity claimed: medium by S6, the class and grade of C10 and C33, a request that admits reads one
way and the upstream another; the auditor noted that a verifier may weigh C36's reading (the product promises
the method and path as sent) against C33's (the binding is what the upstream serves).

Reproducing test: TestC68RoutingOverrideHeaders, package proxy, 76 lines, written by the redteam from the claim
alone, on the fixture of c10_test.go; a row passes if the request is refused or is served without the override,
so a fix may refuse or strip. Run by go test -overlay against the real package, plain and under -race, by the
redteam and again by the orchestrator: the control rows pass (the plain `POST /v1/x` and the plain allowed
repository are served with the real secret, the plain `DELETE /v1/x` and `POST /v2/admin` are refused), and the
six override rows fail, each answered 200 with the upstream's own line: "DELETE /v1/x real-secret", "GET /v1/x
real-secret", "POST /v2/admin real-secret" twice, "GET /octo/other.git/info/refs Bearer real-secret" and "POST
/evil/repo.git/git-receive-pack real-secret". No VM was needed.

Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, which ran the test itself and traced the request along the real path
from the listener through Serve and serveTerminated to the ReverseProxy: admits judges only r.Method and r.URL and
the override header crosses untouched, so the override header is the only difference between a refused row and a
served one. The attacker is in scope and the test takes no power it lacks: the stock harness of the package, with
an upstream that honours the header as the stated precondition. Not intended behaviour: docs/policy.md promises
that method, path and repos narrow the swap and that any other request gets a 403 with the value not read, and the
product already treats a request that the proxy and the upstream read differently as a break of I5 in the direct
sibling C10, under the same precondition of a host behind such a router; C68 is that class by a header where C10
was by a path encoding. Medium under S6: I5 is broken, but only where the bound host honours an override header;
not high, since a host without such a framework is unaffected. The frameworks' behaviour is documented, so S14
does not apply; terminate.go is ported, so the record carries its v1 line and the maintainer sends the same fix to v1.

Parked and handed on: the two tests wait in escape/_pending/S-F50/c67_test.go and escape/_pending/S-F51/c68_test.go,
each with a head that says where it goes: internal/proxy/c67_test.go and internal/proxy/c68_test.go, unchanged. The
live suite lists main's 147 rows, by the orchestrator's compare of the two lists. The test budget had 3 lines of room,
so the 145 lines were paid by 148 layout folds in 34 files under escape/, in a run of the redteam of its own: 103
joins of adjacent code lines (the first row of a table on its opening line and adjacent rows on shared lines where
the table already did that, the closure chain of parallel() in workcell_vm.go, spread literals and conditions),
29 comments moved from a line of their own above a statement to the end of that statement's line, 10 two-line doc
comments joined, and 6 blank lines that gofmt does not require. No row, verdict, string, name or comment word changed:
the orchestrator compared every changed file with its parent by a tool of its own, the Go token stream with every
semicolon kept except one before a closing bracket, and the comment words in order, equal in all 34. The longest
line made has 499 columns, where the tree already held one of 849. Test code stands at 28485 of 28491 and product
at 14994 of 15000. Fix units S-F50 (C67) and S-F51 (C68) stand below S-1005 in PLAN.md, and each starts with the
move of its test. Three things they must know. The auditor's fix shapes measured about 4 product lines for C67
(drop the media-type clause of tokenResponse, let tokenAnswer's form branch also take a body that is valid JSON,
and refuse any other media type whose body names access_token or refresh_token in any case) and about 3 for C68

on a sign-in host every 2xx on an unclaimed path is then held whole, and one over 256 KiB is answered 502, which
matters only where the token host is also a streaming API host. And C68's fix cannot see an override carried in

for ASP.NET MVC); the query form could be judged at a line's cost. Both residuals belong in the fix units' records.

Sweep 3 verdict for this surface: two candidates, C67 and C68, both confirmed at medium. Sweep 3 now stands at
