C67 FIXED by S-F50, commits b2c49ac (the test moved), 3d95817 (the fix) and 9acc6e0 (the review's fix round)
(PR #309). Not v1 code: signin.go is not ported. tokenResponse in internal/proxy/signin.go no longer asks for a
media type before it reads: every 2xx answer of a sign-in host to a request tokenEndpoint did not claim is read
whole by readToken under the 256 KiB bound, identity or gzip, and judged by tokenAnswer. tokenAnswer keeps its
JSON and form branches; the form branch also refuses a body that is valid JSON and issues a token read as JSON,
and for any other media type, or none, a body that names access_token or refresh_token in any case is refused,
with NUL bytes dropped first, so that a UTF-16 or UTF-32 spelling is read too. A refusal is the deny
token_answer_refused and an empty 502, as in C55. Net product lines: 0, paid by three joined comment pairs in
signin.go and a third name on the var line of params and sep.
The review round found the UTF-16 case (I5, the attacker of C67 with an Accept or Accept-Charset header): on the
first fix a token answer labelled text/json or application/vnd.api+json with charset=utf-16 on /oauth/token.json
reached the guest in a 200, because every letter of the key names had a NUL beside it; under application/json it
was refused already as malformed JSON. The fix round is one changed line, and c67_test.go gained two rows
(text/json utf-16le, vnd.api+json utf-16be) and reads the guest's dump with NULs dropped, since the real token is
spelled with NULs there too: nine rows now, where the accept line counted seven. With the fix round's test the
two new rows fail on 3d95817 and all nine pass on 9acc6e0, plain and under -race; with main's signin.go the six
claim rows and the two new rows fail and the control row passes (the orchestrator ran all three by go test -overlay).
What it costs an honest provider, wider than the S-F38 line in PARKED.md, as the unit foresaw: every 2xx on an
unclaimed path of a sign-in host is now held whole before the guest reads a byte, so a streamed answer arrives at
its end; one over 256 KiB, or in an encoding other than identity or gzip, is answered 502; and a page, script or
document of that host whose bytes name access_token or refresh_token is answered 502. A host that is a sign-in
host and also serves large or streamed content loses that content. Paths the endpoint's match claims and hosts
that are no sign-in host are as before.
What is left: a spelling of the key names that is neither ASCII, UTF-16 nor UTF-32 (another charset the provider
would have to offer on request), an answer that carries the token under other key names, and a token in a
response header or trailer, which hide does not scan (parked at S-1005). None has a reproduction.
Sweep 3 now stands at four mediums (C65, C66 and C67, fixed; C68, open) and one low (C64, fixed).

C68 FIXED by S-F51, commits 8169b5b (the test moved), dc91d44 (the fix) and e702890 (the review's fix round)
(PR #310). also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go. admits in internal/proxy/terminate.go now takes the request's
headers too, and a rule that narrows (method, path or repos set) refuses with 403 binding_mismatch, before the
broker is asked, a request that names a routing override: any of x_http_method_override, x_http_method,
x_method_override, x_original_url, x_rewrite_url or _method, as a header name or as a query parameter name, in
any letter case and any mix of "-" and "_", with any value, none, or several. The names are in one package-level
list, overrides, read through cgiName, which spells a name as a CGI-style server spells a header. The refusal was
chosen over stripping: it is less code and it keeps docs/policy.md true as written ("any other request gets a
403, and the value is not read"), so that file is unchanged. A rule that does not narrow is as before. Net product
lines: 2 (terminate.go 498 to 500), after three joined comment pairs, one comment moved to the end of its line and
the ExcludedIPRanges literal folded to one line; product 14996 of 15000, test 28490 of 28494.
The review round found two more readings (I5, the attacker of C68, each run on dc91d44 under a rule for POST
/v1/). The underscore spelling: Go's header canonicalisation leaves "_" alone, so `X_HTTP_Method_Override: DELETE`,
`X-HTTP_Method-Override: DELETE` and `X_Original_URL: /v2/admin` were not found by a lookup of the five names and
crossed, and a server that maps header names the CGI way (RFC 3875 4.1.18; Puma, Unicorn and WEBrick under
Rack::MethodOverride) reads each as the same variable: 200 with the real secret as DELETE /v1/x and POST /v2/admin.
The query string: `POST /v1/x?_method=DELETE` and `?X-HTTP-Method-Override=DELETE` were served with the real secret
where the framework reads a request parameter (Spring's HiddenHttpMethodFilter, ASP.NET MVC's HttpMethodOverride).
The fix round judges every header name and every decoded query parameter name of the request against the list,
a ";" in the query read as "&" so that a pair Go would drop is judged too, and c68_test.go gained two rows (the
underscore header, the _method parameter) and an upstream that honours them: twelve rows now, where the accept
line counted ten. With the fix round's test the two new rows fail on dc91d44 and all twelve pass on e702890, plain
and under -race; with main's terminate.go the six claim rows fail and the four control rows pass (the orchestrator
ran both by go test and by go test -overlay).
What is left, none with a reproduction: an override in a body the proxy does not read (`_method` or the header's
name as a form field, which Rack, Spring, ASP.NET MVC and Symfony all read on a POST); a query pair whose value
fails percent-decoding (`?_method=DEL%ZZ`), which url.ParseQuery drops and a lenient framework might still read;
ASP.NET's `%uXXXX` form in a parameter name; PHP's reading of ".", a space or an unmatched "[" in a parameter name
as "_" (`?.method=DELETE` is `_method` to Symfony); and an override under a name outside the list, the redteam's
X-Forwarded-Prefix, X-Forwarded-Path and X-Forwarded-Uri among them (PARKED.md weighs them). What it costs an honest
client: a request under a narrowed rule that carries one of these names, as a header or a query parameter, with
the placeholder is answered 403, and the answer names the binding and not the header.
Sweep 3 now stands at four mediums (C65, C66, C67 and C68, all fixed) and one low (C64, fixed).

## S-1006, sweep 3: resolver: tunnelling, rebinding, cache and case tricks (I3, I4), as built at main f8fc5ab

Sweep 3 (S8), the last the SPEC allows, fresh context (S3), the whole surface read as built after S-F1 to S-F51,
not a diff. Auditor on the top tier in the cloud session, which has no hypervisor; nothing of this audit needed
a VM. The auditor wrote its own trust boundary before it opened any earlier record.

Trust boundary. Guest root owns every byte and the timing of each vsock stream to host port 5001: the 20-byte
relay header that stream() in cmd/workcell/relay.go decodes and, behind a UDP/53 header at any address, one
2-byte length frame and up to 65535 bytes handed to resolver.Answer, on up to 1024 streams (1023 on Firecracker)
under a 5 s deadline; the guest's resolv.conf, routes and listeners enforce nothing (A1). The network attacker
owns the answers that the host's system resolver returns for an allowed name (A and AAAA sets, CNAME chains,
TTL 0, timing) and every upstream byte at the address it steers the host to; those enter at connect in
internal/proxy/proxy.go (LookupNetIP of the rooted name, then hostNets, then blockedAddr on every address,
then a dial by literal) and through the Transport.DialContext of terminate.go, which re-enters connect. The
operator chooses the allowed set, canonical lower-case ASCII, which reaches the resolver and the proxy as the
same strings; the repository can only narrow. Authority: the supervisor at the operator's uid, which can open
any TCP connection the host can (loopback, LAN, metadata, VPN, NAT hairpin), writes name_not_allowed notes, and
holds descriptors and memory. The resolver answers from policy alone, with no upstream, cache or forwarding,
so for the guest's own queries "no query leaves the host" is structural; connect is the one place where a
guest action makes a query leave the host, and only for a name on the allowlist. Trusted without checking:
the kernel's route and interface tables, the system resolver for addresses (vetted afterwards), and that
blockedAddr's classes plus the interface prefixes and the main table's on-link routes name every address the
host itself answers or sits beside. Not knowable to that vetting, as the auditor listed before it read the
records: an address behind a VPN or a policy table, a NAT hairpin, public space used internally one hop away,
an address the host owns through the local table alone, and a metadata address in public space outside the
list. Both candidates live in the last two items. internal/proxy/proxy.go carries `// Ported from v1`, so
both are ordinary public candidates with a v1 line (SPEC section 13); neither is a defect in Go, the kernel
or anyone else's project, so nothing falls under S14's stop.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: question() wants QDCOUNT 1, plain labels of at most 63 bytes, a name of
at most 253 bytes with the separating dot counted before the check, and type and class only when four bytes
remain; label types 0x40 to 0xFF are refused as long labels; reply() copies at most 255 wire bytes of question
plus the 16-byte record, so maxReply 287 holds exactly; TC, AA, Z, AD and CD are masked and RD is echoed as
sent. A fresh probe of twelve rows beyond TestAnswer (a pointer to a later offset, label types 0x41 and 0x80,
60000 junk bytes after a valid question, RD clear, every flag set, the 253-byte name, types HTTPS and 0, class 0,
opcode NOTIFY, a NUL in a label) gave every reply within the bound, no flag or count leaked, no panic. ReadFrame
allocates at most 65535 bytes per stream under the stream's absolute deadline, 64 MiB at the slot cap. routes()
refuses a malformed row, which fails closed. Fuzz: FuzzAnswer 20 s (4.07 million runs), FuzzDecode 20 s (3.35
million), FuzzReadFrame 20 s (3.30 million), the suite's FuzzParseDNSQuery 20 s and FuzzParseDNSReply 21 s:
no crasher. Logic and state: both sides fold ASCII only and the allowed set is ASCII, so no other spelling
matches (U+0130 and the Kelvin sign shrink under ToLower and are refused by the length check); a rooted name
is the wire form, so the resolver takes it and the SNI check refuses a trailing dot; an allowed name's AAAA,
TXT, ANY, HTTPS and type 0 are NOERROR with no record, so no HTTPS-record ECH path exists; every allowlist
host on any port gets the hint 127.0.0.1, the proxy scopes by port afterwards, and the hint is never dialled;
connect's vetting is all or nothing over one answer set, with Unmap before both the vet and the dial; UDP 53
at any address is the resolver's, and UDP elsewhere closes without a record (C14, intended). Concurrency and
check-to-use: one lookup per connection, the host's networks read after it, every answer vetted before any dial,
the dial by literal under a shared 30 s budget, no second lookup (TestConnectVetsEveryAnswerOnEveryConnection
green); the terminated transport pools per host and re-enters connect for each new upstream connection, so a
pooled connection reuses the address vetted at its dial; a shared lookup hands each caller the same set, and
each vets it; the DNS exchange, its reply write included, runs under the stream's absolute deadline; a host
network that appears between the read and the dial is microseconds and not the attacker's to time. Cryptography
and identity: none on the resolver; the one identity check on the path is the terminated upstream's certificate
for the SNI host (S-1005), which is why both candidates stop at the ClientHello on 443 and matter on a forward
port, where the operator's grant trusts DNS; DNSSEC is not consulted. Failure modes: in hostNets a missing file
adds nothing, and any other read error, a malformed row or an InterfaceAddrs error refuses with blocked_address;
a lookup error or an empty set is resolve_failed, a dial failure dial_failed; a ReadFrame error or a nil Answer
closes the stream with nothing reflected; an Accept error of serveRelay closes every adapter; past the soft
limit every admission is refused while the hint still answers; no error path fails open. Downgrade, rollback
and replay: header version 1 only; the resolver is stateless and echoes the id; the product caches nothing and
vets per connection, so a stale or poisoned answer in the system's cache can only change which vetted address
is dialled, or give resolve_failed. Interaction between surfaces: the refused name that reaches the audit log
is lower-case [a-z0-9.-] of at most 253 bytes or empty; tunnelling moves 253 bytes per refused query into the
host's own log and nothing off the host; the host's only outbound queries are A and AAAA of a rooted allowlist
name; every Isolated row of the suite relies on the product dialling an address that the host owns through a
local route alone (the canary address), which is the mechanism of C69 used as a fixture.

Earlier fixes on this surface, traced again in the code as built, all hold: C7 (S-F4: 168.63.129.16/32 in
blockedPrefixes and Unmap first in blockedAddr; TestBlockedAddr green); C13 (S-F8: TLSHandshakeTimeout and
MaxConnsPerHost in the terminating transport; c13_test green); C23 and C24 (S-F16: handle acts on a nil
Note only, before any dial; unrecorded_test green); C66 (S-F49: hostNets reads both /proc tables, routes
keeps the rows with no gateway that are neither default, local nor multicast; TestRoutes green; the row
rebind-on-link-neighbour-forward is live in the Linux build and escape/_pending/ was gone); C14 (refuted in
sweep 1) stands as relay.go and its tests have it. C69 is the residue of S-F49's own exclusion of the local
table, reproduced now.

Coverage. Read in full: internal/resolver/resolver.go and its test; internal/relay/relay.go and its test;
cmd/workcell/{relay,run_vm,policy,log}.go and relay_test.go; internal/proxy/{proxy,allowlist,terminate}.go
with proxy_test.go, forward_test.go and c13_test.go; internal/policy/policy.go;
internal/audit/audit.go; cmd/workcell-init/{net,main}.go; internal/vmm/vmm.go and both backends;
escape/suite/{dns,dnstests,resolver,rebind,packets,addr_linux,host_linux,priv_linux,relay,https,suite,tests,floods,floods_linux,channel,channel_linux,lifecycle}.go
with dns_test.go and rebind_test.go;
escape/sandbox/{sandbox,workcell,workcell_vm,workcell_linux,control_linux,control_resolver_linux,control_relay_linux}.go;
escape/cmd/payload/main.go; docs/adr/003-network-path.md; loop/SPEC.md; this file's map, its records of
S-1006 in sweeps 1 and 2 and of S-1004 in sweep 3; PARKED.md by search for the surface's terms; both enforced
lists and fuzz-minutes.txt. Not opened: internal/proxy/signin.go and its tests and the other c*_test files;
internal/secret; cmd/workcell/{explain,update}.go; the suite's secrets, signin, terminate, audit, repo and
files rows; escape/sandbox/workcell_darwin.go and the adapter tests; docs/threat-model.md and docs/policy.md;
_legacy/; the Go standard library's sources (sweeps 1 and 2 read net and net/http; this audit relied on
their record and on behaviour). Ran: go test of internal/resolver, internal/relay, internal/proxy (the whole
package) and cmd/workcell's relay tests, the non-VM tests of escape/suite and escape/sandbox, go vet of the
four packages, the five fuzz bursts, three probes by go test -overlay from a scratch directory, and one probe
as root in a network namespace of its own that spoke netlink itself, since the session has no ip tool. Every
listener was a socket the probe itself started inside its own namespace or on loopback, no packet left the
session and no third party was touched (S12, T8); the tree was unchanged at the end. Not run by the auditor:
anything on a real VM, the escape suite, the gate, anything over IPv6 (the session's kernel has none, so the
IPv6 half of C69 is reasoned only), any macOS path, the four-hour fuzz of S10. No model declined a request,
no safeguard re-ran one and no tool permission was refused to the auditor.

Evidence gaps, not findings (PARKED.md holds what a retro must weigh, R3). The suite has no I4 row with an
IPv6 answer, with a mixed answer set (feasible now in the isolated network with the canary address beside
a neighbour, against the head comment of rebind.go) or with a metadata address in public space; a DNS
frame whose header promises more than it sends is unit-tested only. A synthesised AAAA of a NAT64 network
(64:ff9b::/96) is refused, and one refused answer refuses the name, so on an IPv6-only network every allowed
name is blocked_address: closed, a matter of use and no invariant. An on-link public prefix in a routing table
other than main (policy routing, a VPN's own table) is C66's layout outside /proc/net/route; reasoned only.

### S-1006 candidates, sweep 3

C69. ID I4 ("The guest cannot reach host loopback, the LAN, link-local or cloud metadata addresses, or another
session. Names are resolved on the host and the vetted address is the one dialled."). It is the residue of
S-F49's own exclusion of the local table, now reproduced. Attacker: guest root, with the network attacker
as the host's resolver for an allowed name, the model of the rebind rows, of C7 and of C66. Precondition it
does not control: the host owns a public (global unicast) prefix through the kernel's local routing table
alone, an AnyIP route such as `ip route add local 192.175.48.0/25 dev lo` or, on IPv6, `ip -6 route add local
2001:db8:1::/64 dev lo`, the documented way to serve every address of a routed prefix on one machine (anycast
and edge hosts, a server with a routed /64), with no interface address and no main-table route for it; private,
link-local and unique-local prefixes of that kind stay refused by class. Rare on a developer's laptop. Where:
internal/proxy/proxy.go: hostNets reads the interface prefixes and /proc/net/route, which the kernel fills
from the main table only, so no row of the local table is ever seen; routes drops every IPv6 row that carries
RTF_LOCAL on purpose; blockedAddr then has no prefix to hold the address against, and connect dials it. also
in v1 main: egressproxy/proxy.go. Input: that layout; a policy that allows one name on a forward port (a bare
name's 443 is terminated, and the upstream certificate check stops it after the TCP connect and the ClientHello);
the resolver answers the name with any address of the prefix; the guest connects to the name. Effect claimed:
connect dials the address from the host and the kernel delivers the connection to the host itself, which is
what a local route means, so a service bound on the host to 0.0.0.0 or to the prefix receives the guest's bytes:
host-local reach through the vetting. Auditor's evidence: a probe by go test -overlay, run as root in a network
namespace of its own with the route added by netlink: /proc/net/route held the header line only, hostNets
gave 127.0.0.1/8 alone, blockedAddr(192.175.48.2) was false, connect returned a connection and the canary
at 192.175.48.2:8443 read the token; with 192.175.48.1/25 added as an interface address the same address was
blocked. The IPv6 half is reasoned only, since the session's kernel has no IPv6. Severity claimed: medium by S6.

Reproducing test: TestC69AnyIPLocalRoute, package proxy, build tag linux, written by the redteam from the claim
alone. It runs itself again in a user and network namespace of its own, or through `sudo -n unshare -n` where
no user namespace can be made, brings lo up and adds `local 192.175.48.0/25 dev lo` to the local table by raw
netlink, adds 192.175.48.129/25 as an interface address for the control arm, listens at 192.175.48.6:8443, and
calls the product's connect with only the lookup answered by the test, so the real hostNets, blockedAddr and
dial run; it fails when connect admits the address and the listener reads the bytes, and a dial failure is a
fatal layout error, so it cannot pass for want of a route. Run by go test -overlay against the real package,
plain and under -race, by the redteam and again by the orchestrator: "I4: connect admitted 192.175.48.6,
the host's own through the local table alone, and the host's listener read "GET /secret HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n"";
the control arm (192.175.48.130, inside the interface address's prefix, wants blocked_address) passes. The
redteam also ran it as uid nobody through the user namespace and ran the sudo fallback's command by hand,
with the same failure. No VM was needed.

Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, which ran the test itself, saw the same line and the control arm
pass, and traced the real path: a forward-port connection goes from handle through route and Deny to connect,
blockedAddr is called nowhere else in cmd/ or internal/, and terminate.go's dialer reaches the same connect, so
nothing else refuses the address. Its own namespace probe showed the stronger form: a listener on 0.0.0.0:8443 read
the bytes sent to 192.175.48.6, and /proc/net/route held no row for the prefix. The attacker is in scope and the
test takes no power it lacks: the route and the listener are the host's layout, which is the precondition. Not
intended behaviour and not a parked limit: docs/threat-model.md and the accepted decisions say nothing of it;
this file's own records left the local table out (C9 in sweep 1, C66 and S-F49 in this sweep) only so that
the suite's canary address stays dialable, a constraint of the test harness and not a judgement that such an
address is not the host; PARKED.md already says that a public alias on loopback is the host itself. Not low,
because the break is shown by a test, and how rare the layout is is no axis of S6; not high, because it needs
a host layout that the attacker does not control. C66 was graded medium on the same shape.

What the fix costs, for the maintainer (S8): the product must count an address of the local table as the host's
own, and every Isolated row of the suite reaches its canary by exactly such a route (escape/sandbox/sandbox.go,
and localRoute in escape/suite/priv_linux.go), so the fix and a new model of "the Internet" in the suite's
isolated network land together: the canary behind a gateway, for instance a second namespace over a veth pair
with a route `via`. The auditor's fix shape: in routes, stop dropping the rows that carry RTF_LOCAL (about three
product lines fewer, and it closes the IPv6 half); for IPv4, where /proc/net/route cannot show the local table,
read the routes by a netlink dump (RTM_GETROUTE) and keep the local rows and the unicast rows with no gateway
of both families, in place of routes and hexAddr, about forty lines out and forty in, in a Linux file with
a stub beside it. That is a choice about how the suite models the Internet, not a patch. Fix unit S-F52. Not
someone else's project: the kernel does what its documentation says.

C70. ID I4 ("cloud metadata addresses"). Attacker: guest root, with the network attacker as the host's resolver
for an allowed name. Preconditions it does not control: the host runs on Equinix Metal (formerly Packet), and
the policy forwards a plain port. Where: blockedPrefixes in internal/proxy/proxy.go, whose own comment says
it names a cloud metadata address on public space and which holds Azure's 168.63.129.16/32 alone. also in v1
main: egressproxy/proxy.go. Input: the resolver answers an allowed forward-port name with 192.80.8.124, which
the provider's public documentation gives as the address of its metadata service, one that knows its caller by
source address; the guest sends a plain HTTP request on the forward port. Effect claimed: blockedAddr does not
refuse the address or its IPv4-mapped form, so on a host of that platform the proxy would dial the metadata
service from the host's own address and relay the instance's metadata and user data to the guest. Auditor's
evidence: a probe by go test -overlay: blockedAddr(192.80.8.124) is false beside true for 168.63.129.16,
169.254.169.254, 100.100.100.200 and 192.0.0.192; the address's role is from the provider's documentation,
and nothing was sent to it or to any third party (S12). The auditor also went through the metadata endpoints
of seventeen other providers: each is link-local, in the shared address space, unique-local, in 192.0.0.0/24
or the Azure address already listed. Severity claimed: low, because the platform reached its end of life in
June 2026 and no break on a live host is shown.

Reproducing test: TestC70EquinixMetadata, package proxy, 15 lines, written by the redteam from the claim alone;
it calls blockedAddr with no host prefixes, as the existing test does, and touches no network. Run by go test
-overlay against the real package, plain and under -race, by the redteam and again by the orchestrator: the
rows 192.80.8.124 and ::ffff:192.80.8.124 fail ("blockedAddr(...) = false, want true"), and the control rows
pass (168.63.129.16 refused, 192.0.3.1 allowed). No VM was needed.

Outcome: CONFIRMED at low by the verifier, which ran the test itself and traced connect: lookup, then blockedAddr
on every answer as the only gate, then a dial by literal; its own probe with the lookup and the dial stubbed saw
connect dial 192.80.8.124:80 for both spellings where 168.63.129.16 and 169.254.169.254 gave blocked_address,
and a forwarded plain port checks no certificate, so nothing else refuses it. The structure is C7's, which
was medium; this is low because the platform has reached its end of life, so the precondition that made C7
medium cannot be met today: hardening with no demonstrated break. The address's role rests on the provider's
documentation and on the verifier's own knowledge; the repository says nothing of it. The verifier adds that
to list it as residual risk without a code row would also be defensible (S7 lists lows); the fix is one line,
so the fix unit S-F53 stands and the maintainer may strike it.

Sweep 3 now stands at five mediums (C65, C66, C67 and C68, fixed; C69, open) and two lows (C64, fixed; C70, open).

C69 FIXED by S-F52, commits 2a2be63 (the fix, with the test moved into place) and 0f9366c (the test's own re-run
path) (PR #315). also in v1 main: egressproxy/proxy.go. hostNets in internal/proxy/proxy.go no longer reads
/proc/net/route and /proc/net/ipv6_route: routes, hexAddr and rtfLocal are gone, and it asks hostRoutes, a new
Linux file internal/proxy/routes_linux.go with a stub beside it (routes_other.go, no table and no error, as a Mac's
missing /proc was read before). hostRoutes sends one RTM_GETROUTE dump for every family and every table over an
unprivileged netlink socket and reads its parts to NLMSG_DONE; routes, the pure parser, counts as the host's own
every row of type local in any table of either family (so an AnyIP prefix such as `local 192.175.48.0/25 dev lo`
or `local 2001:db8:1::/64 dev lo` is among the host's networks), and every unicast row with no gateway and more
than zero prefix bits, as before. A route that carries a gateway is not the host's, so the suite's canary behind

refuses the whole read, and connect then answers blocked_address for every address, as an unreadable table did.
The interface prefixes are still appended. TestC69AnyIPLocalRoute, now internal/proxy/c69_test.go, fails on main
with its I4 line and passes on the fix, plain and under -race, by the builder, the orchestrator and the reviewer,

runner lets an unprivileged process make a user namespace and then refuses it the namespace's network (EPERM at
the first netlink request), so the test now goes on to `sudo -n unshare -n` whenever its first run failed, and a
true I4 failure fails again there. TestRoutes is rewritten over hand-built netlink bytes in routes_linux_test.go
(local v4 and v6, on-link and through a gateway, another table, no destination, the skipped types, and each
refusal). Hosted on c010c6d, the same tree: gate on a real VM passed 147, failed 0, with the I2, I4, I5, I6, I9
and I11 rows green against a canary that is not in the host's local table; gate-macos, gate-arm64 and guard green.
Paid by folds in internal/proxy alone; product 14999 of 15000, test 28498 of 28498.
What is left, none with a reproduction by an in-scope attacker: an IPv6 row of type anycast is not counted, read
only, since no kernel at hand had IPv6; a dump that the host's own root changes while it is read is not read
again; and the reader refuses more than before where a table reached only through a rule holds a local default
(a TPROXY set-up) or where a route's gateway sits in a nexthop object, both toward refusal (PARKED.md weighs them).
Sweep 3 now stands at five mediums (C65, C66, C67, C68 and C69, all fixed) and two lows (C64, fixed; C70, open).

## S-1007, sweep 3: secrets: sources, placeholders, sign-in token swap, git credentials, logs, crash output (I5), as built at main 0b725e0

Sweep 3 (S8), the last the SPEC allows, fresh context (S3), the whole surface read as built after S-F1 to S-F54,
not a diff. Auditor on the top tier in the cloud session, which has no hypervisor; nothing of this audit needed
a VM. The auditor wrote its own trust boundary before it opened any earlier record.

Trust boundary. Guest root and hostile model output own every byte of a terminated HTTP/1.1 request once
S-1005's parser has it: method, request target, header names and values (the header that carries the
placeholder, Basic values, Content-Type, Accept-Encoding, Host), the body (read whole only at a claimed token
endpoint, 256 KiB; otherwise streamed unread), and the count, rate and timing of requests. They own the guest's
environment, disk and memory, where only placeholders arrive: wcph- plus 32 hex digits, 16 bytes of crypto/rand
per rule and per sign-in row, minted per session by bindings in cmd/workcell/policy.go and handed to the guest
through guest.Exec.Env alone. The repository owns the working directory and workcell.toml, which can only
narrow, and under --mount it writes the directory live; the export follows no symlink. The network attacker owns
no byte here: an upstream is verified against the system pool, plus an absolute SSL_CERT_FILE, for the SNI
host; an allowed provider's answer shape, router and framework are preconditions and not attacks. The operator,
out of scope, owns the [[secret]] rows and the helper programs. Entry points, in order: the handler of
serveTerminated (opaque target 400, TRACE and CONNECT 405, sameHost 421, then per rule placeholderForm, admits
403 and broker.Lookup; tokenEndpoint, then tokenRequest and swapRefresh 502; carriesPlaceholder 502), the
ReverseProxy rewritten to the SNI host, and tokenResponse, readToken, learn, hide and tokenAnswer on the answer.
Authority: the supervisor at the operator's uid reads a value per use (a file open, or a child at a fixed or
operator-named absolute path with a scrubbed environment, cwd /, stdin /dev/null and no shell), writes it into
one outgoing header or token body, holds sign-in tokens for one generation in broker memory, holds the session
CA key, and writes the fsynced ledger. From this surface the ledger receives config-derived bytes only (the
canonical allowlisted host, the rule's lower-cased header, the row's name, constant results). Nothing of the
guest's reaches `explain`, which prints config; `log` prints JSON-escaped lines; the guest gets back 400, 403,
405, 421 and 502 texts that name the header and scope from config and quote its own Host.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: file: wants an absolute path and a regular file, reads one line into one
buffer of 64 KiB plus one, and refuses a CR; cmd: is strings.Fields of the operator's text, an absolute program,
no shell, a 2 minute timeout and a 1 s WaitDelay whose expiry withholds, and its stderr is kept where %v never
prints it; secret-tool and security run at fixed paths (both absent in the session, so only their fail-closed
arms ran). A placeholder is matched by an exact pattern over 128 bits. Bounds: header block 64 KiB (431), token
body and answer 256 KiB plus one before and after gzip (br, zstd and deflate refused), Basic 4 KiB of strict
base64, ledger line 4 KiB, 1024 slots; hide's JSON pass and its replacements are linear in 256 KiB. The rate
limit is 300 grants and 300 recorded denials per fixed minute, each a durable fsync. Fuzz, 20 s each, no
crasher: FuzzCarriesPlaceholder (326274 runs), FuzzSwapRefresh (495332), FuzzHide (232957), FuzzParse (974961),
FuzzEachLine (913; its seeds hold a 16 KiB line). No panic reachable from guest bytes was found, and net/http
recovers a handler panic per connection into the discarded ErrorLog. Logic and state: placeholderForm swaps
the bare, the "Bearer " and the Basic-password forms only, one value; admits judges the path on three readings
(C10, C33) and refuses the six override names as header or query names (C68); tokenEndpoint claims on three
readings; learn takes a 2xx only as one JSON object and hides the broker's tokens, the carried refresh token
and what the answer issues, in plain, URL-encoded and JSON-escaped spellings; every 2xx of a sign-in host on an
unclaimed path is read whole and judged by tokenAnswer (C55, C67). What no code does became the candidates:
nothing reads a form body for the method override that every framework honouring X-HTTP-Method-Override also
reads there (C71), and the check of C54 judges whole absolute words only, so a path spelled inside an option
word is not judged (C72). Concurrency and check-to-use: the grant and token maps are fixed after NewBroker; held
and Issue run under the mutex and hand out clones; Lookup's value goes into the header in the same goroutine;
record follows Resolve, and a failed record zeroes and withholds; the carried refresh token covers the rotation
race (C15); the proxy's write-once fields are set in Terminate before Serve. Cryptography and identity:
placeholder entropy; a P-256 session CA of at most 24 h with critical name constraints and every IP range
excluded, one leaf per allowed name; the upstream verified with the SNI host as ServerName, TLS 1.2 or later,
HTTP/1.1, no client session cache; the ledger's seal is S-1010's. Failure modes: every error path answers 403,
405, 421 or 502 or closes; a bad scheme, a missing tool, an unreadable file, a timeout or a WaitDelay expiry is
a per-use broker_denied whose text the proxy drops; a closed, failing or nil ledger withholds every value; a
ModifyResponse error is an empty 502; nothing fails open but the unread body of C71 and the unjudged option
word of C72. Downgrade, rollback and replay: ALPN http/1.1 only; placeholders are fresh per session and refused
anywhere else, so a persisted one is dead in the next session; the guest never holds a real refresh token; one
generation is held and the replaced one zeroed; a replayed code grant gains nothing. Interaction between
surfaces: audit records carry Event, Host, Header, Name and Result only, and the tests assert that no value is
among them; `workcell log` prints the raw secret line and ocsfLine maps the same fields; `explain` prints name,
header, host, narrowing, sign-in endpoint and variable, never a source; start-up and session errors name file,
line, host, source path and directory, never a value; the guest's Exec environment is PATH, HOME, LANG, the
trust and cache variables, the placeholders and TERM, and the init never logs it; loadPolicy's checks of C34,
C54 and C58 and the narrowing of I13 hold as built (a row whose host is narrowed away goes, a sign-in row whose
token host is narrowed away refuses the session, and --allow does not restore a dropped row).

Earlier fixes on this surface, traced again in the code as built, all hold: C10 (S-F5), C11 (S-F6), C12
(S-F7), C13 (S-F8), C15 (S-F9: tokenRequest clones the released refresh token before swapRefresh clears it,
and learn seeds its swaps with it), C23 and C24 (S-F16), C27 (S-F19), C30 and C53 (S-F22, S-F36), C32 (S-F25),

use) is as it was. The tests of internal/secret, provider, audit, policy and proxy and of cmd/workcell are
green on the unchanged tree, and go vet is clean.

Coverage. Read in full: internal/secret (source.go, broker.go and every test); internal/proxy (terminate.go,

Evidence gaps and notes, not findings (PARKED.md holds what a retro must weigh, R3). basicDecode and

### S-1007 candidates, sweep 3

C71. ID I5 ("A placeholder is useless at any destination other than the one it is bound to"), for a rule
narrowed by method, as the product's own 403 text reads such a rule ("the credential in x-api-key is bound to
method POST under path /v1/"). It is the residue that C68's record and the parked S-F51 line left "with no
reproduction", now reproduced. Attacker: guest root or hostile model output, choosing the Content-Type and
the body of its own request. Precondition it does not control: the bound host's framework takes the method
from a form field of a POST body, a documented feature and not a defect of theirs: `_method` in
Rack::MethodOverride (the default middleware of a Rails application that is not API-only), in Laravel and in
Spring's HiddenHttpMethodFilter where enabled, and X-HTTP-Method-Override as a form field in ASP.NET MVC.
Where: internal/proxy/terminate.go: admits judges r.Method, r.URL and the names of headers and query
parameters; the rule loop of serveTerminated's handler then swaps the placeholder, and the ReverseProxy streams
the body unread. also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go. Input: a rule {Host, Header: x-api-key, Method:
POST, Path: /v1/} with a known real secret; the guest sends POST /v1/x with the placeholder in X-Api-Key and a
body of type application/x-www-form-urlencoded (`_method=DELETE&a=b`, `a=b&_method=put`,
`X-HTTP-Method-Override=PATCH`) or multipart/form-data with one field `_method` = DELETE. Effect claimed: an
upstream that honours the field serves DELETE, PUT or PATCH /v1/x with the real secret, where the plain DELETE
/v1/x with the placeholder is answered 403 binding_mismatch with the secret withheld; no refusal is recorded.
Auditor's evidence: a probe by go test -overlay on the package's own fixture: both control rows as expected
and all four form rows served outside the rule with the real secret; under a fix-shaped overlay the four rows
are 403 and the package is green under -race. Severity claimed: medium by S6, the class and grade of C68.

Reproducing test: TestC71FormMethodOverride, package proxy, 45 lines, written by the redteam from the claim
alone on the fixture of c68_test.go; its fake upstream is a loopback server that reads `_method` and
X-HTTP-Method-Override from the POST form of the body, as Rack reads req.POST, and upper-cases it. Six rows: a
plain POST with a JSON body must be served as "POST /v1/x real-secret" (a whole-body match, so a missing route
or a fixture error fails the test), a plain DELETE must be refused, and four form rows fail when the request is

"PATCH /v1/x real-secret") for the X-HTTP-Method-Override field, and (200, "DELETE /v1/x real-secret") for
the multipart field; the control rows pass. No VM was needed.

Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, which ran the test itself, saw the same four lines and both
control rows pass, so the form body is the only difference between a 403 and a served request, and traced the

not accepted: docs/policy.md promises that any other request gets a 403 and that the value is not read, no

What the fix costs, for the maintainer (S8): the auditor's smallest shape is two product lines in admits: parse
the Content-Type with mime.ParseMediaType and, for a rule that narrows the method, refuse 403 binding_mismatch

Its cost is honest and visible: a form-encoded POST under a method-narrowed rule is refused, so an operator
who needs form posts drops `method`. The precise alternative reads the form body under the token bound and

weighs the two. The redteam's variants that no row expresses are in PARKED.md.

What the fix costs, for the maintainer (S8): the auditor's shape is one product line in the source loop, before

## S-1020, sweep 3: one brought candidate of the secrets surface, and the row it was allowed (I5), as built at main 84468bc

S-1020 is a unit that R-3 made from PARKED.md, so no auditor ran (PLAN.md): the redteam wrote each test from the
claim in the unit line alone, the orchestrator ran each by go test -overlay against the real package, plain and
under -race, and one verifier per candidate, in a fresh context and with no one's reasoning, tried to refute it.
Nothing here needed a VM. The unit line allowed one more row, for a residue that S-F51 parked with no reproduction;
it reproduced, so it is a candidate of its own, C74. Nothing is private (S14): each precondition is a documented
feature of a framework or of PHP, no defect of theirs, and terminate.go is ported from v1's unreleased main.

### S-1020 candidates, sweep 3

C73. ID I5 ("A placeholder is useless at any destination other than the one it is bound to"), for a rule narrowed
by method. It is the residue of C71, as C71 was of C68: found by S-F55's reviewer, outside that unit's accept text,
parked for want of a confirmation under S4. Attacker: guest root or hostile model output, choosing the Content-Type
and the body of its own request. Precondition it does not control: the bound host's framework takes the method from
the top level of a JSON POST body. Where: internal/proxy/terminate.go: admits refuses a form body alone under a
method rule (application/x-www-form-urlencoded, multipart/*, or a body with no parsable type); a JSON type is
neither, no override name stands among the header and query names, so the placeholder is swapped and the
ReverseProxy streams the body unread. also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go. Input: a rule {Host, Header:
x-api-key, Method: POST, Path: /v1/}; the guest sends POST /v1/x with the placeholder and the body
{"_method":"DELETE"} under application/json, or {"_method":"PUT"} under application/vnd.api+json. Effect: an
upstream that honours the name serves DELETE or PUT /v1/x with the real secret, where the plain DELETE with the
placeholder gets 403 binding_mismatch; no refusal is recorded.

Reproducing test: TestC73JSONMethodOverride, package proxy, 55 lines, escape/_pending/S-F57/c73_test.go, on the
fixture of c71_test.go; its fake upstream is a loopback TLS server that, on a POST whose Content-Type holds "/json"
or "+json", decodes the body and takes the upper-cased top-level `_method` as the method. Six rows: a bare POST and
a POST with the JSON body {"a":1} must be served as "POST /v1/x real-secret", a plain DELETE must be refused, and
three override rows fail when the answer names the method outside the rule together with the real secret. Log of
the orchestrator's run, the same lines plain and under -race, and the same the redteam and the verifier saw:

    c73_test.go:52: POST application/json "{\"_method\":\"DELETE\"}": got (200, "DELETE /v1/x real-secret")
    c73_test.go:52: POST application/vnd.api+json "{\"_method\":\"PUT\"}": got (200, "PUT /v1/x real-secret")
    c73_test.go:52: POST APPLICATION/JSON; charset=utf-8 "{\"a\":1,\"_method\":\"delete\"}": got (200, "DELETE /v1/x real-secret")
    --- FAIL: TestC73JSONMethodOverride

The three control rows pass. Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, which ran the test, printed every row by
a probe of its own (the bare POST and the plain JSON POST served; the plain DELETE, the form body and
`?_method=DELETE` answered 403 with the broker not called and one deny record; the JSON `_method` rows served with
the broker called once and no deny record), so the JSON body is the only difference between a refusal and a served
request, and traced the real path, which never looks at the body. Its ruling on the upstream, the question the unit
line put first: real, from its memory of the source and not fetched again, by its own estimate 85 to 90 in 100:
Laravel's Request::capture calls enableHttpMethodParameterOverride, createFromBase replaces the request parameters
with the decoded JSON when the request is JSON, and Symfony's getMethod then reads `_method` from them on a POST
with no override header and upper-cases it; routing reads the method after that. Rack::MethodOverride and Spring's
HiddenHttpMethodFilter read form fields only, so the class is Laravel and the Symfony applications that enable the
override. One over-reach of the fixture: Laravel's own test for JSON is case-sensitive, so the row in capitals
(APPLICATION/JSON; charset=utf-8) would not be JSON to Laravel; the two rows in lower case are faithful and
suffice. Not intended and not accepted: docs/policy.md promises any other request a 403 with the value unread and
tells the operator to send JSON, which this defeats, and docs/adr/accepted/ holds nothing on overrides. Not a
duplicate: C71's record parks it as an unconfirmed residue. Not high, since a host without such a framework is not
affected; not low, since the break is shown on the real package.

What the fix costs, for the maintainer (S8): three shapes, none chosen here. Refusing a JSON media type under a
method rule costs no parser, but most API posts are JSON and the test's own served JSON row would turn. Reading the
body under a bound and refusing a top-level `_method` buffers and parses guest bytes (I10, I12, a fuzz target by
T5) at lines the budget lacks. Saying in docs/policy.md that `method` judges the request line alone leaves the test
failing, so under S4 and S7 only the maintainer can take it. Fix unit S-F57 says the same.

C74. ID I5, the same sentence, for a rule narrowed by method. It is a residue of C68 that S-F51's fix round parked
with no reproduction. Attacker: guest root or hostile model output, choosing the query string of its own request.
Precondition it does not control: the bound host is PHP behind Symfony's HttpFoundation with the parameter override
enabled, as Laravel always enables it. Where: internal/proxy/terminate.go: cgiName lower-cases a name and folds "-"
to "_" only, so admits does not find `.method` in the overrides list, and the Rewrite of the ReverseProxy sends the
query on untouched. also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go. Input: the same rule; the guest sends POST
/v1/x?.method=DELETE, or ?a=b&.method=put, with the placeholder. Effect: PHP stores the name as `_method` in $_GET,
the framework serves DELETE or PUT /v1/x with the real secret, and no refusal is recorded, where `?_method=DELETE`
gets 403.

Reproducing test: TestC74DotMethodQuery, package proxy, 50 lines, escape/_pending/S-F58/c74_test.go; its fake
upstream is a loopback TLS server that, on a POST, takes as the method the upper-cased value of a query parameter
whose name is `_method` once "." is read as "_". Five rows: a plain POST must be served as "POST /v1/x
real-secret", a plain DELETE and `?_method=DELETE` must be refused, and two `.method` rows fail when the answer
names the method outside the rule together with the real secret. Log of the orchestrator's run, the same lines
plain and under -race, and the same the redteam and the verifier saw:

    c74_test.go:47: POST ?.method=DELETE: got (200, "DELETE /v1/x real-secret")
    c74_test.go:47: POST ?a=b&.method=put: got (200, "PUT /v1/x real-secret")

The three control rows pass, so the spelling of the name is the only difference between a refusal and a served
request. Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, which ran the test, traced the path (url.ParseQuery yields

no configuration file, on loopback: parse_str gives `_method` for `.method=DELETE`, and $_GET of POST
/s.php?.method=DELETE&a=b holds `_method` with the request method POST; Symfony's getMethod falls back to the query

reaches `_method` there; an older PHP was not probed. Fix unit S-F58.

C74 FIXED by S-F58, commits d336c8b (the test moved), c17f792 (the fix) and b115d48 (the fix round) (PR #323).
also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go. The shape is the one the unit line named: cgiName in
internal/proxy/terminate.go folds "." to "_" as it folds "-", so under a rule that narrows, a query parameter or a
header named `.method`, or any of the six override names with a dot for an underscore, is refused with 403
binding_mismatch before the broker is asked, as `_method` is (C68). The builder weighed a space and "[" on PHP
8.3.6 and folded "." alone, since neither in place of the dot reaches `_method`.

The fix round, from the one finding of the review (I5, medium, guest root choosing its own query string; R2 held,
every step run, the upstream side on PHP 8.3.6's built-in server): PHP skips leading spaces in the name of an
incoming variable before it folds "." and " " to "_", and reads the name as a C string, so a NUL ends it. So
`?+_method=DELETE`, `?%20.method=DELETE` and `?_method%00=DELETE` land in $_GET as `_method`, and on c17f792 each
was served as DELETE with the real secret and no record. The builder had seen the leading space too and left it
for a reproduction (S1); the reviewer found it alone. cgiName now reads a name as PHP does: leading spaces skipped,
the name cut at the first NUL, then "-", "." and " " to "_" in lower case. The space is folded because PHP stores
`x%20http%20method%20override` as `x_http_method_override`. "[" is not folded: a leading "[" drops the parameter,
`_method[` lands as `_method_`, and `_method[]` lands as an array, which Symfony's InputBag does not hand out as a
string. Only spaces are trimmed, so `%09_method` stays a name of its own on PHP and is still served.

Honest cost: under a rule that narrows, a header or query parameter whose name folds to one of the six override
names by letter case, leading spaces, a NUL, or "-", "." or a space for "_" is answered 403; docs/policy.md says so
in one parenthesis. Still served under the narrowed rule: `?method=`, `?%20method=`, `?a.b=`, `?a%20b=`, a path
such as /v1/x.json. A rule that narrows nothing serves every one of them as before. The test:
TestC74DotMethodQuery in internal/proxy/c74_test.go, eight rows, its upstream reading a name as PHP does; on main's
terminate.go the two `.method` rows and the three of the fix round fail, on c17f792 those three alone, on b115d48
none, plain and under -race. Its control rows are unchanged: the plain POST is served with the secret, and the
plain DELETE and the `_method` spelling get the 403. As S-F55's and S-F57's records hold, this lists one more
reading of an upstream (the fifth: header, form, JSON, header spelling, parameter spelling) and does not make a
rule on the method whole; the maintainer may still prefer the third shape of S-F57.

keeps the v1 line of C54 and C72.

### S-1021 candidates, sweep 3

C75. ID I5 ("Real credential bytes never exist in guest memory, disk, environment, arguments or logs"), the class
of C54, C58 and C72. It is the residue of C72, as C72 was of C54: seen by S-F56's builder, parked for want of the
end of the chain, now reproduced. Attacker: guest root or hostile model output, reading /workspace in clone mode or
the live tree under --mount. Precondition it does not control: the operator's [[secret]] row has a cmd: source
whose program lies outside the working directory and one of whose words is a list that names the working directory
itself before a separator: `--dir=<cwd>:<out>/b` or `--dir=<cwd>,<out>/b`. Where: cmd/workcell/policy.go,
loadPolicy, the source loop: a word is judged from its first slash and after each `:` or `,`, with each lexical
ancestor of those texts. The word from its first slash is `<cwd>:<out>/b`, whose ancestors `<cwd>:<out>` and
`<cwd>:` do not lie within the directory, and the text after the separator lies outside it, so nothing judged is
the directory. also in v1 main: credbroker/cli.go, as C54's record has it. Input: a user config that allows
api.anthropic.com, with [[secret]] name "anthropic" and source `cmd:/bin/sh <out>/get-key.sh --dir=<cwd>:<out>/b`
(or the comma), a key file at <cwd>/.secrets/anthropic.key, and `workcell run` there, clone or --mount. Effect:
loadPolicy accepts the row and mints a binding, the session goes past the export, and in clone mode workspace.ext4
holds the key's bytes, while under --mount the directory is served live; `--dir=<cwd>`, the bare word `<cwd>` and
`--dir=<cwd>/k:<out>/b` are refused with C54's one line before any session directory is made.

    --- FAIL: TestC75WorkspaceBeforeAListSeparator/clone_colon

        c75_test.go:51: I5: session <id> started for cmd:/bin/sh OUT/get-key.sh --dir=WORK:OUT/b: under --mount

The three control arms pass, and no arm reports a helper that missed the key. Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the

word `<cwd>:<out>/b` and `--dir=<cwd>:` each load with one binding and no error, and `--dir=<cwd>`, the bare word
`<cwd>`, `--dir=<cwd>/k:<out>/b`, `--dir=<cwd>/:<out>/b` and `--dir=<out>/b:<cwd>` are refused with C54's line. So
the controls are refused by the very check in question, and a separator joined to the directory's last name is the

repository, the first shape below in one condition, `within(cwd, q) || within(cwd, strings.TrimRight(q, ":,"))`:
this test and those of C19, C28, C29, C54, C58 and C72, with TestBindings and TestProviderPolicy, then pass. So the
test fails for the cause it names and passes once the row is refused.

Its ruling on the question the unit line put first: this is not "a program that reaches the directory by its own
logic", which S-F56's line names as not judged. That clause is about a program whose command line does not spell
the directory (a fixed path, a config file, $HOME). Here the operator's own word spells the directory's absolute
path, and the helper does no more than the splitting that C72's confirmed helper did for `--key=`, carried to the
list separator that S-F56's fix round itself took on when it judged the text after each `:` or `,` of a word. The
check already refuses the directory named alone and a first list element at every depth below it, so depth zero is
a gap in the check's own promise and no shape outside it. S-F56's record lists this residue as a candidate for R-3,
in a sentence apart from the one on a program's own logic, and docs/policy.md and the refusal text ("keep it
outside") promise that a source inside the directory is refused and say nothing of whole paths alone. On the test's
honesty: it takes only the operator's step, as C54 and C72 did; the clone arms fail on the key's bytes in
workspace.ext4, the mount arms on the session existing, as C54 and C72 were graded; running the helper on the host
gives the attacker nothing and is not what an arm fails on. Not a duplicate (C72's record leaves this residue
unconfirmed), not accepted (docs/adr/accepted/ says nothing of sources), not out of scope (the operator's row is
the precondition of S6, not host root or malware). On the precondition: lists of paths joined by a colon or a comma
in one argument are real (a class path, a search path, a wrapper that takes a list as PATH is written), but the row
must name the project root itself as an element, which the verifier holds to be rarer than C72's
`--key=<cwd>/file`. Not high for that reason, and since a keychain, secret-service or config-directory source is
untouched; not low, since the clone arms show the key's bytes in the export on the real package.

What the fix costs, for the maintainer (S8): three shapes, none chosen here. One, cutting a trailing `:` or `,`
before each text is judged, is one condition, and lists two separators: a probe of the orchestrator, by overlay on
loadPolicy, found that `--map=<cwd>=<out>/b`, `--dir=<cwd>;<out>/b` and `--dir=<cwd>|<out>/b` load with a binding
too, and no test here expresses them. Two, refusing every word of a cmd: source that holds the directory's path
anywhere, covers each of those (the redteam ran such a copy of policy.go by overlay, outside the repository: this
test and those of C72 and C54 pass), and as a plain substring test it also refuses a sibling directory whose name
begins with the directory's. Three, saying in docs/policy.md that only whole paths are judged, leaves the test
failing, so under S4 and S7 only the maintainer can take it. S-F56's record holds that a check on the words of a
command line cannot be made whole by listing spellings; this is the third listing (a whole word, a path inside a
word, the directory before a separator). Fix unit S-F59 says the same.

C75 FIXED by S-F59, commits 2389163 (the test moved and widened), 14102c9 (the fix) and baf3543 (the fix
round, one word of docs/policy.md) (PR #325).
also in v1 main: credbroker/cli.go. The shape is the first of
the three, made whole at both ends, chosen by the orchestrator before the redteam wrote its rows: the source
loop of loadPolicy in cmd/workcell/policy.go no longer lists separators. A word of a cmd: source is read as
paths. One may start at the word's first slash and at the first slash after any separator; one may end at the
word's end, before a slash (the lexical ancestors, as before) and before any separator. A separator is every
ASCII byte that is not a letter, a digit, ".", "_", "-" or "/" (the new one-line predicate sep); a byte of
0x80 or above is part of a name, so no cut falls inside a UTF-8 rune. Each such text that is absolute goes
to within(), which is unchanged, so symbolic links on either side are resolved as before, and the refusal is
C54's one error, unchanged, before any session directory is made. A file: source is one exact path: it shares
the new starts and gets no cut at a separator, so `file:<cwd> (old)/key` loads as before.

Why this shape. The first shape as the unit line gave it lists two separators, and the probe of S-1021 already
had the directory accepted before `=`, `;` and `|`, so it would have been a fourth listing with its residue
known on the day it landed. The second shape, a substring test of the directory's spelling, covers every
separator but resolves nothing, so a symbolic link to the directory named before a separator would pass it,
and it refuses the sibling `<cwd>-keys/x`. The shape taken keeps within() as the one judge, judges every text
that main judged and more, and ends a path at a boundary, so a sibling whose name goes on with a name byte
loads. The third shape (say in docs/policy.md that only whole paths are judged) stays open to the maintainer (S8).

Honest cost. Under cmd: a sibling directory whose name is the working directory's name followed by a separator
byte, `<cwd>+old/x` or `<cwd>~/x`, is refused, by an error that says it lies inside the directory; `<cwd>-keys`,
`<cwd>.bak`, `<cwd>_old` and `<cwd>2` load. A character outside ASCII never separates, so the directory before a
full-width colon loads; no program is known to split a list there, and docs/policy.md says "ASCII". Not judged,
as before: a program that reaches the directory by its own logic, a relative path that the program resolves
itself, and a hard link from outside to a key inside. The code: three loop lines changed in place and five lines
for sep, paid by five comment folds (the docs of repoFile and envName in policy.go, of session in run_vm.go, of
artifacts and holds in data.go), product at 15000 of 15000. docs/policy.md has four lines more, three sentences
and a blank, the first words the page has on a source inside the working directory (Markdown 1365 of 2500).

The test: TestC75WorkspaceBeforeAListSeparator in cmd/workcell/c75_test.go, moved from escape/_pending/S-F59/,
which is gone, so escape/_pending/ no longer exists; 61 lines, 17 arms, its first seven unchanged. On main's
policy.go the four separator arms fail, and so do the eight the redteam added against the shape: the bare word
`<cwd>:<out>/b`, `--dir=<cwd>:` alone, `--dir=<cwd>:rel`, `--map=<cwd>=<out>/b`, `--dir=<cwd>;<out>/b` under
--mount, `--dir=<cwd>|<out>/b`, the key after a separator in `--map=<out>/a=<cwd>/.secrets/anthropic.key`, and
a link to the directory in `--dir=<link>:<out>/b`; each with a session started and, in clone mode, the key in
workspace.ext4. The three control arms pass there, and so do two arms that must load on both trees: the sibling
`--dir=<cwd>-keys/x` and `--dir=<out>/a:<out>/b`. On 14102c9 all 17 pass, plain and under -race (redteam on
main, builder and reviewer on the fix, the reviewer on main's policy.go by overlay too). Six arms run in a
directory whose own path holds `=`. The eight rows and the fold of c72_test.go's doc leave test at 28496 of 28500.

The review: one round, no finding. The reviewer ran 541 rows through loadPolicy on both trees: nothing that main
refused loads on the fix, no row wholly outside the directory is refused that main loaded, and the one false

## S-1008, sweep 3: workspace export in both modes, and the return path (I1, I8), as built at main 3972242

Sweep 3 (S8), the last the SPEC allows, fresh context (S3), the whole surface read in full as built after S-F1
to S-F59, not a diff, at the claim commit 4bf6399. The unit line still carries its sweep-1 text (copy four parked
tests for C17 to C20 and run no auditor); those tests are in place, S-F10 to S-F13 are done and escape/_pending/
did not exist, so this run took the other branch of the line's accept and did the audit again as S-1002 says,
as sweep 2 did and as S-1017's record asked. One auditor run on the top tier, finished without a stop: no
model declined and no safeguard re-ran a request. No hypervisor in the cloud session; every probe ran by go
test -overlay against the real fileserve.Server over the package's own harness pipe, from a scratch directory
outside the repository, and every target was an in-process pipe or a file under the test's own temp directory
(S12, T8). The auditor wrote its own trust boundary before it opened any earlier record. No file of this surface
carries `// Ported from v1` (only internal/proxy, internal/secret and internal/audit/lines.go do), so no record
here has a v1 line, and nothing is someone else's project (S14).

Trust boundary. Export (clone): the attacker's bytes are the host directory tree at the working directory, as
a malicious repository, a previous mount guest or a previous pull left it: names, link targets, link topology,
sizes, modes, types, depth and count. They enter at workspace.Export (a descriptor walk, Fstatat and Openat with
NOFOLLOW, Readlinkat, hard links by device and inode) and rootfs.Tree and WriteExt4File, with openSource opening
each file again beneath the export's one descriptor and checking device, inode, size and S_IFREG. Authority:
the operator's uid reads every file beneath the directory and writes one new 0600 image under the session's data
directory. It trusts named() for the directory's identity (C61), holds() for no workcell directory and no mount point
beneath it (C19, C52, C65), and the image's apparent size plus its inode count as the pull's later bound. Mount
(--mount, Linux only): the attacker's bytes are every byte of every FUSE frame on the one vsock 5002 stream;
guest root writes them directly, so the kernel's grammar is no bound. They enter at wire.Conn, fileserve.parse
and op. Authority: the operator's uid runs openat, mkdirat, symlinkat, unlinkat, renameat, pwrite, ftruncate,
fchmod and utimensat relative to directory descriptors beneath the export. It trusts single-component names,
at()'s re-check of the chain by device and inode, the life lock against reused descriptors and half-moved nodes,
single() against a file with a name outside (C41), and the caps maxFDs, maxNodes, grown and the frame pace. Return
path (pull, diff): the attacker's bytes are every Entry, Data and Exit frame from the pull VM's init, which
mounts an image the attacker wrote, so A1 applies there too. They enter at fetch in pull_vm.go, pulled.frame,
guest.DecodeEntry, manifest.add, checkPath and fold, then write and put or compare and sameBytes. Authority:
the operator's uid creates, unlinks, links and writes beneath the destination descriptor through openat2 with
RESOLVE_BENEATH, RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS and RESOLVE_NO_XDEV (Linux) or O_NOFOLLOW_ANY (macOS), one component at
a time, refusing a component that is its directory's .git by inode before and after the create. It trusts the
manifest's byte cap (image size plus inodes times 4096), holds(dest), the TMPDIR rule, named() and the session
lock. Concurrent actors on the host are only the operator's other sessions; a running mount guest controls its
export wholly, so a pull or an export that races it in the same tree gains the guest nothing it lacks. What no
code judged, before the records were read: the work one FUSE frame may ask of the host (the depth of the chain,
the width of a directory page), and allocation against length where growth is charged. Both became candidates.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: parse() walked per opcode against the 7.37 layouts, every index guarded
(fixed(n), the length equations of write and batch_forget, split's NUL rule) and held by FuzzRequest; readdir's
decoding of getdents checks reclen against 19 and len(b); DecodeEntry, DecodeExit and wire.ReadFrame the same,
with FuzzDecode, FuzzPath and FuzzReadFrame (seed corpora only here). Memory is bounded: 64 KiB frames, 16 workers,
maxNodes 2^17, maxFDs 4096, handles within maxFDs, the pull's one million entries and 64 MiB of names. CPU: the
pace of S-F47 bounds frames at 16000 a second on a model of 10 us a frame, and the measured cost of a frame runs
from 25 us to 3.15 ms: C76. Disk: grown charges growth of length and a block per entry (C17, C18 and C57 fixed)
and nothing for a write into a hole of a file that was sparse before the session: C77. The export refuses above
32 GiB, 8.4 million entries or 65000 links, names above 255 and targets above 4095 bytes. Logic and state: put()
traced again for every ordering (a link and then a path through it is ELOOP, a non-empty directory where a file is
wanted is ENOTEMPTY, a host link where a directory is wanted is unlinked and never followed, the same path twice
meets the fold map, .git as any component or by inode meets isGit before and after the create, no setuid bit,
no parent made that was not an entry); the manifest is judged before any byte is written, and Data before the
manifest's end, a Data frame of no bytes, an early Exit and bytes past the last file are each errors; fileserve
answers EIO before INIT and after DESTROY, EPROTO for another major, ENOSYS for LINK, MKNOD, RENAME2, xattrs and
fallocate, masks modes to 0o777, never reuses a node id or a handle, and serves a file of several names read-only
(C41); the export leaves out a socket, FIFO or device and copies a link as a link. Concurrency and check-to-use:
the life lock is read-held by every request that uses a descriptor and write-held by FORGET, RELEASE, RENAME and
Close; at() checks every link of the chain again; a worker blocked in send ends at the 5 s deadline; against a
concurrent mount guest openSource's check of device, inode and size refuses any file but the one the walk saw,
so the bytes copied are always of a file that had a name inside the export; the C61 window stays closed by
`.` and the one descriptor; what C76 adds here is that 16 workers on one guest's requests are the only bound on
parallelism and nothing pins them to --cpus. Cryptography and identity: none by design; identity is device and inode
at the moment of use, node ids are the host's and monotonic, and once{} refuses a second connection to 5000 and
5002. Failure modes: no path fails open; a pull error exits after writing nothing or the documented partial tree;
a failed export removes the image and the session directory; fileserve maps an unknown error to EIO, ends Serve
on any stream error and releases every descriptor; a failed FUSE mount in the guest leaves an empty /workspace;
holds() refuses nothing where /proc/self/mountinfo cannot be read (macOS, as recorded). Downgrade, rollback and
replay: wire version 1 only; the FUSE minor is negotiated down on fixed layouts, so a shorter struct is EINVAL;
INIT twice is EIO; a pull is one shot, a frame out of place is a stream error, and pulling a session twice gives
the same tree. Interaction between surfaces: the file service shares the supervisor process with the proxy, the
resolver and the audit log (A9), and its workers are not under the pin of S-F3, so C76's CPU is taken from them
and from every other session of the host; the export carries the repository's workcell.toml, which only narrows
(I13); a mount guest may leave a workcell.toml, a link or a directory under that name for the next session,
each a narrowing or an ignored file; C56 and C65 stand with their tests green.

Parked leads of this surface, tried again, by the lines of PARKED.md on main at 3972242. Unchanged, no VM or no
Mac here: 17 (the mount dotdot and link-rename rows resolve in the guest kernel), 18 (fallocate, LINK and MKNOD
are ENOSYS, a tmpfs rename is EXDEV), 20 and 21 (os.Root; NFC against NFD on APFS), 66 (the VM rows of C17 and
C18, not written), 67 (its maxFDs note is eased by Go raising the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE to the hard one at start),
86 and 87, 120 and 121 (C41's refusal by Nlink stands), 126, 162, 163, 166 to 170, 185, 188 and 193. Line 124
(compare blocking on a FIFO): the walk skips a FIFO by Fstatat before any open, so only a host actor can place
one after the walk. Line 164 (C56 variants): diff's walk never opens a socket or a FIFO, so it cannot block
on a running session's sockets; the other two variants unchanged. Line 165 (C57, a deep path charged for its
last component only): answered, the pull makes no directory that was not an entry, so each component is sent
and charged. Lines 189 and 190 (C64, S-F47): the pace holds the rate of requests near 16000 a second as those
lines reasoned; what it does not hold is the cost of one request, which is C76.
