### S-1008 candidates, sweep 3

C76. ID I10 ("The guest cannot exhaust host CPU, memory, disk, file descriptors, processes or log volume"), host
CPU in mount mode, the class of C64 with the bound C64's fix did not set; A1 in that the pace of S-F47 holds only
for requests of the cost an honest kernel's usual ones have. Attacker: root in the guest of a --mount session,
by hostile model output or a hook of a malicious repository. The chain shape needs no raw frames and no root:
any guest process can mkdir and chdir a few hundred levels and stat there from several threads. The page shape
at 61440 bytes needs the init's 5002 socket, taken as fuseFlood takes it. Precondition it does not control:
the operator chose --mount (A5), nothing else. Where: internal/fileserve/serve_linux.go: loc() copies the whole
ancestor chain of a node under s.mu, one link per level, and at() makes one Fstatat per link on every request
that names a node; ops_linux.go: readdir() makes per entry of a page an Fstatat and, for READDIRPLUS, child(),
which for a directory entry is an openat, an fstat and a close even when the node is in the table; rename()
walks the chain under s.mu too; Serve paces frames, paceFrames per paceEvery (16000 a second), and hands them
to 16 workers that nothing pins. No code bounds the depth of the tree served or the work one frame may ask for;
the pin of S-F3 covers Firecracker's threads and not the supervisor's goroutines, and the proxy and the audit log
share that process (A9). Not ported. Input: (a) MKDIR d and LOOKUP d repeated to a depth of hundreds or thousands
(each level holds one host descriptor, maxFDs 4096 is the only bound, and the chain stays pinned because children
keep parents), then GETATTR of the deepest node, or LOOKUP of missing names under it, from 16 or more guest
threads or as raw frames with the replies drained; (b) a directory of some thousand subdirectories, OPENDIR, then
READDIRPLUS(fh, offset 0, size 61440) repeated over 16 handles. Effect claimed: one request costs the host 3.15
ms of CPU at depth 3900 (126 times the 25 us at the root), 1.59 ms for a LOOKUP of a missing name at depth 2000,
1.35 ms for one READDIRPLUS page of 384 entries and 0.84 ms for a READDIR page of 1920; the 16 workers then run
flat out below the pace: a flood of 4096 GETATTRs on the deep node took 3.62 of the session's 4 cores at 1030
requests a second, a READDIRPLUS flood 2.90 cores at 1023 a second, against the allowance of one vCPU plus a
second that cpuJudge gives (C64 failed that judge at 5.3 CPU seconds in 3.4 s). The bound is the lesser of 16
and the host's cores: the whole machine on a 4-core runner and on most developer hosts. Auditor's evidence:
two probes by go test -overlay on the package's own harness, their lines above; the CPU figures include the
harness's own goroutine, which a flood at the root bounds at 0.43 cores in all. Severity claimed: high by the
precedent of C17 and C18, medium if --mount is read as a precondition under S6, as C64's verifier read it.

Reproducing test: TestC76WorkOfOneFrame, package fileserve, 67 lines, escape/_pending/S-F60/c76_test.go, written
by the redteam from the claim alone on the package's harness. Two arms, each a flood of one second from a sender
goroutine, ended by a STATFS as marker and drained, and each fails when this process's CPU over wall for the flood
is above 1.5 cores, so that any shape of fix passes: (a) a chain of 300 MKDIRs, then GETATTR of the bottom node;
(b) 512 subdirectories, 16 OPENDIRs, then READDIRPLUS(offset 0, MaxWrite) over the handles in turn. The depth is
300 and not thousands because a pace that counts work would make the building of the chain cost the square of
its depth, and TestDeepChain already wants 300 admitted; on main the redteam saw the same ratio at depths 300,
1000, 2000 and 4000 (3.3 to 3.6 cores). The redteam's caveat: a flood of cheap frames at the full pace costs this
in-process test 0.6 cores plain and 1.6 to 1.75 under -race, harness included, so a depth cap alone that leaves
16000 frames a second of 60 us each would still fail it. Also seen by the redteam: a plain READDIR flood over
a directory of 2000 entries on 16 handles took 3.2 cores, so the frame count as the pace's unit is the common
cause, not the per-entry stats alone.

The orchestrator's run, go test -overlay on main's package at db0dba3, 4 cores: plain, arm (a) "15913 frames under
the pace took 3.53 host cores (3.529525s CPU in 1.00075632s), want at most 1.5" and arm (b) "916 frames under the
pace took 2.65 host cores"; under -race 3.71 cores for 10339 frames and 2.29 for 243. go test ./internal/fileserve/
is green without the overlay.

Verifier: fresh context, the claim, the test and the two logs, no one's reasoning. CONFIRMED, high (medium only
if --mount is read as a precondition under S6), after C17 and C18 and not after C64 and C51. It ran the test as
given (3.41 and 2.71 cores) and then took the harness out of the measure: its own probe, outside the repository,
runs the unchanged Open and Serve in a child process over a unix socketpair and reads the child's CPU from /proc,
so the sender and the reader of replies, which are a real guest's own vCPU, are not counted. The server alone:
GETATTR at depth 0 costs 0.19 cores at 16009 frames a second (the sixth of a core that the comment on the pace
promises), 0.30 at depth 10, 1.47 at depth 100 and 3.21 at depth 300 (6.49 s of CPU in 2.02 s at 14715 a second,
the harness 0.25); READDIRPLUS of 512 directories at MaxWrite 2.54 cores at 975 a second. So what breaks is the
pace's assumption of 10 us a request, not the harness. The attacker has no power it lacks in a session: guest
root writing whole frames on the init's 5002 stream is the precedent of C17 and C64 and ADR-005's own words,
the inputs are 300 MKDIRs (TestDeepChain shows the service serves that chain), 512 MKDIRs and 16 OPENDIRs,
and the flood needs 15000 frames of 54 bytes a second, where the real-VM row mount-cpu-flood showed a guest
of one vCPU writing 2.75 million frames in 3 s. Nothing else bounds it: only the Firecracker child is pinned
(internal/vmm/firecracker/firecracker.go), serveMount runs in unpinned goroutines of the supervisor at the default
GOMAXPROCS, with no cgroup and no rlimit, so the bound is 16 workers and the reader, the whole host on any machine
of up to 17 cores. C64 and C51 were low because their overrun was bounded near one core by short workers; here
the workers are long, and the server's 3.2 cores plus the guest's one fill the hosted 4-core runner, about three
times what the judge of mount-cpu-flood allows. Facts it added: a plain READDIR of the 512-entry directory at
MaxWrite costs the server 2.47 cores at 8800 frames a second; READDIRPLUS at the 4096-byte page that the guest
kernel itself asks for costs 2.79 cores at 11588 a second, so the kernel's page size is no mitigation and an `ls`
loop through the kernel drives the same cost; READDIRPLUS of 512 regular files costs 2.58 cores, so child()'s
work in the node table and the Fstatat per entry carry the cost and not the open of a directory alone; the cost
is linear in depth, and a chain of 100 alone passes one core.

Verdict: C76 CONFIRMED, high (S6; I10, guest root in a --mount session, no precondition beyond the operator's
--mount, as C17 and C18 were graded). Fix unit S-F60. No VM ran: the evidence is Go-level on the real Server,
in process and in a child process, and a real-VM row is left to the fix unit where test lines allow.

C77. ID I10, host disk in mount mode: the cap that --disk sets and the row mount-disk-flood enforces, the class
of C17 and C18 with one gap left in the charge by length. Attacker: root in the guest of a --mount session,
through the ordinary kernel path (dd conv=notrunc, or any write into a file at an offset below its length); no raw
frames. Precondition it does not control: a sparse file lies in the exported tree before the session, the operator's
own (a VM image, a database file, a download in progress, a truncate -s). Where: internal/fileserve/serve_linux.go,
grow(): it charges the end of a write less the file's size, so a write at an offset below the length is free;
opWrite in ops_linux.go calls it before the pwrite, and TestGrowthCap's own words are "Writes in place are
free". The model of cost is the file's length; the host pays in blocks. Not ported. Input: a file of 256 MiB
made by truncate before the open (one block on disk); INIT, LOOKUP, OPEN O_WRONLY, then WRITE(offset i MiB,
60000 bytes) for i from 0 to 39 against a cap of 100000; FSYNC. Effect claimed: every write is accepted, none is
ENOSPC, and the host's blocks for the file grow by 2,461,696 bytes against a cap of 100,000; scaled, the guest
fills every hole of every sparse file in the tree, to the full apparent size of the operator's sparse files,
beyond --disk. The guest's own sparse files are paid for (a SETATTR or a write that sets a length is charged in
full), so only holes that were there before are free; a sparse file that an earlier mount session's guest left,
charged at that session's cap, is filled free by the next, about twice the cap a session. Auditor's evidence: a
probe by go test -overlay, "40 writes of 60000 bytes into holes accepted, 0 ENOSPC; host blocks grew by 2461696
bytes against a cap of 100000", with TestGrowthCap, TestGrowthCapAppend and TestGrowthCapEntries passing on the
same tree. Severity claimed: medium by S6, a shown break with a precondition the attacker does not control.

Reproducing test: TestC77WritesIntoHoles, package fileserve, 52 lines, escape/_pending/S-F61/c77_test.go, written
by the redteam from the claim alone on the package's harness. The host side makes export/sparse as an empty file
truncated to 256 MiB, and the test skips, naming the count of blocks, where the temp directory's filesystem
stores no holes; then a cap of 100000, LOOKUP, OPEN O_WRONLY, 40 WRITEs of 60000 bytes one megabyte apart, an
FSYNC through the service, and it fails when the growth of st.Blocks times 512 is above the cap plus two blocks,
by blocks alone, so that a fix may answer any errno. Also noted by the redteam, not tested: the same free write
holds for any file whose blocks are fewer than its length, such as reflinked or compressed extents.

The orchestrator's run, go test -overlay on main's package at db0dba3, plain and under -race alike: "I10: the
host's blocks for the sparse file grew by 2461696 bytes against a growth cap of 100000, with 40 of 40 writes of
60000 bytes into its holes accepted".

Verifier: fresh context, the claim, the test and the two logs, no one's reasoning. CONFIRMED, and by its evidence
high, not the medium claimed. It ran the test through an overlay of its own with TestGrowthCap beside it:
TestGrowthCap passes and TestC77WritesIntoHoles fails with the line above, plain and under -race. The effect is
judged by st.Blocks, real allocation. The cause it read in the code: grow charges the end less st.Size and charge
returns 0 for nothing or less, so opWrite charges nothing for any write that ends below the length. No power
the attacker lacks: INIT, LOOKUP, OPEN O_WRONLY and a WRITE below the length are the frames a guest kernel's
FUSE client sends for dd conv=notrunc seek=N or a pwrite into an existing file, and the cap is the product's,
since startCapped calls fileserve.Open(export, limit) as openMount in cmd/workcell/mount_linux.go does with
limits.disk(). Not intended: the comment on the charge in serve_linux.go promises that "the host loses at most
limit however the guest mixes them", caps.go says --disk "is how many bytes the guest may write in all", and no
page (ADR-005, docs/policy.md, the explain text) exempts writes in place or names sparse files; TestGrowthCap's
free overwrite is of a dense file, which costs the host nothing; the judge of mount-disk-flood measures apparent
size and free disk against the probe's own writes and never meets a hole that was there before. The precondition:
the attacker can supply it. A checkout by git 2.43 streams a blob and seeks over runs of zeros, so a repository
with a blob of 256 MiB of zeros and one other byte (a pack of 1.4 MB) was checked out with 40 blocks, 20 KiB,
for 268435456 bytes of length. A malicious repository (SPEC section 2) plants the hole at no cost to itself,
so S6's precondition the attacker does not control does not apply. Facts it added: within one session the guest
cannot make a hole for free (SETATTR of a size is charged by apparent size and FALLOCATE is ENOSYS); across two
sessions it can truncate a file to --disk in the first, charged and with no blocks, and fill it free in the second,
twice the cap for that session though the sum of the two caps in all; the row mount-disk-flood cannot see this,
so the Go test is the place for the regression, as for C17 and C18; the test skips where the filesystem stores
no holes, and /tmp here is ext4.

The orchestrator's probe of that fact, outside the repository: a repository with one file of 64 MiB of zeros,
cloned locally by git 2.43.0, has that file at 131072 blocks in the source tree and at 8 blocks in the clone's
working tree.

Verdict: C77 CONFIRMED, high (S6; I10, guest root in a --mount session with a malicious repository, no precondition
the attacker does not control, as C17 and C18 were graded; the auditor and the redteam held medium for want of
the checkout fact). Fix unit S-F61.

Sweep 3 now stands at two highs (C76 and C77, both open, fix units S-F60 and S-F61), ten mediums (C65, C66, C67,

C76 FIXED by S-F60, commits 39e2340 (the test moved), 1a50388 (the fix) and b31a965 (the fix round, two
constants, after a red hosted gate) (PR #327).
The shape is the first of the three, a pace that counts work, chosen by the orchestrator before the redteam ran
and written as a contract of behaviour: no depth cap and no smaller page, every request that main answers is
answered with the same bytes, and only the moment at which Serve takes the next frame changes. In
internal/fileserve/serve_linux.go the reader's count is now in points, unit (40) to the old unit: a frame costs
one unit as before and a BATCH_FORGET one more per perForget entries, so TestPace's arithmetic is unchanged.
Workers charge an atomic tally on the Server, and the reader folds it in before every frame: two points for
each link of the chain that at() is about to stat, charged before the loop so that an error path pays too; one
point for every 24 bytes that a getdents returned to readdir(), which is the most entries those bytes can
hold; and plusEntry (40) for every READDIRPLUS entry made. A point stands for about 0.75 us of host CPU.
Nothing is rounded away between frames, and what is over one period is slept off period by period and not
forgiven. No new option, name, hook or reply. The depth cap and the page clamp were not built: the unit line
shows that neither passes alone, and each refuses or changes something an honest guest does.
Constants, and what set them. The contract asked for 30 us of measured CPU a unit. The listed bytes sit there.
A link is charged 1.5 us and a READDIRPLUS entry 30 us, against 0.9 us and 4 to 8 us measured plain on this
machine, and both for the test's sake and not the plain cost's: the test judges its own process under -race,
where an entry costs about 30 us, and the hosted runner pays about 1.7 times what this machine pays for the
same frames. The first constants (one point a link, plusEntry 20) passed here at 0.95 to 1.09 cores (arm a)
and 0.83 to 0.88 (arm b) under -race, passed the hosted gate once on 1a50388, and failed it on the same code
at afdd911: arm (a), 1862 frames, 1.70 cores against 1.5. So the first green was luck, and the fix round
doubled both charges to leave that runner room.
Evidence. TestC76WorkOfOneFrame, bound 1.5 cores: on main it fails in both arms (redteam: 3.34 and 2.76 plain,
3.67 and 2.30 under -race; reviewer, on an archive of main: 3.54 and 2.65). On the final constants it passes
five runs of five plain and five of five under -race, alone: arm (a) 0.28 to 0.29 cores plain and 0.47 to 0.58
under -race, arm (b) 0.13 to 0.15 and 0.47 to 0.50. The whole package passes under -race here, TestPace,
TestDeepChain and FuzzRequest's seeds included. The reviewer's floods, run on the first constants, in process
with the harness counted: plain READDIR of 20 thousand files at MaxWrite 0.37 cores, READDIRPLUS at 4096 bytes
over 512 directories 0.25 (3.15 on main), a LOOKUP storm 0.49 (0.52 on main), RENAME at depth 300 0.50,
OPENDIR at depth 300 0.53; the fix round only raised charges, so none of these can cost more now.
Hosted gate. On 1a50388, the first constants: green in 285 s with gate-macos, gate-arm64 and guard; the suite
ran on a real VM, 147 rows passed and none failed, mount-cpu-flood with 3.3 CPU seconds in 3.5 s of wall
against 4.5 allowed, mount-disk-flood and the seven I1 mount rows passed, P1 p50 317 ms. On 5ddb0bc, a commit
of state files only: red from a known flake that this fix does not touch, I12 channel-connect-flood, 65 MiB
of available memory lost where the same code lost 58 before; its other 146 rows passed. On afdd911, the same
code again: red from this fix's own test, as said above. The hosted result on the final constants is in
LOG.md, in this unit's entry, since this record is pushed with them.
No VM row holds C76. The redteam added none: a GETATTR flood on the init's own stream draws a reply for a
unique the guest kernel never issued, which the probe cannot read without breaking that stream, and this
session has no hypervisor to try a row on. So the evidence for C76 is Go-level, on the real Server.
Cost to honest use, measured and not small. Charged work on the final constants: a GETATTR at depth 30 is 60
points, 1.5 units over the frame's one; a READDIRPLUS page of 4096 bytes, 25 entries, is 1341 points, 33.5
units, of which 341 points are the 8 KiB that readdir() reads for every page whatever size was asked; a
plain READDIR page of 4096 bytes is 341 points, 8.5 units. With one request in flight and an in-process
client, which answers faster than any guest: 20000 GETATTRs at depth 30 take 3.12 s where main took 1.29 s
(main is at its pace there already), and a READDIRPLUS walk of 4000 files in 4096-byte pages takes 300 to
385 ms where main took 34 to 38 ms. A client with one request in flight never meets the pace at depth 30 if a
round trip takes 156 us or more, and on such a walk only if a page takes 2.16 ms or more. So the unit line's
wish, that honest use is not slowed where it was not before, is not met. A build in a tree 30 deep keeps a
pace of 6400 requests a second, the top of what ADR-005 measured for honest traffic, and an `ls -l` of
thousands of entries is slowed about nine times on its page fetches, near a tenth of a millisecond an entry.
No row of the suite times either shape in a real guest; the mount rows show only that nothing broke.
For the maintainer to weigh, since none of it is a fix for a confirmed finding and so none could land in the
freeze (S1): the charge is as dear as it is because of how the test measures, not because of what a guest can
cost a host. Two things would let it fall with no loss to I10: a measure that is not this process under the
race detector on a shared runner, and a readdir() that fetches no more than the page asked for. Charging the
entries sent and not the bytes read, as the review noted in passing, would not do: by the orchestrator's
reading, not tested, a READDIR that asks for a page too small for one entry still reads 8 KiB and would then
be free. A charge by the time a worker spent, and not by a count of what it did, would hold on any host and
under any detector, but it also charges a wait for the disk, and it is a design and not a constant.
Folds: the fix is net zero product lines, paid by joining lines of the docs of the pace, perForget, at() and
readdir() and by one bytes.Cut for the six lines that cut a name at its NUL (product 15000 of 15000, test
28494 of 28500). Review: one round on the first constants, no finding; its notes are in PARKED.md. The fix
round came from the hosted gate and not from the review, and was not reviewed again (R1).

Sweep 3 now stands at two highs (C76 fixed, C77 open, fix unit S-F61), ten mediums (C65, C66, C67, C68, C69,
C71, C72, C73, C74 and C75, all fixed) and two lows (C64 and C70, both fixed). The next candidate number is C78
and the next fix unit S-F62.

C77 FIXED by S-F61, commits 6c0ccce (the test moved, and a second arm), 943d9f2 (the fix) and 66df578 (the fix
round, after the review) (PR #328).
The shape is neither of the unit line's two as written, and the orchestrator chose it before the redteam ran,
as a contract of behaviour: before the host writes, a WRITE is charged for how far it extends the length, as
before, and for the part of its range that lies in a hole below the length, in whole blocks of the host's
filesystem, since the host allocates whole blocks. grow() in internal/fileserve/serve_linux.go now takes the
write's offset: one lseek with SEEK_HOLE from the offset rounded down to a block (st.Blksize of the Fstat it
already made), and if that hole begins below both the write's end rounded up and the length, the charge runs
from the hole to the lesser of the two. A WRITE whose charge does not fit is refused whole with ENOSPC, as
before; a WRITE into data is charged nothing, as before; nothing is given back. ENXIO from the lseek means no
hole below the length; any other error refuses the request with that errno. SETATTR size passes no range, makes
no lseek and is charged by length as before.
Why not the two shapes of the line. The shorter one, the whole of len(r.Data) when a hole lies in the range,
under-charges small writes: one byte into each of 200 blocks of a hole is 200 bytes charged and 819,200 bytes
of host blocks, which is the second arm the redteam added to the test. The longer one, a walk of the range by
SEEK_HOLE and SEEK_DATA, makes one frame over a file of alternating blocks cost hundreds of system calls
whether it is accepted or refused, which is C76's class (work of one frame that the pace does not count). One
lseek is constant work; its price is an over-charge when data follows the first hole inside one write's range
(builder's probe: 15 alternating blocks, 7 of them holes, a WRITE of 61,440 bytes at 0 charged 14 blocks;
reviewer's: hole then data, 12,288 charged for 8,192 allocated), the safe side.
The three things the line asked to weigh. Two writers racing into one hole are both charged: each charges
before its own pwrite and as if alone. A file that an earlier session's guest truncated up and left empty is
now charged when a later session fills it, since the fill is into a hole. A file whose blocks are fewer than
its length for another cause, reflinked or compressed extents, is NOT closed: SEEK_HOLE does not show it, and
to charge it would be to charge every overwrite in place, which the accept line forbids. It needs a host
filesystem that the attacker does not choose, and what it can take is bounded by the apparent size of the files
that lay in the tree before the session. It is parked with the other notes.
Cost to honest use. On ext4 the lseek is in the noise: 20000 WRITEs of 4096 bytes in place into a dense file,
one in flight, 61.8 to 62.1 us each against 61.7 to 61.9 on main. A file grown by SETATTR size and then filled
below that length is charged twice, once for the length and once for the hole, since the charge keeps no state
per file (builder's probe, cap 100,000: SETATTR to 90,000 and then 64 WRITEs of 4096, 1 accepted and 63
refused, where main took 23). So a program that sets its output's length first and then fills it, as some
linkers and a copy that keeps holes do, gets half the cap for that file. A hole in an unwritten, preallocated
extent and a filesystem whose st_blksize is far above its allocation unit (a network filesystem) are charged
more than they take. All of it is the safe side for I10 and none of it is free to an honest guest.
Review: one round, one valid finding (I10, host CPU, guest root in a --mount session, medium: it needs the
export on tmpfs or another filesystem whose SEEK_HOLE walks the page cache). The first fix made every WRITE and
SETATTR size pay that lseek, and on tmpfs it costs the length of the dense data from the offset on: 5.3 ms of
CPU for a one-byte WRITE at 0 of a dense file of 1 GiB against 30 us on main, and with 16 files of 63 MiB made
by the guest inside the cap and 16 one-byte WRITEs in flight, 3.26 host cores of 4 against 0.26 on main, all at
one unit of pace a frame. The fix round (66df578) charges the time the lseek took to the pace, in points of
0.75 us, and makes no lseek for a SETATTR. The same flood then takes 0.47 cores (builder, reviewer's probe on a
scratch copy; 3.38 measured there on 943d9f2), and a flood on one dense file of 1 GiB 0.50 cores with one
request in flight and 0.23 with 16. This is the charge by time that C76's record called a design and not a
constant, taken here for one system call only: it also charges a wait, so a cold extent tree paces a guest for
a moment. Cost on a tmpfs export, for the maintainer: a rewrite in place low in a large dense file pays the
walk on every WRITE (440 us at 64 MiB, 4.5 ms at 1 GiB) and is paced by it, about a hundred such WRITEs a
second at 1 GiB; an append pays nothing, since its offset is at the end. To skip the lseek when the file's
blocks cover its length would spare honest dense files, but the reviewer showed that it is no bound alone (a
tail hole made by one SETATTR brings the walk back), so it would be a saving beside the charge and not in its
place; it was not built in the freeze (S1). No test holds the review's finding: a steady one needs about 19
lines and tmpfs, test has 3 lines of room, and a bound on CPU judged under -race is what S-F60 found thin. Its
evidence is the reviewer's and the builder's probes on the real Server, not kept in the tree. The fix round was
not reviewed again (R1).
Evidence. TestC77WritesIntoHoles in internal/fileserve/c77_test.go, two arms over one body, judged by st.Blocks
after FSYNC against the cap plus two blocks: on main it fails in both (2,461,696 bytes with 40 of 40 writes of
60000 accepted; 819,200 bytes with 200 of 200 writes of one byte accepted, against 100,000), plain and under
-race, seen by the redteam and again by the reviewer on an archive of main. On the fix it passes without
skipping, five of five plain and under -race on 943d9f2 and three of three on 66df578, on ext4. The package
passes under -race on 66df578, TestGrowthCap (its row "overwrite in place" still 0), TestGrowthCapAppend,
TestGrowthCapEntries, TestPace and TestC76WorkOfOneFrame included. Hosted, on 943d9f2: gate green in 289 s
with gate-macos, gate-arm64 and guard, 147 rows passed on a real VM and none failed, mount-disk-flood (the host
lost 63 MiB under a cap of 64), mount-cpu-flood (3.4 CPU seconds in 3.5 s) and the six I1 mount rows among
them. The hosted result on 66df578 is in LOG.md, in this unit's entry, since this record is pushed with it.
No VM row holds C77: mount-disk-flood writes past the end and into no hole that was there before the session,
the unit line asked for none, and test has no lines for one.
The words. The doc of grown and limit now names the hole charge, so "the host loses at most limit however the
guest mixes them" holds for what the server can see, to within a block of slack a file (reviewer: a write into
a hole in the last, partial block is charged only its bytes inside the length) and not for extents that
SEEK_HOLE does not show. cmd/workcell/caps.go and docs/policy.md say nothing that the fix made false and are
unchanged. Folds: net zero product lines in both rounds, paid by joining lines of the docs of maxNodes, node,
setattr, rename, readdir and the package (product 15000 of 15000). The second arm cost 3 test lines (test 28497
of 28500).

Sweep 3 now stands at two highs (C76 and C77, both fixed), ten mediums (C65, C66, C67, C68, C69, C71, C72, C73,
C74 and C75, all fixed) and two lows (C64 and C70, both fixed). The next candidate number is C78 and the next

## S-1009, sweep 3: policy loading and merge, CLI parsing, `--allow`, adapter data files (I13), as built at main b38a0fa

Sweep 3 (S8), the last the SPEC allows, fresh context (S3), the whole surface read in full as built after S-F1
to S-F61, not a diff, at the claim commit b1f9da8. One auditor run on the top tier, finished without a stop: no
model declined and no safeguard re-ran a request. No hypervisor in the cloud session, and nothing on this surface
needed a VM: every probe ran by go test -overlay on package main of cmd/workcell or against a binary built in a
scratch directory outside the repository, and the only listener was an httptest TLS server on loopback (S12, T8).
The auditor wrote its own trust boundary before it opened any earlier record. Result: two candidates, C78 (I5,
medium) and C79 (I14 hardening, low), each given to the redteam as a claim only, run by the orchestrator, and
ruled on by its own verifier; the records are below. Nothing was fixed (S1). cmd/workcell and internal/policy
carry no `// Ported from v1`; C78 leans on how internal/secret/source.go runs a cmd: source, which is ported,
so its record keeps the v1 line of C54 and C72. Nothing is someone else's project (S14).

Trust boundary. Attacker bytes enter this surface by (a) <cwd>/workcell.toml, owned by the malicious repository
and, under --mount, by guest root between runs: loadPolicy in cmd/workcell/policy.go, ReadRepo in internal/policy
(O_NOFOLLOW and O_NONBLOCK, fstat on the opened descriptor, a regular file, a 1 MiB cap, [update] refused), Parse
(the project's own TOML subset) and Narrow, of which only an allow entry's text and a secret row's name are ever
compared; (b) the working directory itself, its name, links and mounts, exported or served live, judged by holds,
within, named and the TMPDIR rule; (c) files the guest writes indirectly (workspace.ext4, the caches) and the
network (channel.json, artifacts), which this surface only names. Typed by the operator and not the attacker's:
argv (parseRun, allowFlag, cacheFlag, the flags of update, log, verify and pull, validID), the environment
(XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME and HOME under the IsAbs rule of S-F14, TMPDIR under boot's, TERM, SSL_CERT_FILE
and SSL_CERT_DIR in the proxy), the user's config.toml ([[secret]] sources and the C54 check, [update]) and the
embedded provider TOML, fixed at build time and checked by provider.parse. Authority: the supervisor as the
operator's uid before any VM exists. It decides the proxy's maps, the resolver's names, the session CA's permitted
names, the forward ports on the kernel command line, which rows become broker grants and terminate rules (I5),
what the guest sees as /workspace (I1, I13), where data and config live (I7, I9) and what the installer trusts
and installs (I14).

Lenses (S9), each worked in turn.
1. Parsing and resources. FuzzParse for 90 s, 3,212,414 executions, no crasher. By the built binary: a file of
   1 MiB and one byte refused; 20,000 [[secret]] rows naming the user's row narrowed in 54 ms and 30,000 allow
   entries in 50 ms; a FIFO and a symlink as workcell.toml ignored with one line and the user's grants kept, the
   ceiling; [update] in the repository refused at its line; control bytes and non-ASCII outside strings refused,
   and escapes inside a repository string reach only the quoted note. Fifteen --allow forms: the empty value, a
   space, `#`, U+00A0, an IPv4 address, `[::1]:443`, ports 0 and 65536, a leading hyphen, `a_b`, `*.` and
   `a:443:x` refused; a trailing dot and capitals made canonical. Held.
2. Logic and state. Narrow's three rules run through the binary: a repository that widens or respells keeps
   nothing of it and lands in the note; a provider-filled row whose host the repository drops is refused by
   bindings; `allow = []` with `--allow api.anthropic.com` brings back the host and, for a provider-filled row,
   its binding, which is the operator's approval and which explain shows; the C34 check refuses both of its
   shapes, also when --allow gives the hosts back. run refuses a bad repository line before the data directory
   exists. C78 was found here.
3. Concurrency, ordering and check-to-use. ReadRepo judges the descriptor it opened; the policy is fixed before
   boot; named() (C61) refuses a working directory whose name no longer names the process's directory, so a swap
   between loadPolicy and Export is refused; a mount guest that rewrites its own workcell.toml between runs gets
   a narrowing or the ceiling. Nothing new.
4. Cryptography and identity. The [update] key is 32 bytes; ca replaces the roots of the installer's client
   (C79); placeholders come from crypto/rand; the session CA's permitted names are the canonical terminated hosts.
5. Failure modes. Every error path of loadPolicy, parseRun, allowlist, bindings and newInstaller fails closed
   (an unreadable user config, a socket, over 1 MiB, a bad line, a repository [update], a row without name or
   source, HOME unset or relative, a secret row with no allow). Open by design: a missing or non-regular
   workcell.toml gives the user's own grants, the ceiling.
6. Downgrade, rollback and replay. cooloff only lengthens and a huge value is refused; channel is stable, hold
   or https; the serial floor advances only after a verify; --to chooses from the manifest's current and previous
   less the withdrawn. Nothing on this surface.
7. Interaction with other surfaces. Narrowing against the I5 checks (the C34 and C58 shapes hold; C78 is the
   source check against the HOME the broker hands a helper); the layers of every provider attach whatever the
   policy says, a PATH entry and no grant; explain prints the same allow, note and bindings that run uses.

Earlier leads tried again. The PARKED line of S-1007's sweep-3 notes on C72 named `~/` and `$PWD/` as left for
the helper's shell: `~`, `$HOME` and `${HOME}` reproduce as C78, and `$PWD` is harmless because the broker runs
the helper from `/` and does not pass PWD (the verifier's probe: exit status 2). The provider host dropped by the
repository is still refused by bindings; a non-regular workcell.toml is still ignored, the ceiling; --allow after
a dropping repository is as lens 2 says. The tests of C21, C22, C34, C54, C58, C59, C60, C61, C62, C65, C72 and
C75 are green under -race, and the C59 fix holds for every relative spelling; C79 is its absolute sibling. Reasoned
against the code and not run again, unchanged and R3 as recorded: a repository's broken `./claude` on the start
that applied an update, the "." marker of findLayers, the non-ASCII separator, --rollback and the withdrawn list.

Coverage. Read in full: in cmd/workcell policy.go, main.go, data.go, caps.go, explain.go, layer.go, cache.go,

### S-1009 candidates, sweep 3

C78. ID I5 (real credential bytes never exist in guest disk or memory), through the secret-source check of the
policy loader, the class of C54, C58, C72 and C75; nothing widens, so not I13. ATTACKER: the malicious repository
and guest root, who read /workspace. Precondition the attacker does not control, of the same kind as C72's and
C75's: the operator's [[secret]] row spells the key's path under the working directory through the home, as
`~`, `$HOME` or `${HOME}`, which the helper's shell expands and the check does not. SEVERITY: medium (S6). WHERE:
cmd/workcell/policy.go, the word loop of loadPolicy, which reads each word of a cmd: source from its first slash
and at every separator, and for which `~`, `$`, `{`, `}` and `<` are separators: `~/repo/.secrets/k` and
`$HOME/repo/.secrets/k` are both judged as the text /repo/.secrets/k, which is not under the directory. The
broker (internal/secret/source.go) splits the source on spaces, runs it with no shell of its own from `/`, and
passes HOME, so the path is live in the program. INPUT: HOME an absolute home, the working directory <home>/repo
holding .secrets/anthropic.key; config.toml with [network] allow = ["api.anthropic.com"] and a [[secret]] row
named "anthropic" whose source is `cmd:/bin/sh -c cat<~/repo/.secrets/anthropic.key`, or the same with `$HOME`
or `${HOME}`, or `cmd:<abs>/get-key.sh ~/repo/.secrets/anthropic.key` with a helper that expands its argument;
then workcell run, or workcell run --mount, there. EFFECT: loadPolicy returns no error and a binding, where the
same row with the literal absolute path is refused with the C54 line, and the session goes on past the export:
in clone mode the key's bytes lie in workspace.ext4, which the guest gets as /workspace and may carry out through
an allowed host; under --mount the directory is served live. Reproducing test, by the redteam, who was given the
claim and not the auditor's probe: TestC78SecretPathSpelledFromHome, package main of cmd/workcell, 54 lines,
parked at escape/_pending/S-F62/c78_test.go. Eight arms: `~` in a redirect in clone and mount mode, `$HOME` in
clone mode, `${HOME}` under --mount, a helper given `~` in clone mode and `$HOME` under --mount, and two controls
(the literal absolute path, refused on this tree; a source wholly outside the directory, which loads). It drives
loadPolicy and then session() with temporary XDG directories and the dummy artifacts of the C19 test, runs each
row once as the broker splits it, with HOME alone, and requires that it print the key, and fails on any session
directory made. Run by the orchestrator by go test -overlay on the claim tree, plain and under -race, logs saved:
the six finding arms fail with "I5: session <id> started for cmd:/bin/sh -c cat<~/repo/.secrets/anthropic.key:
under --mount <cwd> is served live as /workspace, else its export holds the key", each after the dummy VMM's
"start firecracker: invalid argument", so after the export, and no arm says the row did not print the key; the
two controls pass. Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, who repeated the run and ruled on three questions.
The row is live by the product's own path and not by the test's imitation: a probe of its own, overlaid into
internal/secret, called secret.Resolve on the three /bin/sh spellings and got the key each time, and exit status
2 for `$PWD`. It is a gap in what the check promises and not a program that reaches the directory by its own
logic: docs/policy.md promises that every path a word of a cmd: source names lies outside the directory, the
product itself hands the helper HOME, and loadPolicy has the same HOME, so the spelling is one it could resolve.
The two helper arms are weaker, since the helper's own eval does the expanding, and the /bin/sh arms carry the
finding alone. Medium and not low: the break is shown, with the key's bytes in workspace.ext4 while a placeholder
is minted. This is the fourth residue of one check (C54, then C58, C72, C75 and now C78), and the earlier records
hold that a reading of a helper's words cannot be made whole by listing spellings, so the maintainer may read it
as the design problem of S8; the third shape of S-F59's line, to say in docs/policy.md that only literal paths
are judged, is still theirs alone to take. Variants no arm expresses, from the redteam: another variable the
broker passes that names an ancestor of the directory, `~user`, a `$(...)` substitution, and a glob such as
`/*/u/repo/.secrets/*`. Not S14: policy.go is v2's own. also in v1 main: credbroker/cli.go. Fix unit: S-F62,
below S-1009 in PLAN.md.

C78 FIXED by S-F62, commits c7a9b71 (the test moved and widened), 8bd4711 (the fix) and 80c0365 (the fix round)
(PR #330).
also in v1 main: credbroker/cli.go. The shape is the second of the three, chosen by the orchestrator before the
redteam wrote its rows: the check reads literal paths only, and loadPolicy in cmd/workcell/policy.go refuses a
word of a file: or cmd: source that holds any of twelve characters, `~`, `$`, a backtick, a backslash, `'`, `"`,
`*`, `?`, `[`, `{`, `;` and `&`: the ten that a shell rewrites in a word, and the two on which it runs a second
command. The refusal is one line that names the config file and its line, the secret, the word and the
directory, and says to spell the path out or to put the line in a script outside the directory; it comes at the
place of C54's check, for the same rows, before any session directory or export, and C54's own line still
refuses a literal path under the directory. A row with none of the twelve behaves as on main. docs/policy.md
says the rule in one sentence and the way out in another. Net zero product lines (the four lines that made the
words became one strings.FieldsFunc, which judges the same words) and net zero test lines (seven joins of
comment lines in the c28, c29, c50, c57, c58, c59 and c60 tests paid for seven in c78_test.go).
Why the second shape and not the first: before choosing, the orchestrator gave dash and bash one word, as the
broker would, and each read a file through a backslash inside a name, a pair of quotes inside a name and a
substitution, and bash through a glob in a redirect and through a brace word; the redteam then showed nine such
rows live on main beside the six of the audit, each loading with a binding, each with the key in the export or
the directory served under --mount, each printing the key when run as the broker splits it. A rule for `~`,
`$HOME` and `${HOME}` would have passed the audit's test and left all nine, and the redteam's variants of the
record above with them (`~user`, another variable, `$(...)`, a glob), which the twelve close. The third shape is
the maintainer's alone.
The fix round came from the one review: `cmd:/bin/sh -c cd;cat<repo/.secrets/anthropic.key` holds none of the
first ten characters, and it loaded with a binding and printed the key, since `cd` with no operand goes to the
HOME that the broker passes and the relative path is then read from there (I5, the malicious repository and
guest root, C78's precondition; the reviewer ran it, with `cd&&`, `exec<` and bash as well, and the orchestrator
ran it again). So `;` and `&` joined the set: one word given to a shell can then hold one simple command or a
pipeline, and neither changes directory for a later read. One arm of the test holds it; it failed on 8bd4711
with the key in the export and passes on 80c0365.
Cost to honest use, which the unit line asks to be said: every row with one of the twelve in a word is refused
wherever the word points, a path far outside the directory included. That takes a helper line that uses the
shell (`cmd:/bin/sh -c cat<~/.keys/k`), an argument with a query or a pattern (`?`, `&`, `*`, `[`), a JSON
argument, and a quoted argument, which was never honoured, since the broker splits on spaces with no quoting. It
takes a file: path whose name holds one as well, though the broker opens a file: path itself with no shell, so
there the refusal buys only one rule for both schemes, as the unit line's second shape has it. The way out is in
the error and in docs/policy.md: the literal path, or the line in a script outside the directory. No row of the
tests or the documents used any of the twelve.
Proved: TestC78SecretPathSpelledFromHome, now 18 arms, fails on main in its fifteen finding arms of c7a9b71 and
passes on the fix in all, its two controls unchanged (the literal path refused, a source wholly outside
loading), plain and under -race; the package passes under -race, the C19, C28, C29, C34, C52, C54, C58, C72 and

and makes no session directory. loop/gate.sh GATE PASS, product 15000 of 15000, test 28499 of 28500. Hosted on

Not closed, and said so: this fix closes what a shell does to a word and nothing else, and the check still reads
a command line as text. The orchestrator's probe on 80c0365, by a test overlay that is not kept: `cmd:/bin/cat
<home without its first slash>/repo/.secrets/anthropic.key`, a relative word and no shell, loads with a binding
and prints the key when run from `/` as the broker runs it, and so does the same after `/bin/sh -c cat<`; `./`
before it is refused. The loop judges such a word from its first slash, as /u/repo/... for a home /home/u, and
the comment there, that a relative word never means the directory, is false of a word read from `/`. It is on
main as well, it is neither C78 nor the review's finding, and no verifier has ruled on it, so nothing landed for

that reaches the directory by its own logic, such as a helper that takes a directory to change to as an option;
and a character outside ASCII that some program rewrites.

C79. ID I14 hardening (the trust root of the host's channel and artifact fetches), with I13 (workspace content
decides a host-side trust root); the absolute sibling of C59, which was a relative `ca` resolved against the
working directory. ATTACKER: the malicious repository, which ships the file in its tree, or guest root under
--mount, who rewrites it. Precondition the attacker does not control: the operator's [update] table names an
absolute `ca` that lies under the directory sessions are run in. SEVERITY: low (S6: hardening, no invariant
shown broken). WHERE: cmd/workcell/update.go, newInstaller, which refuses a `ca` that is not absolute, reads
the file and makes it the only root of the installer's client; nothing relates it to the working directory.
INPUT: config.toml with [update], channel = "https://<host>/channel.json", key = "<64 hex>" and ca =
"<cwd>/certs/corp-ca.pem", a file that holds a certificate of the attacker's choosing; the operator runs workcell
run, update or bench start there. EFFECT: the installer's client trusts the attacker's root alone for that
invocation's fetches, so an attacker on the network path presents its own certificate for the channel host and
the pin URLs. channel.Verify still demands the key, a serial no lower than the last seen and an unexpired
manifest, and the fetch still refuses a digest mismatch, so nothing installs past the checks. Reproducing test,
by the redteam from the claim alone: TestC79UpdateCAUnderTheWorkingDirectory, package main of cmd/workcell, 41
lines, parked at escape/_pending/S-F63/c79_test.go. An httptest TLS server on loopback stands for the attacker's
upstream and its certificate is the `ca` file; after newInstaller a HEAD through the installer's client must not
succeed when the file lies under the directory, and must succeed when it lies beside the config, the control arm.
Run by the orchestrator by overlay, plain and under -race, logs saved: the arm under the directory fails with
"newInstaller and a fetch through its transport from the server holding that certificate gave <nil>; want trusted:
false", and the control passes. Outcome: CONFIRMED at low by the verifier, who repeated the run and found that
the test calls the real newInstaller and that manifest() builds its client from the same transport; that run
reaches it after loadPolicy with the repository as the working directory and before holds(), which never compares
the directory with `ca`, so nothing stops a session there; that the precondition is of the kind already accepted
for C54 and C28; and that it is a finding under R2 and not a matter of use, since the loader refuses every other
host-trusted path the operator names under the directory and no page calls `ca` repository content. Low as C59
and for its reason: the certificate alone does nothing without a place on the network, and with one it gains
only the blocking or replay of a signed manifest; not nothing, since the TLS factor that ADR-004 names beside the
key is handed to the repository. Not expressed: a `ca` reached through a link from outside into the directory,
and one under the data directory. Not S14: update.go is v2's own, nothing ported, no v1 line. Fix unit: S-F63,
below S-1009 in PLAN.md.
C79 FIXED by S-F63, commits f13444a (the test moved, with an arm for a link from outside into the directory),
c8d8ebe (the fix) and a815dd1 (the fix round) (PR #334). newInstaller in cmd/workcell/update.go refuses, before
the file is read and before any transport exists, a `ca` that is not absolute, and one any part of whose path
lies in the working directory or is a link into it: each prefix of the path as written is followed with
filepath.EvalSymlinks, in the order the kernel walks it, and the result goes to within() of data.go with the
directory from os.Getwd. The one line names the config file, `ca`, the value and the directory, "must be an
absolute path no part of which lies in or leads into the working directory", and says to move the file. With a
`ca` set and no working directory to judge by (os.Getwd fails) it is refused too, and within() is never given an
empty directory; with no `ca` nothing changes, whatever Getwd says. update prints the line and exits 2, with
nothing fetched and an empty data directory (the builder ran the built binary). docs/policy.md has its first two
lines on `ca`. Net zero product lines (six added in newInstaller, paid by joining six two-line doc comments in
update.go, no wording of behaviour changed) and one test line fewer (the test grew from 41 lines to 48 with five
arms and a count of the requests its server served, paid by eight joins of comment lines in the c28, c52, c58,
c60, data and log tests): product 15000 of 15000, test 28498 of 28500.
The fix round came from the one review. The first fix (c8d8ebe) was the unit line's shape, within(cwd, ca) beside
IsAbs, and within() judges only where a path ends: a `ca` spelled under the directory that is a link to a file
outside it was accepted and read through the link, so the repository, which ships the link, still chose the root.
The reviewer aimed it at the operator's cache image, <data>/workcell/caches/<name>.ext4, which a guest with
--cache <name>:rw writes and in whose bytes pem.Decode finds a certificate; newInstaller returned nil and a HEAD
to the attacker's server through the installer's client was trusted (I14 with I13, low as C79). The reviewer's

else's project (S14).

Trust boundary. Guest root's bytes reach a record as: the raw SNI of a refused 443 connection (any bytes but a
trailing dot, within a 16 KiB hello), the lower-cased name of a refused DNS query, the port of a relay header to
an unserved port (a uint16, 0 admitted), the one byte of the exit status in session_end, and the rate and timing
of attempts. The malicious repository, and guest root of an earlier --mount session, decide the shape of the tree
that the export walks, and so whether session() reaches boot or removes the session directory: the one place an
in-scope actor removes a record and does not add bytes to one (C83). Hostile model output arrives only through
the guest. The network attacker reaches no record: dial_failed, resolve_failed and blocked_address are constants
with the canonical host. Every other field is a constant, an allowlist key, or the operator's own config. All
writers pass one audit.Log under one mutex: proxy.Deny and the Allowed record before a dial or a served request,
the relay's port_not_allowed and the resolver's name_not_allowed through the one closure in boot, the broker's
durable record, and the supervisor's session_start and session_end. The seal is ed25519 over a domain string, the
session id and the SHA-256 chain head, 194 bytes rewritten in place after every line, under <data>/audit.key
(0600, minted O_EXCL on first use). The readers are audit.Verify, ParseLine and the ported eachLine, and the log
verb's feed, denyMessage and ocsfLine, which pass the one free-form field through SafeHost. Pull and bench boots
pass a nil log, every Note and Record of which returns ErrClosed, and have no listeners.

Parsing and resources. Probe TestProbeHostileFieldsThroughLogVerbs (package main): 18 hostile hosts (a newline
with a forged session_end object, OSC, C1 CSI, U+202E, U+2028, U+0085, NUL, 300 bytes of 0xFF, 200 e-acute, the
Kelvin sign, quotes, 16 KiB of x, `-mount`, `--allow`, `..`, empty, a trailing dot, punycode), each as
sni_not_allowed, name_not_allowed and host_mismatch, through the real audit.Create, the log verb in text and in
--format ocsf, and verify: 56 lines, the longest 860 bytes, no raw byte below 0x20 in the file, no control, C1,
bidi or replacement rune in either output, verify exit 0. Probe TestProbeFullRealLogRefusesConnections (package
proxy): 23,373 refusals with 253-byte hosts fill the 8 MiB in 0.76 s, about 32 microseconds each, so the fill is
cheaper with long names than sweep 2 measured, and still ends at SoftLimit. FuzzEachLine ran 30 s with no
crasher, but the engine reported 1,869 executions, so that run proves little (see the notes).

Logic and state. The full, failed and closed states of append were traced again. New, by execution: after the
log_full marker, append reads l.full only inside its overflow branch (audit.go, about line 129), so a record
shorter than the one that tripped the marker still fits the slack, is written, and its connection is served; in
the probe the marker was line 23375 of 23378, the next record was an allowed connect that was dialled, and the
one after got ErrFull and EOF with no dial. Nothing is served unrecorded, so this is a note and not a candidate:
the marker is not the last connection record, as the comment in audit.go and the sentence of the log verb say.
Lifecycle records pass both limits; a failed write fails every later record, session_end included, which S-F16
prints and S-F17 reports as incomplete.

Concurrency and check-to-use gaps. Probe TestProbeNoteRacesSessionEnd (package audit): a goroutine spinning on
Note while Record(session_end) and Close run as session()'s defer does: in 300 rounds no record landed after
session_end, Verify was nil and the last record was session_end every time; had one landed, the verb would say
incomplete, a false alarm and never a false intact. Probe TestProbeVerifyIntactWhileLockHeld: a session with no
session_end is incomplete (exit 1) unlocked and intact (exit 0) while the session lock is held, which is what
fetch() does for a pull since S-F46. No in-scope attacker can hold the lock, or make the supervisor die without
its end record, so this is a note.

Cryptography and identity. The seal binds the host key, the session id and the chain head; the id holds no
space, so the domain string is unambiguous; the head is a fixed-width prefix of each hash input, so there is no
split ambiguity; a session has one complete state, so every earlier (log, seal) pair is refused as incomplete
(sweep 2's probe), and another host's key and a renamed sibling are refused (existing tests). Probe
TestProbeSealTrailingBytes: bytes after the seal's two hex tokens are ignored and verify says intact; the
signature still covers the head, so nothing is gained. LoadKey takes exactly 64 hex bytes and refuses any group
or other mode bit. holds() keeps the key out of an export by spelling, by inode (S-F35) and by mount point
(S-F48); the key is read into memory only.

Failure modes. Every error path on the write side fails closed: ErrFull and a failed write both make handle
close with EOF and dial nothing, the refusal sites refuse whatever their Note returned, and the broker
withholds. One failure path removes a record: session() on a failed export, or a failed write of `inodes`,
removes a session directory that already holds session_start and its seal. That is C83.

Downgrade, rollback and replay. Only the v2 seal string is accepted; rollback pairs are refused by
completeness; the update path moves provider layers only; updates.log is outside the chain and, since S-F1 and
S-F43, carries no in-scope bytes but a once-per-session failed line for a provider this start installed.

Interaction between surfaces. I5: no record carries a value, a placeholder or a guest Host header. I6: allowed
hosts are canonical. I7: rm removes the record, by design. I10: SoftLimit and HardLimit bound the volume;
durable records are 300 a minute through the broker's window, plus Issue at the provider's pace. I11: a full or
failed log refuses every new connection (S-F16). I12: the audit package parses no guest bytes. I13: the deny
line's remedy widens only by the operator's own act. Probe TestProbeResolverRefusalsUnrecorded: a refused name
with class IN leaves one record; the same name with class CH, with opcode IQUERY or with QR set, and an allowed
name with class CH, are refused or unanswered with no record, because the resolver refuses those shapes before
it reads the name. The guest learns and reaches nothing more than with IN, so this is a note (PARKED's line on
refused DNS shapes, now shown by execution).

The fixes since sweep 2, asked for their second order. S-F44, S-F56, S-F59 and S-F62 to S-F66 refuse before
newSession, and a refused start leaves no record, by design. S-F45 changed only how the holds, fetch and session
messages quote the directory. S-F46: running() is now true during a pull, so the completeness rule of S-F17 is
suspended while a session is pulled (the lock probe above). S-F48: more starts are refused before any record,
and the key is kept out of one more class of export. S-F49 and S-F52 to S-F54: more blocked_address refusals
with canonical hosts, bounded by SoftLimit; a failed route dump refuses every connect, with a record. S-F50,
S-F51, S-F55, S-F57 and S-F58: the same two refusal reasons at the same Deny sites, and no new guest bytes in a
record. S-F47, S-F60 and S-F61 touch no record. S-F43: fail returns before any marker when this start installed
nothing. S-F16 and S-F17 hold as built: unrecorded_test.go is green and every Deny caller was traced again; the
stub recorder of S-F16's test differs from a real log only at the slack after the marker.

The parked lines of this surface, each tried again and ruled on, none with an in-scope break behind it: the
seal rewritten per append, pull's nil log and updates.log outside the chain (a crash between append and seal
fails closed); the S-1010 observations (trailing seal bytes and raw C1 and bidi runes in the file, both shown
again); no VM row floods audit.log (S-F16's Go test and the real-log probe are the evidence, and R5 forbids
asking for a row); the relay's reset where EOF was expected (wording); the log verb's sentence after log_full
(now wrong twice: later connections are refused, and up to one record's slack is still recorded); the S-F17
notes; the shed window of S-F8; an allowed connect with no outcome record (the record is the attempt); a
granted ledger line before carriesPlaceholder refuses (a record too many); CPU per recorded refusal (measured,
bounded by the fill); names that still resolve after log_full (design); the S-F46 notes (the second order
above is added); sessions keyed by the spelling of the directory (reasoned only).

Coverage. Read in full: internal/audit (audit.go, key.go, the ported lines.go, audit_test.go); in cmd/workcell
log.go, ocsf.go, verify_test.go, log_test.go, run_vm.go, session.go, relay.go, data.go, main.go, pull_vm.go,
bench_vm.go, policy.go and c19_test.go; in internal/proxy the ported proxy.go, terminate.go and allowlist.go,
signin.go, routes_linux.go and unrecorded_test.go; the ported internal/secret/broker.go and source.go;
internal/relay/relay.go; internal/resolver/resolver.go; internal/rootfs/ext4file.go; escape/suite/audit.go and
lifecycle.go; parts of escape/sandbox/control_linux.go and workcell_vm.go; PARKED.md whole; the map, both
earlier records of this surface and every sweep 3 passage that names the log, the seal, verify or the
recorder; the diff of every surface file since sweep 2. Skimmed or by grep: internal/workspace/workspace.go,
internal/rootfs/tree.go and ext4.go, Narrow in internal/policy, the Exit encoding in internal/guest, the
record and fail functions of update.go, caps.go, the I9 rows of escape/suite/tests.go, the I9 block of
docs/threat-model.md. Not opened: internal/vmm, internal/fileserve (the verifier read its mkdir path for C83),
cmd/workcell-init, internal/wire, the rest of internal/rootfs and internal/policy, the other tests, and
_legacy/; none of them writes or reads a record. Run: the five probe files by overlay, plain and under -race;
the existing tests of internal/audit, cmd/workcell, internal/proxy, internal/secret, internal/relay and
internal/resolver under -race, all green; FuzzEachLine for 30 s. No VM row, no macOS path, no end-to-end run of
the binary. The probes were not kept as tests: none but C83's failed, and the test budget has no room.

### S-1010 candidates, sweep 3

C83. ID I9 (every lifecycle event is recorded on the host; the guest cannot suppress a record): the
session_start record of a session whose workspace export fails. ATTACKER: guest root of an earlier --mount
session of the same directory, by the product's own path: the file service makes a directory by Mkdirat on the
parent's handle and bounds one name to 255 bytes, with no bound on depth or on the whole path, so 60 components
of 100 bytes cost a few dozen mkdirs. The claim also named the malicious repository; the verifier found that
half overstated, since git checks out by a path relative to the worktree and meets ENAMETOOLONG itself, and
only a tool that extracts by component delivers such a tree. SEVERITY: low (S6: hardening, with no break of
what I9 exists to account for). WHERE: cmd/workcell/run_vm.go, session(): newSession makes sessions/<id>/,
takes the lock and records session_start with its seal; when workspace.Export then fails, or the write of
`inodes` after it, session() runs os.RemoveAll on the directory and returns; the deferred session_end is then
written through descriptors that are still open into the unlinked files, succeeds, and prints nothing. The
export fails in internal/rootfs/ext4file.go, where the file is opened by its whole relative path. INPUT: a
working directory that holds one non-empty file whose path below it passes PATH_MAX; then `workcell run` there
in clone mode, the default. EFFECT: the operator sees one line, `copy ... file name too long`, and the host
holds no session directory, no audit.log and no seal, so ls, log and verify show no trace of the start, where a
start that fails at boot keeps session_start and session_end with result failed and verifies intact.
Reproducing test, by the redteam from the claim alone: TestC83ExportFailureKeepsTheSessionRecord, package main
of cmd/workcell, linux, 42 lines, parked at escape/_pending/S-F67/c83_test.go. Two arms share one body: the
export arm makes the deep tree one component at a time and starts a session with dummy artifacts; the control
arm starts one in a shallow directory, which fails at boot. Each wants an error, exactly one new session
directory, a log with session_start and session_end with result failed, and verify exit 0. Run by the
orchestrator by overlay, plain and under -race, logs saved: the export arm fails with "the session failed with
copy ... file name too long and left 0 session directories besides the earlier one", and the control passes.
Outcome: CONFIRMED at low by the verifier, who repeated both runs, traced the removal and the silent deferred
write, and showed the mount guest's path through internal/fileserve. Not medium or higher: the export precedes
boot, so no guest code ran, no connection was tried and no secret was released; mount mode never exports; the
failure is printed to the operator; and the guest of the earlier session cannot touch its own session's record
this way. Not a mere note: R2 is met, and a record that the product wrote is then destroyed without a word,
which the invariant's wording forbids. This corrects two earlier rulings of the same gap (S-1008 and S-1013
of sweep 1), which said no record was owed and that no in-scope attacker could trigger it: the mount guest
can. The verifier's strongest argument against its own ruling: every refusal before boot (holds, named, a
failed newSession) is "no session, no record", the C19 tests assert that, and the export is only the last such
refusal; on that reading nothing is owed. For the fix unit: the export arm does not assert that the error is
the export's own, so a change that only makes the deep path exportable would pass it through the boot
failure; the test asks for the kept directory, so a fix that records session_start only after the export needs
its want rewritten; a kept directory has no image and no `inodes`, so pull and diff in that directory would
pick it as the newest session. S7 lists a low finding and does not demand its fix; the loop adds the unit as
it did for C64, C70 and C79, and the maintainer may strike it. Not S14: run_vm.go, internal/workspace and
internal/fileserve are v2's own, nothing ported, no v1 line. Fix unit: S-F67, below S-1010 in PLAN.md.
C83 FIXED by S-F67, commits 563c5eb (the test moved, with its export arm asking for the contract) and da7ff4c (the
fix) (PR #340). The orchestrator chose the unit line's first shape before the redteam ran and wrote it as a
contract: after a start that fails at the export, or at the write of `inodes` after it, session() returns that
step's own error; the session directory stays, so the deferred session_end records failed into the real log and
verify calls it intact; the directory holds no workspace.ext4 on either path; newest() still picks that session,
as it picks a boot-failed one, and pull and diff refuse it in one line with their exit codes 1 and 2, boot
nothing, and say what is true of both kinds of session that have no image, a --mount one and a start that failed
before its copy was made; rm takes the directory wholly; a start that fails at boot and a --mount start are as on
main. Why the first shape: the product had already written the start, I9 asks for every lifecycle event, and the
fix is two product lines fewer; the second shape would have moved the start record out of newSession and left
the mount guest able to make every later start fail with no trace on the host. The fix: the two RemoveAll lines
of session() in cmd/workcell/run_vm.go are gone; workspace.Export takes its own image away on every error (read
and shown by run), and the `inodes` arm returns its error joined with os.Remove of the image; the refusal of
fetch() in cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go for a session with no image now names the session, both causes and
`workcell rm <id>`. Proved: the test fails with main's product code in its export arm (no new directory) and
passes on da7ff4c, plain and under -race, its control arm passing on both (redteam and orchestrator on 563c5eb,
the reviewer by overlay of main's run_vm.go and pull_vm.go). The export arm now also asks that the error begins
with `copy `, that no image is left, that fetch refuses without the words `mount session`, and both arms that
removeSession takes the directory. The builder and the reviewer drove the built binary through a tree of 60
components of 100 bytes: run prints the export's line and exits 125, the directory holds audit.log, audit.seal,
lock and repo, ls says exited, verify says intact, pull and diff print the one line and exit 1 and 2 with nothing
booted, rm leaves nothing; the builder made the `inodes` write fail on a tmpfs with 14 inodes and saw the same
directory with no image. Review: one round, no finding. Cost to honest use: each start that fails at its export
leaves a directory of about 600 bytes until rm, and pull or diff reaches an older clone session of the same
directory only after rm of the failed one, which the line names. Product 14998 of 15000; the test limit follows
product, so test is 28497 of 28497: the test grew from 42 lines to 45 and six lines were paid, by joined comment
lines in c61_test.go, pull_test.go, relay_test.go and verify_test.go and one blank line of session_test.go; the
reviewer compared the five files with main by go/ast, comments stripped, and no statement differs.

The 42 lines of the parked test were paid by 42 lines of layout folds in nine files under escape/ (table rows
and literals joined in https_test.go, tests.go, secrets_test.go, bench_test.go, channel_test.go, channel.go,
smoke.go, repo.go and sandbox/workcell_linux.go, the comments of joined rows kept in row order at the end of
the line): no test, row, arm or assertion removed. One join had first put the I10 row mount-disk-flood behind
the comment mark of the row before it, which a count of text matches did not show; the orchestrator's
comparison of each file's code with its comments stripped caught it before any commit, the redteam restored
the row, and showed by go/ast and by the compiled tables, on HEAD and on this tree, that every joined literal
has the same number of elements (All holds 147 rows with the same IDs and names in the same order). Product
15000 of 15000, test 28500 of 28500.

After S-1010: sweep 3 stands at two highs (C76 and C77, both fixed), fourteen mediums (C65, C66, C67, C68, C69,
C71, C72, C73, C74, C75, C78, C80, C81 and C82, all fixed) and four lows (C64, C70 and C79, fixed; C83, open).
C83's test waits under escape/_pending/S-F67/. The next candidate number is C84 and the next fix unit S-F68.

## S-1011, sweep 3: pins, selector, verification, bump tool, channel manifest, update client (I14, section 10), as built at main 14a66b7

Sweep 3 (S8), the last the SPEC allows, fresh context (S3), the whole surface read in full as built after S-F1 to
S-F67, not a diff, at the claim commit 858327d. One auditor run on the top tier, finished without a stop: no model
declined and no safeguard re-ran a request. No hypervisor in the cloud session, and nothing on this surface needed
a VM: every probe ran by go test -overlay, plain and under -race where order matters, against files and loopback
processes the probe itself made (T8), with one slip that is recorded under Coverage (S12). Result: one candidate,
C84 (I14 hardening with I13, low), the row that C79's record left open, given to the redteam as a claim only, run
by the orchestrator, and ruled on by a verifier who saw the test and its logs and no one's reasoning; the record is
below. No candidate at medium or above. Nothing was fixed (S1). No file of this surface carries `// Ported from
v1`, so no v1 line is owed, and nothing is someone else's project (S14).

Trust boundary. Rows 2, 27 to 30 and 32 to 35 of the map. The network attacker who holds the channel host or the
path, without the key, sends channel.json through installer.manifest and artifact.Fetch (64 KiB cap, no redirect)
to channel.Verify, and artifact bodies through installer.fetch and artifact.Fetch (512 MiB, https only, three hops)
to the SHA-256 of the signed pin: no byte is used without the manifest's signature or the pin's digest, so that
attacker holds availability alone. Guest root sends one Exit frame with an error as its first frame, which reaches
installer.fail behind the fresh gate (S-F1, S-F31, S-F43); it also writes host files by design, the mount export,
the image of a writable cache and workspace.ext4, none of which the update path reads unless the operator's `ca`
names one (C84). The malicious repository brings workcell.toml, where ReadRepo refuses an [update] table (I13), and
the working directory, which the update path reads only to refuse a `ca` that passes through it. Upstream listings,
Sigstore bundles, npm attestations and OSV answers reach cmd/bump on the runner only, a dry run until H-905; a
hostile upstream is the provider's own service, out of scope, as S-1012 ruled. The holder of the channel key and
the operator's own [update] table are out of scope except where they meet attacker bytes. Authority: update,
startup (apply and the daily check) and fail run as the operator and write layers/<agent>/ with its images and the
markers current, previous and failed, channel.serial, channel.day, channel.next and updates.log under the data
directory; findLayers turns `current` into a drive that both backends attach read-only and that the init mounts
read-only.

Parsing and resources. The 64 KiB cap is of the decoded body: a channel.json served with Content-Encoding gzip, 33
KB on the wire and 16 MiB decoded, is refused as over the cap in 1 to 3 ms; a chunked body of the cap plus one with
no Content-Length is refused; one of exactly the cap verifies; serial and markers stay untouched (probe
TestProbeChannelOversizedEncodings). An artifact whose Content-Length lies short or long is a transport failure,
and one declared over the cap is refused before its body (TestProbeArtifactLengthLies). A signed version of 300
bytes makes the image name pass NAME_MAX, the rename fails and the layer directory stays empty
(TestProbeVersionNameTooLong). Go's transport decodes a gzip Content-Encoding before the bytes are hashed, in
cmd/bump and in the client alike, so a pin's digest is of the decoded body; nobody in scope gains, since the digest
is pinned. Seven fuzz targets ran 20 s each with no crasher: FuzzVerify of the channel (11.6 thousand executions,
so that run proves little), FuzzTarMember and FuzzProvenance of artifact, FuzzAnswer of advisory, FuzzParse of
sigstore and of policy, FuzzLayer of rootfs (each above 100 thousand). The tar and ext4 parsers behind unpack see
digest-pinned bytes only.

Logic and state. Every marker transition was traced and run again: install, --to of the current, the previous, the
failed image on disk (reused without a fetch) and an unknown version, --rollback, apply's skip of the failed
digest, and fail's pair check (TestUpdate, TestFail, TestFailSparesALayerThisStartDidNotInstall and TestChannel,
green plain and under -race). choose applies the user's cool-off to the signed Released only, so it lengthens and
never shortens (B10); its arithmetic wraps for a Released near the top of int64 (TestProbeChooseReleasedOverflow),
a field only the key holder signs. Select drops a withdrawn digest from pins and previous; --rollback and --to of
an image on disk read no manifest (ADR-004, B10). point keeps at most current, previous and failed. Pin names and
architectures are lookup keys only; the version is the one manifest field that becomes a file name, and since S-F18
it holds no slash or backslash.

Concurrency and check-to-use gaps. Two applies at one instant on one channel.next: in nine runs, three plain and
six under -race, one installed and reported fresh, the other read nothing, and one artifact was fetched
(TestProbeApplyConcurrent); the window is the microseconds between the read and the remove, and PARKED's line
stands. The serial floor is read, verified and written with no lock, as sweep 2 measured, with honest manifests
only. The walk of `ca` resolves each prefix and then reads: a mount guest can change only components inside its
export, and the first prefix that enters the working directory already refuses, so making the walk miss needs a
writer outside the directory, who is out of scope. The daily goroutine shares no state with the proxy, the broker
or the session.

Cryptography and identity. The DSSE pre-authentication encoding is over the decoded payload, so base64 spellings
and duplicate JSON keys cannot split what is signed from what is parsed; ed25519.Verify stands behind the 32-byte
guard; the key id must match as well as the signature; NotAfter is judged at now; an invalid signature under a
trusted key id beside a valid one under an untrusted key refuses (TestVerify's rows). Sigstore: the leaf is chained
at the integrated time to the embedded root, the signed entry timestamp is over Rekor's canonical JSON, the body
binds leaf, signature and hash, the identity is compared byte for byte, and Rekor v2 is refused closed. The key
table is empty before H-905, so the compiled rows install with no manifest (S-1018's residual, seen again under
`hold`).

Failure modes. Every refusal leaves the markers and the serial untouched. marker() maps any read error to the empty
string: for channel.serial that is a floor of 0, and a directory in its place is caught at the write
(TestProbeMarkerReadErrors); a serial text past int64 reads as the largest value and refuses every manifest
(TestProbeSerialFloorOverflowText); an unreadable `current` means no layer, which is less and never more. Nobody in
scope writes under the data directory, so these are notes. startup's refusal of a bad `ca` is a printed line and
the session goes on with the zero installer, whose fail reads nothing since S-F43. cmd/bump never turns a failed
verification into a skip: a token, an issue and exit 1 under -newest.

Downgrade, rollback and replay. The binary built at HEAD against a loopback TLS channel
(TestProbeRealBinarySequence): serial 1 installed 1.0.0; serial 2 installed 2.0.0 and kept 1.0.0; serial 1 replayed
was refused as lower than the last one seen, with current, previous and the floor unchanged; --rollback went to
1.0.0's image and read no manifest (B10); update under serial 2 applied 2.0.0 again; `hold` made no channel
request; a user cool-off of 8760 hours on the compiled row was refused with the line that nothing pinned passes the
cool-off. An equal serial passes by design; the replay window is the 14 days plus the skew, per data directory, and
a fresh data directory accepts any manifest that has not expired (ADR-004).

Interaction between surfaces. The update path reads nothing relative to the working directory (with a relative
XDG_DATA_HOME the binary used the home and the working directory stayed empty); ReadRepo refuses [update]; run
orders loadPolicy, startup, findLayers, openCaches and then session's holds(), and startup writes only under the
data directory; the layer is read-only in both backends and in the guest; pull, diff, bench and attach boot without
layers. The one crossing found is C84: files that a guest writes by design meet the update path only through the
operator's `ca`.

The fixes since sweep 2, asked for their second order. S-F43: holds, with TestFail and the C43 and C60 tests green;
the zero installer reads no marker. S-F44, S-F45, S-F46 and S-F48: update calls none of named, list or holds, and
holds() never relates `ca` to the directories it guards. S-F63: the prefix walk holds for the working directory,
with `..` spellings and links in and out; it knows nothing of the data directory or of another session's export
(C84), and an operator whose working directory is `/` or the home is refused with a `ca` set, the known cost.
S-F56, S-F59, S-F62 and S-F64 to S-F66 run in loadPolicy before startup and stop run before any fetch; update does
not call loadPolicy. S-F67 and S-F49 to S-F55, S-F57, S-F58, S-F60 and S-F61 have no path onto this surface.

The parked lines that name this surface, each tried again, none with an in-scope break behind it but C84: Rekor v2
(fails closed); updates.log outside the chain; the B-826d ideas (each holds by TestChannel's rows and the
real-binary run); the compiled-rows fallback (seen); two applies at one instant (measured above); the apply delay,
the refused records per start, the .download residue, two verbs crossing and the odd markers (no in-scope writer);
fail by the base name of the command and the S-F31 residuals (the operator's own); --rollback to a withdrawn image
(S-1018's); the docs line (still true: docs/policy.md says the [update] channel and cool-off are not read yet, and
both are read and honoured); bench dropping the newInstaller error; the floor race, npm withdrawn by digest and a
cool-off over 56 years; the maintainer's two lines on the kernel and Firecracker having no row in pins/ (read again
from code: no product path fetches or verifies vmlinux, initrd.cpio, root.ext4 or firecracker, while doctor says
