### S-1011 candidates, sweep 3

C84. ID I14 hardening (the trust root of the host's channel and artifact fetches), with I13: the file that the
user's `[update] ca` names. ATTACKER: guest root, who by design writes some host files, completed by a network
attacker on the path of a later fetch. SEVERITY: low (S6: hardening with no demonstrated break; the class of C59
and C79). WHERE: cmd/workcell/update.go, newInstaller, which since S-F63 follows each prefix of `ca` and refuses
one that lies in or leads into the working directory, and judges it against nothing else; cmd/workcell/data.go,
where holds() keeps a session out of the data directory and never sees `ca`. INPUT, part (a): the user's
config.toml says `[update] ca = "<data>/caches/npm.ext4"`; a guest of a session with `--cache npm:rw` writes a file
into that cache whose bytes hold a newline and then a PEM certificate; then any later `workcell run` or `workcell
update`, from any working directory. Part (b): `ca` names a file in a tree that the operator later runs `workcell
run --mount` in; startup prints S-F63's refusal and the session runs all the same; the guest rewrites the file; a
later run or update from another directory reads it. EFFECT: the installer's HTTPS client trusts the attacker's
certificate alone for every later channel and artifact fetch, until the file is restored, so an attacker on the
path presents its own certificate for the channel host and the pin URLs and gains what an on-path attacker without
the key has: refusal of service, sight of the requests, or the replay of a signed manifest that has not expired.
The manifest's signature, its serial floor and expiry and each pin's digest still gate every install, so nothing
installs past I14.
Reproducing test, by the redteam from the claim alone: TestC84UpdateCAUnderTheDataDirectory, package main of
cmd/workcell, parked at escape/_pending/S-F68/c84_test.go. Two arms share one body. The attacking arm writes
<data>/workcell/caches/npm.ext4 as 4 KiB of 0xff, a newline, the PEM certificate of a loopback httptest TLS server,
and 4 KiB of 0xff, names it as `ca`, changes to an unrelated directory, calls newInstaller and sends a HEAD through
its client to that server; it wants an error that names ca and no request served. The control arm puts the PEM
beside config.toml and wants the request served. Run by the orchestrator by overlay, plain and under -race, logs
saved: the attacking arm fails with "newInstaller, then a fetch through its transport from the server holding the
certificate in that file, gave <nil> after 1 requests served", and the control passes. The redteam did not run the
guest's write, which needs a VM, and the test writes the file on the host in its place.
Outcome: CONFIRMED at low by the verifier, who repeated both runs. On the power the test takes: the product hands
the guest the whole image of a writable cache as one drive and the host never mounts or reads it, so guest root
holds every byte of that host file, by raw writes to the device too, and a small file lies whole in one block of an
ext4 image, so the certificate is found in a real one. Not medium: no invariant is broken, since the key, the
floor, the expiry and the digest hold, and the precondition is an operator who points `ca` at a cache image, which
none does by mistake; it counts as the mechanical hardening that C79 was granted, and C79's record named this very
row as not expressed. Part (b) is no new finding and has no test: the redteam ran its three steps with a host write
in place of the guest's and found that after the rewrite the file cannot be told from the control arm's, an
absolute path outside the working and the data directory, so no rule on `ca` alone refuses it without refusing the
control; the verifier ruled it the row that PARKED's line of S-F63 notes already holds (a `ca` under the export of
a --mount session run elsewhere), at most low, where the refusal is printed and tells the operator to move the
file. The verifier's strongest argument against its own ruling: (a) needs a `ca` no operator writes and (b) is
refused in a line already, so both are the operator's own act and the candidate could be refuted; it kept low
because C79's verifier accepted this class of precondition. S7 lists a low finding and does not demand its fix; the
loop adds the unit as it did for C64, C70, C79 and C83, and the maintainer may strike it. Not S14: update.go and
data.go are v2's own, nothing ported, no v1 line. Fix unit: S-F68, below S-1011 in PLAN.md; its line names two
shapes, of which the second, a `ca` only within the config directory, would close part (b) as well, at a cost to
honest use that the line states.
C84 FIXED by S-F68, commits b23a088 (the test moved to cmd/workcell/c84_test.go, one comment line reworded, so
escape/_pending/ is gone) and 437bab9 (the fix) (PR #342). The orchestrator chose the unit line's first shape
before the redteam ran and wrote it as a contract: newInstaller refuses, before the file is read and before any
transport exists, an [update] ca any part of whose path lies in or leads into the data directory, by the prefix
walk and within() that S-F63 gave the working directory; every refusal of main stays; the refusal is one line
that names the config file, `[update] ca` and the value, which update and run print, fetching nothing; a ca
outside both directories is accepted as on main, and no test that passes on main changes its verdict. Why the
first shape: the scout showed that the folder of config.toml is <XDG_CONFIG_HOME>/workcell, so under the second
shape the control arm of this test, the control arm of c79_test.go, the ca of update_test.go and the ca that the
VM suite's adapter writes beside its session directory would all be refused, where the accept text wants the
control unchanged, escape/ has no layout left and S1 lets only the fix land; the first costs honest use nothing
but a ca kept under the data directory. The fix: four lines of cmd/workcell/update.go changed and none added, the
walk's verdict being within(cwd, r) || within(in.dir, r), with in.dir the data directory that newInstaller had
already asked for and whose error it already returns; the one message names both directories; the sentence of
docs/policy.md on ca names the data directory too. Proved: TestC84UpdateCAUnderTheDataDirectory fails with main's
update.go in its attacking arm (nil and one request served) and passes on 437bab9, plain and under -race, its
control arm passing on both (the redteam and the orchestrator on b23a088, the reviewer by overlay); the C59, C60
and C79 tests, the package and go test ./... pass. The builder and the reviewer each drove the built binary
against a loopback listener of their own: update exits 2 with the line, run prints it after `workcell: channel:`
and goes on to the boot, the listener saw no request, and a ca beside the config reached the fetch. The reviewer
tried 18 spellings by overlay: refused are a file link and a folder link from outside into the data directory, a
link inside it that leads out, `..` segments, doubled and trailing slashes, a data directory given through a link
and by its real path, a relative XDG_DATA_HOME, the data directory itself and a path under a session's export;
accepted as on main are a ca beside the config, one elsewhere, one beside the workcell folder of the data home
and the data directory's parent. The VM suite's ca lies in a sibling of its data directory, never under it.
Product 14998 of 15000 and test 28497 of 28497, both as before; Markdown 1370. Review: one round, no finding.
Not closed, as the contract chose: part (b), a ca under the export of a --mount session run elsewhere, PARKED's
S-F63 row; and a hard link outside the data directory to a cache image, which only the operator can make.

(loop/settings.sh:39, non-expiring); the Actions policy admits pull_request_target and schedule, always from main;
the merge job holds contents and pull-requests write, runs no pull request code and calls only the merge API, which
the ruleset judges (gate, gate-macos and guard from app 15368, strict, squash, no bypass). (2) Network bytes into
the runner, all over TLS so that N holds availability only: Firecracker v1.17.0 and the x86_64 kernel by URL and
SHA-256 from constants in free paths (escape/sandbox/workcell_linux.go:24, internal/vmm/firecracker/
firecracker_test.go:41-45, spikes/install/install_test.go:33-37; the arm64 pair in workcell_darwin.go:20 and

listings, artifacts, bundles and advisories for cmd/bump, the Go toolchain and modules through proxy.golang.org and
sum.golang.org, and the six actions by SHA. (3) The maintainer's signature chain: guard.yml checks out live main

the linux binaries link golang.org/x/sys/unix alone beyond the standard library (cmd/bump nothing); darwin/arm64

Logic and state. The required checks are gate, gate-macos and guard from app 15368, strict, squash only, no bypass

Concurrency and check-to-use gaps. gate.sh reads the lists and the tree before any repository code runs and runs

Cryptography and identity. The maintainer key was not decoded again (gpg denied); sweep 2's scratch decode stands:

Failure modes. Every run step is bash -e with pipefail; green() turns a gh failure into exit 1; GATE_REQUIRE_VM=1
makes a missing hypervisor a Linux gate failure (seen in gate-test); guard.sh dies with exit 4 on every error and
treats only grep 1 and cmp 1 as no; mkimage removes a half-written output; install.sh installs nothing on any
failure (seen). The failure mode that reality supplied is the replaced kernel of 2026-11-25: the SHA-256 pin refused
the new bytes, every gate failed closed, and no integrity was lost; the cost was W8 (halt 332). No fail-open path.

## S-1013, sweep 3: chains across surfaces, and the start-up, shutdown, crash and upgrade windows, as built at main cf37fd4

Sweep 3 (S8), the last the SPEC allows, at the claim commit 1c7b97b (main cf37fd4 plus one log line), in a fresh
context (S3): the product read as built after S-F1 to S-F68, not a diff. One auditor run, finished without a stop:
no model declined, no safeguard stopped a turn and no tool permission was refused, in the auditor, the two redteam
runs or the two verifiers. No hypervisor in the session and nothing was run on a VM: the candidates were probed by
go test -overlay against the real packages, and the windows were run with the real cmd/workcell binary against a
stand-in VMM (a script that records its pid and execs sleep), with dummy artifacts in a scratch data directory.
Result: two candidates, C85 and C86, both medium, both chains of facts that single-surface audits had refuted or
ruled low, each CONFIRMED by its own verifier; they are recorded below with their tests. Nothing was fixed (S1). The
windows hold as sweep 2 recorded them, with the second order of S-F44 to S-F68 traced and, where it could be, run.
The text below is the auditor's report, condensed by the orchestrator.

Trust boundary. The chained surface has no entry point of its own. Its attacker bytes are those of the single
surfaces: guest frames on vsock 5000, 5001 and 5002; the guest-written workspace.ext4 and rw cache images, attached
and never parsed on the host; the repository tree and its workcell.toml; hostile model output as the agent's conduct
inside a --mount session, where it writes every byte of every file beneath the export as the operator's uid through
internal/fileserve (CREATE, WRITE, SYMLINK, RENAME, UNLINK); and the network attacker as the host resolver's answer
for an allowed name (the model of the rebind rows, C7, C30, C53, C66, C69) and as the channel and artifact server
with availability alone. What is new here is where those bytes meet host state that outlives one session, and the
operator's own environment: the data directory (audit.key; sessions/<id> with audit.log, audit.seal, lock, repo,
vmm, inodes and workspace.ext4; layers/<agent> with its markers; caches; channel.serial, channel.day, channel.next;
updates.log), the VMM socket directory under TMPDIR, the user's config directory, and the operator's variables
(TMPDIR, XDG_*, HOME, SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR). The authority that handles them is the supervisor at the
operator's uid, before any VM exists and again per request: it reads the user's policy (loadPolicy through
policy.Read, an os.Open that follows links), judges cwd against the data and config directories by spelling, inode
and mount point (holds in cmd/workcell/data.go), judges secret sources and the [update] ca against cwd and the data
directory, builds the proxy's upstream root pool once per session from the environment (upstreamRoots in
internal/proxy/terminate.go), runs cmd: helpers on the host per secret use with cwd / (internal/secret/source.go),
and holds the VM child under Pdeathsig. Since sweep 1 the product judges every operator-named path that it later
trusts against the directory a session serves, by identity: cwd (named, C61), the data and config directories
(holds: C19, C29, C52, C65), secret sources (C54, C58, C72, C75, C78, C80 to C82) and the ca (C59, C79, C84). Two
operator-named trust inputs are not judged: the user's config.toml when it is a symbolic link to a file inside the
served tree (holds compares the config directory's resolution, never the file's), and SSL_CERT_FILE and
SSL_CERT_DIR, where upstreamRoots refuses a relative value only. Both are files that a --mount guest can rewrite and
that every later session, anywhere, then reads as the operator's own.

Parsing and resources. No new parser lies on this surface; every guest parser was traced to its bound and fuzzer in
the single records. The pace of S-F47 and S-F60 sleeps only the file service's reader: a negative remainder returns
at once, and Close takes life.Lock, which no worker holds across a send, so a sleeping reader never delays closeAll.
A unix socket path over 108 bytes fails closed, seen again by a slip of the auditor's own: its first window script
used the long scratch path as TMPDIR and every run exited 125 with a bind error, the VMM directory removed by
closeAll and the session directory kept with session_end failed (PARKED line 14's clause, now with S-F67's shape).
Helper processes of a cmd: source are bounded by the broker's 300 per minute window and the two-minute timeout (C16,
low, unchanged). A mount guest learns of a new host file only through FUSE round trips of about 100 microseconds
each, which bounds what it can do inside the microsecond windows of boot. Refuted: a guest that makes the reader
sleep stalls only itself; the RemoveAll of closeAll and of rm follows no final symlink and opens the parent by path,
so a link the guest plants under TMPDIR removes at most a directory of the guest's own name.

Logic and state. The order of a start was traced from run() through session() and boot() in cmd/workcell/run_vm.go
as built after S-F44 to S-F68: parseRun; loadPolicy with the C34, C54, C72, C75, C78, C80, C81 and C82 checks over
every user row; loadArtifacts; startup (newInstaller with the ca prefix walk of S-F63 and S-F68, apply with its
second verify against the floor, the daily goroutine); findLayers; openCaches; then session: Getwd, holds (data and
config by within, mount points by /proc/self/mountinfo, running sessions' VMM directories by their vmm records), the
--mount TMPDIR rule, named, newSession (LoadKey, MkdirAll, flock then pid, repo, audit.Create, session_start),
Export(".") and the inodes write, or the mount; then boot: IsAbs(TMPDIR), the running-mount TMPDIR rule over every
session's repo record, MkdirTemp, recordBoot, listeners 5000 and 5001, adapters, proxy, session CA and broker, the
relay, 5002 and the file service under --mount, Start, accept. Every helper is up before Start, and the first
connection to 5000 is the init's, because no guest code runs before Exec. Shutdown runs the defers in reverse:
attach listener, terminal, the VM killed and reaped with its directory removed, session_end, lock; seen: stop ended
a booting run in 54 ms with exit 143 recorded, SIGINT gave exit 130 and SIGTERM 143, both recorded. The marker
transitions of apply, point, fail and update were walked again for a crash at each step, with no change since sweep
2; S-F43 keeps fail from reading any marker when this start installed nothing. S-F67's kept directory behaves as its
record says; seen: audit.log holds session_start and session_end failed, verify says intact, pull exits 1 and diff 2
with one line naming rm, and rm takes the directory. What no code judges became the candidates: the resolved
location of the config file, and the location of SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR.

Concurrency, ordering and check-to-use. The lock is written only once held, stop reads the lock again before every
rung, rm is refused while a run or a pull holds the lock (seen), two runs in one directory get two sessions and end
on their own signals (seen), and a pull holds the lock for its life (seen: ls says running, rm and a second pull are
refused, the lock file holds the pull's pid, two vmm lines). S-F46's second order against C63 holds end to end: a
--mount start in a directory that holds the TMPDIR under which a pull booted is refused by holds with the pull's VMM
directory named (seen, exit 125). Its twin with bench in place of the pull is admitted, since bench records nothing
(seen; PARKED lines 137 and 144 stand). Pdeathsig: after SIGKILL of the supervisor the stand-in VMM was running at 1
ms, a zombie with parent 1 at 50 ms and gone at 2 s, so the VM dies with the session (A9). The windows that remain
are timed by the operator or by chance and stand as parked: C61's double swap (line 185), a mount start between
another session's MkdirTemp and its recordBoot (line 188), the lock's truncate instant (line 187), two first uses of
audit.key, two applies on one channel.next (line 45). One mechanism inside bench's window that no line names: Start
writes firecracker.json with os.WriteFile, which follows a symlink that a mount guest could plant in the fresh
directory, so the host would truncate a file of the guest's choosing and write the host-built JSON into it; the
window from MkdirTemp to that write is 100 to 300 microseconds of host work, the directory name is random, and the
guest learns of it and acts only through two FUSE round trips of the same order, so the auditor judged it unwinnable
in practice: a note on line 137, in PARKED.md, not a candidate.

Cryptography and identity. Nothing new is signed or verified on this surface. The identity primitive the fixes
converged on, compare inodes and not spellings, is applied at the judge of cwd (named), of the data and config
directories (within's SameFile walk), of mount points (mountinfo) and of the ca (EvalSymlinks per prefix), and is
missing at two places where the product then trusts bytes for the rest of the session or for every later session:
the user's config file is opened by its name through any link, and the proxy's upstream root pool is built once at
Terminate from SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR with only the relative spelling refused, while x509.SystemCertPool
reads both variables itself. A CA planted in such a file gives the network attacker as DNS what C30 and C53 gave it,
and a planted policy gives the attacker the channel key the client trusts, so that I14's checks then guard the
attacker's anchor.

Failure modes. Every error path on this surface fails closed, by reading and by the runs: a failed bind exits 125
with the VMM directory removed and the start recorded as failed; SIGKILL leaves no session_end and verify says
incomplete; an export failure keeps the directory and records failed; running() returns every flock error but
EWOULDBLOCK; a refused ca is one printed line and the run goes on with the zero installer, whose fail reads nothing
(S-F43); a failed audit write fails every later record, session_end included, which verify then reports as
incomplete. The two candidates are checks that no code performs, a fail-open by omission and not by error. Seen and
noted, not a candidate: verify says intact for a session with no session_end while a pull holds its lock, the S-1010
note of PARKED line 231; only the operator causes both the missing end (SIGKILL) and the pull.

Downgrade, rollback and replay. apply removes channel.next first and verifies it again against the floor that the
daily check wrote; the floor only rises; --rollback reads no manifest (line 184 stands); update --to goes through
Select, so a withdrawn digest is refused; the residual of C2 (a forged first frame, or the operator's own ./claude,
sets aside the layer that this start installed) is unchanged and accepted. With C85 the attacker rewrites the
[update] channel and key, so the client's floor, expiry and signature checks all guard a manifest that the attacker
signs; that is a consequence of C85 and not a weakness of the channel code. S-F63 and S-F68 open no new window: the
ca walk runs before any transport, the refusal is printed and the session runs without a channel.

Interaction between surfaces. Both candidates are chains. C85 is the promise of C19 and C65 (holds keeps the config
directory out of every export) times a file-level symlink that holds never resolves, times C40 (a mount guest writes
the whole real tree), times C54's judgement of a cmd: program against the next session's cwd alone, times the broker
running helpers on the host per use. C86 is the S-1005 sweep 3 refutation (an absolute SSL_CERT_FILE inside the
repository needs the operator's environment to name it, resting on C53's "no distinct finding") times C40 times
C66's attacker model, against the precedent of the S-1009 and S-1011 verifiers, who accepted the same shape for the
[update] ca (C79) and under the data directory (C84); the two surfaces disagreed, and the mount rewrite is the lever
that neither considered. Also traced and refuted by reasoning: the S-1002 lead "sessions keyed by the spelling of
cwd" does not reopen boot's running-mount TMPDIR check through nested mount sessions, because the outermost mount
session's repo record is always true and its export holds everything a nested guest could rename. The S-1003 reverse
layout, cwd bind-mounted inside sessions/<id>, needs the operator to mount a repository inside workcell's own
sessions directory under a session-id name, which no layout gives (line 193 stands).

Parked leads, each tried again (line numbers of PARKED.md as of main cf37fd4). Stand with no change: 14 (seen
again), 17, 24, 34, 45, 47 (stop and rm measured again on the host side; the escape row is still missing), 69, 93,
96, 123, 124, 131, 135, 136, 137 (seen by execution, with the one new note above), 139, 140, 143, 144, 145, 162,
164, 167, 168, 169, 170, 171, 176, 178, 182 (the bench clause seen; the spelling clause found closed through

(b), a ca in another session's mount export, is the ca twin of C86's shape and stays low for the ca, since I14 holds
there), 231 (seen), 233 (seen), 234, 235, 236. Settled earlier and still so: 141. The lines on other surfaces'
internals (proxy readings, token shapes, routes, fuzz notes, workflow notes) touch no chain or window and were not
tried again here. No parked row names a config.toml link or an absolute SSL_CERT_FILE under cwd (lines 97, 148 and
151 name SSL_CERT or config.toml for other readings), so both candidates differ from every recorded row.

Coverage. Read in full: loop/SPEC.md; the fix-unit lines S-F47 to S-F68 of PLAN.md; in this file the sweep 2 record
of this unit, every sweep 3 record and the C30 and C53 records; PARKED.md whole; every non-test file of cmd/workcell
and of cmd/workcell-init; of internal: vmm (vmm.go, firecracker/firecracker.go, vz/vz.go and args.go), audit, wire,

release.yml for CGO_ENABLED (the Linux binaries are static, so the pure Go resolver runs and HOSTALIASES cannot

in a provider or in anyone else's project.

### S-1013 candidates, sweep 3

C85. ID I13 (workspace content can only narrow policy: the guest's write beneath its export becomes the user's
config), with I5 (the attacker's [[secret]] rows bind any host file the operator can read to a host of its choosing,
and a cmd: row runs a program of its choosing on the host) and I14 by consequence (the [update] channel and key that
the client trusts become the attacker's). The promise broken is that of holds() itself: a session may not see the
config directory. ATTACKER: guest root in a --mount session, by hostile model output or a malicious repository's
hook, whose export holds the target of the operator's config.toml symbolic link; then the operator's next ordinary
session, anywhere, whose honest agent makes one request to its API host. SEVERITY: medium (S6: an invariant broken,
with one precondition the attacker does not control: the operator's config.toml under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/workcell is a
symbolic link to a file in the mounted tree, the layout of a dotfiles repository managed by ln -s or by stow without
directory folding); the grade of C19, C52 and C65 for an operator layout. WHERE: cmd/workcell/data.go, where holds
compares the resolved config directory with cwd and never the file's resolution; cmd/workcell/policy.go, where
configFile names the file, policy.Read follows the link, and the cmd: judgement of C54 is against the current cwd
only; internal/secret/broker.go and source.go, where the broker runs the program on the host from /. INPUT:
$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/workcell/config.toml is a link to <W>/dotfiles/config.toml, a regular file. Terminal 1: `cd <W> &&
workcell run --mount -- claude`. The guest writes /workspace/evil.sh and rewrites /workspace/dotfiles/config.toml to
allow a host and to hold a [[secret]] row with source cmd:<W>/evil.sh (and, if it likes, a file: row naming a
private key bound to a host it owns, and an [update] channel and key of its own). Terminal 2, later, in any other
directory: `workcell run -- claude`. EFFECT: terminal 1 is admitted; in terminal 2 loadPolicy reads the rewritten
file, C54's check passes because the program lies outside that cwd, a binding is minted, and at the agent's first
request the broker runs <W>/evil.sh on the host as the operator. By contrast the same layout with the config
directory linked is refused (c19_test.go, the link arm).

Reproducing test, by the redteam from the claim alone: TestC85ConfigFileLinkedIntoTheWorkspace, package main of
cmd/workcell, 45 lines, its source below. Two arms share one body: config.toml linked to a file under the working
directory, and the control, linked to a file outside it. Each loads the policy and calls session with --mount on
c19Data's dummy artifacts; admitted means a session directory beside the earlier one. When the attacking arm is
admitted the test writes the program and the new policy by a host write to the link's target, in place of the
guest's write through /workspace, changes to another directory, loads the policy again and resolves the row's source
by secret.Resolve, the broker's own call. Run by the orchestrator by overlay, plain and under -race, logs saved: the
attacking arm fails with "the --mount session in <W> was admitted with <cfg>/workcell/config.toml a link to
<W>/dotfiles/config.toml, inside it; the policy the guest then wrote there is the user's policy of a session in
another directory (<nil>): secret {Name:stolen Source:cmd:<W>/tools/get-key.sh Host:attacker.example
Header:x-api-key}, and the host ran its program: value "C85-TOKEN", <nil>, ran on the host: true", and the control
arm passes. It passes once loadPolicy or session refuses, with no session directory made, in an error that names the
config file or the link's target.

Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, who repeated both runs. On the power the test takes: --mount serves
cwd live and the file service accepts a create and a write on a regular file, so the guest holds the link's target;
the test takes only the operator's own steps, the link and a mount session in the dotfiles tree. On the word
admitted: past holds and named into newSession, the dummy VMM failing at boot, as in the C19 and C54 tests; with a
real VMM the session boots and serves the file. The chain is real: the broker's Lookup calls Resolve per use and run
executes the program from / as the operator, and the marker file shows it; the later loadPolicy runs in another cwd,
so C54's check cannot fire. Not intended behaviour: holds and the link arm of c19_test.go show that the product
means to refuse this placement, and the file-level link slips past the directory-level resolve. Not high: the
ordinary layout, a real file under the config directory, is unaffected. Not low: the break is demonstrated. The
verifier's strongest argument against its own ruling: the operator chose both the link and the labelled --mount
(A5), and PARKED line 17 accepts that mount-mode writes land in the user's tree by design; rejected because the rule
already refuses the config directory in the same position, and the effect outlives the session and reaches every
later session in any directory, which the label does not say. Reasoned by the auditor and the verifier and not
shown: clone mode and the operator's own `workcell pull` into the tree land the same bytes without --mount. Not
recorded before: no row of PARKED.md or of the C19, C54 and C65 records names a config.toml link. Not S14: data.go,
policy.go and internal/policy are v2's own, nothing ported, no v1 line. Fix unit: S-F69, below S-1013 in PLAN.md.
The test is not parked under escape/_pending/: the test budget has no line of room and escape/ no layout left, so,
as C27's record did, this record holds it and the fix unit re-creates it; the source below is the file byte for
byte, each line behind four spaces.

Source of cmd/workcell/c85_test.go (45 lines):

    // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
    // Copyright 2026 Omkhar Arasaratnam
    //go:build linux || (darwin && arm64 && cgo)
    
    // Finding C85 of S-1013, sweep 3 (I13; I5 and I14 by consequence): the user's config.toml is a symbolic link to a file under the directory a --mount session runs in.
    package main
    
    import (
    	"cmp"
    	"os"
    	"path/filepath"
    	"strings"
    	"testing"
    
    	"github.com/omkhar/workcell/v2/internal/secret"
    )
    
    // TestC85ConfigFileLinkedIntoTheWorkspace (I13; I5, I14 by consequence): holds() refuses a workspace that holds the config directory (C19), but not one that holds the target of a config.toml symbolic link (a dotfiles repository), so `workcell run --mount` there is admitted, and guest root rewrites the operator's policy through /workspace: every later session in any directory reads its allow hosts, its [[secret]] rows (a cmd: program it left in the workspace, which the broker runs on the host at the first matching request; the C54 check judges only that session's own cwd) and its [update] table. No hypervisor runs here: the guest's write is modelled by a host write to the link's target, as C54 and C84 model theirs. The session must be refused before a session directory, key or export exists, in an error naming the config file; the same layout with the target outside the workspace (the control arm) must still run.
    func TestC85ConfigFileLinkedIntoTheWorkspace(t *testing.T) {
    	for _, arm := range []string{"config.toml linked to a file under the --mount workspace", "control: linked to a file outside it"} {
    		t.Run(arm, func(t *testing.T) {
    			work, cfg, data, under := must(filepath.EvalSymlinks(t.TempDir())), t.TempDir(), filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "workcell"), !strings.HasPrefix(arm, "control") // macOS: /var is /private/var
    			t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", cfg)
    			t.Setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", filepath.Dir(data))
    			target, program, marker := filepath.Join(cmp.Or(map[bool]string{true: work}[under], cfg), "dotfiles", "config.toml"), filepath.Join(work, "tools", "get-key.sh"), filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "C85-RAN-ON-THE-HOST")
    			must(0, cmp.Or(os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(cfg, "workcell"), 0o700), os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(target), 0o700), os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(program), 0o700), os.WriteFile(target, []byte("[network]\nallow = [\"api.anthropic.com\"]\n"), 0o600), os.Symlink(target, filepath.Join(cfg, "workcell", "config.toml"))))
    			a := c19Data(t, data, "/elsewhere")
    			t.Chdir(work)
    			allow, secrets, _, file, err := loadPolicy(nil, os.Stderr)
    			if err == nil {
    				err = session([]string{"true"}, limits{DiskMiB: 16}, true, a, allow, secrets).err
    			}
    			if admitted := len(must(os.ReadDir(filepath.Join(data, "sessions")))) > 1; !under && !admitted { // admitted: a session directory beyond the earlier one c19Data made; the dummy VMM then fails it at boot
    				t.Fatalf("control: the session with %s a link to %s, outside the workspace, was refused: %v", file, target, err)
    			} else if !under || err != nil && !admitted && (strings.Contains(err.Error(), file) || strings.Contains(err.Error(), target)) {
    				return // refused before a session directory exists, naming the config file: the invariant holds
    			}
    			must(0, cmp.Or(os.WriteFile(program, []byte("#!/bin/sh\necho ran > "+marker+"\necho C85-TOKEN\n"), 0o700), os.WriteFile(target, []byte("[network]\nallow = [\"attacker.example\"]\n\n[[secret]]\nname = \"stolen\"\nsource = \"cmd:"+program+"\"\nhost = \"attacker.example\"\nheader = \"x-api-key\"\n"), 0o600)))
    			t.Chdir(t.TempDir())                                                                 // above, the guest's write through /workspace, modelled on the host: the operator's policy is now the guest's, and so is the program the host runs; here, the operator's next session, in any directory
    			allow, secrets, _, _, err = loadPolicy(nil, os.Stderr)                               // a row is accepted only with its host in the allow list, so an accepted row shows both
    			v, runErr := secret.Resolve(t.Context(), append(secrets, binding{})[0].grant.Source) // what the broker runs at the first request on that host
    			t.Errorf("I13: the --mount session in %s was admitted with %s a link to %s, inside it; the policy the guest then wrote there is the user's policy of a session in another directory (%v): secret %+v, and the host ran its program: value %q, %v, ran on the host: %t", work, file, target, err, append(secrets, binding{})[0].grant, v, runErr, exists(marker))
    		})
    	}
    }

C86. ID I6 (on a terminated connection the upstream certificate matches an allowed name, under the host's trust) and
through it I5 (the real secret goes only into a verified connection); the class and grade of C30 and C53, in the
absolute spelling that those fixes left. ATTACKER: guest root in a --mount session, by hostile model output or a
repository hook, whose export holds the file that SSL_CERT_FILE names or the directory that an SSL_CERT_DIR entry
names, completed by the network attacker as the host resolver's answer for an allowed name (the rebind model of C7,
C30, C53, C66 and C69), against every later session of the operator. Also, with no mount: a malicious repository
that ships the file at that path, when the operator runs a clone session there. SEVERITY: medium (S6: a demonstrated
break with one precondition the attacker does not control: the operator's SSL_CERT_FILE or SSL_CERT_DIR names an
absolute path inside a directory in which they run a session, such as a corporate bundle kept in a dotfiles or certs
tree). WHERE: internal/proxy/terminate.go, where upstreamRoots refuses a relative certFile and a relative
SSL_CERT_DIR entry, then calls x509.SystemCertPool, which reads both variables itself, and reads certFile, called
from Terminate for every session that terminates a name; cmd/workcell/run_vm.go, where boot calls bind, which calls
Terminate, before Start, and session judges cwd against the data, config and temp directories and by identity, never
against the environment's trust files. also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go (the file is ported; the missing
judgement could as well live in cmd/workcell, which is v2's own). INPUT: SSL_CERT_FILE=<W>/certs/corp-ca.pem, or
SSL_CERT_DIR naming <W>/certs, in the operator's environment. Terminal 1: `cd <W> && workcell run --mount --
claude`; the guest writes its own CA's PEM into /workspace/certs/corp-ca.pem, or adds a file to /workspace/certs.
Terminal 2, later, anywhere, with a [[secret]] row bound to an allowed host: `workcell run -- claude`; the resolver
answers that host with the attacker's address, whose server presents a leaf for the name signed by the planted CA.
EFFECT: terminal 1 is admitted; in terminal 2 Terminate builds the pool from the planted file, the leaf verifies,
and the proxy puts the real secret into the request that it sends to the attacker; where the relative spellings are
refused (c30_test.go, c53_test.go) and the same path as [update] ca is refused by newInstaller.

Reproducing test, by the redteam from the claim alone: TestC86SSLCertPathUnderTheWorkingDirectory, package main of
cmd/workcell, 50 lines, its source below. Four arms share one body: a clone session with SSL_CERT_FILE under cwd, a
mount session with the same, a clone session with an SSL_CERT_DIR entry under cwd, and the control, SSL_CERT_FILE
under a directory outside cwd and the data directory. Each writes the certificate of an authority that the test
made, loads a policy that allows one host and calls session on c19Data's dummy artifacts; it wants the session
refused before newSession, with no session directory beside the earlier one, in an error that names the variable,
and the control admitted. The admission loads no system pool, so the SSL_CERT_DIR arm runs in the same process. A
second file is evidence and not the test that a fix turns green: TestC86AbsoluteSSLCertPathUnderTheWorkingDirectory,
package proxy, 44 lines, its source below too; it runs itself again once per variable (C53's pattern, since Go loads
the system pool once per process), writes certs/ca.pem under cwd, calls the real Terminate and sends one request
through the package's own testProxy to a loopback upstream that holds a leaf of that CA. Run by the orchestrator by
overlay, plain and under -race, four logs saved: the three attacking arms fail with "session gave start firecracker:
invalid argument, a session directory made: true; want refused before newSession in an error naming SSL_CERT_FILE:
true" (SSL_CERT_DIR in the third), the control arm passes, and the probe fails in both children with "the attacker's
upstream, holding a leaf of the repository's CA, answered (200, "real-secret"): the real secret left".

Outcome: CONFIRMED at medium by the verifier, who repeated the four runs. The effect claimed is shown across the two
packages, the admission in cmd/workcell and the secret leaving at Terminate in internal/proxy, with no product code
bypassed: session admits on holds, the TMPDIR rule and named only, then boot, bind and Terminate; upstreamRoots
refuses only a value that does not start with a slash. The guest's power is real: the file service serves the
--mount export read-write (mkdir, create, open for writing with truncation, write), so a guest creates certs/ca.pem
or appends its CA to a bundle, and the fixtures (testProxy, fakeBroker, the lookup and dial seams standing for the
DNS position) are those that C30 and C53 were confirmed with. The one link not run, the guest's write through the
file service in a real VM, needs no VM to be believed. The clone variant with no mount is weaker, since the operator
would have to check a hostile repository out onto their own bundle's path; the --mount variant alone carries the
finding. Not higher: it needs the operator's environment. Not lower: unlike C79 and C84, where I14's key, serial,
expiry and digest still gated, here I6 and I5 are shown broken. The verifier's strongest argument against its own
ruling: SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR are the process's trust store, which every Go program honours, and an
operator who points them into a tree and then runs an agent with --mount in that very tree has handed over the root
by their own act, a narrower precondition than C30's and C53's; kept because the product already refuses every other
host-trusted path under cwd (C30, C53, C79, C84), C79's verifier accepted this precondition class as a finding, and
the control arm shows that a fix need not refuse a bundle kept elsewhere. Recorded before, but never as a finding
and never with a test: C53's record ("an absolute SSL_CERT_DIR entry that is the repository's own path ... no
distinct finding") and the S-1005 sweep 3 note that an absolute SSL_CERT_FILE inside the repository needs the
operator's own environment to name it; this record corrects both. No row of PARKED.md holds it. Not S14:
terminate.go is ported from v1 and no v1 release holds it (SPEC section 13), run_vm.go is v2's own, and the reading
of the variables is Go's documented behaviour, not a weakness in Go. also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go. Fix
unit: S-F70, below S-1013 in PLAN.md. As for C85, nothing is parked under escape/_pending/: this record holds the
test, byte for byte behind four spaces, and the fix unit re-creates it; the probe is evidence, and the fix unit need
not keep it.

Source of cmd/workcell/c86_test.go (50 lines):

    // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
    // Copyright 2026 Omkhar Arasaratnam
    
    // Finding C86 of S-1013, sweep 3 (I6, through it I5): SSL_CERT_FILE, or an entry of SSL_CERT_DIR, names by an absolute path a file under the directory the session runs in. The absolute sibling of C30 and C53.
    
    //go:build linux || (darwin && arm64 && cgo)
    
    package main
    
    import (
    	"cmp"
    	"io"
    	"os"
    	"path/filepath"
    	"strings"
    	"testing"
    	"time"
    
    	"github.com/omkhar/workcell/v2/internal/proxy"
    )
    
    // TestC86SSLCertPathUnderTheWorkingDirectory (I6, I5): upstreamRoots refuses a relative SSL_CERT_FILE or SSL_CERT_DIR entry (C30, C53) but takes an absolute one wherever it lies, so SSL_CERT_FILE=<cwd>/certs/ca.pem makes a file of the repository a root of the proxy's upstream pool: a malicious repository ships it, or guest root under --mount writes it for every later session of the operator (modelled by a host write, as C54 does: no hypervisor here), and a leaf of that CA, from the network attacker as the host resolver's answer for an allowed name, verifies and is sent the real secret (the probe internal/proxy/c86_probe_test.go shows it leaving). The session must be refused before newSession in an error naming the variable, as an [update] ca under cwd is (C79); the same file under a directory outside cwd and the data directory (the control arm) is still accepted. The VMM is a dummy: an admitted session fails at boot, after its directory exists. The admission needs no load of the system pool, so the SSL_CERT_DIR arm runs in this process. Precondition the attacker does not control: the operator's environment names a path under the repository.
    func TestC86SSLCertPathUnderTheWorkingDirectory(t *testing.T) {
    	for _, tc := range []struct {
    		name, env    string
    		mount, under bool
    	}{{"clone, SSL_CERT_FILE under cwd", "SSL_CERT_FILE", false, true}, {"mount, SSL_CERT_FILE under cwd", "SSL_CERT_FILE", true, true}, {"clone, an SSL_CERT_DIR entry under cwd", "SSL_CERT_DIR", false, true}, {"control: SSL_CERT_FILE outside cwd and the data directory", "SSL_CERT_FILE", false, false}} {
    		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
    			work, data, config := must(filepath.EvalSymlinks(t.TempDir())), filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "workcell"), filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "workcell") // macOS: /var is /private/var
    			file := cmp.Or(map[bool]string{true: filepath.Join(work, "certs", "ca.pem")}[tc.under], filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "corp", "roots.pem"))       // the attacker's file in the repository, or the operator's own authority elsewhere (the control arm)
    			t.Setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", filepath.Dir(data))
    			t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", filepath.Dir(config))
    			t.Setenv("TMPDIR", t.TempDir()) // --mount refuses a cwd under the temp directory
    			t.Setenv(tc.env, cmp.Or(map[string]string{"SSL_CERT_DIR": "/etc/ssl/certs:" + filepath.Dir(file)}[tc.env], file))
    			ca := must(proxy.NewSessionCA([]string{"api.example.com"}, time.Now().Add(time.Hour))) // the attacker's authority; it keeps the key
    			must(0, cmp.Or(os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(file), 0o700), os.MkdirAll(config, 0o700), os.WriteFile(file, ca.CertPEM(), 0o600), os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(config, "config.toml"), []byte("[network]\nallow = [\"api.example.com\"]\n"), 0o600)))
    			a := c19Data(t, data, "/elsewhere")
    			t.Chdir(work)
    			allow, secrets, _, _, err := loadPolicy(nil, io.Discard)
    			if err == nil {
    				err = session([]string{"true"}, limits{DiskMiB: 16}, tc.mount, a, allow, secrets).err
    			}
    			ents, _ := os.ReadDir(filepath.Join(data, "sessions"))
    			started, refused := len(ents) > 1, err != nil && strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.env) // started: a session directory beside the earlier session's, so newSession ran
    			if started == tc.under || refused != tc.under {
    				t.Errorf("I6: %s=%q, under cwd %t, --mount %t: session gave %v, a session directory made: %t; want refused before newSession in an error naming %s: %t", tc.env, os.Getenv(tc.env), tc.under, tc.mount, err, started, tc.env, tc.under)
    			}
    		})
    	}
    }

Source of the evidence probe, internal/proxy/c86_probe_test.go (44 lines):

    // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
    // Copyright 2026 Omkhar Arasaratnam
    
    // Evidence probe for finding C86 of S-1013, sweep 3 (I6, through it I5): the absolute sibling of C30 and C53. Terminate under SSL_CERT_FILE=<cwd>/certs/ca.pem, or SSL_CERT_DIR=<cwd>/certs, builds the upstream pool from the repository's file, so the attacker's upstream, holding a leaf of that CA for an allowed name, is sent the real secret. The fix lies in cmd/workcell (the session is refused before newSession, see cmd/workcell/c86_test.go, the reproducing test), so this probe shows the effect and stays red on its own: it is not the test the fix turns green.
    
    package proxy
    
    import (
    	"crypto/tls"
    	"net/http"
    	"net/netip"
    	"os"
    	"os/exec"
    	"path/filepath"
    	"strings"
    	"testing"
    	"time"
    )
    
    // TestC86AbsoluteSSLCertPathUnderTheWorkingDirectory re-runs this binary once per variable, since Go loads the system pool once per process and SSL_CERT_DIR reaches it only that way. The child, in a working directory W holding certs/ca.pem (the attacker's CA: the repository ships it, or guest root writes it under --mount, modelled by this host write), under SSL_CERT_FILE=W/certs/ca.pem or SSL_CERT_DIR=W/certs alone, has Terminate take the file, and the attacker's loopback upstream echoes the secret it got.
    func TestC86AbsoluteSSLCertPathUnderTheWorkingDirectory(t *testing.T) {
    	if os.Getenv("C86_CHILD") == "" {
    		for _, v := range []string{"SSL_CERT_FILE", "SSL_CERT_DIR"} {
    			cmd := exec.Command(os.Args[0], "-test.run=^"+t.Name()+"$")
    			cmd.Dir = t.TempDir()
    			cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "C86_CHILD=1", "SSL_CERT_FILE=", "SSL_CERT_DIR=", v+"="+strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Join(cmd.Dir, "certs", "ca.pem"), map[string]string{"SSL_CERT_DIR": "/ca.pem"}[v])) // the one variable set, to an absolute path under the working directory
    			if out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
    				t.Errorf("under %s, an absolute path under the working directory: %v\n%s", v, err, out)
    			}
    		}
    		return
    	}
    	repoCA, sessionCA := must(NewSessionCA([]string{"api.example.com"}, time.Now().Add(time.Hour))), must(NewSessionCA([]string{"api.example.com"}, time.Now().Add(time.Hour)))
    	must(0, os.Mkdir("certs", 0o700)) // the attacker made repoCA and keeps the key of the leaf below
    	must(0, os.WriteFile("certs/ca.pem", repoCA.CertPEM(), 0o600))
    	ln := must(tls.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0", &tls.Config{Certificates: []tls.Certificate{*must(repoCA.leaf("api.example.com"))}}))       // the attacker's upstream, where its DNS answer sends the proxy
    	go http.Serve(ln, http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { _, _ = w.Write([]byte(r.Header.Get("X-Api-Key"))) })) // echoes the credential header it got
    	p, _, _ := testProxy(t, "api.example.com:443", []netip.Addr{netip.MustParseAddr("8.8.8.8")}, ln.Addr().String())
    	if p.Terminate(sessionCA, &fakeBroker{value: "real-secret"}, []TerminateRule{{Host: "api.example.com", Header: "X-Api-Key", Placeholder: testPlaceholder}}) == nil { // a refusal here would hold the invariant as well
    		if code, body := get(t, clientVia(listen(t, p, 443), caPool(t, sessionCA)), "https://api.example.com/v1/x", testPlaceholder); code < 400 || body == "real-secret" {
    			t.Errorf("I6: under SSL_CERT_FILE=%q SSL_CERT_DIR=%q, absolute paths under the working directory, the attacker's upstream, holding a leaf of the repository's CA, answered (%d, %q): the real secret left", os.Getenv("SSL_CERT_FILE"), os.Getenv("SSL_CERT_DIR"), code, body)
    		}
    	}
    }

carried by its own test to the program run on the host. One: the link's target is not made yet, so resolved fell

hard link to a file under the working directory, which no link resolution sees and which the file service lets

its own overlay test on the round and found a third spelling: a relative target read through a linked config
directory was joined to the link's unresolved directory, so its `..` climbed by spelling; the builder corrected

## S-F71: the secret-source check as ADR-006 decides it (I5), the class of C54, C58, C72, C75, C78, C80, C81 and C82

S-F71 built check one, decision (a), of docs/adr/accepted/006-judge-structure.md, commits d95fab2 (the tests) and
25b0488 (the fix) (PR #357). loadPolicy in cmd/workcell/policy.go keeps one loop over p.Secret, the user's rows
whatever workcell.toml kept. The scheme must be exactly file, cmd, secret-service, keychain or signin. The one path
the host itself opens or runs, the `file:` path or the first field of a `cmd:` source as strings.Fields splits it
for Resolve, must be absolute and must not lie in or lead into the working directory or the data directory, by
leadsInto of data.go over every prefix. A `file:` path must also name, by os.Stat at load, a regular file with one
name; a program is not held to one name. No word after the program is read. sep, the word loop, the separator
grammar and the twelve characters are gone. Every refusal is made at load, before a session directory exists.
docs/policy.md says so in two sentences where it had six, and its `file:` bullet names the newly refused rows.

Closed, FIXED by S-F71 at 25b0488, each refused at load:
- C54, for `file:` and for a program in, or linked from, the directory: TestC54SecretSourceUnderTheWorkspace keeps
  those arms (under the directory, through `..`, a program under it, a program and a file through a link in it).
- C58: TestC58RepositoryCannotSwitchOffTheSourceCheck, unchanged, since the loop walks the user's rows.
- C82: TestC82RelativeFileSource, unchanged, since a `file:` path that is not absolute is refused.
- The three rows of the parked line `S-F66 redteam notes`: a scheme in capitals or unknown (`FILE:`, `File:`,
  `foo:`, `Cmd:`); `file://localhost<path>`, which names no regular file; and a hard link outside the directory to
  the key inside, which has two names.
- Newly refused with them: a `file:` that is absent, a directory, a FIFO or a link to a file not made yet; a `cmd:`
  with no program or a relative one; a `file:` path or a program in the data directory or reached through a link
  that leads into it.

Accepted, out of scope by SPEC section 2 (what the program of a `cmd:` secret source reads through its arguments),
with the ADR's reason: each is a word after the program, read by the program, naming a key or script that the
operator placed under the directory; without the row the key is in the export just the same and no check sees it;
and a rule over such words did not converge, eight rows after six fixes. docs/policy.md states the duty.
- C72, C75, C78, C80 and C81. Their tests are deleted: TestC72SecretPathInsideAnOptionWord,
  TestC75WorkspaceBeforeAListSeparator, TestC78SecretPathSpelledFromHome, TestC80RelativeWordReadFromRoot and
  TestC81RelativeTextAfterASeparator. The fixes of S-F56, S-F59, S-F62, S-F64 and S-F65 went with the word loop.
- The two `cmd:/bin/sh <script in the directory>` arms of C54, clone and mount, deleted from its test. This is the
  one accepted row that reaches past the key: under --mount the guest can rewrite a script that the host then runs.
- The five rows of the parked lines `S-F64 redteam, reviewer and builder notes` and `S-F65 redteam and reviewer
  notes` (xargs -a, a file URL with a host, env -C, grep -rh from the parent, a percent-encoded file URL).
- The residues of `S-F69 not closed` and `S-F70 not closed`, as the ADR's table rules them: a link that the
  operator made outside the directory, a name or a member made while a session runs, and a cost at start. The
  reviewer ran the first as a probe: it loads, and neither the guest nor a repository can make that link.
Those five parked lines are deleted from PARKED.md.

Proved: TestSF71SecretSourceJudgedAsTheHostOpensIt, new in cmd/workcell/sf71_test.go, has 30 arms. With main's
policy.go 21 of them fail: 19 rows that main loaded and made a session for, and 2 rows that main refused and the
ADR admits (C72's `--key=<cwd>/...` and `/bin/cat <cwd>/...`). The other 9 pass on main and on the fix: the five
admitted sources (a `file:` of one name outside, `cmd:/bin/sh <outside>/get-key.sh --verbose`, secret-service,
keychain and signin rows), and four rows that main already refused (an empty `file:` path, `cmd:<cwd>/tool` where
tool is a link to /bin/sh, and a program and a file reached from outside through a link into the directory, the
rows the ADR left to be proved by running). With the fix all 30 pass, as do the C54, C58 and C82 tests and
go test ./... (counted by the orchestrator by overlay; run by the redteam, the builder and the reviewer too). No test was replaced: the three kept
tests stand as they were but for C54's two deleted arms. The reviewer, one round, returned no finding. Product
14998 of 15000, test 28285 of 28497, Markdown 1445 of 2500. The Nlink cast on darwin is proved by the hosted
gate-macos alone.

## S-F72: the method-and-path rule as ADR-006 decides it (I6), the class of C10, C33, C68, C71, C73 and C74

S-F72 built check two, decision (d), of docs/adr/accepted/006-judge-structure.md, commits 06647e5 (the tests) and
bcabe43 (the fix) (PR #358). In internal/proxy/terminate.go an unnarrowed rule swaps on any request. A rule with a
`path` or `repos` swaps only when canonical(req.URL) holds, when no header folds under the one RFC 3875 fold
(cgiName) to x_original_url or x_rewrite_url, and when the path as sent is under the rule's path (or the path as
sent plus "/" is the rule's path) or within a repository. canonical is one function: EscapedPath() equals Go's own
escaping of the decoded path, path.Clean leaves it as it is but for one trailing slash, and it holds no `;` and no
backslash. The rule names no method: the `method` key left the `[[secret]]` row, and internal/policy refuses it at
load as an unknown key, naming the line. On a sign-in host a path that is not canonical is refused 400 in the
target_refused check, and tokenEndpoint in signin.go claims the path by EqualFold alone. methodPattern, Method, the
method checks, readable, folded, fold, opaque, params, sep, the PHP fold, four of the six override names and the
scope switch are gone. The proxy forwards with httputil.ReverseProxy, whose Rewrite sets scheme and host only, so
the path judged is the request line sent. docs/policy.md says the rule in 8 lines where it had 11.

Closed, FIXED by S-F72 at bcabe43:
- C10: TestFoldedPathEscapesTheEndpointAndTheRule (c10_test.go), rewritten under its name: each spelling gets no
  token and no secret, and on the sign-in host each gets 400.
- C33: TestC33PathBindingReleasesSecretOutsideBinding (c33_test.go), rewritten under its name: the served arm
  `/v1/a%2Fb/c` is a refused arm, with `%5C` and GET beside it.
- C68: TestC68RoutingOverrideHeaders (c68_test.go), rewritten under its name: the three method-override rows are
  served inside the rule, since nothing names a method, and the two path-override headers are refused under every
  spelling the fold covers.
- C71, C73 and C74: TestC71FormMethodOverride, TestC73JSONMethodOverride and TestC74DotMethodQuery are deleted with
  their files. The row `method in secret` of TestParseRefuses in internal/policy/policy_test.go replaces the three:
  `method = "POST"` in a `[[secret]]` row is refused as `config.toml:7: unknown key "method" in [[secret]]`.
- New: TestSF72AdmittedPathReachesUpstreamAsJudged (sf72_test.go). A local upstream records the request line it
  receives. An admitted path arrives byte for byte as judged, with the real secret, under GET, POST and DELETE.
  `//v1/x`, `/v1%00/x`, a doubled slash, dot segments, `%2e%2e`, `%2F`, `%41`, `;`, `%3B`, `%5C`, `/v2/x` and
  `/v1x` are refused and never reach it.

Proof. Against main's product code the four tests of internal/proxy fail with 41 error lines, counted by the
orchestrator (c10 20, c33 3, c68 3, sf72 15), and the row `method in secret` fails; with the fix all pass, as does
go test ./internal/... ./cmd/... ./escape/... The hosted gate on bcabe43 ran the suite on a real VM: the five I6
rows (sni-host-mismatch-h1, sni-authority-mismatch-h2, ech-hidden-sni, terminated-session-leaf and
upstream-leaf-mismatch) pass, and so does the I5 row placeholder-narrowed, which now narrows by path alone and
fails on `control`. Product 14974 of 15000, test 28198 of 28461, Markdown 1442 of 2500.

Not closed by the design, and left to the maintainer. The reviewer, one round, found the design built as decided
and gave one finding against the design itself: canonical holds for `/v1/%EF%BC%8E%EF%BC%8E/admin` (two fullwidth
stops), `/v1/%252e%252e/admin` and `/v1/%C0%AE%C0%AE/admin`, so a `/v1/` rule swaps on them, and an upstream that
maps such bytes to `.` or decodes a second time would read `/admin`. The orchestrator ran the four spellings
against main and against the fix: both admit them, so the fix did not open this. No such upstream was run, so no
break was reproduced (R2), and the remedy offered, to refuse every byte outside ASCII and every `%` in a decoded
path, changes what the accepted ADR-006 admits, which is the maintainer's to decide. It is parked in PARKED.md
(`S-F72 reviewer finding`) for S-1005 of sweep 4 and for the maintainer.

After S-F72: both checks of ADR-006 are built. Sweep 4, S-1002 to S-1013, is next. Nothing waits under

## S-1002, sweep 4: host-guest channel, guest init, supervisor lifecycle (I7, I10, I12), as built at main cfa8d5f

Sweep 4 (S8), the one further sweep that the maintainer allowed on 2026-11-26 after ADR-006, fresh context (S3),
the whole surface read as built after S-F47 to S-F72, not a diff. Auditor on the top tier in the cloud session,
which has no hypervisor. The auditor wrote its own trust boundary and worked every lens before it opened any
earlier record. One candidate, C87, confirmed by the verifier, who reads it as medium where the auditor claimed low.

Trust boundary. The supervisor (`workcell run`, `pull`, `diff`, `bench`; the operator's uid) owns the VMM
child (Firecracker: Pdeathsig SIGKILL, Setpgid, the forking thread locked and its affinity cut to --cpus; vz:
in-process), the in-process proxy, resolver, broker and audit log, the host key, the session directory, the layer
markers through installer.fail, the operator's terminal in raw mode, and the export and the pull destination as
descriptors. Attacker bytes enter at six points. (1) vsock 5000, one connection taken by `once`: wire frames (6-byte
header, version 1, length checked before allocation at 64 KiB, 5 s per frame once begun, bufio, every error sticky);
output() takes Stdout and Stderr (coalesced, paced at 2^16 frames per 64 ms, raw to the seat and the operator's
terminal by design), Ack (4 bytes), Exit (2 to 257 bytes, Err printed %q); on pull, Entry, Data and Exit through
manifest.add, checkPath, fold, put (openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH, NO_SYMLINKS and NO_XDEV beneath the destination)
and compare. What they can change: the exit code, terminal bytes, the `first` flag that drives installer.fail
inside the fresh window alone, and bytes under the destination. (2) vsock 5001, many connections, 1024 slots:
a 20-byte header within 5 s, then TCP bytes to the proxy's adapter for a served port, or one 2-byte-framed DNS
query to the resolver; what they change: audit Notes (soft 8 MiB) and dials to allowlisted names. (3) vsock
5002 under --mount, one connection: raw FUSE requests to internal/fileserve (16 workers, 4096 descriptors, 2^17
nodes, growth charged to --disk, paced at 1024 requests per 64 ms); what they change: the operator's own tree,
live, by the (handle, name) grammar. (4) The serial console through a paced blocking pipe into a 4 KiB tail,
printed sanitised only when a boot fails. (5) Guest-written disks: workspace.ext4 (never mounted on the host;
booted again for pull), rw caches (attached to later guests only by the operator's --cache). (6) The repository:
exported by a descriptor walk whose files are opened again with O_NOFOLLOW and O_NONBLOCK and a device, inode
and size check, its cwd judged by holds, within, leadsInto and the TMPDIR rule, then compared by named() against
".", which is what Export and openMount use. Host-written and out of the guest's reach: lock (pid), repo, vmm,
inodes, the markers, the attach socket (0700 directory, same uid), firecracker.json and the kernel command line
(integers, fixed words, compiled-in provider names, cache names of a fixed alphabet, uint16 ports). No file
of this surface carries `// Ported from v1` (the markers are in internal/proxy/{proxy,terminate,allowlist}.go,
internal/secret/{broker,source}.go, internal/audit/lines.go and three tests; checked as built), so nothing here
falls under S14.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: readFrame clears the deadline only when nothing is buffered, arms it once at
the first read that must wait, refuses a length over 64 KiB before allocating and never resyncs; output()'s held
buffer never passes MaxPayload and its backing array is reused; guest.DecodeExit, Ack and Entry, relay.Decode
and ReadFrame, resolver.question and fileserve.parse are bounded and round-trip; ten-second fuzz bursts on wire
FuzzReadFrame (1.07M execs), guest FuzzDecode (555k), relay FuzzDecode (20k) and FuzzReadFrame (1.19M), fileserve
FuzzRequest (359k), resolver FuzzAnswer (1.49M) and cmd/workcell FuzzPath (103k), no crasher. The pull manifest
is bounded by MaxEntries, MaxNames and the image's bytes plus a block per inode; the console tail cannot grow;
the relay's slots and the audit soft limit bound a flood of refused streams; host CPU on both guest streams
is paced (S-F34, S-F47). Logic and state: output() ends on Exit, a bad Ack or an unknown type and flushes held
output before any frame of another kind; `first` is true only for the guest's first frame, and fail acts only
while fresh pairs this start's install with what it replaced (the C2 residual stands as accepted); session()
orders holds, the --mount TMPDIR rule, the SSL_CERT_DIR member walk, named(), newSession, Export(".") and boot;
boot refuses a TMPDIR under a running mount session's repo before MkdirTemp and records the VMM directory before
Start; the init's serve loop halts on anything a host never sends; pull's manifest, data, end sequence is strict
and charges apparent sizes; the lock protocol is unchanged and tested. Concurrency and check-to-use: `once` closes
the listener after the first accept; the first connection to 5000 and 5002 is the init's because no guest code runs
before Exec; the seat mutex covers send against sit; the channel has one writer goroutine and one reader; named()
closes C61's swap and Export reads beneath one descriptor with a device, inode and size check; fileserve's `at`
checks every link of a node's chain by identity again, and openFlags admit O_ACCMODE and O_TRUNC alone. The one
check-to-use gap found is C87: compare judges a name by the walk's fstatat and opens it later without O_NONBLOCK,
where openSource, the export's twin, has it. The windows that remain (a mount session the operator starts between
another session's MkdirTemp and its recordBoot, stop's pid reuse, two sessions in one nanosecond with the same
32 random bits) are operator-timed or chance, as recorded. Cryptography and identity: none on the channel by
design; the vsock peer is the VMM through a 0700 per-session directory (Firecracker) or a per-VM device (vz);
the session CA goes to the guest as the public certificate alone, capped at 16 KiB; the audit key stays under
the data directory, which holds() keeps out of every export in both directions, by inode and by mount point (c52
and c65 ran in the auditor's session as root and passed); a relayed stream's LocalAddr reaches the proxy only
as a listener address whose port is read and never dialled. Failure modes: every exit from boot runs closeAll;
session_end is recorded after the VM is gone and before the lock is released; an export failure keeps the session
directory with its failed end (S-F67) and removes the image; named() refuses when either stat fails; fileserve
maps unknown errors to EIO, ends Serve on any stream error and closes every descriptor; the init treats every
setup failure as less, never more. No error path fails open. The one unbounded wait a guest can arrange is C87's
open. Downgrade, rollback and replay: wire version 1 and relay version 1 alone; FUSE major 7 alone, a second INIT
is EIO; no sequence numbers by design; frames after Exit are never read; the fresh-window first-frame rollback
is the accepted C2 residual, unchanged. Interaction between surfaces: Exec carries placeholders and the CA only
(I5, I6); S-F71's loadPolicy judges the one path the host opens or runs with os.Stat, no open, so a FIFO as a
`file:` source cannot park the load, and does so before any session directory exists; the pull VM boots with no
allowlist, no layers and no caches, its relay denies every header and its resolver answers nothing; a mount guest
on an ancestor can still steer pull, log and attach among the operator's own sessions by the spelling of repo
(parked, no gain) and, new here, can park `workcell diff` on a FIFO that the operator's tree holds (C87).

Refuted by the auditor before anything was raised: a guest that connects to 5000 or 5002 before the init (only
the init runs before Exec, and 5002 is dialled in setup); Stdout and Stderr floods (coalesced, paced, dropped
when the seat's client stalls past 5 s); forged Acks and extra Pings or Pulls from the guest (they end its own
session with 125); a halted guest (the same as a command that never ends); a guest that stops the init reading
(the host's Stdin writes fail after 5 s); SIGINT during a long export (buffered, then forwarded once and honoured
twice); the SSL_CERT_DIR member walk against a huge directory under cwd (ReadDir only, then refused by leadsInto);
terminal answerbacks (C4, parked); the forged first frame (C2, accepted). In fileserve: MKNOD and LINK are ENOSYS,
setattr strips setuid bits and refuses chown, an open of a FIFO, socket or device is EPERM after a non-blocking
open, links are ELOOP, files with more than one name are read-only, writes are charged for holes and growth, and
a stolen 5002 connection has exactly the init's authority. The relay: a UDP header for any port but 53 and a TCP
header for an unserved port close with nothing dialled, and slots are released on every path. The export: a swap
of an intermediate component or of the final file between walk and copy is refused by device, inode and size, and
a FIFO at the final component is opened non-blocking and refused as not regular. Pull: put never opens an existing
file (unlink, then O_CREAT with O_EXCL) and dirBeneath is O_DIRECTORY, so only diff's read path can block (C87). A
second `--mount` session of one directory (explicit and labelled, A5); bench and pull leaving directories after
a SIGKILL (recorded, operator action); a diff whose newest session is the running mount session itself (refused
by the lock); a FIFO planted by the guest for C87 (it cannot make one, so the operator's tree must already hold one).

Recorded fixes of this surface, checked as built by the auditor: C1 and C2 (S-F1), C3 (S-F2), C5 (S-F24), C19
and C29, C28 and C56, C50 (S-F33), C51 (S-F34), C52 and C65, C61, C62, C63, C64 (S-F47, TestPace), C83 (S-F67),
C85 and C86 (S-F69, S-F70) and S-F71's one-path judge. Each still holds; `go test -count=1` of cmd/workcell,
cmd/workcell-init, internal/{wire,guest,relay,fileserve,resolver,workspace,audit,rootfs} and internal/vmm/... passed
and `go vet` was clean.

and fileserve.Server, with pipes and FIFOs the probes themselves made (S12, T8). Not run by the auditor: any VM
row, the escape suite, any macOS path, any control adapter run, fuzzing beyond ten seconds a target.

Evidence gaps, not findings, unchanged from earlier records (R3): no escape row exercises `workcell stop` or `rm`
on a running session; the host-disk bound of the workspace image rests on run_test.go's workspace-cap alone;
the vz console copy is unpaced and I10 is not enforced on macOS; the file service's 4096 descriptors assume
headroom under RLIMIT_NOFILE, and the relay's exit on EMFILE is a fail-closed self-denial.

### S-1002 candidates, sweep 4

C87. ID I12 (a host process, here `workcell diff`, hangs on what a guest shaped through the file service's channel),
with R6 (the host reads a tree the guest controlled without non-blocking handling). Attacker: guest root of a
`--mount` session, by hostile model output or a malicious repository's hook running as the agent, whose export
is an ancestor of the directory in which the operator runs `workcell diff` (the C61 layout). Preconditions the
attacker does not control: the operator runs `diff` in a subdirectory of a live `--mount` tree, and a FIFO already
lies somewhere in that tree, because the file service answers MKNOD with ENOSYS and git carries no FIFO, so the
guest can only move one. Where: cmd/workcell/pull_linux.go:24 fileBeneath (openat2 with O_RDONLY, O_NOFOLLOW
and O_CLOEXEC, RESOLVE_BENEATH, NO_SYMLINKS and NO_XDEV, and no O_NONBLOCK), called from sameBytes inside
compare in cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go; the twin in pull_darwin.go:26 has the same shape and no in-scope route,
since macOS has no --mount. internal/rootfs/ext4file.go:98 opens with O_NONBLOCK "so that a file swapped for
a FIFO cannot hold the open", and compare does not. Input: session A is `workcell run --mount` in /work, live;
the operator runs `workcell diff` in /work/proj, which has an earlier clone session. Guest root in A, through its
own mount: LOOKUP of an existing FIFO under /work, then RENAME of it over /work/proj/README, after the diff's walk
(guest.Walk skips a FIFO by fstatat) and before compare opens README; the window is the rest of the walk and the
transfer of every file that precedes README in the manifest, and the guest may swap in a loop. Effect claimed:
`workcell diff` parks in open(2) for as long as no writer opens the FIFO, holding the clone session's lock, so
`workcell rm` refuses. No byte leaves the host and nothing is written: a hang of one operator verb, not a break
of I1 or I8. Severity claimed by the auditor: low, as hardening.

Reproducing test (S4): TestC87CompareFIFOReturns, a Go test of package main in cmd/workcell, 56 lines, written by
the redteam from the claim alone, with no VM and so no T2: a temporary directory with regular files a and b and
a FIFO f; the manifest is the host's own walk on a separate descriptor; the source callback renames f over b at
its first call, which compare makes after its walk judged b and before sameBytes opens b; the judged property is
only that compare returns within 3 s, and on a timeout the test fails, opens b for writing and waits, so nothing
is left behind. It waits in escape/_pending/S-F73/c87_test.go (commit ab4e460), which Go does not compile. Run by
the orchestrator on 0f6ee5b with `go test -overlay`, plain and with -race: `--- FAIL: TestC87CompareFIFOReturns
(3.00s)`, `compare is still parked 3s after opening a FIFO that no writer holds: workcell diff hangs (I12)`. The
redteam's cross-check: with O_NONBLOCK added to fileBeneath by overlay the test passes in 0.00 s, so it does
not fail whatever the code. The power the test gives itself: it places the rename in the window by the callback,
where the attacker must win a race; the window is real and wide, but no run on a VM showed the race won end to end.

Outcome: CONFIRMED by the verifier, from its own run of the test and three probes of its own, and read by it as
medium, not low. Its evidence. One: the test fails as recorded. Two: through the real file service by overlay,
`LOOKUP f: errno 0 mode=010000`, `RENAME f -> b: errno 0`, b on disk is then a FIFO, and `MKNOD g (FIFO): function
not implemented`; so a mount guest can rename an existing FIFO over a regular file and cannot make one, and the
test claims no power the guest lacks beyond the timing. holds() and fetch do not refuse a diff directory inside
a running mount session's export. Three: the S-1008 sweep-3 record refuted "compare blocking on a FIFO" because
"only a host actor can place one after the walk"; that refutation missed RENAME by a mount guest and does not
cover this. Four: the operator cannot end it by Ctrl-C: a probe sent SIGINT and SIGTERM to the parked process and
compare was still parked 3 s later with both signals buffered, because fetch's signal.Notify takes them and they
are read only inside pulled.frame; `workcell stop` reaches it at its SIGKILL rung, after about 10 s, or a writer
opens the FIFO. The auditor reported the same of SIGINT; the redteam supposed the opposite without running it, and
the verifier's probe settles it. Severity (S6): the verifier holds that a hang of a host process is demonstrated
and is reached through the file-service channel, with preconditions the attacker does not control, which is the
letter of medium, and that "hardening with no demonstrated break" understates it. The auditor's case for low was
that only a verb parks, with two preconditions, until the operator stops it. The record follows the independent
verifier: C87 is CONFIRMED at medium, and S-1017 counts it so. S7 asks for the fix before cutover at either level.

Fix unit: S-F73 (boundary, fable, env:any), directly below S-1002 in PLAN.md: add O_NONBLOCK to fileBeneath's
flags in pull_linux.go and pull_darwin.go, no added line, and in sameBytes fstat the opened descriptor and treat
anything but a regular file as differing, about two lines, so that a FIFO with a writer that never writes cannot
park the read either. Product has 26 lines of room and test 207 with the parked file counted. Variants not written
(redteam): a FIFO whose writer never writes (the read parks; the fstat arm covers it); the macOS twin; the same
swap against `workcell pull`, where put unlinks and creates with O_EXCL and so meets EEXIST, not a hang. Not S14:
no file involved is ported, and none is someone else's project.

Sweep 4 verdict for this surface: one candidate, C87, confirmed at medium by the verifier's reading of S6 (claimed
low by the auditor), open, with fix unit S-F73. No model declined and no safeguard re-ran a request in the audit,
the redteam or the verifier, and no tool permission was refused to any of them.

## S-F73: compare opens without blocking and reads only a regular file (I12 with R6), finding C87

C87 is FIXED by S-F73 at f9a2ed2. fileBeneath in cmd/workcell/pull_linux.go and pull_darwin.go opens with O_NONBLOCK,
so a FIFO that took a regular file's name after the walk cannot hold the open. sameBytes in cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go
then fstats the opened descriptor, by openSource's idiom, and what is not a regular file differs and is never read,
so a FIFO whose writer writes nothing cannot hold the read either. `workcell diff` prints `M` for such a name and
returns. Product grew by two lines, both in pull_vm.go. What a regular file prints is unchanged.

Test (S4). TestC87CompareFIFOReturns moved from escape/_pending/S-F73/ to cmd/workcell/c87_test.go, and that folder
is gone. Before it moved the redteam gave it two arms over one body: `unheld`, the arm of the audit, where no writer
holds the FIFO and the open parks; and `held`, new, where the test holds a writer that writes no byte, so the open
returns and the read parks. Each arm has a 3 s bound and frees the reader on a timeout. 75 lines.

Proof, each run by the orchestrator with `go test -overlay` and main's files kept outside the tree. Against main's
pull_linux.go and pull_vm.go both arms fail at 3.00 s, plain and with -race: `compare is still parked 3s after a
FIFO (writer held: false) took a regular file's name: workcell diff hangs (I12)`, and the same with `true`. With the
fix both pass in 0.00 s, and three times with -race. Each half is needed: with O_NONBLOCK and main's sameBytes only
`held` fails; with the fstat arm and main's fileBeneath only `unheld` fails. `go test -race ./cmd/workcell` passes,
TestCompare and TestWrite among it. The reviewer repeated the fail-on-main run, the pass and the first half alone.

Hosted, on f9a2ed2: gate green in 366 s on a real VM (/dev/kvm writable, sandbox ready in 3 s), 147 rows passed and
none failed, among them the seven pull rows (pull-runs-hook, pull-obeys-git-config, pull-fetches-submodule,
pull-dotdot-path, pull-through-symlink, pull-case-collision, pull-writes-dotgit), and the package cmd/workcell `ok`;
gate-macos green in 168 s, which is the only build of the darwin twin; gate-arm64 and guard green.

Not shown. The suite has no row that runs `workcell diff`, so the accept's "diff rows" are the package tests of
compare, not a row on a VM. No run on a VM shows a guest's rename met by the fix end to end: the test places the
