## S-1003, sweep 4: VM configuration and device model, Linux and macOS backends (I1, I4, A7), as built at main 98a20bd

Sweep 4 (S8), the one further sweep that the maintainer allowed on 2026-11-26 after ADR-006, fresh context (S3),
the whole surface read as built after S-F73, not a diff. Auditor on the top tier in the cloud session, which has
no hypervisor and is Linux, as root, so the bind-mount tests ran for real and nothing ran on a VM or on macOS.
The auditor wrote its own trust boundary and worked every lens before it opened any earlier record. No candidate.

Trust boundary. Attacker bytes reach this surface by three routes. (1) What guest root does with the devices the
host hands it: virtio-blk requests to the root drive (read-only on both backends), the workspace image (read-write,
the session's own 0600 file), layer drives (read-only) and cache drives (read-only, or read-write by the operator's
`--cache NAME:rw`); AF_VSOCK connects to CID 2 at any port, which Firecracker turns into connect(2) on
<Dir>/vsock_<port> (only 5000, 5001 and 5002 ever exist; 5000 and 5002 take one connection through once{} and are
unlinked) and vz into a registered listener; bytes on the console, read on Linux through a paced blocking pipe
into a 4 KiB tail that is printed, sanitised, only when a boot fails; reboot, panic and halt (reboot=k and
panic=-1 end Firecracker; on vz a Ping every 2 s ends a restarted guest). (2) Guest-written ext4 images attached
again later: workspace.ext4 to the pull guest (no network, no layers, no caches) and rw caches to later guests by
the operator's flag; the host never mounts or parses either. (3) The repository and the live export, judged on
this surface only by the layout of cwd: holds (data and config directory in both directions, config.toml hard
links, every mount point beneath cwd from /proc/self/mountinfo, the vmm records of running sessions), the TMPDIR
rules of --mount, boot and fetch, and named(). Host-built and out of the guest's reach: firecracker.json (0600 in a
0700 MkdirTemp directory under an absolute TMPDIR), the kernel command line (integers, fixed words, compiled-in
provider names, cache names of a fixed alphabet, uint16 ports, device letters), drive paths under the data
directory and sessions/<id>/, the lock, repo, vmm, inodes and marker files. The operator's environment is
trusted, with layouts refused where they would show the product's state to a guest. Authority: the supervisor is
the operator's uid; it execs <data>/firecracker by absolute path with Pdeathsig SIGKILL, Setpgid, stdin /dev/null
and a CLOEXEC pipe, from a locked thread whose CPU mask is cut to --cpus; the child has the same uid, the default
seccomp filter, no jailer and no rlimit; on macOS the VM lives in the entitled supervisor and Apple's helper.
No file of this surface carries `// Ported from v1`.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: no parser of guest bytes lies on this surface; encode is json.Marshal of
host strings, the init reads a host-written command line, the console goes to a bounded tail through a bounded
sanitiser, the vz state is an enum; CPU is bounded by pin() and the paced pipe on Linux, memory by mem_size_mib,
Firecracker's own vsock connection limit, the relay's 1024 slots and vz's 16-deep backlog, disk by images of fixed
sparse size and charged growth in mount mode; a console flood fills the pipe and blocks the guest's own vCPU.
Logic and state: Listen before Start, Start once, Kill and Close idempotent and safe before Start; the drive order
and the init's device letters agree on both backends; once{} takes one connection and then removes the listener;
openCaches stats, locks (shared for readers, exclusive for the writer), creates under a temporary name and
renames, with the lock held for the session; findLayers refuses a marker that is not a bare name. Concurrency and
check-to-use: the Pdeathsig thread stays locked for the child's life and the child inherits the narrowed mask;
exitErr is written before exited closes; holds, the TMPDIR rule, the SSL_CERT_DIR walk, named(), newSession,
Export and boot run in that order, and recordBoot precedes Start; the windows that remain are the recorded
operator-timed ones (a mount session started between another session's MkdirTemp and its recordBoot; the
unrecorded directory of a bench), unchanged. Cryptography and identity: none on this surface by design; the vsock
peer is the VMM through a 0700 per-session directory or a per-VM device. Failure modes: every exit from boot runs
closeAll; accept ends on the connection, the VMM's death, 20 s or a signal; a missing socket is a reset to the
guest; a failed layer or cache mount in the init gives less, never more; the nil audit log of pull and bench is
nil-safe; nothing fails open. Downgrade, rollback and replay: markers are host-written; the pull guest boots the
image with no more authority than the first guest had; a stale vmm record removes only an absolute, existing
directory named wc* that is not a link. Interaction: the listeners of 5001 and 5002 end with the machine's Close,
which ends the proxy's Serve loops (A9); an rw cache is a channel between guests by the operator's own flag
(S-1013's ruling, unchanged); a mount point equal to cwd is admitted and one strictly beneath it is refused, and
the mountinfo decoder handles the kernel's four octal escapes.

Refuted before anything was raised: a TMPDIR through a symlink inside a live mount export (the host resolves the
directory only at MkdirTemp, Listen and Start, before any guest code runs, and a later connect needs the random
wc name that the guest cannot see; the sweep-2 and S-1013 rulings stand); drive-letter overflow and command-line
truncation (the operator's, and less, never more); a cache named root or workspace (the drive id is prefixed);
pull attaching the image read-write (no gain); SIGHUP inherited by Firecracker (its own group and handler); a
guest that halts without restart (stop ends it); two --mount sessions on nested trees (explicit, A5).

Recorded fixes, each checked as built, all holding: C6 (S-F3: pin(), the affinity cut and the paced console
pipe), C5 (S-F24: the 2 s probe on vz, read and not run), C52 (S-F35), C65 (S-F48: the mountinfo refusal in holds
and RESOLVE_NO_XDEV on the three openat2 masks of pull_linux.go), C19 and C29 (S-F12, S-F21), C28 (S-F20), C56
(S-F39), C61 (S-F44), C63 (S-F46), C26 (S-F18), the once{} wrapper, C83 (S-F67), C85 and C86 (S-F69, S-F70) and
C87 (S-F73). TestC52BindMountAliasEvadesWithin and TestC65DataDirectoryBindMountedBeneathCwd ran as root, not
skipped, and pass; go test -count=1 is green on cmd/workcell, cmd/workcell-init, internal/vmm/firecracker,
internal/vmm/vz (its Go-only test) and internal/workspace, and go vet is clean on the three trees.

Ran, by the auditor, in a scratch directory and with nothing added to the repository. Ten-second fuzz bursts
through overlay test files: lastLines in cmd/workcell (printable ASCII and newlines only, at most n lines, a tail
never over 4096 bytes), 263,932 executions; the init's reading of the command line in cmd/workcell-init (no
panic, no name with a slash or a dot, no device outside /dev/, no port 0, no negative disk), 463,066; encode in
internal/vmm/firecracker (root read-only, workspace read-write, layers read-only, caches read-only unless
writable, in order, with the machine and vsock fields intact), 117,700 with valid UTF-8 paths; no failure of the
product in any. Two probes, each against a process the probe started: the paced reader copied from
firecracker.go, against a child that writes one byte at a time for 3 s, made 870 reads a second and spent 0.31
CPU s where the unpaced reader made 433,784 a second and spent 1.96; and Start's process pattern (locked thread,
mask cut to one CPU, exec with Pdeathsig and Setpgid) left the child with one allowed CPU of four and gone after
SIGKILL of its parent.

Coverage. Read in full: internal/vmm/vmm.go; every file of internal/vmm/firecracker and internal/vmm/vz with
their tests and test guests; in cmd/workcell the files backend_linux, backend_darwin, run_vm, session, caps,
run_other, main, data, layer, cache, cache_vm, pull_vm, pull, pull_linux, pull_darwin, bench_vm, term_vm,
term_linux, term_darwin, mount_linux, mount_darwin, relay, policy and update, and the tests of run_vm, session,
caps, data, layer, cache and cache_vm; cmd/workcell-init (main, mount, net, exec, root, pull); internal/workspace,
internal/guest, internal/wire and internal/relay; the parts of internal/proxy and internal/audit that boot calls;
the size cap and openSource of internal/rootfs; the escape suite's and the harness's files of this surface; the
accepted ADR-001 and ADR-006; and, as data, the sources of the pinned Code-Hex/vz v3.8.0 that the backend calls.
Not examined: the bodies of internal/fileserve, resolver, secret, policy, provider, channel, pins, artifact and
sigstore, cmd/mkimage and cmd/bump, which are other surfaces. Not run: anything on a real VM, the escape suite,
any macOS path. The darwin backend could not be compiled here (cgo cannot target darwin from this session), so
vz.go and backend_darwin.go were read and the hosted gate-macos is their only build.

## S-1004, sweep 4: network path and proxy core: routing, SNI, ECH, connection handling, fail-closed behaviour (I2, I4, I11), as built at main 5dd34dd

Sweep 4 (S8), the one further sweep that the maintainer allowed on 2026-11-26 after ADR-006, fresh context (S3),
the whole surface read as built after S-F73, not a diff. Auditor on the top tier in the cloud session, which has
no hypervisor and is Linux, as root, so the namespace probes ran for real and nothing ran on a VM or on macOS.
The auditor wrote its own trust boundary and worked every lens before it opened any earlier record. No candidate.

Trust boundary. Guest root owns every byte of every AF_VSOCK stream it opens to host port 5001, and their count,
rate, timing and closing: on Linux Firecracker connects each to the unix socket vsock_5001 in the session's 0700
MkdirTemp directory (muxer cap 1023), on macOS to vz's listener (backlog 16). First host code is serveRelay in
cmd/workcell/relay.go (1024 slots), then stream: a 5 s deadline, io.ReadFull of exactly 20 bytes, relay.Decode
(length 20, version 1, proto 6 or 17). Proto 17 at port 53: one ReadFrame of at most 65535 bytes to
resolver.Answer under the same deadline, one reply, close. Proto 6 to a port in allow.Ports(): the deadline is
lifted and the connection goes to that port's adapter, which proxy.Serve (1024 slots) takes into handle and
route: the forward map, or the crypto/tls ClientHello peek on a 16 KiB recording connection under 10 s, ECH
extension 0xfe0d refused, ToLower with a length check, exact allowlist membership; then one Allowed record that
gates admission (I9); then serveTerminated for every SNI host (443 is never spliced in the product) or connect:
one rooted LookupNetIP (10 s), hostNets read on every connection (interface prefixes plus the netlink route dump
of routes_linux.go: every local row and every on-link unicast row of more than 0 bits, both families, all
tables; routes_other.go returns nothing on a Mac), blockedAddr on every answer before any dial, a 30 s budget
shared across answers, the dial by literal, a splice with no idle timeout. Anything else closes the stream; a TCP
header to an unserved port is recorded port_not_allowed. The network attacker owns the host resolver's answers
for allowed names (the rebind model) and the upstream bytes after the dial, raw on a forward port and x509-bound
on 443. The repository reaches this surface only by narrowing (S-1009) and, under --mount, by the working
directory (C86, fixed). Authority: the supervisor `workcell run`, one process (A9), with the operator's uid and
network reach, holding the VMM child, the session CA key, the broker and the audit log. The guest-side code of
cmd/workcell-init/net.go enforces nothing (A1); no backend has a network device, so I2 reduces to the relay's
and the proxy's admission. Ported (`// Ported from v1`): internal/proxy/proxy.go, allowlist.go, terminate.go
and their tests, and internal/audit/lines.go. Not ported: routes_linux.go, routes_other.go, signin.go,
internal/relay, internal/resolver, cmd/workcell/relay.go, run_vm.go, the init and both backends.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: the header is a fixed 20-byte array read under an absolute deadline before
any allocation, and Decode is total; a DNS frame is one allocation of at most 65535 bytes; the hello is parsed by
crypto/tls on a connection capped at 16 KiB under 10 s; forward ports are never parsed; slots cap at 1024 twice
and Firecracker's 1023 keeps the relay below its cap; the route dump is read in parts with truncation checked.
The cost of hostNets on each connection, measured: 52 microseconds with a base table and 1.21 ms with 3072 extra
routes, bounded in total by the audit log's soft limit of about 55 thousand admissions (I10). Logic and state: a
port other than 443 routes to the forward map's one host and 443 by SNI; no non-ASCII name of equal length
matches an ASCII key; crypto/tls rejects a trailing-dot or duplicate server_name; the lowered name serves the
leaf, the rewrite and the record; the served ports are the init's list; ParseAllowlist refuses IP literals, port
0, names that are not DNS names and two hosts on one forward port; routes() keeps local rows of any table and
on-link unicast rows, skips gateway, default, broadcast, multicast and unreachable rows, and refuses a malformed
row, a cut part and a netlink error. Concurrency and check-to-use: one lookup per connection, every answer vetted
before any dial, the dial by literal, no second lookup; the terminated transport's dial re-enters connect for each
upstream connection and refuses a host outside the terminated set; the fields that Terminate writes are written
before any Serve goroutine starts; every relay connection is closed once and frees its slot once; the Allowed
record precedes the dial. Cryptography and identity: SNI is routing identity only; the leaf is issued for the
lowered SNI under a CA with critical name constraints; ALPN is http/1.1 alone; ECH is refused by extension type
on the outer hello before any name is read; upstream identity on 443 is x509 with the SNI host as ServerName,
TLS 1.2 at least, and no proxy from the environment; forward ports carry no identity, by the operator's grant
(ADR-003); DNS answers are vetted, never trusted. Failure modes: every error path refuses or closes: a deadline
or a failed peek is no_sni, a lookup error or an empty set resolve_failed, an unreadable interface list or route
dump or one blocked answer blocked_address, a dial failure dial_failed; a failed record dials nothing (S-F16); a
nil log refuses everything; serveRelay ends on any Accept error and closes every adapter, which ends every Serve
loop; a panic in handle would end the supervisor and so the VM (I11); Firecracker dies with the supervisor by
Pdeathsig and vz's VM with the process. Downgrade, rollback and replay: header version 1 only; TLS 1.2 at
least on both sides; a replayed stream is another connection that meets the same checks; the relay holds no
state across streams; there is no DNS cache; the transport reuses a connection only to a host it vetted.
Interaction: DNS frames to the resolver in the same process (S-1006), 443 to serveTerminated (S-1005; the
hand-off, the choice of leaf and the host closure belong to this surface and ADR-006 did not change them), every
refusal and admission to the audit log (S-1010), the sockets in the 0700 directory that S-F20, S-F21, S-F35 and
S-F48 keep out of every export (S-1003); the machine's Close ends the listeners and so the Serve loops (A9).

Refuted before anything was raised: a macOS twin of C66 and C69 (routes_other.go reads no table; S-F49 left it
for a unit of its own and PARKED.md holds it; no Mac here and no new evidence); VPN on-link half-defaults and a
local default in a marked table (they block everything, toward refusal); a stream shed at the 1024 cap leaving
no record (C8's refutation stands); GREASE ECH clients refused as no_sni (parked); a route change during the
dump (host root's act, parked); multipath routes read as on-link (over-blocking, parked); serveRelay ending on
EMFILE (fails closed, parked); a forward port whose host is also terminated at 443 (raw by the operator's
grant); a non-ASCII SNI of equal byte length (never an allowlist key); /etc/hosts entries for allowed names
(loopback is blocked); X-Forwarded-For showing the relay address (the rewrite strips it); a secret or a CA in
the kernel command line (none); the proxy as a pivot to networks behind a routed gateway (outside I4's list,
C9's residual, for the report); UDP to a port other than 53 leaving no record (C14, intended).

Recorded fixes, each traced as built and run, all holding: C7 (S-F4, the 168.63.129.16/32 row and TestBlockedAddr),
C70 (S-F53, 192.80.8.124/32), C66 (S-F49) and C69 (S-F52) (hostNets appends the route dump to the interface
prefixes; TestRoutes and TestC69AnyIPLocalRoute pass as root), C13 (S-F8, the three transport limits,
TestUpstreamHandshakeEndsWithTheGuest green under -race), C23 and C24 (S-F16, handle acts only on a recorded
connection), B-835 (the 16 KiB hello cap), C11 (S-F6), C27 (S-F19), C30 and C53 (S-F22, S-F36, upstreamRoots),
and the hand-off of S-F72 into serveTerminated (TestSF72AdmittedPathReachesUpstreamAsJudged green). C8 refuted
and C14 intended stand.

socket or namespace that the probe itself started (S12, T8). go test -count=1 green on internal/proxy,
internal/relay, internal/resolver and cmd/workcell; the relay, routing, connect, peek, forward, unrecorded, C13,

## S-1005, sweep 4: TLS termination and HTTP handling: smuggling, HTTP/2, WebSocket, redirects, CONNECT, CA handling (I5, I6), as built at main 62d606a

Sweep 4 (S8), the one further sweep that the maintainer allowed on 2026-11-26 after ADR-006, fresh context (S3), the
whole surface read as built after S-F73, not a diff. Auditor on the top tier in the cloud session, which has no
hypervisor and is Linux, as root, so nothing ran on a VM or on macOS. The auditor wrote its own trust boundary and
worked every lens before it opened any earlier record, and then took up the parked `S-F72 reviewer finding`, as the
entries of S-F72 and S-1004 asked. One candidate, C88, which is that row's doubled escape with the upstream it
lacked.

Trust boundary. Guest root and hostile model output own every byte of a 443 relay stream after the 20-byte header
that stream() in cmd/workcell/relay.go reads: the ClientHello (peeked under the 16 KiB cap on S-1004's path and
replayed byte for byte into the per-connection tls.Server of serveTerminated), then the whole HTTP/1.1 stream that
net/http parses: request line, target, method, headers (64 KiB), bodies, trailers, pipelining, Upgrade and Expect,
their count, rate and timing, and the body of a token-endpoint request, which tokenRequest reads whole (256 KiB).
They own the relay header's address too, used only for sameHost's port, which the adapter fixes at 443. The
malicious repository owns the supervisor's working directory (judged by session() for SSL_CERT_FILE and
SSL_CERT_DIR: C30, C53, C86) and workcell.toml, which only narrows. The network attacker owns every host off the
allowlist and, in the I4 model, the resolver's answers for allowed names; it does not own an allowed host's x509
identity. Trusted without checking: crypto/tls, net/http and httputil of go1.27.4; the host resolver and root store;
the compiled-in provider data; the operator's config and environment; and every byte an allowlisted upstream
answers, its router's reading of a path included, which is where C88 lies. Authority of the code that handles these
bytes: the supervisor's uid, the session CA key (leaves for allowed names only, name-constrained), the broker (file,
cmd and keychain reads per use; sign-in tokens held one generation), the audit log (one Allowed record per
connection, one refusal per refused request, one ledger line per release), and a transport that dials only the
terminated hosts on 443 through p.connect with the SNI host as ServerName. The handler's order: an opaque target, a
scheme without a host, or a path that is not canonical on a sign-in host (400); TRACE and CONNECT (405); sameHost
against the SNI (421); per rule placeholderForm, then admits (403), then Lookup; tokenEndpoint then tokenRequest
(502); carriesPlaceholder (502); then the ReverseProxy, whose Rewrite forces scheme, URL host and Host to the SNI
host and whose ModifyResponse is tokenResponse. Ported (`// Ported from v1`): internal/proxy/terminate.go, proxy.go
and allowlist.go with their three tests, internal/secret/broker.go and source.go, internal/audit/lines.go. Not
ported: signin.go, relay.go, run_vm.go, policy.go, internal/guest/trust.go.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: the hello is capped at 16 KiB and 10 s; the header block at 64 KiB with a 10 s
ReadHeaderTimeout, under which the handshake also runs, since the server sees a closeNotifyConn and handshakes on
the first read; a token body and a token answer at 256 KiB plus one byte before and after gzip, other encodings
refused; a Basic value at 4 KiB of strict base64; 1024 slots; MaxConnsPerHost 1024, IdleConnTimeout 90 s,
TLSHandshakeTimeout 10 s; no idle or body deadline, by design and recorded. Inbound smuggling: net/http deletes
Content-Length where the body is chunked and refuses differing duplicates, and the ReverseProxy writes its own
framing, so no second inbound parser exists to desynchronise; an undeclared trailer is merged into the inbound
request only after the body and the outgoing request carries the declared set alone, and a declared one is refused.
Every index on guest bytes is guarded and no panic path from guest bytes was found. Logic and state: sameHost's
ASCII-only fold with its length check, the port rule and Go's reading of an absolute-form target over Host hold;
Rewrite forces the upstream Host, so the upstream never sees the guest's spelling; admits judges the bytes that the
ReverseProxy sends, and canonical makes them Go's own escaping of the decoded path with no dot or empty segment, no
`;` and no backslash; the override check folds header names the CGI way; tokenEndpoint claims by EqualFold on a path
already canonical; swapRefresh swaps only the row's own field of a form or a top-level JSON object; learn wants one
JSON object at 2xx and hides the broker's tokens, the carried token and the issued pair in three spellings;
tokenAnswer refuses an unclaimed 2xx of a sign-in host that looks like a token answer. What no code does: refuse a
literal `%` in a judged path (C88). Concurrency and check-to-use: the fields that Terminate writes are written once
before any Serve goroutine starts; the leaf cache is under a mutex and keyed by allowed names; the broker is under a
mutex and hands out clones; the token context rides the request context into the cloned outgoing request; nothing
changes r.URL between admits and the clone; the peek and the terminating server parse the same replayed bytes with
the same library; the rotation race of C15 is covered by the carried swap. Cryptography and identity: a P-256
session CA of at most 24 h, NotBefore one minute back, critical PermittedDNSDomains equal to the 443 allowlist,
every IP range excluded, path length 0; one leaf per lowered allowed name with ServerAuth and a 128-bit random
serial, minted only for the routed host; the key never leaves the host and the guest gets the PEM (16 KiB cap) as
data; a fresh tls.Config per connection, so no ticket resumption across connections, no 0-RTT, no renegotiation and
no client certificate; the upstream is verified against the explicit pool (system roots, an absolute SSL_CERT_FILE,
SSL_CERT_DIR members judged absolute and outside the working and data directories) with the SNI host as ServerName,
TLS 1.2 at least, HTTP/1.1 only and no proxy from the environment. Failure modes: every error path refuses or
closes: a leaf error fails the handshake; an upstreamRoots error fails Terminate before any boot; a broker error is
502 broker_denied; a token reason is 502 with nothing forwarded; a ModifyResponse error is an empty 502 before any
upstream header or byte is copied; a failed Note half-closes before any dial (I9); a 2xx of a sign-in host in br or
zstd, or over 256 KiB, is 502; `Connection: X-Api-Key` drops the swapped header, a self-harm. Nothing fails open but
the admitted `%25` of C88. Downgrade, rollback and replay: TLS 1.2 at least on both sides; an h2-only ALPN is
refused; the h2 preface is 421 without Host and crosses as the method PRI with one (parked); HTTP/1.0 without Host
is 421; a placeholder is fresh per session and refused anywhere else; a replayed request meets every check anew; the
guest never holds a real refresh token, and the broker keeps one generation and zeroes the replaced one; a replayed
or attacker-chosen code grant replaces the operator's tokens with the attacker's own and gains nothing. Interaction:
the resolver's vetted address is the one dialled, per dial (S-1004, S-1006); every refusal and every release is
recorded, and S-F16 refuses connections once the log is full, a loss and never a gain (S-1010); loadPolicy refuses a
dropped sign-in row whose token host stays (C34) and judges the trust-store variables (C86) (S-1009); the guest
trust store is a convenience (A1); the one gap between surfaces is the one ADR-006 accepted, the upstream's own
reading of the bytes the proxy sends, and C88 names a front end that reads them twice.

Refuted before anything was raised: CL.TE and TE.CL (chunked wins and the proxy frames anew; sweeps 1 and 3 ran the
bytes, not run again); undeclared chunked trailers (dropped) and declared ones (refused, by test); `Connection:
X-Api-Key` (self-harm); WebSocket or any Upgrade (the secret is only in the judged 101 request and the tunnel goes
to the verified SNI host; the parked notes stand); HTTP/2 (ALPN http/1.1 alone, by test; upstream HTTP/1.1 only); an
absolute-form target that names another host (421) and userinfo in a target (in RequestURI, so a placeholder there
is refused, and the transport makes no Authorization of it); `//evil/path` (not canonical, by S-F72's test) and
`OPTIONS *` (C27); `Host: example.com:` with an empty port (false in the product, where the port is 443); a
percent-encoded placeholder in a header or a body (not swapped, crosses, useless upstream), in the query (decoded
once and refused) and encoded twice (crosses, useless); a lowercase `basic` scheme (crosses unswapped, parked); bare
`!'()*[]` and lowercase hex escapes in a path (refused under a narrowed rule and 400 on a sign-in host, a cost and
no break, parked); `/v1/x/..%00/admin` and NUL (nginx and Apache answer 400 themselves, run); `%2F` decoded to `/`
by nginx's proxy_pass with a URI part and `%3B` decoded to `;` by Apache's ProxyPass, ProxyPassMatch and RewriteRule
[P], both seen here (canonical refuses both spellings already); nested tokens, id_token, Set-Cookie or a token in a
header or trailer of a token answer (the provider's shape, no lever, parked); a 101 at a token endpoint (parked); br
on an unclaimed 2xx of a sign-in host (502, the cost S-F50 records); two concurrent sign-ins; X-Forwarded-Prefix,
X-Original-URI and X-Accel-Redirect as path overrides (no framework shown to route by them, the parked line stands);
session resumption and 0-RTT; a relative or in-tree SSL_CERT_FILE or SSL_CERT_DIR (refused before boot: C30, C53,
C86). Of the parked row's four spellings, three are ruled out by run: the fullwidth stops
`/v1/%EF%BC%8E%EF%BC%8E/admin` and fullwidth slashes `/v1/x%EF%BC%8F..%EF%BC%8F..%EF%BC%8Fadmin` pass nginx 1.24 and
Apache 2.4.58 in every shape as bytes that neither maps, and Go's, nginx's and Apache's normalisers see no `.` or
`/` in them; Tomcat and Jetty decode them to the fullwidth code points and normalise ASCII dots alone (by their
documents, not run), and the one named ASCII best-fit of fullwidth characters is a file-system behaviour of Windows
ANSI APIs and no HTTP routing; the overlong `/v1/%C0%AE%C0%AE/admin` passes nginx and Apache as bytes, Tomcat
refuses invalid UTF-8 in a URI, Java's and Python's decoders yield U+FFFD, and the one server that decoded it to `.`
dates from 2000. The fourth, the doubled escape, is C88.

Recorded fixes, each traced as built and run, all holding: C10 (S-F5, then S-F72: canonical refuses `;`, backslash,
`%2e`, `%5C` and dot segments; c10_test green), C11 (S-F6, MaxHeaderBytes), C12 (S-F7, hide's three spellings;
FuzzHide green), C13 (S-F8, the three transport limits), C15 (S-F9, the carried refresh token; c15_test green with
the real broker and ledger), C23 and C24 (S-F16, handle acts only on a recorded connection, both ports), C27
(S-F19), C30 and C53 (S-F22, S-F36: upstreamRoots; c53_test with its three re-execs), C32 (S-F25, the opaque and
scheme-without-host refusal is the handler's first statement), C33 (S-F26, then S-F72), C34 (S-F27, traced in
policy.go), C55 and C67 (S-F38, S-F50: every unclaimed 2xx of a sign-in host read whole and judged), C68 (S-F51,
then S-F72: the two override names under the CGI fold), C69 (S-F52, in a user namespace here), C86 (S-F70, run_vm.go
judges SSL_CERT_FILE and every SSL_CERT_DIR member), S-F71 (the secret-source check as the ADR decides; sf71_test
green), S-F72 (canonical, and `method` refused at load; sf72_test green) and B-835 (the 16 KiB hello cap).

Ran, by the auditor, in a scratch directory and with nothing added to the repository; every target a loopback
process that the audit itself started and stopped (S12, T8); no third-party host. go vet clean on internal/proxy; go
test -race -count=1 ./internal/proxy/ ok in 19.1 s, 55 top-level tests and none failing; go test -count=1 green on

`/%252e%252e/admin`: nginx's proxy_pass with a URI part, its rewrite with proxy_pass, and its proxy_pass without one
all forward `%252e%252e`; Apache's ProxyPass, ProxyPass nocanon, ProxyPassMatch and RewriteRule [P] forward

admin file and answers the doubled, fullwidth and overlong forms 404.

### S-1005 candidates, sweep 4

C88. ID I5 (a placeholder is useless at any destination other than the one it is bound to: docs/policy.md binds a
`[[secret]]` row narrowed by `path` or `repos` to that path, "judged on the path as the upstream receives it, which
must have one reading"), the class that S-F72 records under I6. Attacker: guest root or hostile model output,
choosing the path of its own request. Preconditions the attacker does not control: the operator narrowed the row by
`path` or `repos` (a row that is not narrowed swaps anywhere on its host by design); the bound host's front end
decodes the path once and forwards the decoded form; and the backend behind it decodes an encoded dot segment and
normalises it. Where: internal/proxy/terminate.go:127-130, canonical, used at :116 by admits for every narrowed rule
and at :369 for every request on a sign-in host; the promise is docs/policy.md:38-40. The file is ported. also in v1
main: egressproxy/terminate.go. Input: on a terminated connection with SNI v.example.com, under the rule {Host:
v.example.com, Header: x-api-key, Path: "/v1/"}: `POST /v1/%252e%252e/admin` with `X-Api-Key:` the session's
placeholder. Effect claimed: canonical holds, because `%25` is Go's own escaping of a literal `%` and path.Clean
sees a segment `%2e%2e` and no `..`; admits returns true, the broker releases the secret with a granted record, and
the proxy sends the line byte for byte. A front end that decodes once and forwards the decoded path, named as Apache
httpd with `RewriteRule ^/v1/(.*)$ http://backend/api/$1 [P,NE]`, hands the backend `/api/%2e%2e/admin`, which nginx
normalises to `/admin` and serves with the real secret: the secret is used on the bound host at a path outside its
binding, with no refusal. It never reaches the guest and never leaves the bound host (I6 holds). The auditor's unit
probe found the `repos` twin admitted as well, `/octo/allowed.git/%252e%252e/other.git/git-receive-pack` under repos
`octo/allowed`, with no git host's front end shown to forward it decoded. Severity claimed: medium, as C10, C33 and
C68 were. No claim is made about the edge of any shipped provider, which T8 forbids probing.

The auditor's evidence, run and not reasoned, with the two real servers on loopback: through the product by `go test
-overlay`, a terminating proxy before Apache 2.4.58 with mod_ssl and that RewriteRule, and nginx 1.24.0 behind it:
`POST /v1/x` is served with the real secret (control); `/v1/%2e%2e/admin` and `/v1/../admin` are 403 from the proxy;
`/v1/%252e%252e/admin` is answered 200 by the backend at uri `/admin` with the real secret; the fullwidth and
overlong forms are served as bytes under `/v1/` and nothing maps them. Refuted by the same runs: Apache's ProxyPass,
ProxyPass nocanon, ProxyPassMatch and RewriteRule [P] without NE, and nginx as a front in three shapes, all of which
hand the backend `%252e%252e` again. The probe and its configuration lived in a scratch directory and are not kept.

Reproducing test (S4): TestC88DoubledEscapeLeavesTheBinding, a Go test of package proxy, 57 lines, written by the
redteam from the claim alone, with no VM and so no T2: the package's own terminating proxy with a rule of path
`/v1/`, and a loopback TLS upstream whose one handler models the two readings (url.PathUnescape once for the front
end, then again with path.Clean for the backend) and records the path it finally serves with the key it saw. It
fails when the real secret is served at a path outside `/v1/`, and it does not judge how a fix answers. Controls:
`POST /v1/x` is served at `/v1/x` with the real secret, and `/v1/%2e%2e/admin` is refused with the secret withheld.
It waits in escape/_pending/S-F74/c88_test.go, which Go does not compile. Run by the orchestrator on 55649f7 with
`go test -overlay`, go1.27.4, plain and with -race, one error line each: `--- FAIL:
TestC88DoubledEscapeLeavesTheBinding`, `c88_test.go:54: I5: the upstream served "/admin" with the real secret: the
credential bound to /v1/ was used outside its binding`; both controls pass. go vet with the overlay is clean. The
power the test gives itself: its upstream is a model in Go, and the model leaves out the rewrite to `/api/`; the
redteam had no httpd and did not check it against one.

Outcome: CONFIRMED by the verifier at medium, from its own run of the test and its own run of the named front end.
Its evidence. One: the test fails as recorded and both controls pass. Two: the model is faithful to shipping
software: Apache 2.4.58 on loopback with `RewriteRule ^/v1/(.*)$ http://127.0.0.1:18082/api/$1 [P,NE]`, before a
backend that logs the raw line and before nginx 1.24.0; for `POST /v1/%252e%252e/admin` with a key the raw backend
logged `POST /api/%2e%2e/admin HTTP/1.1` with the key, and nginx answered 200 with `uri=/admin
request_uri=/api/%2e%2e/admin` and the key; `/v1/x` went to `/api/x`, and `/v1/%2e%2e/admin` was 403 from Apache
itself. So decode once and forward (Apache with NE) before decode and clean (nginx) is what two shipping servers do,
and the test gives itself no power the guest lacks: it uses the package's standard fixtures and a request line and a
header that the guest chooses. Three: it is not intended behaviour: docs/policy.md promises one reading and `%25` is
what canonical admits, yet the upstream reads it twice; ADR-006's rulings on C10 and C33 never rule on `%252e`. It
was carried only as a residual with no reproduction: the sweep-1 record of this surface ("double decoding"), the
S-1016b tool note and the `S-F72 reviewer finding` in PARKED.md. The verifier holds it an accepted residual that now
has a reproduction, and so a finding under S4. Four, severity by S6's letter: medium. I5 is broken only with the
three preconditions above, none of which the attacker controls; the secret reaches only the bound host and never the
guest, so it is not high; a break is demonstrated, so it is not low. Five: not S14: the file is ported and no v1
release holds it, and Apache's NE flag and nginx's normalisation are documented behaviour, not weaknesses of those
projects.

On ADR-006, for the maintainer. Decision (d) stands as built, and C88 does not ask for a second reading or a model
of a router. The Path row of the accepted ADR says a path is admitted when it is Go's own escaping of the decoded
path, clean, with no `;` and no backslash, and calls that one reading; for a literal `%` that is too strong, since a
documented front end reads `%25` twice. The fix narrows what that row admits by one byte, toward refusal. The loop
does not edit an accepted ADR: S-F74 builds the narrower rule in free paths and its record says where code and ADR
then differ, and the maintainer amends the ADR or rules the row residual instead.

Fix unit: S-F74 (boundary, fable, env:any), directly below S-1005 in PLAN.md: in canonical refuse a literal `%` in
the decoded path as `;` and backslash are refused, one character in the set of strings.ContainsAny and no added
product line, with the comment on that line and the sentence of docs/policy.md saying so. The auditor ran that
change by overlay: the probe's claim row became 403 and the whole package passed under -race, the admitted arm
`/v1/%E2%9C%93` of sf72_test.go included. Its cost: under a narrowed rule a path that carries `%25` is 403, and on a
sign-in host 400; no path of a shipped provider and no git smart-HTTP path carries a literal percent. Product has 24
lines of room and test 134 with the parked file counted. Variants not written (redteam): `%25%32%65` for a front end
that decodes twice; `%252F`, `%255C` and `%253B`, a doubled slash, backslash and `;`; the `repos` twin; a `+` in the
path for a front end that reads it as a space; the mixed case `%252E`. The one character refuses every one of them
that holds `%25`.

Sweep 4 verdict for this surface: one candidate, C88, confirmed at medium by the auditor's claim and the verifier's
reading alike, open, with fix unit S-F74. Sweep 4 now holds two confirmed mediums, C87 on S-1002 (fixed) and C88
here, which S-1017 counts (S8). No model declined and no safeguard re-ran a request in the audit, the redteam or the
verifier, and no tool permission was refused to any of them.

C88 FIXED by S-F74, commits 8fddd81 (the test moved, with a `repos` row) and edff113 (the fix) (PR #365). The fix
is one byte in internal/proxy/terminate.go: canonical's last clause reads strings.ContainsAny(p, `;\%`), so a
decoded path that holds a literal `%`, which is sent as `%25`, has no single reading and is refused as `;` and the
backslash are; the comment on that line and the doc comment of canonical say so. No product line was added (the
file stays at 483). docs/policy.md's `path` bullet now also lists "no literal percent sign (`%25`), which a front
end decoding once would read as a second path", one Markdown line more. also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go.

Test (S4). TestC88DoubledEscapeLeavesTheBinding moved from escape/_pending/S-F74/ to internal/proxy/c88_test.go
with its body unchanged and one head line reworded, and escape/_pending/ is gone. The `repos` twin is one row at

`octo/allowed`, `POST /octo/allowed.git/%252e%252e/%252e%252e/other.git/git-receive-pack` with the placeholder,
want 403 and no secret. On 8fddd81, go1.27.4, plain and with -race, run by the redteam and again by the

"r.example.com  auth=Basic ...")`, whose value decodes to the real secret, with the broker and deny counts off by

under -race with the fuzz seed corpora, c10_test.go, c33_test.go, c68_test.go and sf72_test.go included, and the
arm `/v1/%E2%9C%93` is still admitted. The reviewer ran the same before and after by overlay.

Cost, measured by the builder with a throwaway test that is not kept: under a narrowed rule a path with `%25` and
the placeholder is 403 binding_mismatch, and without the placeholder it passes as before; under a rule that is not
narrowed it is swapped as before, since admits returns before canonical; on a sign-in host every path with `%25`
is 400 target_refused, placeholder or not; the API host of a sign-in rule is not judged. No file under cmd/,
internal/, escape/ or docs/ sends such a path through a narrowed rule or a sign-in host, and no provider or policy
data names a path or repository with a percent. No edge of a shipped provider was asked (T8).

Where code and ADR differ, for the maintainer. The Path row of docs/adr/accepted/006-judge-structure.md admits a
path that is Go's own escaping of the decoded path, clean but for one trailing slash, with no `;` and no backslash.
The code now refuses one byte more, a literal `%` in the decoded path, toward refusal. The loop did not edit the
ADR: amend that row to name the `%`, or rule the row as written and take the byte out again.

Review, one round, no finding that meets R2. The reviewer probed the fixed canonical: every spelling it tried that
carries `%25` is refused (`%2525`, a trailing `%25`, `%252F`, `%25%32%65`, mixed with `%2e`), and `/v1/a%20b`,
`/v1/x%3F/admin`, `/v1/x%23/admin` and `/v1/%E2%9C%93` stay admitted, none of which one decoding turns into a
slash, a percent or a dot segment. Its notes are one line in PARKED.md. Not shown: nothing here ran on a real VM
or on macOS before the hosted gate, and no real front end was run against the fix, only the Go model of the test.
With C88 fixed, sweep 4 holds two confirmed mediums, C87 and C88, both fixed; S-1017 still counts them (S8).
Nothing waits under escape/_pending/. The next candidate number is C89 and the next fix unit S-F75.

## S-1006, sweep 4: resolver: tunnelling, rebinding, cache and case tricks (I3, I4), as built at main 5e69a02

Sweep 4 (S8), the one further sweep that the maintainer allowed on 2026-11-26 after ADR-006, fresh context (S3),
the whole surface read as built after S-F74, not a diff. Auditor on the top tier in the cloud session, which has
no hypervisor and is Linux, as root, so the namespace probes ran for real and nothing ran on a VM or on macOS.
The auditor wrote its own trust boundary and worked every lens before it opened any earlier record. No
candidate.

Trust boundary. Attacker bytes enter at three places. One: guest root, and through it the repository and the
model's output, owns every byte and the timing of each AF_VSOCK stream to host port 5001. serveRelay in
cmd/workcell/relay.go admits it into one of 1024 slots, stream reads exactly 20 bytes under a 5 s deadline,
relay.Decode wants version 1 and proto 6 or 17, and a UDP header to port 53 at any address hands one frame of at
most 65535 bytes (relay.ReadFrame) to resolver.Answer under the same deadline. Answer replies from the policy
map alone and calls back with a refused name (lower-case [a-z0-9.-] of at most 253 bytes, or the empty string),
which p.Deny turns into one audit Note. The guest's resolv.conf, routes and listeners (cmd/workcell-init/net.go)
enforce nothing (A1). Two: the same guest owns the SNI and the HTTP bytes of a 443 stream and nothing else that
chooses a name: route returns a host only from the allowlist, the terminated transport's DialContext refuses a
host outside p.terminate, and Rewrite forces the upstream URL host and Host to the SNI host, so the only names
the host ever resolves are allowlist strings with a trailing dot. Three: the network attacker (LAN DNS, any host
off the allowlist) owns the answers that the host's system resolver returns for those rooted names (A and AAAA
sets, CNAME chains, off-bailiwick records, TTL, truncation) and every upstream byte at the address it steers the
host to. Those enter proxy.connect: one LookupNetIP per connection, then hostNets (interface prefixes plus one
netlink RTM_GETROUTE dump of every table of both families; kept rows are RTN_LOCAL of any table and RTN_UNICAST
with no gateway and more than 0 bits), then blockedAddr on every address before any dial, then a dial by literal
of the unmapped address under a shared 30 s budget. Authority: the supervisor at the operator's uid, which can
open any TCP connection the host can and holds the VMM child, the session CA key, the broker and the audit log.
Host configuration that the attacker does not control (routes, /etc/hosts, resolv.conf) is a precondition, not
an input. Ported: internal/proxy/proxy.go, allowlist.go and terminate.go. Not ported: internal/resolver,
internal/relay, cmd/workcell/relay.go, routes_linux.go and routes_other.go.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: question wants QDCOUNT 1, plain labels of at most 63 bytes and a text of at
most 253 bytes with the separating dot counted before the check, and reads type and class only when four bytes
remain; a label byte above 63 (extended types, pointers) is FORMERR; non-plain bytes make the name empty, so it
matches nothing; reply copies at most the header, the question and the 16-byte record, so maxReply 287 holds;
TC, AA, Z, AD and CD are masked, RD echoed, RA clear, NSCOUNT and ARCOUNT zeroed. ReadFrame allocates at most
65535 bytes per stream under the stream's absolute deadline, 64 MiB at the slot cap. Logic and state: both sides
fold ASCII only and the allowlist is lower-case ASCII, so no non-ASCII spelling, Kelvin sign or dotted I can
match; wire names have no trailing dot and canonicalHost strips one from the policy; punycode is compared
literally; wildcards and underscores are refused; AAAA, TXT, ANY, HTTPS or any other type of an allowed name is
NOERROR with no record, so there is no HTTPS-record path to ECH; a class other than IN or an opcode other than
QUERY is REFUSED with no callback; a response (QR set) gets silence, so nothing is reflected; the hint 127.0.0.1
is never dialled; forward-port hosts are answered too and the proxy scopes by port afterwards. Concurrency and
check-to-use: one lookup per connection, the host's networks read after it, every answer vetted before any dial,
the dial by literal of the vetted address, no second lookup and no Happy Eyeballs; a pooled upstream connection
reuses the address vetted at its dial; p.terminate, p.signin and the transport are written once before any Serve
goroutine; the resolver's map is read-only after New; the refused callback runs with no lock and p.Deny
serialises on the audit mutex; relayConn frees its slot once. Cryptography and identity: none on the resolver,
and DNSSEC is not consulted; the one identity check of the dial path is the terminated upstream's x509 for the
SNI host (TLS 1.2 at least, an explicit root pool, HTTP/2 off, no proxy from the environment), which is why a
rebind on a 443 name stops at the handshake and matters only on a forward port, where the operator's grant
trusts DNS (ADR-003). Failure modes: a lookup error or an empty set is resolve_failed; an unreadable interface
list, a failed or cut route dump, a malformed row or one blocked answer is blocked_address; a dial failure is
dial_failed; a ReadFrame error or a nil Answer closes the stream with nothing written; a failed Allowed record
dials nothing (S-F16); a nil log refuses everything; an Accept error of serveRelay closes every adapter; past
the soft limit every admission is refused while the hint still answers, a loss and never a gain. No error path
reaches a dial or a splice. Downgrade, rollback and replay: header version 1 only; the resolver is stateless and
echoes the id, so a replayed frame gets the same reply; EDNS and TC on a query are ignored; the product caches
no DNS answer and vets per connection, so a stale or poisoned entry of the host's cache can only change which
vetted address is dialled, or give resolve_failed. Interaction: the refused name reaches the audit log clipped
at 253 bytes and JSON-escaped, and the readers pass it through SafeHost (S-1010); tunnelling moves at most 253
bytes per refused query into the host's own log and nothing off the host; the host's only outbound DNS is A and
AAAA of a rooted allowlist name, set off by a guest connect, which carries timing and no data; the terminated
transport (S-1005) and the sign-in and git paths all dial through the one connect; the relay's slot cap and the
proxy's are equal (S-1004); explain and the resolver read the same allow.Hosts().

Refuted before anything was raised, by the auditor's own derivation and run unless marked. Search suffixes on
the host: the rooted name makes Go ask for it alone (under `search corp.internal` and `ndots:5` the product's
lookups were A and AAAA of `api.example.com.` and nothing else, where an unrooted control asked
`api.example.com.corp.internal.` first). /etc/hosts on the host: read for the rooted name with no DNS query, and
the result is vetted. CNAME chains: the stub does not chase, and the A records of the recursive answer are
vetted. Off-bailiwick A records: taken by Go, vetted. A mixed public and loopback set: the whole set refused.
IPv4-mapped loopback in AAAA, the unspecified address, an interface address on lo, an AnyIP address of the local
table (C69's layout), and a truncated UDP answer followed by loopback over TCP: all blocked_address, and the TCP
retry asked for the same rooted name only. A guest-side search suffix, 0x20 case, trailing dots, IDNA U-labels,
wildcards and non-ASCII: refused and recorded, or matched exactly. Zoned IPv6 addresses from a hosts entry: no
prefix contains a zoned address, so publicIPv6 refuses them (reasoned, toward refusal). Re-used from earlier
records and not derived again: DoT, DoH, TCP DNS and DoQ from the guest (TCP 53 and 853 are not served unless
the operator forwards one, UDP is relayed on 53 alone, and DoH to an allowed 443 host is HTTPS to an allowed
host); the macOS twin of C66 and C69 (routes_other.go reads no table; parked, no Mac here); networks behind a
routed gateway, VPN split tunnels and multipath rows (C9's residual, toward refusal); a route change during the
dump (parked by S-F52 and S-1004, with one refinement in the notes below); UDP to a port other than 53 and a
stream shed at the cap leaving no record (C14 intended, C8 refuted); the soft limit filled by refused queries,
the clear RA bit, the absent OPT and address-shaped names (parked); Mac resolver caches (parked, reasoned only).

Recorded fixes of this surface, each traced as built and run by the auditor, all holding: C7 (S-F4, the
168.63.129.16/32 row and Unmap first in blockedAddr) and C70 (S-F53, 192.80.8.124/32), by TestBlockedAddr under
-race; C13 (S-F8, TLSHandshakeTimeout and MaxConnsPerHost in Terminate's transport), by
TestUpstreamHandshakeEndsWithTheGuest under -race in 10.22 s; C66 and C69 (S-F49, S-F52: hostNets appends the
netlink dump of every table to the interface prefixes, and routes refuses a malformed part), by TestRoutes and
TestC69AnyIPLocalRoute under -race and by the live probe below; C23 and C24 (S-F16), in the plain run; C53
(S-F36), by TestRelativeSSLCertDirIsRefused under -race. S-F54's rows (rebind-host-network-forward and -sni with
Isolated, and rebind-on-link-neighbour-forward) were traced in the suite and not run, since they need a VM. C14
intended stands.

Ran, by the auditor, in a scratch directory and with nothing added to the repository; every target a process,
socket or namespace that the probe itself started (S12, T8). go test -count=1 green on internal/resolver,
internal/relay, internal/proxy and cmd/workcell (0.017 s, 0.015 s, 12.961 s, 6.660 s); go vet clean on the four;
under -race the eight tests of the recorded fixes in internal/proxy (15.3 s), the six relay tests of
cmd/workcell (2.0 s), and the whole of internal/resolver and internal/relay. Fuzz bursts in a copy of the tree,
with no crasher: FuzzAnswer 2,694,020 executions in 45 s, FuzzDecode 2,915,208 in 45 s, FuzzReadFrame 2,482,975
in 45 s, FuzzPeekSNI 168,265 in 30 s when run alone. A live chain, as an overlay test in package proxy, as root
in a network and mount namespace of its own with a resolv.conf of `nameserver 127.0.0.1`, `search corp.internal`
and `options ndots:5`, a hosts file naming an allowed name at 127.0.0.1, 192.175.48.129/25 on lo and `local
192.175.48.0/25 dev lo` by netlink, canaries at three addresses, and a scripted DNS server on 127.0.0.1:53 over
UDP and TCP that recorded every question; the real connect, the real net.DefaultResolver and the real hostNets:
twelve cases, pass in 0.21 s. A public answer was dialled (dial_failed, no route in the namespace); loopback,
the interface address, the AnyIP address, the mixed set, the CNAME to loopback, the off-bailiwick A, the mapped
AAAA, 0.0.0.0, the truncated answer with loopback over TCP and the hosts entry were each blocked_address; an
empty answer was resolve_failed; no canary was reached and every question the host asked was A or AAAA of the
one rooted name. An exchange probe as an overlay test in cmd/workcell, through the real serveRelay and resolver
with a 300 ms wait, pass in 0.80 s: a frame that promises 65535 bytes and sends ten was dropped after 301 ms, a
reply never read ended the stream at the deadline, and a 65535-byte frame of one letter was answered with a
12-byte FORMERR and a close.

Coverage. Read in full: internal/resolver (resolver and its test); internal/relay (relay and its test); in
cmd/workcell the files relay, relay_test, run_vm, session, policy and backend_linux; internal/proxy (proxy,
allowlist, routes_linux, routes_other, terminate, signin, proxy_test, routes_linux_test, c69_test, c13_test,
sf72_test, c53_test); internal/audit (audit, lines); internal/secret (broker, source); internal/vmm/vmm.go and
firecracker/firecracker.go; cmd/workcell-init (net, main) as data (A1); in escape/suite the files dns, dnstests,
resolver, rebind, relay and tests; in escape/sandbox the files control_resolver_linux, workcell_linux and
workcell_vm; loop/SPEC.md; and, after the audit's own pass, the S-1001 map, the S-1006 records of sweeps 1, 2
and 3, the sweep-4 records of S-1004 and S-1005, and PARKED.md whole. Skimmed or by search: terminate_test,
signin_test and providers_test of internal/proxy for helper names; the on-link row in
escape/suite/priv_linux.go; the boot call of cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go. Not examined: explain, log, ocsf and
update of cmd/workcell and the other c-tests of cmd/workcell and internal/proxy; internal/policy,
internal/provider, internal/guest, internal/wire, internal/fileserve, internal/workspace and internal/vmm/vz;
escape/sandbox/workcell_darwin.go and the adapter tests; the suite's other files; docs/; `_legacy/`; the sources
of Go's standard library, whose behaviour was taken from the runs. Not run: anything on a real VM, the escape
suite by the auditor, any macOS or vz path, any IPv6 layout (this session's kernel has no IPv6, so the IPv6 half
of routes rests on TestRoutes' hand-built rows, as in sweep 3), the four-hour fuzz of S10, govulncheck. The
clone is shallow, so the change since sweep 3 was taken from the records and not from git.

### S-1006 candidates, sweep 4

None. The auditor raised no candidate: nothing at medium or above, and nothing at low that names an invariant an
in-scope attacker puts at risk with a reproducible input (R2). So no reproducing test was written, no verifier
ran, no fix unit is added and escape/_pending/ stays absent; the next candidate number is still C89 and the next
fix unit S-F75. Four shapes are R3 notes, in PARKED.md: routes() does not read the kernel's mark of an
interrupted dump, a hardening note with no input that reproduces it; a hosts entry comes back from the lookup in
mapped form and is vetted after Unmap, which a test pins; the fuzz rate of FuzzPeekSNI depends on what runs
beside it; and Go's stub takes an A record whatever its owner name, which gives the attacker who already owns
the answer nothing more, since every address is vetted. Nothing falls under S14: no weakness of Go, the kernel
or any other project was found, and the ported files of the surface hold nothing new.

Sweep 4 verdict for this surface: no candidates, so it adds nothing at medium or above; sweep 4 holds two
confirmed mediums, C87 (S-1002) and C88 (S-1005), both fixed, which S-1017 counts (S8). S11: a safety classifier
stopped one turn of the auditor and withheld it; the tool calls of that turn did not run, the auditor went on
without sending that content again, and the orchestrator rephrased nothing. No model declined a request and no
safeguard re-ran one on another model.

## S-1007, sweep 4: secrets: sources, placeholders, sign-in token swap, git credentials, logs, crash output (I5), as built at main b47bf10

Sweep 4 (S8), the one further sweep that the maintainer allowed on 2026-11-26 after ADR-006, fresh context (S3), the
whole surface read as built after S-F71, S-F72 and S-F74, not a diff. Auditor on the top tier in the cloud session,
which has no hypervisor and is Linux, as root; nothing of this audit needed a VM, and nothing ran on one or on
macOS. The auditor wrote its own trust boundary and worked every lens before it opened any earlier record, then
traced and ran every recorded fix of the surface. Two candidates, C89 and C90, both confirmed by a verifier; the
records are under the next heading.

Trust boundary. Attacker bytes enter at two places, and a third attacker owns none here. One: guest root and hostile
model output own every byte and the timing of each terminated HTTP/1.1 request after S-1005's parser: method,
target, header names and values (the credential header and its Bearer and Basic forms, Content-Type,
Accept-Encoding, Connection, Host), the body (read whole only at a claimed token endpoint, under 256 KiB, else
streamed unread), pipelining and Upgrade; and every byte they can write into the guest's memory, disk and
environment, where only placeholders arrive (`wcph-` and 32 hex digits, 16 bytes of crypto/rand for each rule and
each sign-in row, minted per session by bindings in cmd/workcell/policy.go and handed to the guest through
guest.Exec.Env alone in run_vm.go; pull and bench boot with no secrets). Two: the malicious repository owns the
working directory and workcell.toml, which only narrows (policy.Narrow), and under --mount rewrites the directory
live. Three: the network attacker owns no byte of this surface, since an upstream is verified by x509 against the
explicit pool with the SNI host as ServerName; what an allowed provider answers, how its router reads a path and
whether it echoes or issues credentials are preconditions, not attacks. Out of scope: the operator's rows, sources,
helper programs and environment, and what a cmd: program reads through its arguments (SPEC section 2, ADR-006).
Authority of the code that handles those bytes: the supervisor at the operator's uid reads a value on each use (a
file opened, or a child at a fixed or operator-named absolute path with a scrubbed environment, directory `/`, no
shell, two minutes), writes it into one outgoing header or token body, holds sign-in tokens for one generation in
broker memory under a mutex, holds the session CA key, records every release and denial in the fsynced ledger before
the value leaves, rewrites a claimed token answer before the guest reads a byte of it, and exports or serves the
working directory. What the guest can see: the upstream's HTTP answer, which is the one channel that matters; the
Exec environment (placeholders only); the export or mount of the working directory (ADR-006's duty); the CA
certificate; the kernel command line; DNS answers for allowed names; the cache images. Ported:
internal/secret/source.go and broker.go, internal/proxy/terminate.go, proxy.go and allowlist.go,
internal/audit/lines.go. Not ported: internal/proxy/signin.go and cmd/workcell/policy.go.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: a file: source is absolute, Stat then regular, one buffer of 64 KiB and a byte,
one line, a CR refused; a cmd: source is strings.Fields of the operator's text, an absolute program, no shell,
stderr kept where no format prints it, partial output zeroed on every error path; a value with control bytes is
refused by the Transport's header check, whose error omits the value; Basic values are strict base64 of at most 4
KiB; a token body and a token answer are bounded at 256 KiB before and after gzip, and br, zstd and identity as an
encoding are refused; the header block is 64 KiB; the broker gives 300 grants and records 300 denials in each fixed
minute; hide and learn decode under encoding/json's depth cap. No panic from guest bytes; the fuzz bursts were
clean. Logic and state: the handler's order is 400 (opaque target, scheme without host, a path that is not canonical
on a sign-in host), 405 (TRACE, CONNECT), 421 (sameHost), then for each rule placeholderForm, admits (403) and
Lookup, then tokenEndpoint and tokenRequest (502), carriesPlaceholder (502), and the ReverseProxy with Rewrite to
the SNI host and ModifyResponse = tokenResponse. canonical is Go's own escaping of the decoded path, clean, with
none of `;`, backslash and `%`; it admits control bytes spelled in upper-case hex (C90). admits names no method.
tokenEndpoint matches by EqualFold on a canonical path; learn hides the broker's pair, the carried refresh token and
the issued pair in three spellings; tokenAnswer refuses an unclaimed 2xx of a sign-in host that is token-shaped at
the top level. What no code does: read any answer of a bound host that is not a sign-in host (C89), and refuse a
control byte in a judged path (C90). Concurrency and check-to-use: the grant and token maps are immutable after
NewBroker; held and Issue run under the mutex with clones; the value goes into the header in the goroutine that
fetched it; the record follows Resolve, and a failed record zeroes and withholds; the carried token covers C15's
race; nothing changes r.URL between admits and the outgoing clone; S-F71's Stat and Nlink at load against the
kernel's walk at use have no in-scope mover, since every prefix lies outside the working directory and the data
directory and the guest writes only under the former. Cryptography and identity: 128-bit placeholders; a P-256
session CA of at most 24 hours with critical name constraints and IP ranges excluded, one leaf for each allowed
name, the key in host memory; the upstream verified with ServerName the SNI host, TLS 1.2 at least, HTTP/1.1, a
fresh tls.Config for each guest connection. Failure modes: every error path answers 400, 403, 405, 421 or 502, or
closes; a Resolve error becomes broker_denied and its text does not reach the guest; a nil, closed or failing ledger
withholds every value; an error of Terminate ends the start before any VM; a ModifyResponse error is an empty 502;
the servers' error logs are discarded, and a traceback prints words, not bytes. Nothing fails open but the two
candidates. Downgrade, rollback and replay: placeholders are fresh per session; one token generation is held and the
replaced one zeroed; a replayed or attacker-chosen code grant replaces the operator's tokens for the session, a loss
and no gain; TLS 1.2 at least on both sides and ALPN http/1.1 alone. Interaction: ledger lines carry event, host,
header, name and result and never a value; `log`, its OCSF form, `explain` and the start-up errors name file, line,
name, host and path, never a value; the VMM child inherits the operator's environment, which holds no resolved
value; the Exec environment is PATH, HOME, LANG, the trust and cache variables, the placeholders and TERM; narrowing
(I13) holds: a row whose host is narrowed away goes, a dropped sign-in row whose token host stays refuses the
session, and --allow does not restore a dropped row; SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR are judged before boot (C86).

Refuted before anything was raised, by the auditor's run unless marked. An id_token beside the pair in a claimed 2xx
reaches the guest verbatim: U-403's class, parked. Unclaimed 2xx shapes on a sign-in host: a JSON array, a nested
object, `{"token":..}` and a bare JSON string pass and `{"access_token":..}` is 502, the documented exception,
parked. The refresh token echoed in a response header at a claimed endpoint passes, since hide reads the body alone:
parked, no real identity provider named. `Connection: x-api-key`: the ReverseProxy drops the swapped header after
the ledger recorded the grant, an over-report and self-harm, parked. `/v1/%00x` under `/v1/`: admitted and sent byte
for byte, and it stays under the prefix; Apache 2.4.58 refuses `%00`; the `repos` twin with a NUL is refused by
within. A form-framed 2xx at the claimed path is 502 (reasoned from learn, as sweep 2 ran). A placeholder
URL-encoded in a body crosses and is useless (reasoned). Two values, mixed case, the user position of Basic and a
lower-case `basic `: refused or crossing unswapped (existing tests). Upgrade and 101 at a token endpoint: parked,
bounded (reasoned). Hop-by-hop removal, X-Forwarded stripping and the query cleaning of the ReverseProxy: the order
confirmed by run and by reading. A bound host that echoes the presented value: residual by design in the earlier
records; C89 is what those records do not cover. S-F71's check attacked afresh: prefixes through links into the
working directory or the data directory, `..` in a program path, a FIFO, a hard-linked file, relative and
capitalised schemes (reasoned on the code, and the 30 arms of sf71_test run green). A repository that narrows away a
token host or the API host of a sign-in row: fails closed (reasoned, and c34's test run).

Recorded fixes of this surface, each traced as built and run by the auditor, all holding: C10 (S-F5, then S-F72) by
TestFoldedPathEscapesTheEndpointAndTheRule; C12 (S-F7) by TestLearnHidesTheEncodedSpelling and FuzzHide; C15 (S-F9)
by TestConcurrentRefreshHidesTheReplacedToken; C32 (S-F25) by TestC32OpaqueRequestTarget; C33 (S-F26, then S-F72) by
TestC33PathBindingReleasesSecretOutsideBinding; C34 (S-F27) by TestC34SignInRowDropped; C35 (S-F28) by
TestC35CmdHelperDoesNotObeyTheRepository; C53 (S-F36) by TestRelativeSSLCertDirIsRefused; C54, C58 and C82 with the
rule of S-F71 by their tests and TestSF71SecretSourceJudgedAsTheHostOpensIt; C55 (S-F38) and C67 (S-F50) by
TestC55TokenEndpointFormatSuffix and TestC67TokenAnswerInAnotherMediaType; C68 (S-F51, then S-F72) by
TestC68RoutingOverrideHeaders; C85 and C86 (S-F69, S-F70) by their tests; S-F72 as the ADR decides it, `method`
refused at load; C88 (S-F74) by TestC88DoubledEscapeLeavesTheBinding and the `repos` row of
TestTerminateNarrowedRule. C16 (low, a source resolved on each Lookup) is as it was.

Ran, by the auditor, in a scratch directory and with nothing added to the repository; every target a loopback
process that the probe itself started (S12, T8). go build of the module; go test -count=1 green on internal/secret
(0.263 s), internal/proxy (12.917 s), internal/policy, internal/audit, internal/provider and cmd/workcell (7.401 s);
under -race internal/secret (1.307 s) and internal/proxy (18.015 s), and by name the tests of the recorded fixes: 20
in internal/proxy, 11 in cmd/workcell, 13 in internal/secret; go vet clean on the six packages. Overlay probes
through the real terminating proxy, the real broker with a file: grant and a real ledger: seven of the shapes above
and the two candidates. Fuzz bursts of 25 s each in a copy of the tree, with no crasher: FuzzHide 241,397
executions, FuzzSwapRefresh 747,786, FuzzCarriesPlaceholder 124,664. Apache 2.4.58 from the distribution's archive
as a plain-HTTP front end on loopback with `RewriteRule ^/v1/(.*)$ http://127.0.0.1:18082/api/$1 [P,NE]` before a Go
recorder: six requests, for which see C90.

Coverage. Read in full: internal/secret (broker, source and their tests); internal/proxy (terminate, signin, proxy,
allowlist, routes_linux, routes_other, and the tests terminate_test, signin_test, git_test, proxy_test);
internal/policy/policy.go; internal/provider/provider.go and its four data files; internal/audit (audit, key,
lines); internal/relay/relay.go; internal/wire/wire.go; internal/guest (guest, trust, walk); internal/vmm/vmm.go and
