escape/suite the files secrets, signin and terminate; in escape/sandbox the files workcell, workcell_linux and
sandbox; docs/policy.md; docs/adr/accepted/006-judge-structure.md; loop/SPEC.md; and, after the audit's own pass,
the S-1001 map, the S-1007 records of sweeps 1, 2 and 3, the records of S-F71 and S-F72, the sweep-4 record of
S-1005 with C88 and S-F74, and PARKED.md whole. Skimmed or by search: the head comments of the other c-tests of
cmd/workcell and internal/proxy; the test names of policy_test.go; the head of S-1016b; escape/suite/tests.go for
the 16 rows of I5 and escape/enforced.txt; the sign-in lines of docs/providers.md. Not examined: internal/fileserve,
internal/resolver, internal/rootfs and internal/vmm/vz; update, pull, pull_vm, bench, cache and layer of
cmd/workcell; mount, net, pull and root of cmd/workcell-init; escape/sandbox/workcell_vm.go and the control
adapters; the rest of escape/suite; `_legacy/`; the sources of net/http, httputil and crypto/tls, whose behaviour
was taken from the runs. Not run: anything on a real VM, the escape suite by the auditor, any macOS path, the
keychain: and secret-service: sources beyond their fail-closed arms (this session has neither `security` nor
`secret-tool`), any real provider (T8), nginx, the four-hour fuzz of S10, govulncheck.

### S-1007 candidates, sweep 4

C89. ID I5 (real credential bytes never exist in guest memory) and A4 (placeholder credentials are the only
credential path, and no mode stages a real secret in the guest); docs/policy.md says that the guest never holds the
value. Attacker: guest root or hostile model output, choosing the request it sends to the bound host. Precondition
the attacker does not control: the operator bound a credential whose provider issues or rotates a credential for its
holder under the row's host and path, with a scope that allows it. Where: internal/proxy/terminate.go, where the
ReverseProxy's only answer hook is ModifyResponse = tokenResponse (:353-361) and the swap is made (:399-406), and
internal/proxy/signin.go:133-138, where tokenResponse returns at once for a host that has no sign-in rule, so no
answer of a bound API host is ever read. terminate.go is ported and signin.go is not. also in v1 main:
egressproxy/terminate.go. Input: a `[[secret]]` row with host gitlab.example.com, header private-token and a file:
source; the guest sends `POST /api/v4/personal_access_tokens/self/rotate` with `Private-Token:` the session's
placeholder. Effect claimed: the proxy swaps the real value in, the provider issues a new credential of the
operator's account and answers 200 `{"id":42,"token":"glpat-NEW-REAL"}`, and the answer crosses to the guest unread:
a real and durable credential in guest memory, which outlives the session and can leave through the same bound host.
Nothing leaves the bound host on the request side, so I6 holds. Severity claimed: medium. The auditor named other
providers with such endpoints from their documents and probed none (T8); by its knowledge of their APIs, and by no
run, none of the four shipped provider rows reaches such an endpoint with its bound key, so the precondition is a
row that the operator wrote.

The auditor's evidence, run: an overlay probe through the real terminating proxy, the real broker with a file: grant
and a real ledger, before a loopback TLS upstream that answers the rotate path only when it sees the real value; the
guest's client read the 200 with the new token.

Reproducing test (S4): TestC89MintedCredentialReachesTheGuest, a Go test of package proxy, 49 lines, written by the
redteam from the claim alone, with no VM and so no T2: the package's own terminating proxy with a rule that is not
narrowed, and a loopback TLS upstream that models a provider acting as designed. It fails when the guest reads the
issued token. Controls: `GET /api/v4/user` with the placeholder is served, so the upstream saw the real value, and
the rotate request with a wrong token is 401 with nothing issued. It waits in escape/_pending/S-F76/c89_test.go,
which Go does not compile. Run by the orchestrator on 2eb8bb1 with `go test -overlay`, go1.27.4, plain and with
-race, one error line each: `c89_test.go:47: I5/A4: the guest read "{\"id\":42,\"token\":\"glpat-NEW-REAL\"}": the
proxy signed a request that mints a credential and passed the answer unread`; both controls pass. gofmt and go vet
with the overlay are clean.

Outcome: CONFIRMED by the verifier at medium, from its own run of the test and its own reading of the rulings. Its
evidence. One: the test fails as recorded and both controls pass; it uses only the package's shared fixtures and the
real Terminate, and a placeholder in the bound header to the bound host is the designed use, so the test gives
itself no power. Its upstream is an honest model of the documented endpoint; the one thing it leaves out, that the
real provider also revokes the token presented, does not favour the claim. Two: the attacker is in scope, and no row
of SPEC section 2's out-of-scope list covers it: the provider is not compromised, it acts as designed. Three: it is
not ruled intended. Every ruling in the records is about an echo of the value presented: the sweep-1 record of this
surface ("a bound host that echoes the credential header returns the real bytes to the guest ... residual risk"),
the sweep-2 record ("an allowed host that echoes the bound header: residual by design"), the S-1013 record and the
PARKED line of S-1007; U-403's line covers an id_token at a claimed token endpoint; nothing in docs/adr/accepted/,
docs/policy.md or docs/threat-model.md accepts a credential that the bound provider newly issues. Four, severity by
S6's letter: medium, "the same, but only with an extra precondition the attacker does not control"; not high, since
a provider with no such endpoint, or a row narrowed away from it, is out of reach; not low, since the break is shown
on the real package. Five: not S14: an endpoint that rotates a token for its holder is a documented feature of that
project, not a weakness in it.

No patch is known, for the maintainer. The auditor, the redteam and the verifier each looked for a product change
and found none that closes C89 in general: the product cannot tell which answer of a bound host is a credential;
`path` cannot part GitLab's rotate endpoint from the rest of its API by prefix unless the operator narrows below
`/api/v4/`; a check of answer text is the kind that ADR-006 took out of both checks, and it would have to buffer
answers that are streamed. What can be said today is a duty: bind a credential of the least scope, and narrow `path`
away from endpoints that issue credentials. Under that reading no change makes the parked test pass while the bound
API stays usable, so S4's "passes after the fix" has no fix to follow, and S7 wants every medium fixed before
cutover. That is a design question of the kind S8 names, like the secret-source check before ADR-006.

Unit: S-F76, directly below S-1007 in PLAN.md, and written as a spike (fable, env:any), not as the boundary unit
that the phase note gives a finding: it writes ADR-007 as a proposal that compares the duty in docs/policy.md with a
row in SPEC section 2, the same with a `path` in the compiled-in provider rows, a swap only under a narrowed row,
and any design that judges a structure the host itself sends, each with its cost; it builds nothing, and the parked
test stays in escape/_pending/S-F76/ until a unit builds the accepted design. A boundary unit would have had to
judge answer text or fail three times. The orchestrator chose this and the maintainer may rewrite the line. C89
stays open until then. Variants not written (redteam): other endpoints that issue a credential at the same host; an
answer in another media type; a new token in a response header or a cookie; a rotate under a `path` rule whose
prefix covers the endpoint, which the narrowing does not help.

C90. ID I5 (a placeholder is useless at any destination other than the one it is bound to: docs/policy.md binds a
row narrowed by `path` or `repos` to that path, "judged on the path as the upstream receives it, which must have one
reading"), the sibling of C88 with control bytes in place of `%25`. Attacker: guest root or hostile model output,
choosing the path of its own request. Preconditions the attacker does not control: the operator narrowed the row by
`path` or `repos`; the bound host's front end puts the decoded path back into the request line that it sends on; and
the backend behind it reads HTTP/1.x. Where: internal/proxy/terminate.go:127-130, canonical, whose refused set is
`;`, backslash and `%` and which has no clause for a control byte; used by admits (:116) and by the target check of
a sign-in host (:369). The file is ported. also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go. Input: under the rule {Host:
api.example.com, Header: x-api-key, Path: "/v1/"}: `POST /v1/x%0D%0A%0D%0AGET%20/admin` with `X-Api-Key:` the
session's placeholder; also canonical today: `/v1/x%0A`, `/v1/x%0D`, `/v1/x%7F`, `/v1/x%01y` and `/v1/x%09y`. The
lower-case `/v1/x%0d%0a` is not Go's escaping and is refused. Effect claimed: admits is true, the broker releases
the secret with a granted record, and the upstream receives the line byte for byte with the real secret; a front end
that decodes once and writes the raw bytes into its own request line hands the backend a second request line, at a
path outside the binding, with the original headers. The secret never reaches the guest and never leaves the bound
host (I6 holds). Severity claimed by the auditor: low, since the one such front end it could name was Apache httpd
2.4.0 to 2.4.55 (CVE-2023-25690, public and fixed in 2.4.56), and Apache 2.4.58 refused each control byte in its run
(403, AH10415) while passing the C88 control.

Reproducing test (S4): TestC90ControlBytesInACanonicalPath, a Go test of package proxy, 59 lines, written by the
redteam from the claim alone, with no VM and so no T2. One half asks canonical about each spelling; the other sends
each through the package's own terminating proxy under a rule of path `/v1/` to a loopback TLS upstream that models
a front end which decodes once and reads the bytes again, and fails when the upstream receives the real secret at a
path that holds a control byte or lies outside `/v1/`, so the model does not carry the failure alone. Controls:
`POST /v1/x` is served at `/v1/x` with the real secret, and the lower-case `/v1/x%0d%0a` is refused before the
upstream sees a request. It waits in escape/_pending/S-F75/c90_test.go. Run by the orchestrator on 2eb8bb1 with `go
test -overlay`, go1.27.4, plain and with -race, twelve error lines each: six of `c90_test.go:25:
canonical("/v1/x%0D%0A%0D%0AGET%20/admin") = true` and its fellows, and six of `c90_test.go:56: I5: the upstream
received "/admin" with the real secret` and its fellows; both controls pass. The redteam saw it pass with a scratch
overlay of canonical that also refuses bytes below 0x20 and 0x7F, so a pass means the effect is gone.

Outcome: CONFIRMED by the verifier, and read by it as medium where the auditor claimed low; the record follows the
verifier, as with C87. Its evidence. One: the test fails as recorded and both controls pass; admission, the broker's
release and the forward run through the real proxy, and only the upstream is a model. Two: the model is honest about
one shipping server in a documented configuration, and not about Apache: nginx 1.24.0 from the distribution, on
loopback, with `location /n3/ { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:18082$uri; }` wrote to a backend that logs raw bytes
`POST /n3/x`, CR LF CR LF, `GET /admin HTTP/1.0` and the header `X-Api-Key: real-secret`; a strict backend answers
the claim's own spelling 400, since its first line is then malformed, but for the spelling
`/v1/x%20HTTP/1.1%0D%0AHost:%20b%0D%0AContent-Length:%200%0D%0A%0D%0AGET%20/admin`, which canonical admits, a Go
net/http backend behind that nginx served `GET /admin` with the real secret. Apache 2.4.58 re-encodes in ProxyPass,
nocanon, ProxyPassMatch and RewriteRule with [P] and with [P,NE,B] and refuses with [P,NE]; nginx with a plain
proxy_pass, with a URI part, with `rewrite ... break` and with `$request_uri` forwards the bytes encoded. The five
rows of a single control byte show no break by themselves and are hardening. Three: the attacker is in scope and the
test gives itself nothing the guest lacks. Four: it is not intended behaviour: docs/policy.md promises one reading;
the Path row of ADR-006 does not rule on control bytes; the parked residuals name a NUL, double decoding, a trailing
space and overlong UTF-8 only. It has the standing of C88, a documented and not default configuration of a shipping
front end. Five, severity by S6's letter: medium; I5 is broken only with the three preconditions above; a break is
shown against a current front end, so it is not low; the secret never leaves the bound host, so it is not high. Six:
not S14: the file is ported and no v1 release holds it, nginx's substitution of a variable as it stands is
documented behaviour, and Apache's case is a public CVE that is fixed.

Fix unit: S-F75 (boundary, fable, env:any), directly below S-1007 in PLAN.md and above S-F76: in canonical refuse a
decoded path that holds a byte below 0x20 or 0x7F, one more clause on the existing return line and no added product
line, with the comment on that line and the sentence of docs/policy.md saying so. The auditor tried that clause in a
copy of the tree: the file stays at 483 lines, gofmt is clean, the package passes, both of its probe rows become 403
and the admitted arm `/v1/%E2%9C%93` of sf72_test.go stays admitted. The verifier's spelling also needs `%20`; a
space alone splits no line, and the unit weighs it. Cost: under a narrowed rule a path with a control byte is 403,
and on a sign-in host 400; no client sends one. As with C88 the change narrows the Path row of the accepted ADR-006
toward refusal, the loop does not edit the ADR, and the fix's record says where code and ADR then differ. Variants
not written (redteam): other C0 bytes and `%7F` under a `repos` rule, which shares canonical; a control byte in the
query, which no rule judges by design and which a front end that reads the request line again would still see; a
sign-in host's token path with `%0D%0A`.

Sweep 4 verdict for this surface: two candidates, both confirmed at medium by a verifier, both open: C90 with fix
unit S-F75, and C89 with the design question S-F76 and no patch. Sweep 4 now holds four confirmed mediums, C87
(S-1002) and C88 (S-1005), both fixed, and C89 and C90 here, which S-1017 counts (S8). Product is at 14976 of 15000.
The next candidate number is C91 and the next fix unit S-F77. No model declined, no safeguard stopped or re-ran a
request of the auditor, the redteam or either verifier, and no tool permission was refused to any of them. The
auditor and one verifier installed apache2 and nginx from the distribution's archive for their probes, every
listener on loopback and stopped afterwards (S12). Nothing falls under S14.

C90 FIXED by S-F75, commits 288a62b (the test moved, with one more arm and a `repos` row) and d83242b (the fix)
(PR #368). The fix is one clause in internal/proxy/terminate.go: canonical's return line now also holds
`!strings.ContainsFunc(p, func(r rune) bool { return r < 0x20 || r == 0x7f })`, so a decoded path that holds a byte
below 0x20 or the byte 0x7F, which Go sends as its upper-case escape, has no single reading and is refused as `;`,
the backslash and `%` are; the comment on that line and the doc comment of canonical say so. No product line was
added (the file stays at 483, product at 14976 of 15000). docs/policy.md's `path` bullet now also lists "no byte
below a space or DEL (`%0D%0A`, which a front end decoding once would read as a second request line)", one Markdown
line more. also in v1 main: egressproxy/terminate.go.

The space, as the unit asked: a bare space (0x20, sent as `%20`) stays admitted, and the arm `/v1/a%20b` of
sf72_test.go is unchanged. Reason: a space alone starts no second request line; the verifier's spelling needs CR and
LF beside it and is refused for those; a front end that splits on a space rejects the request or cuts the path
there, which leaves a prefix of the judged path, still under the rule's prefix or inside its repository; and real
API paths carry `%20` in names. The reviewer tried and could build no parser that leaves `/v1/` by a space without
CR or LF.

Test (S4). TestC90ControlBytesInACanonicalPath moved from escape/_pending/S-F75/ to internal/proxy/c90_test.go
with its two controls byte for byte as parked, one head line reworded and the verifier's spelling
`/v1/x%20HTTP/1.1%0D%0AHost:%20b%0D%0AContent-Length:%200%0D%0A%0D%0AGET%20/admin` as a seventh arm on the existing
line; escape/_pending/S-F75/ is gone and escape/_pending/S-F76/ is untouched. The `repos` twin is one row at the
end of TestTerminateNarrowedRule in terminate_test.go, by the redteam, before any fix: under repos `octo/allowed`,
`POST /octo/allowed.git/git-receive-pack%0D%0A%0D%0AGET%20/admin` with the placeholder, want 403 and no secret. On
288a62b, plain and with -race, run by the redteam, again by the orchestrator and again by the reviewer: seven lines
of `c90_test.go:25: canonical(...) = true`, seven of `c90_test.go:56: I5: the upstream received ... with the real
secret`, two of them at `/admin`, and for the row `got (200, "r.example.com  auth=Basic ...")`, whose value decodes
to the real secret, with the broker and deny counts off by that one swap; both controls pass there. On d83242b all
pass, and the whole package passes plain and under -race, c10_test.go, c33_test.go, c68_test.go, c88_test.go and
sf72_test.go included, the arm `/v1/%E2%9C%93` still admitted. The reviewer also sent, through the real proxy on
loopback: under the `path` rule a NUL, 0x1F, 0x7F, a tab in the prefix, a control byte in a middle and in the last
segment, one before a query and the mixed-case `%0d%0A`, each 403 with no secret; under the `repos` rule a control
byte before `.git`, in the owner, in the last segment and the second-request spelling, each 403; on a sign-in host
four spellings, each 400; a raw control byte in the request target is answered 400 by Go's server before any
handler runs.

Cost, measured by the builder with a throwaway test that is not kept: under a narrowed rule a path with a control
byte and the placeholder is 403 binding_mismatch; on a sign-in host it is 400 target_refused, placeholder or not;
under a rule that is not narrowed the swap is unchanged (200 with the real secret), since such a rule binds the
host alone. No path that the repository, a provider row or git smart HTTP sends holds a control byte.

Where code and ADR differ, for the maintainer: the Path row of the accepted ADR-006
(docs/adr/accepted/006-judge-structure.md, line 42) says that a path is admitted when it is Go's own escaping of the
decoded path, is path.Clean of itself but for one trailing slash, and holds no `;` or backslash. The code refuses
two things more, both toward refusal and both for the row's "one reading": a literal `%` since S-F74 (C88), and a
byte below 0x20 or the byte 0x7F since this unit (C90). The loop did not edit the ADR. Review: one round, no finding
that meets R2; its three notes are one line in PARKED.md. Sweep 4 now holds four confirmed mediums, C87, C88 and C90
fixed and C89 open with the design question S-F76, which S-1017 counts (S8).

C89, the design question (S-F76): OPEN, with a proposal, and not fixed. docs/adr/007-issued-credentials.md
(ADR-007, 75 lines, `status: proposed`) is the architect's answer to the question that the record above left: it
compares four options and recommends the first. A proposal decides nothing: it counts only once the maintainer
has moved the file to docs/adr/accepted/, and no product line, test or user document changed in this unit.

The recommendation: no check. The product stays as it is (0 product lines, no operator row newly refused); the
duty is stated in docs/policy.md (the guest never holds the value that was bound; what the host sends back is not
read, so bind a credential of the least scope and narrow `path` away from endpoints that issue one);
docs/providers.md says per shipped row what its key can reach; and SPEC section 2 gains a row, which only the
maintainer can add, for what an allowlisted provider sends back to the holder of a bound credential, an echo or a
credential it issues or rotates. The ADR words that row and has it replace the four echo rulings (W15). Not
recommended, each with its cost in the ADR's table: a `path` in the compiled-in provider rows (1 to 3 product
lines; it narrows only the two rows whose issued tokens are short-lived, bets on CLI routes that the suite measures
with one request per provider, and leaves an operator's own row as it is); a swap only under a narrowed row (it
refuses every row without `path` or `repos`, the example of SPEC section 5 among them, and a row narrowed to
`/api/v4/` still holds the rotate endpoint); a judge of the answer (8 to 15 lines and open-ended, a read of
answers that are streamed, and the check of text that ADR-006 took out).

The four shipped rows, from the providers' public documents alone, read on 2026-11-28 (T8: no provider was asked):
claude (api.anthropic.com, x-api-key): no such endpoint for the bound key. codex (api.openai.com, authorization):
yes, short-lived, a realtime client secret of 10 to 7200 seconds; a durable key only where the operator binds an
Admin key, which serves the CLI nothing. gemini (generativelanguage.googleapis.com, x-goog-api-key): yes,
short-lived, an ephemeral Live API token under the root the CLI uses. copilot (api.githubcopilot.com,
authorization): none documented. So the S-1007 record's line, that none of the four shipped rows reaches such an
endpoint, was the auditor's knowledge and is corrected here for codex and gemini: both reach one that issues a
token of minutes to two hours, good only at the bound host. Evidence gap: only Anthropic's page was read in full;
the hosts of the other three and of GitLab did not resolve from the session, so their rows rest on search excerpts
of the official pages, and Gemini's longest lifetime was not reached.

The parked test: escape/_pending/S-F76/c89_test.go is untouched and still fails as recorded. Under the
recommendation no change makes TestC89MintedCredentialReachesTheGuest pass while the bound API stays usable, so
S4 has no "after": it waits until the maintainer accepts the ADR and adds the row, and the unit that then builds
the design, which the maintainer adds, deletes the folder, edits the three documents and records C89 as accepted,
not as fixed. For the maintainer: S7 wants every medium fixed before cutover and the recommendation moves C89 out
of scope instead, which no proposal can do; until the ADR is accepted and the row is in SPEC section 2, or the
unit line is rewritten, C89 is an open medium of sweep 4, which S-1017 counts (S8). also in v1 main:
egressproxy/terminate.go.

## S-1008, sweep 4: workspace export in both modes, and the return path (I1, I8), as built at main b3fbe2c

Sweep 4 (S8), the one further sweep that the maintainer allowed on 2026-11-26 after ADR-006, fresh context (S3), the
whole surface read in full as built after S-F71 to S-F76, not a diff, at the claim commit ac18402. The unit line
still carries its sweep-1 text (copy four parked tests for C17 to C20 and run no auditor); those tests are long in
place and S-F10 to S-F13 are done, so this run took the other branch of the line's accept and did the audit again as
S-1002 says, as sweeps 2 and 3 did and as S-1017's line asks of sweep 4. One auditor run on the top tier, finished
without a stop. No hypervisor in the cloud session, which is Linux, as root: every probe ran by `go test -overlay`
or a scratch program outside the repository, against processes, pipes, files and one overlay mount that the probe
itself made and removed; nothing ran on a real VM or on macOS. The auditor wrote its own trust boundary and worked
every lens before it opened FINDINGS.md, PARKED.md or LOG.md, then traced and ran every recorded fix of the surface
and tried its parked leads again. Two candidates, C91 and C92; the records are under the next heading.

Trust boundary. Clone export: the attacker's bytes are the shape of the operator's working directory as a malicious
repository, an earlier `--mount` guest or an earlier pull left it: names, link targets, link topology, types, sizes,
depth and count. They enter at workspace.Export (internal/workspace/workspace.go: `.` opened once, a descriptor
walk, Fstatat with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW, Openat with O_NOFOLLOW and O_DIRECTORY, Readlinkat, hard links by device and
inode, sockets, FIFOs and devices dropped) and at rootfs.Tree and WriteExt4File, where openSource
(internal/rootfs/ext4file.go) opens each file again beneath the one export descriptor and checks device, inode, size
and S_IFREG again. Authority: the operator's uid reads every file beneath cwd and writes one 0600 sparse image and
the `inodes` record under sessions/<id>/; it trusts holds() (data and config directories, mountinfo, the VMM
directories of running sessions) and named() (C61), and attaches the image read-write to the guest. Mount: the
attacker's bytes are every byte of every frame on the one vsock 5002 stream, since guest root writes raw frames and
the guest kernel's grammar is no bound. They enter at wire.Conn (frames of 64 KiB, 5 s a frame), at fileserve.parse
(lengths per opcode, names of one component) and at op. Authority: the operator's uid runs openat, mkdirat,
symlinkat, unlinkat, renameat, pwrite, ftruncate, fchmod and utimensat relative to directory descriptors beneath the
export, under life and mu, with the chain check of at(), single() for files of several names, the caps maxFDs 4096
and maxNodes 2^17, grown against limit, and the pace in points. It holds no notion of `.git`: under --mount the
guest writes the real tree whole (C40, by ruling). Return path: the attacker's bytes are every Entry, Data and Exit
frame from the pull VM, which mounts the image the attacker wrote, with no network, the caps of defaults() and a nil
audit log. They enter at fetch and pulled.frame (cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go), guest.DecodeEntry, manifest.add,
checkPath and fold (pull.go), then write and put, or compare and sameBytes. Authority: the operator's uid, with the
destination open as a directory, openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH, NO_SYMLINKS and NO_XDEV one component at a time
(pull_linux.go); it unlinks what is not a directory and empty directories, makes directories 0755, symbolic links of
any target and files 0644 or 0755 of the guest's bytes, and refuses a component that is its directory's `.git`, by
the device and inode of `.git` taken without following a link, before and after the create. What no code judges,
found before the records were read: what the name `.git` resolves to when it is a symbolic link or a `gitdir:` file
that names a directory inside the tree (C91), and the kernel's cost of a directory seek, which the pace charges as
one unit (C92). Concurrent actors: only the operator's other sessions; a mount guest owns its export wholly, so a
race with a pull or an export in that tree gains it nothing. No file of this surface is ported.

Lenses (S9). Parsing and resources: parse() walked again for each opcode against the sizes of FUSE 7.37 (fixed(n),
the length equations of WRITE and BATCH_FORGET, the NUL rule of split, a link target under 4096, names of at most
255 bytes with no slash or NUL); the dirent decode of readdir; the bounds of DecodeEntry; the manifest limits (a
million entries, 64 MiB of names, the image's bytes plus 4096 an inode); the 64 KiB and the deadline of wire; on the
export side the 4097-byte Readlinkat buffer against the 4095 of validate, and ErrTooLarge above 32 GiB, 8.4 million
entries or 65000 links. FuzzRequest, FuzzReadFrame, FuzzDecode and FuzzPath ran 45 s each (359 thousand, 1.6
million, 2.9 million and 482 thousand executions) with no crasher. Memory is bounded (16 workers of 64 KiB, the node
table, a pull manifest of about 250 MiB at most). CPU: the pace charges frames, chain links, dirent bytes,
READDIRPLUS entries and the time of SEEK_HOLE, and not the directory seek of READDIR: C92, measured. Disk: grown
against limit and the block per entry hold. Logic and state: put() traced for every order (a link and then a path
through it, ELOOP; a file and then a path under it, ENOTDIR; a directory that is not empty where a file is wanted,
ENOTEMPTY; a host link where a directory is wanted is unlinked and never followed; one path twice, the fold map;
`.git` by name and by the inode of `.git` itself); the gap is that isGit takes the identity of the link or the
gitfile itself, so the directory that `.git` names is reached under its real name: C91, measured, and git ran the
hook. The manifest is judged before any byte is written, and end() refuses Data left over or missing and any Exit
that is not zero. The FUSE state machine stands (EIO before INIT and after DESTROY, EPROTO for another major, ENOSYS
for LINK, MKNOD, RENAME2, xattr and fallocate, modes masked to 0777, ids never reused). Concurrency and
check-to-use: 1500 rounds with 16 workers of an OPEN for writing on a file node raced on the wire by UNLINK and a
SYMLINK of the same name to `../secret`, in both orders, with a WRITE through every handle obtained: the secret
beside the export was unchanged, 1048 writes landed in the real file opened before the swap and one open answered
ELOOP, so I1 holds (O_NOFOLLOW and the S_IFREG check after the open); life and mu, the chain of at(), RENAME under
life.Lock and the order of Close and Serve were read again, and the fileserve tests pass under -race; an export
against a mount guest on an ancestor admits only the file that was walked (openSource); a pull against a mount guest
of the destination equals the guest's own writes (C40). Cryptography and identity: none by design; identity is
device and inode at use everywhere but in the choice of which inode stands for `.git` (C91); sessions are keyed by
the spelling of cwd (parked by S-1013, unchanged). Failure modes: nothing fails open; a failed Export removes the
image and keeps the record (C83); fetch refuses a session without its image or its `inodes`; an error of put leaves
the documented partial tree; fileserve maps an unknown error to EIO and Close releases every descriptor; Note on the
nil log of the pull VM returns ErrClosed, so a denial there cannot panic (read, not run); serveRelay exits on
EMFILE, so the network is lost and not gained. Downgrade, rollback and replay: wire version 1 only; the FUSE minor
is negotiated down over fixed layouts and a second INIT is EIO; a pull is one shot, a frame out of place is an
error, and a second pull gives the same tree; the `inodes` record is written by the host before the guest runs and
bounds an image that the guest made again. Interaction between surfaces: the clone export carries `.git` (its hooks
and config run in the guest only), workcell.toml (which only narrows, I13) and every symbolic link as a link; what a
mount guest writes to workcell.toml or `.git` for the next session is C40, parked; the file service shares the
supervisor with the proxy and the log (A9), so the CPU of C92 is taken from them.

### S-1008 candidates, sweep 4

C91. ID I8 ("Bringing results back to the host never executes or obeys guest-controlled content: no hooks, filters,
config, attributes, submodule URLs, symlink or path traversal"); A1 in that the host trusted the name `.git` and not
the directory that the name stands for; row 19 of docs/threat-model.md says that git metadata the guest writes
returns only through row 5. Attacker: root in the guest of a clone session, by hostile model output or a hook of a
malicious repository; no forged frame is needed, since the honest init reports the tree. Precondition the attacker
does not control: the operator's repository keeps its git directory inside the work tree under another name, so that
`.git` is a symbolic link to an in-tree directory, or a gitfile `gitdir: <path>` as `git init --separate-git-dir
./gitdir` writes it; a `.git` that names a directory outside the tree is not affected. Where:
cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go, isGit (:294-297), which takes the device and inode of `.git` by Fstatat with
AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW, so the identity is that of the link or of the gitfile itself and never of the directory it
names, and the loop of put (:303), its check (:312) and the check after the create (:338) compare with the wrong
inode; cmd/workcell/pull.go, checkPath (:80-81), which refuses the spelling `.git` alone; internal/guest/walk.go:35,
which skips the name `.git` alone, so the init walks `gitdir/` and reports it; workspace.Export copies `.git` as the
link or the file it is and `gitdir` as a plain directory. Input: on the host `git init -q --separate-git-dir
./gitdir` in the repository (or `mv .git gitdir && ln -s gitdir .git`), then `workcell run` there in clone mode; in
the guest the agent writes /workspace/gitdir/hooks/pre-commit, executable, and /workspace/gitdir/config; then
`workcell pull`. As frames: Entry dir `gitdir`, Entry dir `gitdir/hooks`, Entry file `gitdir/hooks/pre-commit` with
Exec, Entry file `gitdir/config`, their Data, Exit. Effect claimed: manifest.add admits every path and put writes
them into the host's real git directory, so the operator's next `git commit` runs the guest's pre-commit hook on the
host, and a config value such as core.fsmonitor is obeyed at the next `git status`; with the link shape an honest
`git commit` by the agent in the guest brings its objects, refs and hooks back into the host's live git directory as
well. Severity claimed: medium. No file here is ported, so there is no v1 line.

The auditor's evidence, run: an overlay test in package main of cmd/workcell through the real manifest.add and
write, with git 2.43.0: in both shapes write returned nil, the hook lay in the real git directory, and `git status`
ran the hook that the guest's config named as fsmonitor (the canary file existed).

Reproducing test (S4): TestC91GitDirectoryUnderAnotherName, a Go test of package main of cmd/workcell, 61 lines,
written by the redteam from the claim alone, with no VM and so no T2: the real manifest and the real writer of the
pull, a destination whose `.git` names the in-tree directory `gitdir` in the two forms git reads, the repository
made by git's own `git init --separate-git-dir` where git is on PATH (only that part is skipped without it), and a
guest tree of `gitdir/hooks/pre-commit` and `gitdir/config`. It fails when the guest's hook and config lie in the
directory that git obeys, and again when a `git commit` on the host makes the hook's canary. Controls: the manifest
still refuses `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, and a `.git` that names a directory outside the destination leaves the plain
in-tree `gitdir` writable as before. How a fix refuses is not judged. Run by the orchestrator on ac18402 with `go
test -overlay`, go1.27.4, plain and with -race, the same lines each time, for the arms `a symbolic link .git ->
gitdir` and `a gitfile .git naming gitdir`: `c91_test.go:51: I8: after the writer (<nil>) the guest's hook lies in
gitdir: true, its config: true; gitdir is the git directory git obeys: true, and must take both exactly when it is
not` and `c91_test.go:56: I8: git commit on the host (<nil>, "") ran the guest's pre-commit hook: <temp>/canary
exists`; the control arm passes. gofmt and go vet with the overlay are clean, by the redteam.

Outcome: CONFIRMED by the verifier at medium, as claimed, from its own run of the test, plain and with -race, and
its own reading of the code and the records. Its evidence. One: the test gives itself no power: the manifest goes
through the real manifest.add and checkPath, the destination is opened as fetch opens it (holds, within and named
never look at the shape of `.git`), and the writer is the real write and put; the honest init reports such a tree,
since Export copies `.git` as it is and Walk skips only the name. Two: it is not ruled: no line of FINDINGS.md,
PARKED.md, docs/threat-model.md, docs/policy.md, README.md or docs/adr/accepted/ speaks of a gitfile, of
`--separate-git-dir` or of a git directory under another name; C40 rules `.git` under --mount only; C44 is the
precedent, the same effect (a pull lands a hook and the operator's next git command runs it) under a precondition on
the operator's side, confirmed at medium, and its fix S-F32 judges `.git` by the device and inode of the name alone;
the sentence of S-F32 that the destination is the operator's choice is about which directory is pulled into, not
about where its git directory lies. Three: the precondition is the operator's, so medium and not high, by its own
runs in a temporary repository: a tree that holds `.git` as a link or as a gitfile blob is made by `git mktree`, but
`git clone` of it answers `error: invalid path '.git'` and leaves `.git` a plain directory; the gitfile of a
submodule or a worktree names a directory under the top `.git` or outside the tree, which the pull refuses or cannot
reach; an earlier pull cannot make or replace `.git`; a mount guest could lay the shape but writes `.git/hooks`
directly already (C40), so that chain gains nothing. Only `git init --separate-git-dir ./gitdir` or a link made by
hand gives it; both are legal to git. Four: not low, since the break is shown on the real writer and I8 names hooks
and config in its own text. Not S14: the code is v2's own, and git reads a gitfile and a linked `.git` as its
documents say.

Fix shapes, from the auditor, and the unit chooses none. One: isGit compares with what `.git` names: Fstatat that
follows the link covers the link shape, and where `.git` is a regular file the `gitdir: ` line is read and that path
is taken for the identity, about five product lines; a `.git` that names anything outside the destination then
matches no in-tree component, as today. Two: fetch, after holds(dest), and session() refuse a directory whose `.git`
is a link or a gitfile that resolves inside the directory, with one error line in the style of holds(); that covers
the top-level `.git`, the shape git's own tools make, and leaves a nested `sub/.git` gitfile that names an in-tree
directory, which would need every gitfile read. Variants that the redteam could not express, for the fix unit to
weigh and for S-1018: the same `gitdir` under --mount is written live with no pull at all, which is C40's ruling and
no new finding; an operator's config whose core.hooksPath names an in-tree directory such as `.githooks/` makes a
plain directory one that git obeys, by the operator's own config; the target of the link spelled in another letter
case on a host that folds case.

Shape chosen by the orchestrator of S-F77, before the redteam ran: one, at the writer, and carried down the walk.
put takes the device and inode of the directory that each `.git` on the way names, the link followed and a gitfile's
`gitdir: ` path resolved by the kernel from the directory that holds it, and refuses any component of a guest path
that is that directory, at any depth below. Reasons. One: it is the lesson of this record, the identity git obeys
and not the name, at the one place that writes, so a later caller of the writer is covered with no second check.
Two: the line's own form of shape one compares in the same directory alone, and `git init --separate-git-dir
./meta/gitdir` is as legal as `./gitdir`, so the identity must go down the walk; that also closes a nested
`sub/.git` gitfile whose target lies below `sub/` (not every nested one: corrected after the review, see FIXED
below), and the target spelled in another letter case, since the kernel resolves it. Three: shape two refuses the session and the pull of an operator whose git directory lies in the tree,
for good, where the gitfile that git's own tool writes holds an absolute host path, is inert in the guest and pulls
honest work cleanly under shape one; and it judges by path text at two call sites away from the writer. Its one
gain, an early denial for the hand-made link where an honest `git status` in the guest rewrites gitdir/index and the
pull then refuses, is given up: the refusal names the path. The gitfile is read as git reads it, the prefix and the
trailing line ends, and a looser reading can only refuse more.

C91 FIXED by S-F77, commit ca01f01 (PR #372), shape one as chosen above. isGit in cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go takes a
list that put carries down the walk: for each directory on the way of a guest path, the root included, it adds the
device and inode of that directory's `.git`, taken without following as before (C44), and of what the `.git` names,
a link followed by Fstatat or, for a regular file alone, opened by fileBeneath and read for at most PATH_MAX and 16
bytes, the path after `gitdir: ` with its line ends cut, resolved by Fstatat from that directory; a component whose
identity is in the list is refused, in the walk, at the last name and after a create, which is taken away again.
Product 14976 to 14992 of 15000, 16 lines; no check in fetch, holds or session, no new refusal of a session, no
program run, docs unchanged (the I8 rows of docs/threat-model.md and docs/policy.md stay true). Test (S4):
cmd/workcell/c91_test.go is this record's source with its fifth line reworded and no other byte changed (sha256 of
the 61 lines checked before the edit, diff of one line after). It failed on main in its two arms, at :51 and :56 as
recorded, and passes on the fix, plain and with -race, its control arm and manifest control unchanged; so do
TestWrite, TestCompare, TestManifestAdd, TestC20PullWriteErrorQuotesGuestPath and TestPullGrowthCapEntries (C57),
C44's TestPullWritesDotGitHFS is built on darwin alone; gate-macos is green. Three rows joined TestWrite: `.git -> meta/gitdir`
refuses `meta/gitdir/hooks/pre-commit` and makes no hooks directory, a nested `sub/.git` gitfile `gitdir: x`
refuses `sub/x/config`, and beside a plain `.git` directory a directory named `gitdir` still lands. The 83 new test
lines are paid by folds of table rows in five test files outside escape/, no case and no assertion lost (counted by
the reviewer): test 28477 of 28488. Closed, by run of both: the link and the gitfile at the top, absolute or relative, one
level or deeper; a nested gitfile or link whose target lies at or below the directory that holds it; a dangling
`.git -> gitdir` that the guest fills (made and removed again); a gitfile with CRLF; a FIFO named `.git` does not
block. Review, one round, one finding that meets R2 and it is against this record, not the code: the sentence above
first said that every nested gitfile is closed. NOT closed, reproduced by the reviewer through the real write: a
nested gitfile whose target is beside it and not below, `git init --separate-git-dir ../b/gitdir a` in the tree, so
that `a/.git` holds `gitdir: ../b/gitdir`; a guest path `b/gitdir/hooks/pre-commit` never passes `a`, its `.git` is
never read, and the hook lands (write returned nil). Same attacker and the same kind of precondition as C91, rarer,
and no tool of git makes it unasked; closing it needs every gitfile of the destination read, at pull or at start.
It is no candidate of an audit and no verifier saw it: S-1013 and the verdict S-1017 weigh it, and PARKED.md holds
the line. Also not closed, as the unit says: a `.git` above the destination that names a directory inside it (a
pull into a subdirectory of a repository), an operator's core.hooksPath, and --mount (C40). No builder fix round.

Unit: S-F77, directly below S-1008 in PLAN.md (boundary, fable, env:any). The test is not parked under
escape/_pending/: with it the test count is over its limit, and escape/ has no layout left to fold (the redteam's

Source of cmd/workcell/c91_test.go (61 lines):

    // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
    // Copyright 2026 Omkhar Arasaratnam
    
    // Candidate C91 of S-1008 sweep 4 (I8): the pull refuses the name .git and what shares its inode, so a repository whose .git is a symbolic link to, or a gitfile naming, a git directory kept in the work tree under another name (git init --separate-git-dir ./gitdir) has that directory written by the guest: its hooks and config are obeyed at the operator's next git command. Fails until the fix lands.
    // Parked under escape/_pending/S-F77 until the fix unit S-F77 moves it to cmd/workcell/c91_test.go and removes the folder.
    
    //go:build linux || (darwin && arm64 && cgo)
    
    package main
    
    import (
    	"os"
    	"os/exec"
    	"path/filepath"
    	"testing"
    
    	"github.com/omkhar/workcell/v2/internal/guest"
    )
    
    // TestC91GitDirectoryUnderAnotherName: the real writer, a destination whose .git names the in-tree directory gitdir in the two forms git reads, and a guest tree of gitdir/hooks/pre-commit and gitdir/config. Where git is on PATH the repository is git's own, and a commit afterwards shows whether the hook ran. Controls: the name .git is still refused by the manifest, and a .git that names a directory outside the destination leaves the plain in-tree gitdir writable as before. How a fix refuses is not judged.
    func TestC91GitDirectoryUnderAnotherName(t *testing.T) {
    	git, _ := exec.LookPath("git")
    	if err := (&manifest{limit: 1 << 20}).add(fileEntry(".git/hooks/pre-commit", 1, true)); err == nil {
    		t.Error("control: the manifest admitted .git/hooks/pre-commit")
    	}
    	for _, tc := range []struct {
    		name  string
    		point func(g, in, out string) error // makes .git at g; in is the in-tree gitdir, out a directory outside
    		real  bool                          // gitdir is the git directory git obeys
    	}{
    		{"a symbolic link .git -> gitdir", func(g, _, _ string) error { return os.Symlink("gitdir", g) }, true},
    		{"a gitfile .git naming gitdir", func(g, in, _ string) error { return os.WriteFile(g, []byte("gitdir: "+in+"\n"), 0o644) }, true},
    		{"control: .git -> a directory outside", func(g, _, out string) error { return os.Symlink(out, g) }, false},
    	} {
    		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
    			parent := t.TempDir()
    			dest, outside, canary := filepath.Join(parent, "dest"), filepath.Join(parent, "outside"), filepath.Join(parent, "canary")
    			gitdir := filepath.Join(dest, "gitdir")
    			must(0, os.MkdirAll(gitdir, 0o755))
    			must(0, os.Mkdir(outside, 0o755))
    			if git != "" {
    				must(exec.Command(git, "init", "-q", "--separate-git-dir="+gitdir, dest).CombinedOutput())
    				must(0, os.Remove(filepath.Join(dest, ".git")))
    			}
    			must(0, tc.point(filepath.Join(dest, ".git"), gitdir, outside))
    			hook, config := "#!/bin/sh\ntouch "+canary+"\n", "[core]\n\tbare = false\n"
    			err := write(openDir(t, dest), judged(t, []guest.Entry{dirEntry("gitdir"), dirEntry("gitdir/hooks"), fileEntry("gitdir/hooks/pre-commit", int64(len(hook)), true), fileEntry("gitdir/config", int64(len(config)), false)}), from([]byte(hook+config)))
    			h, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(gitdir, "hooks", "pre-commit"))
    			c, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(gitdir, "config"))
    			if hk, cf := string(h) == hook, string(c) == config; hk != cf || hk == tc.real {
    				t.Errorf("I8: after the writer (%v) the guest's hook lies in gitdir: %t, its config: %t; gitdir is the git directory git obeys: %t, and must take both exactly when it is not", err, hk, cf, tc.real)
    			}
    			if tc.real && git != "" {
    				out, err := exec.Command(git, "-C", dest, "-c", "user.name=c91", "-c", "user.email=c91@example.invalid", "commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "c91").CombinedOutput()
    				if _, found := os.Stat(canary); found == nil {
    					t.Errorf("I8: git commit on the host (%v, %q) ran the guest's pre-commit hook: %s exists", err, out, canary)
    				}
    			}
    		})
    	}
    }

C92. ID I10 ("The guest cannot exhaust host CPU, memory, disk, file descriptors, processes or log volume"), host CPU
in mount mode, the class of C76 with one system call that the pace does not charge. Attacker: root in the guest of a
--mount session, sending raw FUSE frames on the init's 5002 stream as C17, C64 and C76 did; raw frames are needed,
since the guest kernel sends only offsets that the server returned. Precondition the attacker does not control: the
exported directory is a merged overlayfs directory, one that exists in a lower layer as well as in the upper, as the
workspace that a container image ships is; a directory that the guest makes itself exists in the upper layer alone,
and overlayfs serves that one with a cheap seek. Where: internal/fileserve/ops_linux.go:387, where readdir() calls
unix.Seek on the directory handle for whatever offset the frame carries, then ReadDirent (:393); the only charge is
s.work.Add(int64(n / direntLen)) at :400 for the bytes returned, and one unit a frame in Serve (serve_linux.go:192).
On a merged overlayfs directory the kernel's ovl_dir_llseek walks its cached list of entries, in time linear in the
smaller of the offset and the entry count, under the inode lock, at every offset that differs from the file
position. grow() at serve_linux.go:131-132 already charges SEEK_HOLE by the time it took; readdir charges no time.
Input: an export on a merged overlayfs directory; INIT; one directory of about 100000 entries, which the tree holds
or which the guest fills (20000 entries made through the mount cost 80 MiB of the default 1 GiB of --disk and are
enough, by the verifier's run); OPENDIR 16 times; then READDIR (opcode 28) on those handles in turn with offset
1<<40 plus a counter and size 8192, as fast as the host takes them. Effect claimed: each frame costs the host about
3 ms of kernel CPU in the list walk and is charged one unit, so the real Server takes about two host cores with one
sequential client, where the row mount-cpu-flood allows one vCPU plus a second, and the same flood costs 0.39 cores
on ext4 and 0.58 on tmpfs; the CPU is taken from the proxy and the audit log of the same supervisor (A9). Severity
claimed: medium. No file here is ported, so there is no v1 line.

The auditor's evidence, run as root in the session: an overlay mount with 100000 entries in the lower layer, made
and removed by the probe, and an overlay test in package fileserve on the package's own harness: 642 frames in 2.036
s at 2.16 cores, 6.8 ms of CPU a frame and 3.16 ms for one far seek with getdents alone; controls on the same host
and flood: ext4, 3350 frames at 0.39 cores, and tmpfs on this 6.18 kernel, 1805 frames at 0.58 cores.

Reproducing test (S4): TestC92SeekOfOneFrame, a Go test of package fileserve, 84 lines, written by the redteam from
the claim alone, with no VM and so no T2: a directory of 100,000 entries in the lower layer of an overlay that the
test mounts in its own temp directory and unmounts in cleanup, one entry in the upper so that the directory is
merged, the package's own harness, 16 handles, READDIR frames at offsets of 1<<40 and up for two seconds, judged by
the process's CPU over wall against 1.5 cores, the bound of c76_test.go. It needs root once, for the mount: as root
it mounts directly, otherwise it runs itself again through `sudo -n` as c65_test.go does, and it skips only when
neither works. Control: the same flood on the same directory in the lower layer, a plain filesystem. Run by the
orchestrator on ac18402 with `go test -overlay`, go1.27.4: plain, `c92_test.go:80: I10: 632 READDIR frames under the
pace took 2.14 host cores (4.356026s CPU in 2.036302229s), want at most 1.5`; with -race, 641 frames at 2.15 cores;
the control arm passes each time; no mount was left. The redteam measured 2.09 to 2.20 cores over four runs and 0.36
cores for the control with its bound taken away. gofmt and go vet with the overlay are clean, by the redteam.

Outcome: CONFIRMED by the verifier at medium, as claimed, from its own runs. Its evidence. One: the test fails as
recorded, 2.17 cores plain and 2.14 with -race, and the control passes. Two: the server pays, not the harness: its
own probe ran the unchanged Open and Serve in a child process over a socketpair and read the child's CPU from /proc:
on the merged directory the server alone took 1.91 cores, 0.01 of user time and 1.91 of system time, with 0.02 for
the harness and 11.6 ms for one far READDIR sent alone; on plain ext4 with 100000 entries the server took 0.37
cores, 277 us a frame. The bound of 1.5 is a fair and slightly lenient reading of the suite's own judge (cpuJudge in
escape/suite/floods.go allows one vCPU of wall plus a second, about 1.3 cores over 3.4 s), and the server alone is
above it, so this is not C64's case of an overrun bounded near one core. Three: the test gives itself no power: raw
frames, 16 handles and far offsets are what C17, C64 and C76 allowed guest root; the entries need not come from the
operator, since an arm with one seed entry in the lower layer and 20000 made through the mount gave 1.97 cores for
the server alone, 2.0 ms a frame. What the guest cannot do is make the directory merged, so the precondition is the
operator's environment: a container or an image whose workspace lies in a lower layer, with /dev/kvm passed in. This
session and the hosted runner are on ext4, so no row of the suite shows it. Four: no ruling accepts a host
filesystem's slow operations; the fix round of C77 graded the cost of SEEK_HOLE on tmpfs as I10 at medium under the
same kind of precondition and charged the seek's time to the pace, and PARKED.md parks only the blocks that reflink
and compression leave uncharged, not CPU. Severity by S6: medium, as that finding was; not high as C76, which needed
nothing beyond --mount; not low as C64. Not S14: the linear seek of overlayfs is public kernel code that works as
designed, and the missing charge is this project's.

Fix shapes, from the auditor, and the unit chooses none. One: two lines in readdir(), a time taken before the Seek
at ops_linux.go:387 and `s.work.Add(int64(time.Since(t0) / (750 * time.Nanosecond)))` after the ReadDirent, the form
that grow() uses for SEEK_HOLE, so that the pace holds the walk to about 30 ms of host work in each period of 64 ms,
about half a core, with no option and no changed reply. Two, with a change of behaviour: answer EINVAL to an offset
that is neither 0 nor one that this handle returned, after which a seekdir back to an earlier page fails. Variants
that the redteam could not express, for the fix unit to weigh: MKDIR and UNLINK in the merged directory between the
READDIR frames change the overlay's version, so each READDIR builds the whole cache of 100000 entries again, about
100 ms a frame; 16 handles spread over several merged directories escape the one inode lock and take more cores;
READDIRPLUS at far offsets on a merged directory; other exports whose seek is linear, tmpfs before kernel 6.6 and
exports that FUSE or NFS back. A charge by time covers each of them where the time is spent inside the Seek and the
ReadDirent; the unit says in its record which it measured.

Unit: S-F78, below S-F77 in PLAN.md (boundary, fable, env:any). As for C91, the test is not parked under
escape/_pending/: this record holds it, byte for byte behind four spaces, and the fix unit re-creates it, paid by
folds outside escape/.

Source of internal/fileserve/c92_test.go (84 lines):

    // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
    // Copyright 2026 Omkhar Arasaratnam
    
    // Candidate C92 of S-1008 sweep 4 (I10): a READDIR at an offset far from the handle's position costs the host a walk of the whole listing when the directory is a merged overlayfs one, and is charged as one cheap frame, so a flood of them under the pace takes host cores. Fails until the fix lands.
    // Parked under escape/_pending/S-F78 until the fix unit S-F78 moves it to internal/fileserve/c92_test.go and removes the folder.
    
    //go:build linux
    
    package fileserve
    
    import (
    	"cmp"
    	"fmt"
    	"os"
    	"os/exec"
    	"path/filepath"
    	"testing"
    	"time"
    
    	"golang.org/x/sys/unix"
    )
    
    // TestC92SeekOfOneFrame is I10 on the host's CPU, as c76: a directory of 100,000 entries that lies in a lower layer and the upper one, so the overlay merges it, exported; 16 handles; READDIR frames at offsets of 1<<40 and up, 8 KiB each, as fast as the service takes them for two seconds. Judged by this process's CPU over wall against one core plus slack. Control: the same flood on the same directory in the lower layer, a plain filesystem. Root is used once, for the overlay mount: the test re-runs itself through sudo -n, as c65 does.
    func TestC92SeekOfOneFrame(t *testing.T) {
    	if os.Geteuid() != 0 {
    		if err := exec.Command("sudo", "-n", "true").Run(); err != nil {
    			t.Skip("not root, and sudo -n fails:", err)
    		}
    		exe, _ := os.Executable()
    		out, err := exec.Command("sudo", "-n", "env", "TMPDIR="+os.TempDir(), exe, "-test.run=^TestC92SeekOfOneFrame$", "-test.v", "-test.count=1").CombinedOutput()
    		if t.Logf("as root:\n%s", out); err != nil {
    			t.Fatal(err)
    		}
    		return
    	}
    	const bound, budget, entries = 1.5, 2 * time.Second, 100000
    	base := t.TempDir()
    	lower, upper, work, merged := filepath.Join(base, "lower", "big"), filepath.Join(base, "upper", "big"), filepath.Join(base, "work"), filepath.Join(base, "merged")
    	if err := cmp.Or(os.MkdirAll(lower, 0o755), os.MkdirAll(upper, 0o755), os.Mkdir(work, 0o755), os.Mkdir(merged, 0o755), os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(upper, "x"), nil, 0o644)); err != nil {
    		t.Fatal(err)
    	}
    	dir, err := unix.Open(lower, unix.O_RDONLY|unix.O_DIRECTORY|unix.O_CLOEXEC, 0)
    	for i := 0; err == nil && i < entries; i++ { // the lower layer holds the listing; one entry in the upper makes the directory a merged one
    		err = unix.Mknodat(dir, fmt.Sprint(i), unix.S_IFREG|0o644, 0)
    	}
    	if err != nil {
    		t.Fatal(err)
    	}
    	if err := unix.Mount("overlay", merged, "overlay", 0, "lowerdir="+filepath.Dir(lower)+",upperdir="+filepath.Dir(upper)+",workdir="+work); err != nil {
    		t.Skip("root without the right to mount an overlay here:", err)
    	}
    	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = unix.Unmount(merged, unix.MNT_DETACH) })
    	cpu := func() time.Duration { // this process's CPU time, user and system
    		var ru unix.Rusage
    		_ = unix.Getrusage(unix.RUSAGE_SELF, &ru)
    		return time.Duration(ru.Utime.Nano() + ru.Stime.Nano())
    	}
    	for _, tc := range []struct{ name, dir string }{{"control: the plain directory", lower}, {"the merged overlay directory", filepath.Join(merged, "big")}} {
    		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
    			k, stop, _ := started(t, tc.dir)
    			defer func() { _ = stop() }()
    			fhs := make([]uint64, workers)
    			for i := range fhs {
    				fhs[i] = le.Uint64(k.ok(reqOpendir(rootID)))
    			}
    			c0, w0, n0, done := cpu(), time.Now(), k.n, make(chan uint64, 1)
    			go func() { // frames until the budget is spent, then a STATFS with unique 0 as the marker; done says how many went before it
    				for i := 0; time.Since(w0) < budget; i++ {
    					k.send(reqReaddir(rootID, fhs[i%workers], 1<<40+uint64(i), 8192, false))
    				}
    				k.raw(reqStatfs())
    				done <- k.n - n0
    			}()
    			for got, want := 0, -1; got != want; got++ {
    				if k.recv().unique == 0 {
    					want = int(<-done) + 1
    				}
    			}
    			if c, w := cpu()-c0, time.Since(w0); c.Seconds() > bound*w.Seconds() {
    				t.Errorf("I10: %d READDIR frames under the pace took %.2f host cores (%v CPU in %v), want at most %.1f", k.n-n0, c.Seconds()/w.Seconds(), c, w, bound)
    			}
    		})
    	}
    }

Shape chosen for C92 by the orchestrator of S-F78, before the builder ran: shape one, the charge by time. Reasons.
One: it is two statements where product had 8 lines of room, and shape two needs a record on every handle of the
offsets it returned, memory that the guest then grows and that would want a cap of its own. Two: no reply changes,
so a seekdir back to an earlier page sees what it saw before, and an honest guest kernel is refused nothing. Three:
the cost that the model could not count is the host filesystem's, and a charge by time counts it whatever the
filesystem is, as grow() does for SEEK_HOLE since C77; shape two would close the far offset alone and leave the
cache that MKDIR and UNLINK make the overlay build again.

C92 FIXED by S-F78, commit 21128fb (PR #373), shape one as chosen above. readdir() in internal/fileserve/ops_linux.go
takes a time once it holds the handle's lock and, by one defer, adds the time elapsed over 750 ns to s.work when the
frame returns. One charge a frame covers the Seek, every ReadDirent pass, the stats of READDIRPLUS and each error
return; a wait for the handle's own lock is not charged, a wait for the kernel's inode lock behind another handle
is, as in grow(). Product 14992 to 14995 of 15000, 3 lines (the two and the import of time); two comments reworded
in place; docs unchanged, no page of docs/ states how the pace charges. Test (S4): internal/fileserve/c92_test.go is
this record's source with its fifth line reworded and no other byte changed (sha256 of the 84 lines checked before
the edit by the redteam and again by the reviewer, diff of one line). It failed on main in its overlay arm, 2.35
cores plain and 2.32 under -race by the redteam, 2.33 by the reviewer with main's file laid over, and passes on the
fix plain and under -race with no skip, its control arm unchanged; a probe of the same flood gave 22 frames at 0.12
cores where main gave 828 at 2.22. Its 84 lines are paid by 74 lines of folds in seven test files outside escape/,
rows of tables and wrapped comments joined, each file the same bytes but for white space and comment marks.
Where it ran and where it skipped: as root, mounting directly, in the cloud session, by the redteam, the builder,
the reviewer and the orchestrator; the `sudo -n` path was never taken. In the hosted gate on 21128fb the package
internal/fileserve is ok in 34.0 s, but the log names no test of it, so whether the test ran there through `sudo -n`
or skipped is not shown.
Variants weighed, each by a probe that is not kept, 16 handles, floods of 2 s, cores of the whole test process, main
then fix. By the builder: MKDIR and UNLINK between far READDIR frames 2.19 then 0.18; four merged directories of
100000 entries 3.46 then 0.22; READDIRPLUS at far offsets 2.24 then 0.11, and at offsets inside the listing 1.07
then 0.08. By the reviewer, with its own probes: READDIRPLUS far 2.11 then 0.10; far READDIR with MKDIR and RMDIR
between 2.46 then 0.26; READDIR at offset 0 with MKDIR and RMDIR between 2.04 then 0.23; 16 merged directories of
20000 entries, which escape the one inode lock, 3.87 then 0.40; a cycle of OPENDIR, READDIR at 0 and RELEASEDIR, whose
freeing of the overlay's cache in RELEASEDIR is not charged, 1.04 then 0.67. Each is closed, under 1.5 cores. Not
measured: an export on tmpfs before kernel 6.6, on FUSE or on NFS, and the server alone in a child process.
Cost to honest use: one handle listing 100000 entries from offset 0 in 4 KiB frames, as the guest kernel asks. Plain
directory on ext4: 456 ms on main and 581 ms on the fix by the builder, 455 and 580 by the reviewer, 27 per cent
slower; the listing was bound by the pace before (783 frames, about 1680 a second, now 1280), and the charge of one
point for 24 bytes at ops_linux.go:400 stood for the time that is now charged as well, so READDIR pays twice for the
same work. A directory under about 12000 entries fits one period and is not slowed. Merged overlay directory: 1.80 s
then 2.11 s by the builder, 1.78 s then 3.17 s by the reviewer, who names the cause: readdir() reads 8 KiB by
getdents and returns 4 KiB, so each honest frame seeks back and overlayfs walks its list from the head; that was so
before this unit, and S1 lets only the fix land. A guest's `ls -l` uses READDIRPLUS, where plusEntry already holds
100000 entries to about 6 s and this charge adds under a second. The mount rows of the suite on a real VM, hosted
gate on 21128fb, 270 s: all eight pass, mount-cpu-flood with 3.2 CPU s in 3.4 s of wall where 4.4 are allowed.
Review: one round, no finding that met R2, no fix round. Unit S-F78 was env:kvm, not env:any as written above.

Trust boundary, as the auditor wrote it before the records were opened. Attacker bytes enter this surface at
(a) `<cwd>/workcell.toml`, owned by the malicious repository and, between sessions of a --mount directory, by
guest root: loadPolicy in cmd/workcell/policy.go, then ReadRepo of internal/policy (O_NOFOLLOW, O_NONBLOCK and
O_NOCTTY on the relative name, fstat of the opened descriptor, a regular file only, 1 MiB, a repository [update]
table refused by its line), then Parse (the project's own TOML subset: tables, bare keys, basic strings with \u
escapes, integers whose value is discarded, arrays of strings, every other construct refused with its line),
then Narrow, of which only an allow entry's exact text and a secret row's name are ever compared, and whose
strings reach the operator only quoted in the `asked` note; (b) the working directory itself, its spelling, links
and mounts, exported or served live, judged by holds, within, resolved, leadsInto, named and the TMPDIR rules;
(c) files the guest writes that the host later trusts: workspace.ext4, read only by the pull's judges, the cache
images, attached and never read, and through a pull whatever lands in the destination the operator names (C93);
(d) the network only as channel.json and artifacts, which this surface names in [update] and S-1011 judges. The
operator's own and not the attacker's: argv (parseRun: --cpus 1 to 32, --memory from 128 MiB, --disk, --mount,
a repeatable --allow kept verbatim and judged by allowlist() and ParseAllowlist, --cache by a regular expression,
the command verbatim into guest.Exec; update's --to, --rollback and agent; log's -f and --format; ids by validID;
thirteen verbs, no `secret`), the environment (XDG_CONFIG_HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME only when absolute, HOME which
must be absolute, TMPDIR which boot refuses when relative, TERM into the guest, SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR
judged by session against the working directory and the data directory, HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY honoured by the
update client alone), the user's config.toml ([network]; [[secret]] rows whose file: or cmd: path leadsInto judges
against the working directory and the data directory, a file: being one regular file with one name; [update]
with channel stable, hold or https, cooloff not negative, a key of 32 bytes and a ca that leadsInto judges;
[workspace] and [resources] parsed and ignored) and the four embedded provider files, checked by provider.parse
at load, whose hosts grant nothing. Authority: the supervisor as the operator's uid before any VM exists, and
the CLI under explain, update, pull and diff. It decides the proxy's sni and forward maps, the resolver's names,
the session CA's permitted names, the ports word of the kernel command line, which rows become broker grants and
terminate rules with fresh placeholders (I5), what the guest sees as /workspace (I1, I13), where data and config
live (I7, I9), what the installer trusts (I14) and, through holds, where a pull may write and a session may run.

Lenses (S9), each worked. One, parsing and resources: the scanner and parser derived again, tokens of constant
size under the 1 MiB cap with no backtracking, CR only before LF, control bytes and non-ASCII outside strings
refused, \u escapes checked as scalar values so that \u0000 and \u000a pass Parse and are refused downstream by

### S-1009 candidates, sweep 4

C93. ID I8 ("Bringing results back to the host never executes or obeys guest-controlled content"), with I5 by
consequence, since the guest's program then runs on the host as the operator in the place of the credential's
source; the lesser arms touch I6 with I5 (SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR) and I14 (the [update] ca). The auditor
also named I13, by the reasoning of C85; the verifier read that as a stretch, since no policy text changes,
and the record follows the verifier, though the test's head and messages say I13. Attacker: root in the guest
of a clone session, by hostile model output or a hook of a malicious repository, who writes an executable file
at a name of its choice in the tree that the pull returns; for the SSL_CERT arm the network attacker as well,
as in C86. Precondition the attacker does not control: the operator runs `workcell pull <dest>` with an explicit
destination that holds, or lies above, the directory of a path that their own config or environment trusts. The
plain `workcell pull`, into the working directory, is not affected: a session in a directory that holds such
a path is refused at load (C58, S-F71; C86). Where: cmd/workcell/data.go, holds() (:33-65), the judge of a
pull destination, which compares the destination with the data directory, the config directory, the file that
config.toml resolves to (S-F69), the mount points and the VMM directories of running sessions, and never reads the
user's policy or the environment; cmd/workcell/pull_vm.go, fetch (:76-121), which judges the destination by open,
holds, the TMPDIR rule and named() alone and never calls loadPolicy, and put (:314-378), which unlinks what lies
at a guest's path and creates it anew, 0755 for an Exec entry; cmd/workcell/policy.go (:79-98), where loadPolicy
judges a file: path and the program of a cmd: source by leadsInto against the working directory of that session
and the data directory alone; cmd/workcell/update.go:128 for the ca and cmd/workcell/run_vm.go:93-104 for the
SSL_CERT paths, each judged against the working directory and the data directory at run time alone. Input:
config.toml with `[network] allow = ["api.anthropic.com"]` and `[[secret]] name = "anthropic"`, `source =
"cmd:/home/u/tools/bin/getkey"`, an honest script of the operator's; `workcell run -- claude` in /home/u/proj,
where the guest writes /workspace/getkey, mode 0755, a script of its choice; `workcell pull /home/u/tools/bin`,
or `workcell pull /home/u/tools` since the guest's tree may name `bin/getkey`; later `workcell run` in any
directory, and the agent sends its placeholder once. Effect claimed: the pull writes the guest's getkey over
the operator's program, the next session's loadPolicy admits the row and mints a placeholder, and at the first
request the broker's Resolve runs the guest's program on the host as the operator, in every later session in
every directory. Lesser arms of the same missing judgement: a file: key under the destination is replaced with
the guest's bytes; an [update] ca under it becomes the root of the channel fetches; SSL_CERT_FILE, or a member
of an SSL_CERT_DIR entry, under it becomes an upstream root of every later session's proxy. Severity claimed:
medium. No file of the missing check is ported, so there is no v1 line; internal/secret/source.go, which is
ported, runs the program that the policy names and is not weak here, as C85's record held.

The auditor's evidence, by overlay into package main of cmd/workcell: with a config that holds a cmd: program, a
file: key and an [update] ca under a scratch home, holds answered nil for the directory of each and for the parent
of the program's directory, loadPolicy from another directory loaded both rows with no error, and loadPolicy
in the program's own directory was refused with C54's line; then the chain with the real writer and the real
broker call: holds nil, write returned nil and the file held the guest's bytes, loadPolicy gave one binding,
and secret.Resolve returned the guest's value while the guest's script made its marker file. The SSL_CERT arm
was reasoned from holds' code and not run.

Reproducing test (S4): TestC93PullDestinationHoldsATrustedPath, a Go test of package main for cmd/workcell, 88
lines, written by the redteam from the claim alone, with no VM and so no T2. A scratch home with config.toml,
an honest getkey under tools/bin, a file: key under keys and a ca under certs. A table of five rows asks holds()
for a destination that holds the cmd: program (the parent of its directory), the file: secret, the [update] ca,
SSL_CERT_FILE and an SSL_CERT_DIR entry, and wants an error for each. Two controls: a destination that holds none
of the paths is admitted, and the policy loaded in the program's own directory is refused. The main arm then
judges tools/bin as the pull does; if holds refuses it the arm ends there, and otherwise the pull's own writer
lands one executable entry getkey through manifest.add and write, the policy is loaded in another directory, the
row's source is resolved as the broker resolves it, and the arm fails when the marker file of the guest's script
exists, whatever a fix does to prevent that. The real verb cannot run without a VM: the boot, the init's tree and
the call of fetch itself are not in the test. Run by the orchestrator on 6476b44 with `go test -overlay`, go1.27.4,
plain and with -race, FAIL each time in the five rows (`c93_test.go:63: I13: the pull destination <home>/tools is
admitted, and it holds the cmd: program`, and so for keys, certs and roots) and in the main arm (`c93_test.go:85:
I13, I5: pull into <home>/tools/bin was admitted, the guest's getkey replaced the operator's, and a session in
<home>/proj loaded the row (<nil>) and ran it on the host: {Name:anthropic Source:cmd:<home>/tools/bin/getkey
Host:api.anthropic.com Header:x-api-key} gave "C93-TOKEN", <nil>`); the controls passed. gofmt and go vet with
the overlay are clean, by the redteam.

Outcome: CONFIRMED by the verifier at medium for the main arm, the cmd: program, and by C86's precedent for the
SSL_CERT arms; the [update] ca and the file: arm are low. Its evidence. One: the test fails as recorded, plain
and with -race. Two: nothing that the test skips would refuse: its own probe, by overlay, showed that every
judge of fetch before the boot answers nil for a destination that holds the program (holds nil, within(dest,
TempDir) false, named nil), that checkPath admits `getkey`, and that the real put replaced the operator's script
of mode 0700 with the guest's bytes at mode 0755; broker.Lookup (internal/secret/broker.go:128) calls Resolve
on the grant's source, the call the test makes. Three: the attacker is in scope and the test gives it no power:
it writes one executable at the root of its export, and the other steps are the operator's own and are the
precondition. The clause of SPEC section 2 on what a human later does with code they pulled does not fit, since
no human acts on the program: workcell's own broker runs it at the next ordinary `workcell run`, and loadPolicy
says nothing. The clause on what the program of a cmd: source reads through its arguments does not fit either:
ADR-006 and the comment at policy.go:79 give the swap of the program as the reason for the refusal under the
working directory, and the record of C54 names this chain, the operator's own pull and the next session's first
use, as its effect; S-F37 and ADR-006 closed the working directory at load, and an explicit destination is judged
at neither end. docs/policy.md:10 says that pull refuses the data directory, the config directory and config.toml,
and no document says that a pull may land the guest's version of a trusted program. Four: no ruling accepts or
parks it. C85's record reasons that the operator's own pull lands the same bytes, and S-F69 put config.toml's target
into holds for that door; C19 and C29 hold for the data directory in both directions; C40 is about --mount alone;
the sentence of S-F32 that the destination is the operator's choice and is not judged speaks of which directory
and not of what in it is trusted, as C91's verifier read it, and holds judges the destination already; no line of
PARKED.md names a pull destination that holds a secret source, a ca or an SSL_CERT path. Severity by S6: medium
for the main arm, a break that was run with one precondition the attacker does not control, the grade of C54, C85,
C86 and C91; not high, since the plain pull into the working directory is closed. The SSL_CERT arms are medium
by C86's confirmed probe, but this test shows only that the destination is admitted, and its SSL_CERT_FILE row
names a file that it never creates: the fix unit's test carries the consequence or cites C86. The ca is low,
as C79 and C84 were ruled: the signature, the serial, the expiry and the digest still stand. The file: arm is
low: the real key never reaches the guest, and the loss is the operator's key file replaced at a destination
that they named; one clause closes all of them. Not S14: data.go, pull_vm.go and policy.go are this project's own.

Fix shapes, from the auditor, and the unit chooses none. One: in holds(dir), after the loop over the held
directories, read the user's policy (the file that configFile names) and refuse when leadsInto holds for the
destination and the path that loadPolicy judges of a [[secret]] row (the file: path, or the first word of a cmd:
source), the [update] ca, SSL_CERT_FILE, or an SSL_CERT_DIR entry or readable member, the list that session()
builds already; one error in the style of holds' others, which names the destination and the path. Since session()
and fetch both call holds, run and pull then share one judge, and the checks of loadPolicy, newInstaller and
session may shrink to pay the lines. Two: the same judgement in fetch alone, beside its call of holds, which
leaves run as it is and fails the five table rows of the test, which ask holds; a unit that takes it says so and
rewrites the rows to ask what it built. Cost to honest use, by the auditor: none where a run in such a directory
is refused already; only a pull from elsewhere into the directory of a trusted path changes its verdict, and
the error names the path.
