Source of cmd/workcell/c93_test.go (88 lines):

    // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
    // Copyright 2026 Omkhar Arasaratnam
    
    // Candidate C93 of S-1009 sweep 4 (I13; I5, I14, I6 by consequence): holds() judges a pull destination against the
    // data directory, the config directory and the file config.toml resolves to, and knows nothing of the other paths the
    // host later runs, opens or trusts from the user's config and environment: the program of a cmd: source, the file of
    // a file: source, the [update] ca, SSL_CERT_FILE and the entries of SSL_CERT_DIR. So `workcell pull <home>/tools/bin`
    // is admitted, the guest's getkey replaces the operator's, and the broker runs it on the host at the next session in
    // any other directory, where loadPolicy judges cwd alone. Fails until the fix lands.
    // Re-created as cmd/workcell/c93_test.go by the fix unit S-F79 from the record of C93 in loop/state/FINDINGS.md; it
    // lives there, in the suite, from that unit on.
    
    //go:build linux || (darwin && arm64 && cgo)
    
    package main
    
    import (
    	"cmp"
    	"io"
    	"os"
    	"path/filepath"
    	"testing"
    
    	"github.com/omkhar/workcell/v2/internal/guest"
    	"github.com/omkhar/workcell/v2/internal/secret"
    )
    
    // TestC93PullDestinationHoldsATrustedPath: a user config.toml whose cmd: program, file: secret and [update] ca lie
    // under the home directory, and an environment that names roots there. Each destination is judged as pull judges it.
    // On the main arm the pull's writer then lands one executable entry getkey, the policy is loaded in another directory
    // and the row's source is resolved as the broker resolves it; the arm fails when the guest's program ran on the host,
    // whatever a fix does to prevent it. Controls: a destination that holds none of the paths is admitted, and the policy
    // loaded in the program's own directory is refused, as today.
    func TestC93PullDestinationHoldsATrustedPath(t *testing.T) {
    	home := must(filepath.EvalSymlinks(t.TempDir())) // macOS: /var is /private/var
    	t.Setenv("HOME", home)
    	t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".config"))
    	t.Setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".local", "share"))
    	t.Setenv("TMPDIR", t.TempDir())
    	tools, keys, certs := filepath.Join(home, "tools", "bin"), filepath.Join(home, "keys"), filepath.Join(home, "certs")
    	roots, proj := filepath.Join(home, "roots"), filepath.Join(home, "proj")
    	cfg, marker := filepath.Join(home, ".config", "workcell"), filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "C93-RAN-ON-THE-HOST")
    	program, key, ca := filepath.Join(tools, "getkey"), filepath.Join(keys, "anthropic"), filepath.Join(certs, "ca.pem")
    	for _, d := range []string{tools, keys, certs, roots, proj, cfg} {
    		must(0, os.MkdirAll(d, 0o700))
    	}
    	config := "[network]\nallow = [\"api.anthropic.com\", \"api.openai.com\"]\n\n[[secret]]\nname = \"anthropic\"\n" +
    		"source = \"cmd:" + program + "\"\n\n[[secret]]\nname = \"openai\"\nsource = \"file:" + key + "\"\n\n" +
    		"[update]\nca = \"" + ca + "\"\n"
    	must(0, cmp.Or(os.WriteFile(program, []byte("#!/bin/sh\necho honest-key\n"), 0o700), os.WriteFile(ca, nil, 0o600),
    		os.WriteFile(key, []byte("honest\n"), 0o600), os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(cfg, "config.toml"), []byte(config), 0o600)))
    	for _, tc := range []struct{ name, dest, env, val string }{
    		{"the cmd: program", filepath.Dir(tools), "", ""}, {"the file: secret", keys, "", ""},
    		{"the [update] ca", certs, "", ""},
    		{"SSL_CERT_FILE", roots, "SSL_CERT_FILE", filepath.Join(roots, "roots.pem")},
    		{"an SSL_CERT_DIR entry", roots, "SSL_CERT_DIR", "/etc/ssl/certs:" + roots},
    	} {
    		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
    			if tc.env != "" {
    				t.Setenv(tc.env, tc.val)
    			}
    			if err := holds(tc.dest); err == nil {
    				t.Errorf("I13: the pull destination %s is admitted, and it holds %s", tc.dest, tc.name)
    			}
    		})
    	}
    	if err := holds(proj); err != nil {
    		t.Errorf("control: the pull destination %s, which holds none of the paths, was refused: %v", proj, err)
    	}
    	t.Chdir(tools)
    	if _, _, _, _, err := loadPolicy(nil, io.Discard); err == nil {
    		t.Error("control: the policy loaded in the cmd: program's own directory was admitted")
    	}
    	if err := holds(tools); err != nil {
    		return // the pull is refused: the invariant holds
    	}
    	script := "#!/bin/sh\necho ran > " + marker + "\necho C93-TOKEN\n" // the guest's getkey, pulled over the operator's
    	entries := []guest.Entry{fileEntry("getkey", int64(len(script)), true)}
    	must(0, write(openDir(t, tools), judged(t, entries), from([]byte(script))))
    	t.Chdir(proj) // the operator's next session, in any other directory
    	_, secrets, _, _, err := loadPolicy(nil, io.Discard)
    	row := append(secrets, binding{})[0].grant
    	v, runErr := secret.Resolve(t.Context(), row.Source) // what the broker runs at the first request on that host
    	if exists(marker) {
    		t.Errorf("I13, I5: pull into %s was admitted, the guest's getkey replaced the operator's, and a session in %s "+
    			"loaded the row (%v) and ran it on the host: %+v gave %q, %v", tools, proj, err, row, v, runErr)
    	}
    }

Shape chosen for C93 by the orchestrator of S-F79, before the redteam ran: shape one, the judgement in holds().
Reasons. One: holds() is the one judge that run (session, with the working directory) and pull (fetch, with the
destination) both ask, and the record of S-1009 holds that it grew by one path at each finding and never read the
policy; a second judge in fetch alone would be the next list to fall behind. Two: the test's five rows ask
holds, so shape one passes the test as recorded and shape two would rewrite the rows of a confirmed test. Three:
the SSL_CERT judgement of session() can move into holds whole, which pays most of its own lines; the checks of
loadPolicy and newInstaller stay, since explain, bench and update reach them without holds. The contract given
to the builder. holds(dir) reads the user's config.toml, the file configFile names, and refuses when the path
that loadPolicy judges of a [[secret]] row (a file: path, or the first word of a cmd: source), the [update] ca,
SSL_CERT_FILE, or an SSL_CERT_DIR entry or readable member lies in dir or has a prefix that leads into it, by
leadsInto, in one error that names dir and the path, before the pull VM boots and with nothing written. A missing
config.toml grants nothing and refuses nothing. A config.toml that cannot be read or parsed refuses the pull with
that error, since its rows cannot be judged; run refuses such a file at load already. Cost to honest use, as
chosen: a run is judged as today, since loadPolicy, newInstaller and session refuse the same paths against the
working directory before or where holds is asked; a pull into a directory that holds none of these paths goes
on as before; a pull whose destination holds or lies above one of them is refused until the operator names
another destination or moves the path, and a pull with a broken config.toml is refused until it is mended. The
SSL_CERT rows of the test show an admitted destination alone, and its SSL_CERT_FILE row names a file it never
creates: the consequence, a planted root that verifies the network attacker's leaf, is carried by the test of
C86, cmd/workcell/c86_test.go with its record above, and is not built again here. The fix note below says what
was built and measured.

C93 FIXED by S-F79, commits 04a5065 and f893891 (PR #375), shape one as chosen above. judge(dir, pull) in
cmd/workcell/data.go is the old holds with the new judgement at its end: it reads the user's config.toml by
policy.Read and refuses, in one error that names what trusts the path, the path and dir, when leadsInto holds for
the path of a [[secret]] row, SSL_CERT_FILE, or an SSL_CERT_DIR entry or readable member, and in a pull for the
[update] ca as well. holds(dir) is judge(dir, true), the pull's judge, so the recorded test and c19_test.go ask it
unchanged; session() asks judge(cwd, false). sourcePath in cmd/workcell/policy.go is the one reading of a source,
the file: path or the first word of a cmd: source, that loadPolicy and judge share. The SSL_CERT block of session()
moved into judge whole; the checks of loadPolicy and newInstaller stay, since explain, bench and update reach them
without holds. Against main: data.go 26 lines added and 6 removed, policy.go 8 and 2, pull_vm.go 4 and 11,
run_vm.go 5 and 19, docs/policy.md one sentence in its line 10; product 15000 of 15000, test 28494 of 28500,
the test's 88 lines paid by 81 lines of folds in twenty test files, white space alone (checked by the orchestrator
and the reviewer). Where the build differs from the contract above, and why. One: the [update] ca is judged in a
pull alone. A run in a directory that holds the ca starts today, since startup() only prints the installer's
refusal, and the builder's first tree refused that run; it was sent back before any commit, because every run that
starts today must go on (S1). Two: a pull is judged against its destination alone, a run against the working
directory and the data directory as before; 04a5065 judged both against the data directory, so a ca there refused
every pull.
Three: a relative ca is not judged in a pull, since the installer refuses it and it is never a root. Proved, the
test first: cmd/workcell/c93_test.go re-created from the record by the redteam (sha256 matched, then two head
lines reworded; diff checked by the orchestrator); on main it fails in its five rows and its main arm, run by the
redteam, the orchestrator and the reviewer, and on the fix it passes plain and under -race, the controls unchanged,
with the C19, C29, C54, C58, C79, C84, C85, C86 and C91 tests. The reviewer's 28 cases, run on main and on 04a5065:
every run verdict the same; the pull verdicts that changed were the destinations that hold or are led into by
a path, a link on either side included, a path not made yet, an SSL_CERT_DIR member, a broken config.toml and,
on 04a5065 alone, a path under the data directory and a relative ca, which f893891 gave back to main's verdict. Its
real pull([]string{"."}) with the ca under the working directory returned 1 with the one line before any boot, where
main went on to start the VMM. Cost to honest use, as built: a run is judged as before, though a run with two
faults under --mount now names the SSL_CERT path before the temp directory; a pull or a diff whose destination
holds or leads into one of the paths is refused until another destination is named or the path moved; a pull or a
diff with a config.toml that cannot be read or parsed is refused; a relative secret word or SSL_CERT value is read
against the directory pull is started in, so only a pull into that directory is refused for it, and no run starts
with such a value. Not shown: the real verb on a VM beyond the hosted suite's own pull rows; the three corrections
after the review were measured by the builder's probes, which are not kept, and no second review ran (R1).

## S-1010, sweep 4: audit log, seal, key storage, `verify` (I9), as built at main aac1c8f

Trust boundary, as the auditor wrote it before the records were opened. Attacker bytes that reach a record:
the raw SNI of a refused 443 connection (route in internal/proxy/proxy.go returns it as sent; crypto/tls
refuses only a trailing dot; bounded by the 16 KiB hello), the lower-cased name of a refused DNS question (the
resolver's question: letters, digits, dot and dash within 253 bytes, or the empty string when any other byte),
the port of a relay header to an unserved TCP port (a uint16), the command's exit status (one byte, as `exit
N`), and the rate and timing of every attempt, which drive the log's volume to SoftLimit and choose the moment
of the session's end. Every other field is a host constant, an allowlist key (canonical: lower case, checked
by dnsName) or the operator's config (a secret's name and header; the repository's policy can only keep the
user's own rows). Time is the host clock. The network attacker reaches no record (dial_failed, resolve_failed
and blocked_address are constants beside the canonical host), and the repository reaches none: it can only have a
start refused before any record, or fail the export (C83, fixed). Entry: append in internal/audit/audit.go clips
the five string fields to 253 bytes and marshals by encoding/json, so no raw byte below 0x20 and no second line;
one mutex; one write for a line; the seal (ed25519 over `workcell-audit-seal-v2 `, the session id and the SHA-256
chain head, 194 bytes) rewritten in place after every line; Record also syncs both files. Exits: audit.Verify,
ParseLine (a strict decoder, unknown fields refused, 16 KiB), eachLine (ported; MaxBytes is HardLimit and two
lines), the log verb's feed, and denyMessage and ocsfLine, which pass the one free field through SafeHost; raw
lines are printed only for records whose fields are host or config strings. Authority: the supervisor, as the
operator's uid, owns sessions/<id>/audit.log and audit.seal (0600) and audit.key in the data directory (0600,
made with O_EXCL at first use, refused with any group or other bit, read into memory only); log and verify read
as the same uid. Writers: the proxy's Deny (the Allowed record before the terminate check and before the dial,
and the refusals), the relay's port_not_allowed and the resolver's name_not_allowed through the one closure
in boot, the broker's durable record (it acts on nil alone), and the supervisor's session_start (newSession)
and session_end (deferred). The boots of pull and bench pass a nil log, every Note of which is ErrClosed, and
have no listeners. The guest never reaches the files: judge() refuses a working directory or a pull destination
that holds, lies in or is another name of the data directory (by spelling, inode and mount point), and the key
goes to no kernel command line, environment, CA or secret program. The offline editor of I9's last clause is,
in scope, an actor without the key: the chain and the seal show any changed byte, and an editor with the key
is the operator.

Lenses (S9), each worked, in this order. One, parsing and resources: the writer's most, HardLimit with the
log_full marker and two lifecycle lines, is under the reader's MaxBytes, every field is clipped and a line
stays under the reader's line limit; FuzzEachLine for 180 s, 23495 executions, no crasher (the engine is slow
on this target, as sweep 3 found); nothing. Two, logic and state: one note, in PARKED.md (newSession). Three,
concurrency and check-to-use: C94. Four, cryptography and identity: the domain string, a session id that holds

140 (acts on nil, then closes the write side and drains) and 152; terminate.go 279 (the dial callback fails

### S-1010 candidates, sweep 4

C94. ID I9, in the order of the record and the verdict of `workcell verify`: the host writes connection
records after session_end, and verify then calls an honest, whole and unedited record `incomplete: the
session's end was not recorded`. Attacker: root in the guest, or hostile model output that runs a few lines
of shell there. Precondition: none. Where: cmd/workcell/run_vm.go, the deferred end of session() (:102-111),
which calls Record(session_end) and then Close() as two critical sections, with b.close() (:126) run before
it, so that the VM's death wakes every proxy handler first and nothing joins them; internal/audit/audit.go,
append (:108-141) and Close (:171-181), where nothing ends the log at the end record; internal/proxy/proxy.go,
handle (:133-138), where a 443 connection that ends before a ClientHello is refused with a `no_sni` Note;
cmd/workcell/log.go, the completeness rule of the verify verb (S-F17). Input: in the guest, open about 1000
TCP connections to an allowed name on port 443, send nothing, keep them open and exit 0. The proxy waits up
to 10 s for a hello on each; when the VMM dies every wait ends at once, about 1000 handlers call Note, and
the supervisor writes session_end in the same instant and holds the mutex through its syncs. Under that crowd
the mutex is handed to the waiting Notes before Close() takes it. Effect: audit.log ends with connect records
whose times are after session_end; audit.Verify returns nil, chain and seal intact, and `workcell verify <id>`
exits 1 with `incomplete: the session's end was not recorded`, for good, for that session; `workcell log`
shows refusals after the end. No record is suppressed, forged or altered, and every offline edit is still found.

Evidence of the auditor, by probes that are not kept. In package audit, 256 goroutines that Note while
Record(session_end) and Close() run as session() runs them: 20 of 20 rounds held records after session_end, 256
to 381 a round, Verify nil and the last event connect. In package proxy, the real Proxy and a real audit.Log,
400 idle 443 connections closed in a loop and then the end record and the close with no delay: 402 records,
session_end at index 393 and 8 connect records after it; with a delay of 1 ms or 5 ms, none. The same with
200, 600 and 1000 connections held by a child process that is killed: 0 of 9 on the session's tmpfs, which
the auditor reported as not reproduced.

The earlier records, weighed by the auditor and by the verifier. Sweep 1 took `a late Deny during teardown
lands after session_end or gets ErrClosed` as a note. Sweep 2 (TestProbeLateNoteAfterSessionEnd, one parked
Note, 0 of 50) and sweep 3 (TestProbeNoteRacesSessionEnd, one spinning goroutine, 0 of 300) kept it a note
because no record ever landed, and said that one that landed would be a false alarm with nothing suppressed,
forged or altered. Their measured ground does not stand: each probe had one writer, which loses the lock to the
Close() already running, while a crowd of waiters is served first. Their judgement of the consequence stands,
and it is the grade here. PARKED.md also holds, from S-F17, a passing `incomplete` between verify's read and
its lock probe, which is another thing: it is gone at the next run of verify, and this one is not.

The test. The redteam wrote it from the claim alone, as a Go test of package audit with no VM:
TestC94NothingIsRecordedAfterTheSessionEnds, 69 lines, a control arm with no writer and a finding arm of ten
rounds with 256 writers. Run by the orchestrator on fad9318 with go1.27.4 by `go test -overlay`, three times
plain and three times with -race: the control arm passed in all six, and the finding arm failed in all six,
`10 of 10 rounds recorded after session_end` in five and 9 of 10 in one under -race, each with `256 records
after session_end; Verify = <nil>, last.Event = "connect"`; no data race was reported. The redteam's own runs:
10 of 10 plain and 5 of 5 under -race failed in the finding arm, the control passing in all, about 0.34 s a
run plain and 2.6 s under -race.

Ruling of the verifier, who saw the claim, the test and the two logs and none of the auditor's reasoning:
CONFIRMED at low, the grade claimed. It ran the test again, 3 of 3 failing in the finding arm with the control
passing. It then built the shape of the product, with no power that the guest lacks, in a probe of package
main of cmd/workcell that is not kept: the wiring of boot() (newAdapters, proxy.New and serveRelay) on a unix
listener in a temp directory, a child process in the VMM's place that opens 1000 relayed streams to port 443
with a header and no hello, the child killed and reaped, then Record(session_end) and Close() in the order
of session()'s defers. One round gave session_end at line 59 with 943 records after it and the verify verb's
exit 1 with the incomplete line; of 20 further rounds 4 showed it (396, 396, 208 and 134 records after the end)
and 16 did not, about one session in five on this machine; the control with no connection verified intact with
exit 0. On the grade: no record is suppressed, forged or altered, no edited log verifies (TestVerify passes:
dropped, altered, truncated, repeated, swapped, emptied, another key and a renamed session each exit 1),
and verify fails closed with a different word for an edit (`changed`) than for this (`incomplete`); so I9
holds and only the completeness rule of S-F17 misfires, which is hardening with no break, low under S6. It
is a finding and not nothing because an in-scope attacker brings about, at will and for good, a false alarm
in the operator's own check. The verifier corrects one clause of the claim: the operator can tell this from a
SIGKILL by reading the log, where a killed session has no session_end at all, though not by verify's verdict
alone. S14: nothing private. The defect is the order in audit.go and run_vm.go, v2's own; proxy.go, where
the trigger lies, is ported and holds no weakness here. also in v1 main: egressproxy/proxy.go (the `no_sni`
refusal at the end of a connection, the trigger alone).

Fix, for S-F80, as the auditor gave it: end the log at the end record, in the critical section that writes
it. In append, once the write of a session_end record has succeeded, set the log's failed state to ErrClosed,
so that every later Note and Record fails and adds no line; Close keeps closing the files. About two product
lines, paid by folding the two `return ErrFull` arms of the overflow branch into one. The verifier named
a second shape, joining the handlers before the end record, which is more code in run_vm.go and leaves the
broker's and the resolver's writers to the same gap; the unit line takes the first. Variants that the redteam
could not express and that the first shape also closes, to be asked by the reviewer of S-F80: a durable Record
of a secret use from the broker that lands after session_end, and a session_start record after it.

Not shown: nothing ran on a real VM or on macOS, and no real session ran, so no `workcell verify` of a session
that a guest ended this way was seen; the product shape is the verifier's probe, one session in five here,
and was not run under -race; how often it lands on a real disk, where the end record's syncs hold the lock for
longer, was not measured. The head comment of the test says in its lines 4 and 5 that Verify accepts the log as
complete, where audit.Verify returns nil and the verify verb then says incomplete; S-F80 rewords those lines. The
test is not parked under escape/_pending/, since the test budget has six lines of room: this record holds it,
byte for byte behind four spaces (sha256 0a2f7b9b6b1b88d41fe44a58021252a4c6dcb740f08a14c1f5cdd417887e256c),
and the fix unit re-creates it, paid by folds outside escape/.

Source of internal/audit/c94_test.go (69 lines):

    // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
    // Copyright 2026 Omkhar Arasaratnam
    
    // C94 (I9): between Record(session_end) and Close the lock is free, so a guest-driven connect
    // record can land after session_end and Verify accepts the log as complete. Fails until S-F80's
    // fix lands; S-F80 puts it at internal/audit/c94_test.go.
    
    package audit
    
    import (
    	"crypto/ed25519"
    	"fmt"
    	"os"
    	"path/filepath"
    	"strings"
    	"sync"
    	"testing"
    	"time"
    )
    
    // c94Round ends a session while writers Note refused connections. It returns how many records
    // follow session_end, whether Verify accepts the log as ended, and a line describing both.
    func c94Round(t *testing.T, writers int) (after int, ended bool, got string) {
    	t.Helper()
    	key, _ := LoadKey(t.TempDir())
    	dir := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "ws-c94")
    	os.Mkdir(dir, 0o700)
    	l, _ := Create(dir, key, time.Now)
    	l.Record(Record{Event: SessionStart})
    	var wg sync.WaitGroup
    	for range writers {
    		wg.Go(func() {
    			for l.Note(Record{Event: Connect, Port: 443, Result: "no_sni"}) == nil {
    			}
    		})
    	}
    	time.Sleep(3 * time.Millisecond)
    	l.Record(Record{Event: SessionEnd, Result: "exit 0"})
    	l.Close()
    	wg.Wait()
    	if l.Note(Record{Event: Connect, Port: 443, Result: "no_sni"}) == nil {
    		t.Error("a Note after Close returned nil")
    	}
    	b, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, LogName))
    	lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(string(b), "\n"), "\n")
    	after = len(lines) - 1 - strings.Count(string(b[:max(strings.Index(string(b), `"event":"`+SessionEnd+`"`), 0)]), "\n")
    	last, err := Verify(dir, key.Public().(ed25519.PublicKey))
    	got = fmt.Sprintf("last line %s; %d records after session_end; Verify = %v, last.Event = %q", lines[len(lines)-1], after, err, last.Event)
    	return after, err == nil && last.Event == SessionEnd, got
    }
    
    func TestC94NothingIsRecordedAfterTheSessionEnds(t *testing.T) {
    	t.Run("control: no writer", func(t *testing.T) {
    		if after, ended, got := c94Round(t, 0); after != 0 || !ended {
    			t.Error(got)
    		}
    	})
    	t.Run("finding: 256 writers racing the end", func(t *testing.T) {
    		bad, got := 0, ""
    		for range 10 {
    			if after, _, g := c94Round(t, 256); after > 0 {
    				bad, got = bad+1, g
    			}
    		}
    		if bad > 0 {
    			t.Errorf("%d of 10 rounds recorded after session_end; %s", bad, got)
    		}
    	})
    }

C94 FIXED by S-F80, commit d3c9caa (PR #377), in the shape its unit line chose. append in
internal/audit/audit.go ends the log at the end record: when the write of a session_end record has returned nil
it sets the log's failed state to ErrClosed in the same critical section, so every later Note and Record returns
`audit: the log is closed` and adds no line to the log or the seal, and Close goes on closing both files and
returns what it returned before. Nothing in cmd/workcell/run_vm.go changed and no handler is joined, so the
broker's writer is under the same rule as the proxy's. Against main: audit.go 11 lines added and 8 removed, the
two `return ErrFull` arms of the overflow branch folded into one with one log_full marker and then ErrFull as
before, and the Proxy literal of New in internal/proxy/proxy.go three lines shorter to pay the rest; product
15000 of 15000, test 28498 of 28500, the test's 69 lines paid by 65 lines of folds in sixteen test files, line
breaks alone (checked by the orchestrator, with all white space and a comma before a closing bracket taken out
of both sides, and by the reviewer on the token stream). The test is internal/audit/c94_test.go, the source
above with lines 4 to 6 of its head reworded and no other byte changed: on the claim f0d99e1 its finding arm
fails in 10 of 10 runs plain and 10 of 10 under -race, 256 to 263 records after session_end with Verify nil,
and on d3c9caa it passes 10 of 10 both ways, its control arm passing on both trees. The variants the test does
not express, each run by the builder and again by the reviewer on both trees: a durable Record of a secret use
after the end, a session_start after it, a Note and a second session_end are each refused with no byte added,
where main took all four; a session whose end record itself fails is left as on main, failed with the write's
error and not ErrClosed, later writers refused with that error, Close closing the log file, and verify calling
it incomplete, which is true of it; Close after a good end returns nil. Nothing honest records after the end
today: the only writers are session() and newSession in run_vm.go, Deny in proxy.go and record in
internal/secret/broker.go, the VMM is dead before the end record is written, a start that fails in newSession
writes no end, a start that fails at the export or the boot writes session_end failed last, and the pull and
bench boots hold a nil log. No Event is taken from guest bytes, so a guest cannot have the end record written
early. Not shown: no real session ran on a VM in the cloud session; the hosted gate ran its I9 rows on d3c9caa.
also in v1 main: egressproxy/proxy.go, the trigger alone (the `no_sni` refusal); the defect was v2's own.

## S-1011, sweep 4: pins, selector, verification, bump tool, channel manifest, update client (I14, section 10), as built at main 34357e7

Sweep 4 (S8), the one further sweep that the maintainer allowed on 2026-11-26 after ADR-006, fresh context
(S3), the whole surface read in full as built after S-F71 to S-F80, not a diff, at the claim commit 0f5127f.
One auditor run on the top tier, finished without a stop. One of its responses, a step of building its test
overlay, was stopped by a safety classifier and withheld; it did not send that step again and went on with a
leaner overlay (S11). No hypervisor in the cloud session, and nothing on this surface was run on a VM: every
probe ran by `go test -overlay` from a scratch directory outside the repository, on go1.27.4, against files
and loopback listeners that the probe itself made (S12, T8). One thing left the host, by the auditor's own
account: its first `go version` fetched the go1.27.4 toolchain through the Go module proxy, as the go command
does by default, before it set GOPROXY=off; no probe reached a third party. The auditor wrote its own trust
boundary and worked every lens before it opened the records of this surface, then traced and ran every
recorded fix and tried the parked leads again. Result: no candidate at medium or above and two at low, C95
(I14) and C96 (I14 with B9 and B10), each given to a redteam as a claim only, run by the orchestrator and
ruled on by its own verifier, who saw none of the auditor's reasoning: both CONFIRMED at low; the records are
under the next heading. Nothing was fixed (S1). No file of this surface carries `// Ported from v1`, and
nothing is someone else's project (S14).

Trust boundary, as the auditor wrote it before the records were opened. A network attacker holds the path of a
host fetch and not the channel key: `channel.json` comes through installer.manifest and artifact.Fetch (64 KiB
cap, no redirect followed) to channel.Verify, and artifact bodies through installer.fetch and artifact.Fetch
(512 MiB, https only, at most three redirects) to a SHA-256 compared with the signed pin before unpack; no
byte is used without the manifest's signature or the pin's digest, so this attacker holds availability and the
sight of requests. Guest root and a malicious repository: one Exit frame with an error as the guest's first
frame reaches installer.fail behind the pair gate of `fresh` (S-F1, S-F31, S-F43); the repository also chooses
the working directory and `workcell.toml`, where policy.ReadRepo refuses an `[update]` table (I13) and the
installer reads the working directory only to refuse a `ca` that leads into it (S-F42, S-F63, S-F68); the
guest writes host files by design (the mount export, writable cache images, workspace.ext4) and the update
path reads none of them unless the operator's `ca` names one, which S-F68 refuses for the data directory.
Upstream bytes (npm packuments, release listings, vendor manifests, OCI tag lists and manifests, Sigstore
bundles, npm attestations, OSV and REST answers) enter cmd/bump on the runner, dry-run only until H-905; a
hostile provider service is out of scope, as the S-1012 ruling has it, so there the questions are robustness:
nothing injected into rows, branch names, pull-request bodies or issues, no silent skip of a verification
(B5), no auto-merge of a trusted security bump. Out of scope except where they meet attacker bytes: the holder
of the channel key, for every signed field, and the operator's own `[update]` table. Authority: `workcell
update`, startup (apply and daily) and fail run as the operator and write layers/<agent>/ (the images and the
markers current, previous and failed), channel.serial, channel.day, channel.next and updates.log under the
data directory; findLayers turns `current` into a drive that both backends attach read-only and that the init
mounts read-only; the bump tool runs in CI with a read-only token today and would hold the App's contents and
pull-request write after H-905.

The lenses of S9, each worked in turn. Parsing and resources: channel.Verify is a strict envelope over a
lenient payload, one signature by a trusted key over the DSSE PAE of the raw payload bytes, the 64 KiB cap
equal in Fetch and Verify, the serial window from the last one seen to now plus 24 h, the expiry at most
serial plus 14 days, and the sha256, https and no-slash checks over pins and previous; a probe showed that
versions such as `..`, one with a NUL, one with a newline and an escape, and one of 300 bytes all verify, each
placeable by the key holder alone and each harmless or refused later (a NUL fails at the rename, 300 bytes at
NAME_MAX, as sweep 3 showed). internal/sigstore caps a bundle at 64 KiB, 1 to 10 certificates and 1 to 10 log
entries; internal/pins/sources.go caps a body at 64 MiB, follows three https-only redirects, drops
Authorization across hosts and reads 30 OCI manifests at most; rootfs.Apply behind unpack cleans names, links
only to existing entries, and its device nodes and setuid bits land in the guest-only image. Seven fuzz
targets ran three minutes each with no crasher. Held. Logic and state: every marker transition was traced and
run (install, already current, `--to` for the current, the previous, a failed image on disk and an unknown
version, `--rollback`, apply's skip of the failed digest, fail's pair check); choose applies the user's
cool-off to the signed `released` alone and never shortens (B10); Select drops a withdrawn digest from pins
and previous, and `--to` cannot name a withdrawn version; in the bump tool, plan never turns a failed
verification into a skip, Select never moves backwards and the trusted security lane never merges. Held, but
for the gap of C96. Concurrency and check-to-use: the daily goroutine is never awaited and shares no state
with the session; writeMarker is a temporary file and a rename with one fixed temporary name per marker, and a
probe of two writers over 400 rounds found, at the end of each round, no value that neither wrote whole (the
verifier of C95 later saw the store empty in passing, which that record holds); fetch hashes and unpacks the
same descriptor in the operator-only layer directory; apply installs at the start within channelBound, 10
minutes, and a probe against a loopback listener that accepts and never answers held it past 3 s, which sweeps
1 and 3 ruled R3. Held at the time, and C95's record now holds the passing state. Cryptography and identity:
ed25519 behind the 32-byte guard, the key id the SHA-256 of the raw key, NotAfter judged at now, and the
signed bytes are the parsed bytes, so base64 spellings and duplicate JSON keys cannot split them; in Sigstore
the leaf is chained at the Rekor integrated time to the embedded root, the SET verified over Rekor's canonical
JSON, the body binds leaf, signature and hash, the identity is compared byte for byte, and Rekor v2 is refused
closed. The TLS root of the host's fetches does not carry I14, which is why C59, C79 and C84 were low. Held.
Failure modes: every refusal leaves markers and serial untouched; a failed newInstaller gives the zero
installer whose fail reads nothing (S-F43); fetch leaves nothing behind on a digest mismatch or an unpack
refusal. One check fails open, the reading of the serial store: C95. Downgrade, rollback and replay: the
replay window is 14 days plus 24 h of skew for each data directory, by design; an equal serial passes; a fresh
data directory accepts any unexpired manifest; `--rollback` and fail read no manifest (ADR-004, a proposal),
which is the ground of C96. Interaction between surfaces: run orders loadPolicy, startup, findLayers,
openCaches and then session's judge; startup writes only under the data directory and reads the working
directory only for the `ca` rule; ReadRepo refuses `[update]`; layers are read-only in both backends and in
the init; pull judges the `[update] ca` as a trusted path (S-F79); updates.log stays outside the signed audit
chain, as its parked line says. Held.

Recorded fixes of the surface, each traced in the code as built and its test run under the auditor's overlay,
plain and with -race where it says so. S-F1 and S-F31 (C1, C43): apply pairs each installed image with the one

within and judge in data.go read and traced; their tests need the helpers that the auditor's overlay dropped

Parked leads of the surface, each tried again, none changed. Rekor v2 is refused closed. Green in

### S-1011 candidates, sweep 4

C95. ID I14, its clause `a serial no lower than the last one seen`: the one stateful check of the channel
fails open on a store that is present and holds no number. Attacker: a network attacker on the path of the
channel fetch who serves the host an older manifest that is validly signed and not expired; that takes a break
of TLS or the channel's host, and no key. Precondition, which the attacker does not control:
`<data>/channel.serial` is present and holds no number. Where: cmd/workcell/update.go, installer.verify
(:218-225), whose line 219 reads the floor by strconv.ParseInt of the marker and drops the error, so that
absent, empty and not a number are all floor 0; writeMarker (:462-468), which writes every marker through one
fixed temporary name, opened with truncation and never synced. Input: the damaged store, then a signed,
unexpired manifest whose serial is below the floor last verified. Effect: verify returns nil, line 224
rewrites the floor to the older serial, and the caller installs that manifest's pins: the rollback protection
is reset by no one who holds the key. The replay stays inside what the expiry leaves, 14 days at most, and
every pin in it is one the key holder signed.

Evidence of the auditor, by a probe that is not kept: TestProbeSerialStoreFailsOpen refused the older manifest
while the store held the floor and returned nil with the store holding "", "x" and "\n". It named three honest
causes of such a store, a crash, a full disk and two concurrent verifies; its own probe of two writers over
400 rounds looked at the value left at the end and found none torn.

The earlier record, weighed by the auditor and by the verifier. Sweep 3 of this surface took an unreadable
serial store that counts as floor 0 as a note, parked on the ground that no in-scope attacker writes under the
data directory, and no verifier ruled on it. The ground does not stand for this sibling: the writer is the
product itself.

The test. The redteam wrote it from the claim alone, as a Go test of package main in cmd/workcell with no VM
and no listener: TestC95DamagedSerialStoreRefusesOlderManifest, 53 lines. Its controls: with no store the
newer manifest verifies, against the intact store the older one is refused, and with the store removed at the
end the newer one verifies again, so an absent store may keep floor 0. Its finding arm asks, for each of the
three contents, an error and the store left as it was. Run by the orchestrator on 0f5127f with go1.27.4 by `go
test -overlay`, plain and with -race: the controls passed and the finding arm failed in its three rows both
times, `verify(older) = <nil>` and the store rewritten to the older serial; no data race was reported. The
redteam's own two runs gave the same.

Ruling of the verifier, who saw the claim, the test and the log and none of the auditor's reasoning: CONFIRMED
at low, the grade claimed. It ran the test again, plain and with -race, with the same three failing rows and
the controls passing. It then asked whether the product alone can leave such a store, by a probe that is not
kept: two goroutines that call writeMarker on channel.serial and a reader. Of 954,334 reads, 9,464 saw the
store present and empty, and 7,763 writes failed at the rename of a temporary file that was gone: both writers
share `channel.serial.tmp`, opened with truncation, so one writer's rename publishes the other's file before
its bytes are written. Writers that can meet exist: apply at a start, the day's check in its goroutine, and
`workcell update` run by hand. The empty state passes in a moment unless a writer is killed in that window, or
power is lost before the unsynced rename reaches the disk. Two of the three causes the claim named fall away:
a full disk and a plain crash fail before the rename and leave the store untouched. On the grade: SPEC section
2 names no attacker who alone can serve a validly signed older manifest at the channel's address, and the gain
is bounded to a signed, unexpired pin at most 14 days old, so this is hardening and low, not refuted and not
medium.

Not shown: nothing ran on a real VM or on macOS and the built binary did not run. The verifier's probe is two
goroutines in one process, not two processes of the product; no run left the store empty for good, which takes
a kill or a power loss in the window, and how wide that window is on a real disk was not measured. No older
manifest was served to a real fetch: the test calls verify. Variants that the redteam named and did not
express, none run: a number with bytes after it or one beyond int64 reads as floor 0 the same way, a negative
number is a floor below every serial, and the same dropped error is reached through apply and the day's check.
The test is not parked under escape/_pending/, since the test budget has two lines of room: this record holds
it, byte for byte behind four spaces (sha256
9bbd98f3ff55339d7b26a6537e1517a6efe2bd38ccab50fd11974bd010ce9bd3), and the fix unit S-F81 re-creates it, paid
by folds outside escape/.

    // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
    // Copyright 2026 Omkhar Arasaratnam
    
    // C95 (I14): a channel.serial store that is present but holds no number must not count as floor 0. This file belongs at cmd/workcell/c95_test.go.
    
    package main
    
    import (
    	"crypto/ed25519"
    	"crypto/rand"
    	"encoding/json"
    	"os"
    	"path/filepath"
    	"testing"
    	"time"
    
    	"github.com/omkhar/workcell/v2/internal/channel"
    )
    
    // TestC95DamagedSerialStoreRefusesOlderManifest: against an intact floor a signed manifest with a lower serial is refused (control); against a store that is present but holds "", "x" or "\n" it must be refused too, the store left as it was (finding); with no store at all the newer manifest verifies (control).
    func TestC95DamagedSerialStoreRefusesOlderManifest(t *testing.T) {
    	pub, key, _ := ed25519.GenerateKey(rand.Reader)
    	now := time.Now()
    	in := installer{dir: t.TempDir(), keys: []channel.Key{{Public: pub, NotAfter: now.Add(time.Hour)}}}
    	sign := func(serial int64) []byte {
    		body, _ := json.Marshal(channel.Manifest{Serial: serial, Expires: serial + 13*24*3600})
    		raw, err := channel.Sign(body, []ed25519.PrivateKey{key})
    		if err != nil {
    			t.Fatal(err)
    		}
    		return raw
    	}
    	newer, older, store := sign(now.Unix()-60), sign(now.Unix()-3600), filepath.Join(in.dir, "channel.serial")
    	if _, err := in.verify(newer, now); err != nil {
    		t.Fatalf("control: the newer manifest with no store yet: %v; want accepted", err)
    	}
    	if _, err := in.verify(older, now); err == nil {
    		t.Fatal("control: the older manifest against the intact store was accepted; want refused as a lower serial")
    	}
    	for _, damaged := range []string{"", "x", "\n"} {
    		if err := os.WriteFile(store, []byte(damaged), 0o600); err != nil {
    			t.Fatal(err)
    		}
    		_, err := in.verify(older, now)
    		if after, _ := os.ReadFile(store); err == nil || string(after) != damaged {
    			t.Errorf("finding: store holding %q: verify(older) = %v, store now %q; want an error and the store untouched", damaged, err, after)
    		}
    	}
    	os.Remove(store)
    	if _, err := in.verify(newer, now); err != nil {
    		t.Errorf("control: the newer manifest with the store absent: %v; want accepted", err)
    	}
    }

C95 FIXED by S-F81, commit 81fde0b (PR #379), in the shape its unit line chose. installer.verify in
cmd/workcell/update.go reads `<data>/channel.serial` itself, by os.ReadFile, and no longer through marker():
absent is floor 0 as before; a store that is present must be a decimal number of zero or more with at most the
one newline that writeMarker leaves, and one that is anything else, or that cannot be read, is refused before
channel.Verify with `<path> holds no serial number of zero or more; removing it starts the floor anew`, the
store left as it was. marker() and writeMarker are unchanged. Against main: update.go 7 lines added and 1
removed, one of them the io/fs import, paid by three one-statement funcs written on one line (Zero in
internal/secret/source.go, New in internal/vmm/firecracker/firecracker.go and in internal/vmm/vz/vz.go);
product 15000 of 15000, test 28500 of 28500, the test's 53 lines paid by 51 lines of row joins in six test
files, line breaks alone (checked by the orchestrator, with all white space and a comma before a closing
bracket taken out of both sides, and by the reviewer on the token stream of all nine files). The test is
cmd/workcell/c95_test.go, the source above with no byte changed (sha256 checked by the redteam, the builder,
the orchestrator and the reviewer): on the claim e01641b its three finding rows fail, verify nil and the store
rewritten, plain and under -race, by the redteam and the reviewer; on 81fde0b it passes plain and under -race,
by the builder, the orchestrator and the reviewer, its controls unchanged. Hosted on 81fde0b: gate (284 s, VM
suite included, so its I14 rows), gate-macos (144 s), gate-arm64 (91 s) and guard green.
Rulings, each run by the reviewer on both trees: refused with the store untouched are `5x`, a number beyond
int64, `-1`, two newlines, a leading or a trailing space, CR LF, `0x5`, `1_0`, a store that is a directory and
one of mode 0 read as another uid; taken as a floor are the number with or without its newline, `+5`, `0` and
`-0`. Through the verbs, called in the test process against a loopback channel: `workcell update claude` with
a store of "", "x" or a lone newline returns 1 with the one line on stderr, installs nothing and leaves the
store; apply prints the line after `workcell: channel:` and installs nothing; the day's check keeps no
channel.next and prints nothing, as it never prints. With the store absent the first manifest verifies and the
floor is written. The builder ran the built binary once, with a store of "x": the same line, exit 1.
Cost, as the unit line foresaw: a start that reads in the empty moment of another start's write now refuses a
good manifest once (the reviewer's probe of four concurrent verifies was refused more often than accepted,
where main accepted at floor 0), and in apply the kept channel.next is gone by then, so that manifest waits
for the next day's check; the store always ended holding a serial. NOT closed: a store left empty for good, by
a writer killed in that window or by lost power, now stops every channel check until the operator removes the
file, and only `workcell update` by hand says so, since a start's daily check drops the error; writeMarker's
one temporary name is the cause and the product budget has no line for it. S-1013 and S-1017 weigh it.
Correction to the record above: a number beyond int64 read on main as the largest int64, not as floor 0, and
was refused there as a lower serial.

C96. ID I14 in its downgrade lens, with B9 and B10: the self-rollback returns to an image whose digest the
kept manifest withdraws, and the failed marker then keeps the automatic path from leaving it. Attacker: root
in the guest, reached by a malicious repository's hook that speaks before the agent's first byte.
Precondition, which the attacker does not control: this very start applied a new layer, which is C2's, and the
manifest the host keeps withdraws the digest of the image that layer replaced. Where: cmd/workcell/update.go,
fail (:283-304), which names the new image in `failed`, points `current` back to the previous one and reads no
manifest, and apply (:264), which skips the pin whose image `failed` names and prints nothing. Input: the kept
manifest pins B and withdraws A's digest; apply installs B over A, so `fresh` holds that pair; the guest's
first frame is an Exit with an error; later starts keep the same manifest. Effect: current = A, the withdrawn
image, failed = B and previous empty; each later apply installs nothing for the provider and says nothing, so
every session runs the withdrawn CLI until the maintainer moves the pin or the operator runs `workcell update
<agent>`; updates.log holds a `failed` line for B and no line that names A. No invariant breaks: A was
installed under a manifest that verified, fail installs nothing, and the layer is guest content on a read-only
drive.

Evidence of the auditor, by a probe that is not kept: TestProbeFailReturnsToWithdrawn, where after fail
`current` named the image that stood for the withdrawn digest, `previous` was empty, `failed` named the new
one, and the one line on stderr was B9's.

The earlier records, weighed by the auditor and by the verifier, none of exactly this shape. C1 with S-F1, and
C2, accept the self-rollback to the image before, which lasts until the pin changes or the user runs update,
and never weigh that image being withdrawn. The parked lines on `workcell update --rollback`, which asks no
Withdrawn list, accept that because the next apply applies the pin again and because B10 names the verb as the
user's own act; neither holds here, where the failed marker stops the next apply and the guest, not the user,
is the cause. The parked line on a set-aside image that stays on disk is another residual. ADR-004, a
proposal, says that fail reads no manifest by design.

The test. The redteam wrote it from the claim alone, as a Go test of package main in cmd/workcell with no VM
and no listener: TestC96WithdrawnImageIsNotCurrentAfterSelfRollback, 66 lines, two arms over one sequence: the
state that an apply of B over A leaves, then fail, then the next start's apply. The control arm, A not
withdrawn, asks that current be A, which is the designed self-rollback; the finding arm, A withdrawn, asks
that current not be A, so that it passes with B current again and also with the return to A refused. The pin's
URL is an address that nothing contacts. Run by the orchestrator on 0f5127f with go1.27.4 by `go test
-overlay`, plain and with -race: the control arm passed and the finding arm failed both times, `current is A
..., the withdrawn image, after fail current=A failed=B`, with fail's one line and none from apply; no data
race was reported. The redteam's own two runs gave the same.

Ruling of the verifier, who saw the claim, the test and the log and none of the auditor's reasoning: CONFIRMED
at low, the grade claimed. It ran the test again, plain and with -race, with the same result. It traced the
state that the test writes by hand, and found it to be what honest calls leave: for a manifest that pins B and
withdraws A's digest, channel.Select returns B alone; update fetches B and point leaves current = B and
previous = A; apply appends the pair to `fresh`; verify writes the manifest's serial. startup runs the day's
check after apply, so on a new UTC day the unchanged channel.json is fetched into channel.next again, and
Verify refuses only a lower serial, so the same manifest verifies at the next start. fail then writes failed =
B, current = A and previous empty and reads no manifest, and apply's line 264 skips without a word. The test
takes no power that the guest lacks: its call of fail is what run_vm.go makes of the first-frame Exit, the
path of C1 and C2. On the grade: I14's sentence governs what is installed, A was installed under a valid
manifest and fail installs nothing, and `withdrawn` is a word of ADR-004 and not of an invariant, so nothing
breaks and the grade is low, not medium.

Not shown: nothing ran on a real VM or on macOS, no real session forged the frame here, and the built binary
did not run: the forged frame is the call of fail, as in the records of C1 and C2, and the install of B over A
is the verifier's trace of the code and not a run. Variants that the redteam named and did not express, none
run: `workcell update --rollback` reaches a withdrawn `previous` the same way, which its parked line holds; a
withdrawal that arrives in a later manifest for an image that is only `previous`, followed by a fail that
returns to it; and that updates.log shows no line for the return to A. The test is not parked under
escape/_pending/, since the test budget has two lines of room: this record holds it, byte for byte behind four
spaces (sha256 84ba62e7efb1561b50fdd7a3701446e14ba4bd2a20519c69d0917b9ed8f2a777), and the fix unit S-F82
re-creates it, paid by folds outside escape/.

    // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
    // Copyright 2026 Omkhar Arasaratnam
    
    // C96 (I14 with B9): the self-rollback must not leave a withdrawn image current. This file belongs at cmd/workcell/c96_test.go.
    
    package main
    
    import (
    	"bytes"
    	"crypto/ed25519"
    	"crypto/rand"
    	"crypto/sha256"
    	"encoding/hex"
    	"encoding/json"
    	"errors"
    	"net/http"
    	"os"
    	"path/filepath"
    	"runtime"
    	"strconv"
    	"testing"
    	"time"
    
    	"github.com/omkhar/workcell/v2/internal/channel"
    	"github.com/omkhar/workcell/v2/internal/pins"
    	"github.com/omkhar/workcell/v2/internal/provider"
    )
    
    // TestC96WithdrawnImageIsNotCurrentAfterSelfRollback: this start's apply installed B over A, and the guest's first frame is an Exit with an error, so fail sets B
    // aside and points current back at A, reading no manifest; the next start's apply skips B's pin, because B is marked failed. Finding arm: the kept manifest
    // withdraws A, and after apply A must not be current (B installed again, or the return to A refused). Control arm: A not withdrawn, current = A is B10's self-rollback.
    func TestC96WithdrawnImageIsNotCurrentAfterSelfRollback(t *testing.T) {
    	p := must(provider.All())[0] // fail finds the provider by its binary among the built-in ones
    	pub, key, _ := ed25519.GenerateKey(rand.Reader)
    	sum := func(s string) string { d := sha256.Sum256([]byte(s)); return hex.EncodeToString(d[:]) }
    	a, b := "1.0.0-"+sum("a")+".ext4", "1.0.1-"+sum("b")+".ext4"
    	run := func(t *testing.T, withdrawn []string) (cur, said string) {
    		dir := t.TempDir()
    		layers := filepath.Join(dir, "layers", p.Name)
    		now := time.Now().Unix()
    		m := channel.Manifest{Serial: now - 60, Expires: now - 60 + 13*24*3600, Withdrawn: withdrawn, Pins: map[string]map[string]channel.Pin{p.Install.Pin: {runtime.GOARCH: {Version: "1.0.1", URL: "https://127.0.0.1:1/b", SHA256: sum("b")}}}}
    		body, _ := json.Marshal(m)
    		raw, err := channel.Sign(body, []ed25519.PrivateKey{key})
    		// what an apply that installed B over A leaves: both images, current B, previous A, the serial of the manifest it verified; and the day's check kept that manifest again
    		err = errors.Join(err, os.MkdirAll(layers, 0o700), os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(layers, a), nil, 0o600), os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(layers, b), nil, 0o600), writeMarker(layers, "current", b), writeMarker(layers, "previous", a))
    		if err = errors.Join(err, writeMarker(dir, "channel.serial", strconv.FormatInt(m.Serial, 10)), writeMarker(dir, "channel.next", string(raw))); err != nil {
    			t.Fatal(err)
    		}
    		in := installer{dir: dir, rows: []pins.Pin{{Name: p.Install.Pin, Release: pins.Release{Version: "0"}}}, client: &http.Client{}, channel: "https://127.0.0.1:1/channel.json", keys: []channel.Key{{Public: pub, NotAfter: time.Unix(1<<40, 0)}}, fresh: []string{b + "\n" + a}}
    		var out bytes.Buffer
    		in.fail(p.Binary, &out) // the attacker's one act: the forged Exit frame, as run reports it
    		said = "after fail current=" + marker(layers, "current") + " failed=" + marker(layers, "failed") + "; "
    		in.apply([]provider.Provider{p}, &out)
    		return marker(layers, "current"), said + out.String()
    	}
    	t.Run("control: A not withdrawn, the self-rollback leaves A current", func(t *testing.T) {
    		if cur, said := run(t, nil); cur != a {
    			t.Errorf("current %q, %s; want A %q", cur, said, a)
    		}
    	})
    	t.Run("finding: A withdrawn, A must not be current", func(t *testing.T) {
    		if cur, said := run(t, []string{sum("a")}); cur == a {
    			t.Errorf("current is A %q, the withdrawn image, %s; want B %q current again, or the return to A refused with a line that says so", cur, said, b)
    		}
    	})
    }
